title: The early reviews for the Madden movie aren't good
summary: The Madden movie, starring Nicolas Cage as the legendary coach, broadcaster, and video-game mogul, has landed on Prime Video.
full_text: The Madden movie, starring Nicolas Cage as the legendary coach, broadcaster, and video-game mogul, has landed on Prime Video. In the eyes of critics, it has landed with a thud. The current consensus at Rotten Tomatoes, based on 16 reviews, is 13 percent . The folks at Sports Business Journal have collected and summarized some of the feedback. Owen Gleiberman of Variety calls it a "stunt biopic on cinematic amphetamines," adding that " it’s like an SNL sketch shot and edited by Scorsese ." Then there's this incredible lede from David Rooney of the Hollywood Reporter : "Imagine being cornered at a party while sober by a wired cokehead determined to tell you a long, painstakingly detailed story without pausing for breath and you might have some idea of the exhausting experience of watching Madden ." Bryan Curtis of The Ringer says "[i]t's not quite as awful as the trailers made it look," but that it still "isn't good." Curtis also says Christian Bale is "mesmerizing" as Al Davis, which raises the question of why they didn't just make an Al Davis movie? Of course, I'll still watch it. You should, too. But I have a feeling that, throughout the experience, I'll be wondering how much John Madden himself would have hated it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Wan'Dale Robinson out for season with ankle injury
summary: The Titans will not have one of their key receivers for the rest of 2026.
full_text: The Titans will not have one of their key receivers for the rest of 2026. Receiver Wan'Dale Robinson is out for the season after being placed on injured reserve this week with an ankle injury, head coach Robert Saleh told reporters in his Wednesday press conference. Robinson signed with the Titans as a free agent in the offseason, reuniting him with former Giants head coach Brian Daboll, who serves as Tennessee’s offensive coordinator. In nine games with three starts this season, Robinson caught 38 passes for 272 yards with three touchdowns.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Todd Monken: Getting flexed into Sunday night is really cool for our players
summary: If someone had told you at the beginning of the season that the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders would get flexed into Sunday Night Football, you probably would have responded with some healthy skepticism.
full_text: If someone had told you at the beginning of the season that the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders would get flexed into Sunday Night Football, you probably would have responded with some healthy skepticism. But with the way the season has unfolded, that's exactly what's happened. With the Browns at 6-4 and the Raiders at 4-6 — and now starting the league's No. 1 overall pick at quarterback — the two clubs make for one of the most compelling matchups of Thanksgiving weekend that wasn't already in a standalone window. Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Wednesday that getting flexed is “really cool for our players.” “I said it at the beginning of the year. I mean, you want to be on Thursday Night, Sunday Night, Monday Night — you want to be flexed, means you’re having a good year,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “As nice as it is to have a one o’clock schedule every week, I mean, I said that, early in the [year]. I mean, you’re on a trajectory to be fired at some point because you’re at one o’clock every week. So, you’re fighting like hell to get to where you’re on national TV. So, if people are going to watch football, and more importantly than that, an opportunity to get to seven [wins].” Monken also agreed that it’s a good test for the Browns as a young team. “I think you earn where you’re at in the present moment, and that only lends itself to what’s in front of you and how important that’s going to become,” Monken said. “You know, getting the bye at 6-4 and putting yourself in position where the rest of the games matter, and especially the one coming up.” This will be the Browns’ first Sunday night game at home since 2019, which should make for a rowdy atmosphere on the shores of Lake Erie. “Oh, it’s a huge advantage. Huge advantage,” Monken said of the anticipated environment. “Making it hard for the opposing offense, cadence-wise, being able to function, and making an advantage for us when we’re on offense. I mean, it’s a huge advantage, and it should be playing at home.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: No practice for Baker Mayfield on Wednesday
summary: Word on Tuesday was that Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield's outlook for this week's game against the Lions was not promising and Wednesday didn't bring any better news.
full_text: Word on Tuesday was that Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield's outlook for this week's game against the Lions was not promising and Wednesday didn't bring any better news. Mayfield is dealing with a foot injury that had him in a walking boot during the team's bye week and he watched practice in street clothes on Wednesday. The Buccaneers have not made any official determination of his status, but things appear to be trending in the wrong direction. Jalon Daniels will make his fourth start of the season if Mayfield is unable to play this weekend. The Bucs added Easton Stick to the roster as a third quarterback this week. Reporters at the open portion of practice also noted that safety Antoine Winfield was not taking part for Tampa.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tory Horton's heads up play earns him NFC special teams player of the week
summary: Late in Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made a heads-up play on special teams that helped seal the win.
full_text: Late in Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made a heads-up play on special teams that helped seal the win. The league has recognized Horton for his efforts, naming him special teams player of the week. There was 2:04 remaining in the fourth quarter after Las Vegas narrowed Seattle’s lead to one possession with a 43-yard field goal. The Raiders tried to send the kickoff out of the end zone to preserve the two-minute warning, having just two timeouts left. But Horton leapt up and tipped the ball into the end zone to prevent a touchback. He then signaled for Rashid Shaheed to pick up the football, as he’d stepped out of bounds, to prevent an illegal touch. Shaheed returned the ball 22 yards, taking the clock down to 1:59. While the play was flagged for an illegal bat, Las Vegas declined it. A re-kick would have taken more time off the clock. Quarterback Drew Lock then sealed the victory with a 15-yard run. This is Horton’s first career player of the week award.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cam Little is AFC special teams player of the week for second week in a row
summary: Jaguars kicker Cam Little turned in another strong game against the Titans last Sunday.
full_text: Jaguars kicker Cam Little turned in another strong game against the Titans last Sunday. Little made all four field goals and all four extra points he attempted in Jacksonville's 40-23 win. It was the second straight week that Little made four field goals and the NFL recognized his accomplishment both times. Little was named the AFC special teams player of the week for the second week in a row. It's the first time that's happened since Cameron Dicker in 2024 and Little joins punter Bryan Barker as the only Jaguars players to pull off the double. Little is now 18-of-20 on field goals and 29-of-30 on extra points for the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Colts CB Justin Walley named the AFC defensive player of the week
summary: The Colts ended a five-game losing streak with last Sunday's win over the Dolphins and a defensive touchdown played a big role in the 24-22 win.
full_text: The Colts ended a five-game losing streak with last Sunday's win over the Dolphins and a defensive touchdown played a big role in the 24-22 win. Cornerback Justin Walley got home on a blitz deep inside Miami territory and separated Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord from the ball. Defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore recovered the ball for a touchdown. Walley had five tackles, two tackles for loss and two passes defensed overall in the win. The third-round pick has 40 tackles, two sacks and three forced fumbles to this point in his rookie season. The NFL named Walley the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday. It's the first time a Colt has won the award since early in the 2024 season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaelan Phillips wins first NFC defensive player of the week award
summary: The Panthers moved into sole possession of first place in the NFC South with their victory over the Saints on Sunday.
full_text: The Panthers moved into sole possession of first place in the NFC South with their victory over the Saints on Sunday. Now one of their players has been recognized for his performance in the win. Edge rusher Jaelan Phillips has been named NFC defensive player of the week. Phillips had five total tackles with three for loss, a sack, and a fumble recovery that led to a Panthers touchdown in the 20-17 victory. According to the league, Phillips is the second player in the conference to have three TFLs and a fumble recovery in a single game in 2026. This is Phillips’ first career defensive player of the week award. In his first season with Carolina, Phillips has tallied 3.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, and eight QB hits so far in 2026.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jahmyr Gibbs wins second NFC offensive player of the week award of the season
summary: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs continued his terrific 2026 season in Sunday's win over the Patriots in Munich.
full_text: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs continued his terrific 2026 season in Sunday's win over the Patriots in Munich. Now the league has recognized him for his performance in that contest. Gibbs has been named NFC offensive player of the week. Gibbs put up 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing, 99 receiving) along with two rushing touchdowns in the 35-10 win. According to the league, Gibbs is just the second player under the age of 25 in NFL history with at least 250 yards from scrimmage and two rushing touchdowns in multiple games, joining Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson. He also scored his 61st and 62nd touchdowns, which puts him past Hall of Famer Terrell Davis for the most touchdowns by a player in his first four seasons in league history. The 252 yards were the most by a player in a single game so far this season. They were also the second most in an international game in league history. Gibbs now has five career offensive player of the week awards. He last won it for Week 5 of this year. Through nine games, Gibbs leads the league with 1,000 rushing yards, 1,384 yards from scrimmage, 11 rushing touchdowns, and 13 total TDs.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Joe Burrow named AFC offensive player of the week for second time this season
summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is the betting favorite to be the NFL MVP this season and games like the one he had last Sunday are the reason why he's in that spot.
full_text: '' Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is the betting favorite to be the NFL MVP this season and games like the one he had last Sunday are the reason why he's in that spot. Burrow lit up the Steelers during a 38-18 win that extended Cincinnati's winning streak to five games. Burrow was 35-of-44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the victory. The four touchdowns moved him up to 20 over the course of the winning streak and he leads the league with 27 touchdown passes over the entire season. The NFL announced on Wednesday that Burrow has been named the AFC offensive player of the week. It's the second time he's won that prize this season and the 10th time in his career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Geno Smith will be limited in Wednesday's practice
summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith avoided a major ankle injury in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, but his Week 11 status remains uncertain.
full_text: Jets quarterback Geno Smith avoided a major ankle injury in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, but his Week 11 status remains uncertain. Head coach Aaron Glenn said at his press conference that Smith will be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice as the team works to get ready to face the Chargers. Glenn said that the team will see how the week plays out before making any determination about Smith's availability for the game. Fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut against the Bills and will make his first pro start if Smith is unable to play. Wide receivers Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will not practice on Wednesday due to injuries suffered in Week 10.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ben Johnson sees Bears' 4.2 yards per carry average as "a deceiving statistic"
summary: League wide, NFL teams average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt.
full_text: League wide, NFL teams average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt. The Bears also average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt. Bears coach Ben Johnson doesn't much care about that. What Johnson does care about is that the running game is efficient, and Johnson would like to see better efficiency than he has seen so far from his offense. Johnson noted that an occasional long run can skew the yards per carry average, and if there are too many runs getting stuffed for no gain, that's a problem. On the flip side, a one-yard run will bring down any team's average, but it's a great play if it happens on fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line. "I don't see it as bigger chunk runs, necessarily. The yards per carry is a deceiving statistic in a lot of ways," Johnson said. "We run the ball a lot in the red zone, and when you're down there a four-yard carry is really an explosive." Johnson said what he cares more about is efficiency. Many teams look at running success rate, which means the percentage of runs on which a team gains at least 40 percent of yardage needed on first down, at least 60 percent on second down, or at least 100 percent on third or fourth down. The Bears' success rate this season is 49.2 percent, and Johnson says that's not good enough. "We go off efficiency, and we're under 50 percent efficient running the ball. We set our bar higher than that. We want to be closer to 55 percent, so we've got some work to do and all our guys know it," Johnson said. Ultimately, Johnson wants to see rushing first downs and rushing touchdowns. Yards per carry is secondary to that.
author: Michael David Smith

title: 49ers likely won't cut Brandon Aiyuk until they have to
summary: With a roster exemption that lasts until November 24 and with no requirement to pay him a penny until the exemption expires, the 49ers have shown no inclination to release receiver Brandon Aiyuk until they absolutely have to.
full_text: With a roster exemption that lasts until November 24 and with no requirement to pay him a penny until the exemption expires, the 49ers have shown no inclination to release receiver Brandon Aiyuk until they absolutely have to. Nine days since Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers haven't cut him. At this point, with only six days to go, the 49ers surely will kick the can as long as they can. They gain nothing from delaying Aiyuk's return, other than the relatively minor strategic advantage of keeping him away from a competitor. With all signs pointing to Aiyuk landing in Washington, he's no threat to San Francisco's playoff interests. Of course, the receiver-needy Rams could get involved. Or perhaps the Vikings, who are currently without Jordan Addison. Or maybe the Seahawks, who don't have a clear No. 2 option behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If the 49ers are simply squatting on Aiyuk out of spite, that's a bush-league move that creates bad karma. Let the guy get back in the league. They apparently still have the ability to pursue upwards of $13 million in bonus money from him; use that process as the vehicle for getting a pound of flesh. Regardless, the 49ers apparently won't be letting him go until the exemption expires. At that point, he'll pass through waivers, his contract won't be claimed, and he'll become a free agent.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings prepare to face his former team
summary: Sunday night's game in Mexico City between the Vikings and 49ers has multiple interesting subplots.
full_text: Sunday night's game in Mexico City between the Vikings and 49ers has multiple interesting subplots. One relates to a player who had spent his entire career with the 49ers before signing with Minnesota. Jauan Jennings is in his first season as a Viking. In six games with two starts, he has only six catches for 54 yards. And there was a strong possibility of a trade back to the 49ers. He ultimately decided to stay where he was . The Vikings will need him on Sunday night, especially with receiver Jordan Addison out due to a thumb injury. “With us being down Jordan Addison, we’re gonna need him to make some plays in the pass game ," coach Kevin O'Connell said Tuesday on KFAN. Jennings didn't play in Week 10 at Green Bay due to a calf injury. During five seasons with the 49ers, Jennings caught 210 passes for 2,581 yards and 22 touchdowns in 75 regular-season games. He also had 23 catches for 289 yards and a touchdown in 11 postseason games — including four catches for 42 yards and a touchdown and a touchdown pass in Super Bowl LIX. Without Addison, Jennings could get more opportunities. And he will surely have a little extra incentive to show his former team that they should have kept him around.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Jaguars C Robert Hainsey week-to-week with knee injury
summary: Jaguars center Robert Hainsey left last Sunday's win over the Titans with a knee injury and it looks like he will need some more time to recover.
full_text: Jaguars center Robert Hainsey left last Sunday's win over the Titans with a knee injury and it looks like he will need some more time to recover. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that Hainsey is dealing with a sprain and is considered week-to-week when it comes to a return to action. While Hainsey is set to miss time, he is not expected to be out through the rest of the regular season. Hainsey has started every game this season and he started all 15 games he played for the Jags last season as well. Jonah Monheim replaced Hainsey against the Titans and he also started for the Jags when Hainsey missed time in 2025.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Mike Pettine takes over as Cowboys' defensive play-caller
summary: Christian Parker will remain the defensive coordinator.
full_text: This one was inevitable, perhaps from the moment Mike Pettine arrived last month as an assistant. Via ESPN, Pettine will be taking over as the play-caller for the Dallas Cowboys defense. Pettine supplants defensive coordinator Christian Parker, a Pettine protege who is in his first year as the coach in charge of an NFL defense. Parker will remain the team's defensive coordinator. It was obvious that something was coming. Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers included an embarrassing performance from the defense, highlighted by multiple players running the wrong way when receiver Deebo Samuel rumbled 70 yards for a rushing touchdown. Some would say Pettine is part of the problem, given that he has been there for multiple weeks. Short of firing everyone and hiring someone off the street, however, there's not much that can be done right now. The first test comes on Sunday, when the Cowboys host the one-win Titans. Four days later, Dallas faces the two-win Eagles. If the Cowboys don't win both, they'll likely be de facto done for 2026.
author: Mike Florio

title: For the Seahawks this year, Drew Lock's numbers blow Sam Darnold's away
summary: When Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Sam Darnold will start in Week 12 against the 49ers, assuming he is medically cleared, it was no surprise: The Seahawks signed Darnold to a three-year, $100 million contract last year and won the Super Bowl with Darnold at the helm.
full_text: When Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Sam Darnold will start in Week 12 against the 49ers , assuming he is medically cleared, it was no surprise: The Seahawks signed Darnold to a three-year, $100 million contract last year and won the Super Bowl with Darnold at the helm. Quarterbacks like that don't often get benched. But Drew Lock has made it reasonable to question whether Darnold should get benched. That's because Lock has played three full games, and most of a fourth, while Darnold has missed time with injuries this season. And Lock hasn't just been better than Darnold. Lock has been so much better that there's no comparison between the two. The Seahawks are 4-0 in the games when Lock was their primary quarterback. They're 2-4 in the games with Darnold as the primary quarterback. Of the 37 NFL quarterbacks who have thrown at least 90 passes this season, Lock ranks first with a passer rating of 125.6. Darnold ranks 31st with a passer rating of 79.5. Lock has still not thrown an interception this season. Darnold has thrown nine. Lock has completed 73.1 percent of his passes. Darnold has completed 60.2 percent. Lock is averaging 9.0 yards per pass. Darnold is averaging 7.0 yards per pass. Lock has been sacked on 5.1 percent of his dropbacks. Darnold has been sacked on 7.5 percent of his dropbacks. With seven games left in the season, the 6-4 Seahawks are going to have a battle to get back to the playoffs. Macdonald believes Darnold is the best quarterback for the job. The numbers call that into question.
author: Michael David Smith

title: C.J. Stroud: "There's still a lot of ball to be played"
summary: With Sunday's loss to the Browns, the Texans have fallen to 3-6 on the season.
full_text: With Sunday's loss to the Browns, the Texans have fallen to 3-6 on the season. At this point, Houston will have to rip off several wins in a row to have a chance at the postseason. Quarterback C.J. Stroud is remaining optimistic. “There's still a lot of ball to be played, if I can remember I think we'll be fine,” Stroud said on Tuesday, via transcript from the team. “It's not perfection that is what's needed, but it's a chase of excellence from everybody. Me and [ Will Anderson Jr.], we try to set the standard every day for everybody in the building to look at us and be like, 'Hey, those are two guys that I want to follow after,' and it's up to us to keep that standard going. “It doesn't mean because you lose a couple games that everything got to switch or change. There's a lot of ball to be played left, so we're still excited about what's coming next.” So Stroud remains motivated and wants that attitude to permeate throughout the team. "What else are we going to do? Cry about it and hold our heads down? Woe is us, woe is this team? I don't believe in that,” Stroud said. “It sucks, yeah, I'm not the happiest camper, but I think the motivated me is one of the best me's that I've seen. “I think even as this team, the motivated Texans is a scary team. It's up to us. We don't need anybody else. That's my message to the guys. We don't need anybody else to have faith in us or to think that we can do this or can't do this. It doesn't really matter. We're the ones on the field making plays and we have the opportunity. Everybody can have an opinion, but when you have the opportunity, you've got to go and do it and I think it just starts one thing at a time."
author: Myles Simmons

title: Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla: "We’re very happy with both the team and the location right now"
summary: A pattern has emerged during the early months of Vinod Khosla's ownership of the Seahawks.
full_text: A pattern has emerged during the early months of Vinod Khosla's ownership of the Seahawks. First, he'll make a less-than-unequivocal comment about the future of the team in Seattle. Two, people will hear his words and repeat them. Three, he will complain about that. Most recently, Khosla was asked directly during an appearance on CNBC whether he'd consider moving the team. "I’ve not made any plans or even discussed -- I know the press like to make a big deal of it," Khosla said, via Sports Business Journal . "We’re very happy with both the team and the location right now." And there it is. "Right now." Why add "right now"? Just end the sentence at "location." The same thing happened last month, when Khosla was interviewed by Axios . Asked point-blank whether he'd make a commitment to keeping the Seahawks in Seattle over the long term, Khosla said, “ I will never say never . Will this team be in Seattle 500 years from now? But I have no current plans to change anything about the team, including the coach, president, operation or Lumen Field. It all functions well.” It's not difficult (although apparently it is). The question is simple. Will you move from Seattle? While there's an element of taxpayer-funding leverage that arises regarding future stadium renovations and/or construction in Seattle, there's a way to answer the question that doesn't sacrifice future bargaining power. "We have every intention to remain in Seattle" is the easiest reply. With no further elaboration or explanation. Frankly, his latest comments are more ominous than his response to the Axios question. Beyond the fact that he now knows anything he says will be repeated (indeed, he prefaced his response by saying "the press like to make a big deal of it"), Khosla added the ultimate caveat that will cause local consternation. "Right now." Right now isn't "500 years from now." Right now is subject to change. Because right now applies only to — wait for it — right now. Right now is later from the last time I typed " right now ." Here's what Khosla should do: Write a check right now to someone who will give him a script to recite whenever he's asked that question in the future right now .
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL flexes Raiders-Browns to Sunday night in Week 12
summary: Originally scheduled for SNF, Patriots-Chargers moves to 4:05 p.m. on CBS.
full_text: Reigning No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza will make his primetime debut sooner than originally scheduled. The NFL announced on Tuesday that it has flexed the Week 12 matchup between the Raiders and Browns in Cleveland to Sunday Night Football . The two teams were originally scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. with Patriots-Chargers scheduled for Sunday night. New England and Los Angeles will now kick off at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The matchup between the Titans and Jaguars in Jacksonville has also been moved to 1 p.m. on Fox. Currently 4-6, the Raiders will have a chance to be 5-6 when they come to Cleveland as they’ll take on the Broncos in Denver this weekend. It will be Mendoza’s second career start, with the matchup against the AFC North foe in Week 12 his third. The surprising 6-4 Browns got back in the win column with a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday. All six of Cleveland’s victories this season have come via a fourth-quarter comeback. The Browns are on their bye in Week 11. Cleveland and Las Vegas faced one another last season, with the Browns coming away with a 24-10 victory in Week 12. It was the first start of Shedeur Sanders’ career, though he is now serving as the backup to Deshaun Watson. This will be the first Sunday night game in Cleveland since 2019, when the Browns fell to the Rams in Week 3.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jahmyr Gibbs is on pace to break the NFL record for yards from scrimmage in a season
summary: The current record belongs to Chris Johnson, who had 2,509 yards for the Titans in 2009.
full_text: Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs hasn't just been the most productive running back in the NFL this season. He may produce more yardage than any player in NFL history this season. Through nine games this season, Gibbs has an NFL-high 1,000 rushing yards. Gibbs also has 384 receiving yards. That total of 1,384 yards from scrimmage leads the league, and with an average of 153.8 yards per game, Gibbs is on pace total 2,614 yards from scrimmage over a 17-game season. That would break the NFL record, held by Chris Johnson of the Titans, who totaled 2,509 yards from scrimmage (2,006 rushing yards and 503 receiving yards) in 2009. Gibbs has touched the ball an NFL-high 240 times this season, combining 199 carries and 41 catches. With that kind of workload, the biggest concern for the Lions will be whether he can stay healthy for 17 regular-season games and, the Lions hope, some playoff games after that. But given how well Gibbs is playing, it would be hard for Dan Campbell and the Lions' coaching staff to reduce his workload. He's having a special season. He's halfway to one of the greatest seasons any running back has ever had.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Brian Flores: Vikings plan to rotate players in order to deal with altitude in Mexico City
summary: The 49ers are spending the week in Colorado in order to acclimate to the altitude at which their Week 11 game in Mexico City will be played.
full_text: The 49ers are spending the week in Colorado in order to acclimate to the altitude at which their Week 11 game in Mexico City will be played. The Vikings are not . But the Vikings have a plan for ensuring that their players are ready for the conditions. "It's a tough place to play," Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores told reporters on Tuesday regarding the game in Mexico. "I think it's certainly taxing, you know, I think you're — I think as a staff, we're already talking about, 'Hey, we're gonna have to rotate these guys and get, you know, everybody's gonna have to be ready to play.' And so, yeah, I mean, it's certainly something that we're going to have to deal with. "But there's always, you know, elements that we're dealing with, whether it's cold or rain or things like that. Obviously, we're indoors, so we don't deal with much of that. But that's the environment we're gonna be in. I think we prepare them to play in that environment, but I'm not gonna be silly and say, 'Hey, everybody, hey, you've got to go in there for 12 straight plays.' I mean, we're not doing that. "So we'll have rotations, we'll have a plan in place. Inevitably, we're gonna have to fight through some of that. It's not gonna be your average game where, you know, altitude, you just have — you literally have less oxygen. So we've got to do a great job as a staff of making sure — watching guys, and making sure we got guys in and out, you know, as much as we can." His broader message to the defense is clear: "We're gonna need everybody." Regardless of the plan to rotate players, the question becomes whether the 49ers will be able to rely more heavily on their best players because they're properly acclimated to the thinner air. The Vikings are choosing a different strategy, and it's going to create an obvious apples to apples comparison between the approaches that the two teams have taken — especially if the 49ers players seem to be fresh and the Vikings players seem to be gassed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Gardner Minshew had surgery to repair torn ligament in throwing elbow
summary: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew has had surgery to repair the elbow injury that ended his season.
full_text: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew has had surgery to repair the elbow injury that ended his season. Minshew had the surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament on Monday and is expected to make a full recovery , according to ESPN. Although tearing the UCL is a famously brutal injury for baseball pitchers that necessitated the development of the Tommy John surgery procedure, it tends not to be as severe for the throwing motion of a quarterback. Brock Purdy tore his UCL in the 49ers' playoff loss in January of 2023, had surgery to repair it in March, and was healthy enough to play the full season and lead the 49ers to the Super Bowl the next year. Minshew, who will be a free agent in March, should be healthy enough to sign with some team and play in 2027. Where he'll be playing remains a question.
author: Michael David Smith

title: When Brian Flores defenses face Kyle Shanahan offenses, Flores is 5-0
summary: Teams with Flores as a head coach or defensive assistant have played against teams with Shanahan as a head coach or offensive assistant five times, and Flores is 5-0.
full_text: Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores will face off with 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan on Sunday night in Mexico City, and if history is any guide, Flores has the advantage. Teams with Flores as a head coach or defensive assistant have played against teams with Shanahan as a head coach or offensive assistant five times, and Flores is 5-0. Since becoming defensive coordinator of the Vikings, Flores has coached against Shanahan's 49ers twice, with Flores' team coming out on top both times. In 2023, the Vikings beat the 49ers 22-17. In 2024, the Vikings beat the 49ers 23-17. Flores and Shanahan coached against each other as head coaches once, in 2020, when Flores' Dolphins beat Shanahan's 49ers 43-17. The most famous game with Flores and Shanahan on opposite sides came in Super Bowl LI, when Flores was linebackers coach for the Patriots and Shanahan was offensive coordinator for the Falcons. Shanahan's Falcons jumped out to a 28-3 lead, only to have Flores' Patriots come back and win 34-28 in overtime. And in 2011, New England beat Washington 34-27 when Flores was a defensive assistant in New England and Shanahan was offensive coordinator in Washington. Shanahan was once on a coaching staff that got a win against a team with Flores on the staff, in the final game of the 2009 season, when the Patriots had already clinched their playoff spot, rested starters and lost to a Texans team with Shanahan as offensive coordinator. But Flores was a special teams assistant, not a defensive assistant, on that Patriots team, so that game wasn't a Flores defense vs. Shanahan offense competition. When it's Flores coaching defense against Shanahan coaching offense, the result has been the same across different teams and in different coaching roles: Flores has five wins and Shanahan has none.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dan Campbell says Buccaneers are better than their record says they are
summary: Lions head coach Dan Campbell played in the NFL for Bill Parcells, who liked to say, "You are what your record says you are."
full_text: Lions head coach Dan Campbell played in the NFL for Bill Parcells, who liked to say, "You are what your record says you are." That's not how Campbell views this week's opponent. With the Lions preparing to face the 3-6 Buccaneers on Sunday, Campbell said he thinks they're a much better team than that record suggests, and he noted that Tampa Bay is only a game out of first place in the NFC South. "It's a physical team. These guys play with violence. Todd Bowles always does a great job. Their record is not indicative of the type of team they are. They're in the hunt for the South. So we know what we have in front of us," Campbell said. In the NFL's worst division, the Buccaneers have a real chance to be a playoff team, and Sunday's game could even be a playoff preview. That's how Campbell wants his players to view it: As a game against a playoff opponent, not against a team that's 3-6.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Caleb Williams remains frustrated with four interception game
summary: In his last game, Caleb Williams threw four interceptions.
full_text: In his last game, Caleb Williams threw four interceptions. The quarterback has not had a chance to truly put it behind him yet as the Bears had an off week in Week 10. He called two of the picks "funky" and a third "a bad decision." "The biggest thing is, the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me, personally, I always don't want to let my teammates down," Williams said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. " That’s always big for me . And in that situation, in those situations, I feel like I did. And so, that's the frustrating part that lingers." Williams had thrown four total interceptions in the 11 games before the Bucs game, dating to Nov. 28, 2025. He had never thrown more than two in a game. "He's playing fast right now," Johnson said. "He's got a great approach. He's doing a good job downloading the game plan. We don't feel like we're hindered in any way as a coaching staff from the schematics of what we're able to put in, the details, the alerts. He's just able to digest a lot more. He's seeing coverage really well with where his eyes should be tied into his feet also. So, we're really encouraged with where he's at. We've just got to continue to push that envelope and see how far it will take us." During his break, Williams' close friend, Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, won the National League MVP award. Williams' odds to win NFL MVP are +3500. Williams was asked whether Chicago is big enough to handle two MVPs. "Damn right," he said, smiling.

title: 49ers-Cowboys cranks out 27.13 million viewers
summary: Fox's Sunday tripleheader culminated in the national telecast of the 8-1 49ers at the record-doesn't-matter Cowboys.
full_text: Fox's Sunday tripleheader culminated in the national telecast of the 8-1 49ers at the record-doesn't-matter Cowboys. As expected, it delivered. On average, 27.13 million watched the 46-40 barnburner, which ultimately underscored the fact that: (1) the 49ers are elite; and (2) the old "Doomsday Defense" nickname has a much different meaning now. The performance of the game reconfirms the fact that 4:25 p.m. ET has become the most valuable weekly window. It currently rotates between CBS and FOX, with multiple simultaneous games per year. It's hard not to imagine the NFL considering breaking that window away from the standard Sunday afternoon packages and selling it to one network. Given the size of the audiences, it would be the most lucrative package the NFL could offer. This week, the NFL moved Steelers-Eagles from the late-afternoon window on CBS and shifted Jaguars-Giants into the spot. Raiders-Broncos also starts at 4:25 p.m. ET.
author: Mike Florio

title: With Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores, Vikings-49ers will be a matchup for the modern NFL
summary: The winner of the battle between Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores could define what the NFL becomes schematically
full_text:
In the long-running anime One Piece, there's an incident at the World Government headquarters, Marineford, known as "The War of the Best." The strongest pirates in the world of One Piece fought the strongest Marines the World Government had to offer, and it ultimately became the most important arc in the One Piece world, shaping the direction of the story that's still being told today.
In the NFL , it feels like we have a game every year that is similar to War of the Best -- two titans facing off against each other, where the outcome will shape the next wave of the NFL on both sides of the ball:
Kyle Shanahan vs. the Legion of Boom in 2016.
Sean McVay vs. Vic Fangio, then Bill Belichick, in that year's Super Bowl .
Andy Reid vs. Lou Anarumo in the second half of the 2022 AFC Championship.
Sean McVay vs. Mike Macdonald last season.
This year, the new NFL meta will be defined Sunday night in Mexico City, where the San Francisco 49ers and Shanahan will face the Minnesota Vikings and defensive coordinator Brian Flores in one of the most anticipated matchups of the year. Both the Niners' offense and Vikings' defense are resetting what their respective sides can and should do, and seeing which side blinks first could be a blueprint for how offenses and defenses attack each other in the near future.
If we recall a story I wrote earlier this season , NFL teams are blitzing at an astronomical rate. Over ten weeks, defenses league-wide have a 32.3% blitz rate, the second-highest since 2010 and one of only four seasons with a blitz rate over 30% (2011, 2013, and 2010). The number jumps even higher when teams go under center to an astounding 50.5%, the highest since 2010 and the only season TruMedia has recorded in that time period with a blitz rate over 50% against under-center offenses. When these defenses blitz, they have a 54.9% defensive success rate overall, and that number drops to 50.1% when offenses are under center.
At the forefront of this are Flores and the Minnesota Vikings, who are redefining what it means to be aggressive. The Vikings currently sit with an absurd 72.6% blitz rate, by far the highest for any team through 10 weeks since 2010. In fact, you have to go all the way back to the 2006 Miami Dolphins to find a team that went higher than that (what was Nick Saban cooking in 2006?). The way that Minnesota can dictate the flow of not only a play, but the entire game through their pressure looks that completely stymie opposing offenses.
The Vikings are essentially playing rock-paper-scissors on every play, daring you to throw anything other than rock. One way they can dictate the flow is by forcing teams to leave extra pass protectors in to help against pressure looks.
Imagine you're Packers quarterback Jordan Love . You come to the line of scrimmage, and this is what you see:
The alarm bells are ringing. This is the most obvious Cover 0 all-out blitz look, eight guys up at the line of scrimmage. The common answer for the Packers and Love has been to keep the RB and TE in the protection, calling it max protection. This is the Packers throwing rock, hoping to catch the Vikings in a Cover 0 look and hit them for an explosive.
The Vikings actually spin everyone out of this except the four defensive linemen and run Cover 3, frazzling Jordan Love before he ends up throwing it 10 yards short of the first-down marker on third down. The Vikings got the Packers to throw rock, then they throw paper.
This ability to force offenses to keep seven people in to protect the QB is unprecedented at the NFL level. According to Sumer Sports, the 2026 Vikings are facing dropbacks where all five eligible receivers are out to catch a pass on 35.7% of their dropbacks, the lowest in the NFL by a significant margin. They're the only team in the NFL below 50% in that metric, with the New York Giants in second place…at 58.5%! Flores and the defense force offenses to play a completely different sport when they play Minnesota, using pressure to dictate the terms of the passing game. They force you to waste backs and tight ends in pass protection, then force you to play with a hand behind your back.
If you want to get four out in the passing concept, good luck, because that doesn't work either.
Welcome to hell https://t.co/dEC8w0gUok pic.twitter.com/QVqDriBZlP
You're probably wondering, "Yes, the Vikings defense is amazing, but what does that have to do with the 49ers and how this will decide the state of NFL schematics?" The answer lies in the protection plans. The Vikings see the lowest amount of five-out in the passing concept in the NFL. Well, guess which team leads the NFL in percentage of dropbacks with all five eligible receivers out in the passing concept? That's right, Kyle Shanahan and the San Francisco 49ers.
I'd describe the Niners' offense as "malleable." They can use multiple players in multiple ways, keeping their best players on the field while putting linebackers in a blender. They do that by getting all five guys out in the passing concept. If we include chip blocks, the Niners get all five eligibles out at an 80.1% clip, the highest in the NFL (not including chips, that number drops to 60.8%, second in the NFL behind the Pittsburgh Steelers ). Against pressure looks where linebackers are mugged, or showing that they're blitzing, the 49ers like to get everyone into the concept and spread teams out. The Niners (and Bengals as well) are zagging when everyone else is zigging, spreading out and getting five eligibles into the concept against the blitz.
With simulated pressures, there's always a law of equivalent exchange: for every guy you add, a guy has to drop. For most defenses to stay structurally intact while showing these pressures in two-high shells, someone has to drop from the defensive line. Shanahan knows this, and knows he has the personnel to live in five-out looks (we'll get to that later). If we're going to the rock, paper, scissors comparison again, the Niners are choosing to throw paper instead of rock, because if they can find the weakest point in the pressure, they'll hammer it.
This 3rd down against the Cowboys is a great example. Dallas lines up in a pressure look that has seven at the line of scrimmage. The Niners see this and have five guys as eligible route runners. Instead of checking into max protection, they stay with what they have, giving RB Christian McCaffrey a choice route on the backside. Cowboys spin out and drop into Cover 2, but CMC has already found the hole, and Brock Purdy finds him to move the chains.
DAL comes out with 7 up at the LOS on 3rd down, but drop everyone into the coverage. SF gets 5 out into the look, and run CMC on a choice route underneath that picks up the first down. Their ability to get 5 out into the concept is huge against pressure looks pic.twitter.com/L9sYfVOUuJ
This touchdown for McCaffrey against the Raiders is another way that the 49ers can undress the pressure looks by getting five receivers out into the concept. San Francisco motions FB Kyle Juszczyk into the backfield, then bumps him out right before the snap. The Raiders' secondary bumps with him, then sends the blitz while dropping the 2 DTs. However, LB Quay Walker hesitates just a little bit on his blitz, giving McCaffrey enough time to get wide open.
The reason the 49ers can live this way is not only because of Kyle Shanahan, but because of the personnel on the field. LT Trent Williams is a mute button at left tackle. Having him on the field lets the rest of the line slide the other way and leave Williams on an island. Having McCaffrey also helps in a big way: a guy who can run the offense as well as anyone and run choice routes against zone coverage. But this all comes together because of Brock Purdy and his ability to create out of structure. If the Niners go to five-man protection, and there's someone hot off the edge, Purdy is trusted to make them miss and extend the play. That's why he became the starter in the first place: he can…
author: JP Acosta

title: NFL Week 11 upset alert: Two straight losses for Steelers? Can Titans shock Cowboys?
summary: The Jets could also send the Chargers back into the loss column
full_text:
As expected, following a Week 9 where favorites owned the slate, underdogs bit back in Week 10. In turn, we were fortunate enough to pinpoint a trio of them in our five upset alert picks last week, so you had a peek behind the curtain on those favorites falling if you were with us.
We accurately highlighted the Commanders chances of heading into MetLife Stadium and beating the Giants , the new-look Vikings beating the Packers at Lambeau Field now that Kirk Cousins is in the fold, and Carolina taking down the Saints at the Superdome. We whiffed on the Patriots and Steelers as possible upset candidates, but three out of five ain't too shabby if you ask us.
Now, we turn our attention to Week 11, which is sort of a wonky slate. On top of featuring the fewest number of games (13) as six teams are on the bye, it also includes some hefty spreads. As of Wednesday morning, when this is being written, there are five double-digit spreads, including favorites like the Chiefs and Bills, who are laying over two touchdowns. That makes it a little more difficult to find those potential upsets, but they're there, and we've highlighted five favorites who could fall by the time Week 11 concludes.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Cowboys play up or down depending on the competition. This season, their defense has remained abysmal, ranking last in the NFL in total yards allowed per game (393.8) and in rushing yards allowed per game (154.1). That last figure could be a key factor in Tennessee's chances of pulling off the upset. Tony Pollard , who began his career with the Cowboys in 2019, could enact some revenge on his former team as he's been one of the hottest running backs in the NFL as of late. Over his last three games, Pollard has rushed for 279 yards, recorded 112 receiving yards, and totaled six touchdowns. Last week, the 49ers ran for 214 yards and three touchdowns against the Cowboys' defense.
Sure, the change from Christian Parker to Mike Pettine as the defense play-caller could give Dallas a boost, but it might not be an immediate change. If Tennessee can continue to find success on the ground with Pollard in a favorable matchup, a ball-dominant game script could be the recipe for a shocking upset.
Meanwhile, AT&T Stadium hasn't been too kind to the Cowboys either, allowing 31.8 points per game over their last six games in which they are 1-5.
Yes, Baker Mayfield is at risk of missing this game due to a foot injury. However, Jalon Daniels is no stranger to coming in under duress for Mayfield, as he's already made three starts this season. That includes an upset win on the road against Dallas in Week 5. Moreover, Mayfield hasn't been lights-out this season, ranking fourth-worst in EPA per dropback among qualified QBs through Week 10 since 2000. He also has a league-worst 28% completion rate on throws of 15-plus air yards this season. That isn't meant to dump on Mayfield per se, but to highlight that Tampa might be able to win this game regardless of who is under center.
After all, the Buccaneers are a run-first offense this season, leading the league in rushing yards per game (163.9) and tied for the lead in yards per rush (5.0). Meanwhile, the defense is allowing the fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL (79.1), which will be particularly helpful as they look to contain a high-octane Lions offense that's spearheaded by Jahmyr Gibbs . When it comes to the Lions' passing attack, Jared Goff has been a little loose with the football, throwing an interception in three straight games entering Week 11. That could also play into Tampa Bay's hands as its 16 interceptions in the season lead the league.
The Lions are also in a tough spot regarding the scheduling of this game. The Bucs will be well-rested after their bye, while Detroit returns from an international game in Munich, Germany, in Week 10.
The Chargers finally got into the win column on Monday after taking down the Ravens in Baltimore. However, a winning streak might not be in the cards for L.A. as they host the Jets. On top of playing on a short week, it's still hard to buy into the Chargers at this point. The loss might speak more to where the Ravens are at currently without Lamar Jackson than L.A. turning a corner. In that victory on Monday, they were just 2-for-13 on third down while Justin Herbert didn't light it up through the air either, tossing for 129 yards, no touchdowns, and no picks. This is still not a great football team.
The Jets aren't that much better, but I did think they gave Buffalo a game in the first half of their Week 10 defeat before things fell off over the final two quarters. Geno Smith was also in and out of the lineup due to injury, but reportedly is on the mend and should play on Sunday. They have enough talent on both sides of the ball to absolutely go into SoFi Stadium and walk away with a win.
The international tour for the NFL brings us to Mexico City this week for a primetime doozy between the Vikings and 49ers. Given how well both of these teams have played this season, this could very well be an NFC Championship preview.
While his numbers didn't jump out of the box score, I thought Kirk Cousins was sharp in his first game back with the Vikings after being acquired at the trade deadline. He gives the Minnesota offense some much-needed stability under center, and it's no surprise to see them post their second-highest scoring day of the season with him in the fold. This will be an opportunity for Cousins to bounce back against San Francisco, as he threw three interceptions against them back in Week 9 when he was still quarterbacking the Raiders . Some could see that poor showing as a bad sign for Cousins, but you can also see it as him having very recent familiarity with how they plan to attack him.
Of course, the true main event for this game will be Minnesota's defense against the 49ers offense. The Vikings are the best scoring defense (14.0 PPG allowed) in the NFL this season, while San Francisco is the second-best scoring offense (31.2 PPG). This is also a historically great matchup in the red zone, with the Vikings defense holding opponents to a 25% touchdown rate in the red area while the 49ers are scoring touchdowns on 83% of their trips. Both are the best of any team in a season since 2000.
This shows how razor-thin the margins are in this game, and it might be worth simply going with the underdog in Minnesota for value. It's also worth noting that Brock Purdy is 0-2 in his career against the Vikings, with his teams averaging 17 points per game as he's committed four turnovers.
History is not on the Steelers' side in this matchup, as they've lost 11 straight road games against the Eagles. The last time they won was back in 1965 at Franklin Field. Given the slew of injuries that have impacted Philly this season (namely to quarterback Jalen Hurts ), this could present a golden opportunity to snap that streak, but it's certainly not an automatic, considering how Pittsburgh looked on Sunday night.
The Bengals steamrolled the Steelers in primetime. While Joe Burrow can make any defense look foolish, the big concern for Pittsburgh was its inability to do anything on offense. They managed just 18 points and averaged 3.8 yards per play. If that's who they are in this matchup against the Eagles, Joe Milton and Co. will be able to hang around.
Philadelphia will also be well-rested for this matchup after its bye. Over his tenure as head coach, Nick Sirianni is 5-0 in his regular-season career coming off the bye.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: 49ers might have just outsmarted the Vikings with unique travel plan for Week 11 NFC showdown in Mexico City
summary: The 49ers-Vikings game will be held at an elevation of almost 7,400 feet. The two teams are taking an opposite approach with their preparation
full_text:
For the second time this season, the San Francisco 49ers are set to play an international game, and once again, their travel schedule could end up being a key factor in the game's outcome.
Back in Week 1, the 49ers were sent to Australia to play the Rams , and the two teams took opposite approaches to travel. The 49ers headed to Melbourne a full week before the game while the Rams showed up just 24 hours before kickoff. By the time the game kicked off, the 49ers were fully acclimated to the 17-hour time difference, and it showed: San Francisco won 27-7.
The 49ers outsmarted the Rams with their travel plan in Week 1, and they might try to do the same this week against the Vikings in Mexico City.  Mexico's capital creates a unique challenge for NFL teams because it sits at an elevation of about 7,350 feet. To put that in perspective, Denver has the highest altitude of any NFL city at 5,280 feet, over a quarter-mile of elevation below what the 49ers and Vikings will be dealing with in Mexico.
When you're playing at an altitude that high, it's not easy to get acclimated, so the 49ers have decided to spend their entire practice week in Colorado Springs at Air Force Academy's Falcon Stadium, which sits at 6,621 feet .
Niners coach Kyle Shanahan was raised in Denver, so he knows how difficult it can be to adjust to high altitude, which is why he decided to move the team's base to Colorado this week.
"I think it helps," Shanahan said this week, when discussing practice at a higher altitude. "I grew up mainly in Denver, and I always know how bad it would be for me. It didn't matter how good a shape you're in. Like, when I came home from college, you'd run up the stairs and be out of breath. It takes some time to get used to it. It just is what it is with altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver, it's always a challenge, and I know Mexico City's higher than Denver. It's not make-or-break by any means, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better."
The 49ers have shown that they're willing to adjust their travel plan for the chance to be a "couple percent" better. They did it for Australia, and now, they're doing it for this trip. This will mark the NFL's first game in Mexico City since 2022, and the 49ers also played in that game. Four years ago, they also spent a full week in Colorado before heading to Mexico, and it apparently helped, because they ended up beating the Cardinals 38-10.
On the Vikings' end, they won't be making any changes to their practice location to prepare for the high altitude in Mexico. Instead, the Vikings will spend the week at their practice facility in Eagan, Minnesota, which sits at an altitude of 945 feet.
Minnesota might not be adjusting its travel schedule, but the team knows it's going to be difficult to play in Mexico City. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores previously coached a game there as a member of the Patriots ' coaching staff in 2017 — a game New England won 33-8 over the Raiders — so he has some first-hand experience with what the trip will be like. During an interview on Tuesday, Flores admitted he'll probably have to change his substitution patterns since the high altitude will likely cause his players to get winded faster.
"There's less oxygen, it's a tough place to play," Flores said of Mexico City . "It's certainly taxing. As a staff, we're already talking about, 'Hey, we're going have to rotate these guys and everybody's going to have to be ready to play.' And so, yeah, it's certainly something that we're going to have to deal with."
Flores has faced Shanahan three times as a head coach or defensive coordinator, and he's won all three games, but this presents a different challenge. The Vikings have had the best defense in the NFL this year, but it will be interesting to see if the altitude changes that. If the defense is winded, it will be tough for them to keep up with San Francisco's offense.
Although the 49ers should be acclimated to the altitude by the time they arrive in Mexico City, the same can't be said for Minnesota. The Vikings will be stealing a page from the Rams' playbook when it comes to traveling this week. The Rams showed up in Australia one day before the game, and that's exactly what the Vikings plan on doing, with the team arriving on Saturday .
This a huge game that could ultimately decide the No. 1 seed in the NFC and the 49ers have decided not to leave anything to chance. The 49ers and Vikings kick off at 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday night in what will be the final international game of the NFL season.
author: John Breech

title: Why Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence has legitimate 2026 NFL MVP case, is destined to win one at some point
summary: Across Lawrence's last 17 regular season games, he has 15-plus wins and 45-plus TD. He is only 1 of 10 QBs to achieve that feat
full_text:
Entering the 2026 NFL season, Jacksonville Jaguars Pro Bowl quarterback Trevor Lawrence was underrated . With the Jaguars off to a 7-2 start and first place in the AFC South division once again, the secret's out: Lawrence is a legitimate NFL MVP candidate.
Yes, it may be weird to read the words "NFL MVP candidate" next to the quarterback of the Jaguars, which is understandable. Jacksonville is the only current franchise in the league that has never had a player receive a first-place MVP vote. However, Lawrence is performing like an MVP-caliber quarterback for a Jaguars team whose 7-2 record is tied for the next-best record in the NFL, behind only the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers and the 8-1 Buffalo Bills . It's just the third time in franchise history the Jaguars have started 7-2 or better through their first nine games, and the first time since 1999, according to Stathead. Among qualified quarterbacks, Lawrence ranks top-five in the league in pass yards per attempt, passing touchdowns, passer rating, success rate, and EPA (expected points added) per dropback, plus a top-10 finish in touchdown-to-interception ratio and completion percentage, per NFL Next Gen Stats.
Expected points added (EPA) per dropback
That's why DraftKings Sportsbook is currently giving him the fourth-best odds (+550) to take home the NFL MVP hardware entering Week 11. The only three players with better odds are Joe Burrow (-125), Josh Allen (+370), and Brock Purdy (+450). However, Lawrence is also racking up eye-popping numbers in an offense without any other established NFL stars, unlike the three quarterbacks ahead of him. Burrow has five-time Pro Bowler Ja'Marr Chase and Pro Bowler Tee Higgins at wide receiver, plus four-time Pro Bowler Orlando Brown Jr. at left tackle. Allen has 2025 NFL rushing champion James Cook at running back and five-time Pro Bowler Dion Dawkins at left tackle. Purdy has 2023 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Christian McCaffrey at running back, seven-time Pro Bowler George Kittle at tight end, and arguably the best left tackle in the NFL since 2010 in 12-time Pro Bowler Trent Williams .
Close your eyes and think. Who is the most accomplished Jacksonville offensive player outside of Lawrence? Running back Bhayshul Tuten is in just his second NFL season and his first as a lead back. No. 1 wide receiver Parker Washington , a 2023 sixth-round pick, is in his fourth NFL season and has never recorded a 1,000-yard receiving season -- he is well on pace to do so for the first time in 2026 with 645 yards receiving in the first 9 games of the year, which ranks 16th in the league. None of his offensive linemen have ever earned a Pro Bowl selection. Lawrence is uplifting a cast of solid, budding young talent and producing at an elite level similar to, or better than in some metrics, the other quarterbacks up for NFL MVP through 10 weeks.
This first-half performance in 2026 isn't a fluke either. Once Lawrence adjusted to coach Liam Coen's scheme halfway through 2025, their first season together, he led the entire NFL in total touchdowns with 24 across the last eight games of the 2025 regular season, a span in which Jacksonville went a perfect 8-0 to finish 13-4 and win the AFC South. Lawrence's 38 total touchdowns ranked as the third-most in football last season behind only the league's last two MVP winners: Matthew Stafford (46) and Josh Allen (39). That's how he finished fifth in 2025 NFL MVP voting, behind only Stafford, Drake Maye , Allen, and McCaffrey last season.
Across the final six games of the 2025 season, Lawrence produced a ridiculous 19 total touchdowns to just one turnover. That feat made him just the third player in NFL history to record 19-plus total touchdowns and one or fewer turnovers in the final six games of a season. The other two players to do so are 2019 Drew Brees (20 total touchdowns to one turnover) and 2020 NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers (21 total touchdowns to one turnover). Combining the second half of last season and the first half of this season, Lawrence has 15 wins and 45 total touchdowns in his last 17 regular-season games. He's been one of the NFL's best for the last year's worth of regular-season games.
* Minimum 4 starts in span
How rare is 15-plus wins and 45-plus total touchdowns in a 17-game span? According to CBS Sports Research, Lawrence is just the 10th quarterback in league history to do it, and the previous 9 all won NFL MVP honors at some point in their storied careers.
15-plus wins and 45-plus TDs in a 17-game span, NFL history
* All won NFL MVP in their career besides Lawrence
It will likely take Lawrence repeating his second-half effort from 2025 once again in 2026 to swipe the league MVP award out of Burrow's hands, but there's a chance he could do just that. If 2026 isn't the year Lawrence takes home NFL MVP honors, it's coming in the not-so-distant future.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Cowboys make defensive coaching changes, name Mike Pettine as play caller as struggles continue
summary: Christian Parker will remain on as the defensive coordinator, at least in title
full_text:
Three days after surrendering 584 yards — most ever in a home game — in a 46-40 loss to the 49ers , the Cowboys are making a big change in their defensive coaching responsibilities. Senior defensive analyst Mike Pettine will call defensive plays for Dallas, starting this weekend against the Titans , though first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker will retain his job, CBS Sports' Garrett Podell has confirmed .
Sunday's performance was far from a one-off, as Dallas' defense ranks last in yards per game allowed (393.8), tied for last in points per game allowed (28.2) and 31st in yards per play allowed (6.2).
Against San Francisco, Dallas gave up three plays of 50+ yards — all for touchdowns. On the season, Dallas has allowed nine plays of 50+ yards, four more than any other team.
Monday, coach Brian Schottenheimer said the organization was "still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation" when asked about a change at defensive coordinator. Team owner Jerry Jones then hinted at a potential change Tuesday.
"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about that here, but we are talking about those things," Jones said Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday, via The Dallas Morning News .
Dallas is currently 4-6, with the defense largely to blame. The Cowboys' offense, in stark juxtaposition to the defense, ranks top 10 in yards per game, points per game and points per drive. After entering the season with high expectations, Dallas is fighting to simply stay in the playoff race, two games behind the Giants in the lowly NFC East.
The Cowboys initially brought Pettine, 60, aboard last month after Dallas' slow start on defense. He has not called plays since 2020, when he was the Packers ' defensive coordinator. Green Bay finished ninth in total defense and 12th in scoring defense that year. Since then, he has bounced around, spending 2021 as a senior defensive assistant with the Bears and 2022-25 as a Vikings assistant head coach, working with outside linebackers in 2024 and 2025.
This is a considerable demotion — not in title, but certainly in responsibilities — for Parker, 34, who came to Dallas this season highly regarded after doing strong work as the Eagles ' defensive backs and pass game coordinator from 2024-25.
Pettine has considerable history with both Schottenheimer and Parker. He spent 2009-11 as the Jets ' defensive coordinator while Schottenheimer was New York's offensive coordinator. When he was with Green Bay, Pettine gave Parker his first NFL job as a defensive quality control coach.

title: Why Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba may go back-to-back as NFL Offensive Player of the Year
summary: The league might be witnessing the greatest season ever by a wide receiver, which could earn him the first back-to-back OPOY honors in a quarter century
full_text:
Greatness is unfolding in the Pacific Northwest. Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is in the midst of a potentially legendary season — one unlike any in NFL history.
A year after he blossomed into a superstar, Smith-Njigba is on pace to break the league's single-season receiving record and could become the first player to win Offensive Player of the Year in consecutive seasons since Marshall Faulk rattled off three straight award wins from 1999 to 2001.
Before Faulk, only Earl Campbell (1978-1980) had achieved the rare feat of winning OPOY multiple years in a row. Both of them were running backs, so Smith-Njigba would be the first wide receiver to pull it off if he secures the trophy come February.
Considering the award has only gone to a wide receiver six times since its inception in 1972, Smith-Njigba's victory last year was a rarity in the first place. To up the tally to seven wide receivers and account for two of them, in back-to-back years, would put him in a league of his own in the award's history.
Smith-Njigba leads all players this season in receptions (79), receiving yards (1,207) and receiving touchdowns (10) heading into the Seahawks' Week 11 bye. Let it not be forgotten that he is fresh off a Super Bowl title, too. At just 24 years old, he has already accomplished more at both an individual level and team level than most wide receivers dream of. As far as wideouts go, it's JSN's world, and everyone else is living in it.
When the Seahawks traded D.K. Metcalf in 2025, they did so clearly knowing that Smith-Njigba was ready to handle the lion's share of targets on their offense. He had already proven capable of reaching the 100-catch mark with Metcalf in the group, so the expectation was that he would take the next step as the bona fide No. 1 weapon among Seattle wide receivers. The Ohio State product did just that when he rolled to the league's receiving title in 2025.
One year later, Smith-Njigba is not only on track to repeat as the NFL's most productive pass-catcher, but he is also on pace to beat Calvin Johnson's record for the most receiving yards in a single season. He does have the benefit of a 17-game season whereas Johnson played during the 16-game era, but that is not to discredit the historic heights he could reach by the end of the campaign.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba's current pace
Again, the breakout season Smith-Njigba strung together last year in the wake of the Metcalf trade placed him at the top of the 2025 yardage standings. Stack that season with the even greater 2026 production, and the result might end up being the best two-year run by a receiver the sport has ever seen
Jaxon Smith-Njigba's current pace
Even if he slows down over the final seven games of the year, Smith-Njigba has already done enough through the first 10 to put himself in rare company. He became the fourth player in NFL history and the first since the 1970 merger to rack up 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns in the first 10 games of a season. The last time that occurred was 65 years ago.
In college football , there is the "Heisman moment." Whatever the Offensive Player of the Year equivalent of that is, Smith-Njigba just had his. In the Week 10 win over the Las Vegas Raiders , he turned in the greatest quarter of his career and highlighted it with a ridiculous play that stands competitively among the best he has ever recorded.
The third quarter of that triumph at Allegiant Stadium was special. Smith-Njigba amassed 144 yards and became the first Seahawk to tally 128+ receiving yards in a quarter. When he tacked on more in the next period, he entered another new echelon as the first Seattle player with 150+ receiving yards in a half in the play-by-play era, which dates back to 1991.
Nearly half of his third-quarter yardage came on one single play: A 71-yard burst to the end zone.
BIG PLAY JSN 😮‍💨 @jaxon_smith1 71 YARDS TO THE HOUSE. 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/0sDwRbuiOK
Smith-Njigba slipped while running his route, immediately stood back up, spun past a defender, beat two safeties to a deep ball and sprinted 40 more yards to the goal line. If the slip at the start of the route was accidental, then credit to him for bouncing back to complete a monster play. If it was intentional to get the safety to bite, then it was a masterclass in baiting a defender out of position. Either way, it belongs on his career highlight reel.
So often in this league, when a starting quarterback goes down with an injury, his top wide receiver's production falls off a cliff. Look at what happened in Minnesota when Justin Jefferson dealt with a revolving door at quarterback, or what Zay Flowers continues to experience in Baltimore amid Lamar Jackson's absence.
Smith-Njigba has actually been better with his No. 2 quarterback than with his starter.
Sam Darnold has been in and out of the lineup due to multiple injuries, which thrust Drew Lock into action during the season opener, Week 2 and each of the last two games. The two longest touchdowns of Smith-Njigba's career came with Lock, not Darnold, operating the offense: last week's 71-yard explosion and an 81-yard score in the second game of the year.
Here is how Smith-Njigba's production stacks up by quarterback:
Opposing defenses cannot stop Smith-Njigba. Apparently, quarterback injuries can't either. He is operating in a different universe from every wide receiver in the NFL and may be recognized for it at the end of the year with another piece of hardware in his already stocked trophy case.

title: Buccaneers vs. Lions NFL parlay: Baker Mayfield may sit, while Detroit begins life without Aidan Hutchinson
summary: The Bucs may be without QB Baker Mayfield on Sunday in Detroit, while the Lions will be without star pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson
full_text:
Maybe the biggest single play so far this NFL season happened this past Sunday in Munich, Germany. That was when Lions pass-rushing superstar Aidan Hutchinson sacked Patriots quarterback Drake Maye , the 2025 NFL MVP runner-up, in the first quarter of Detroit's 35-10 win. Maye broke his ankle on the play and probably is done for the season, then Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating the sack, and he's certainly finished for 2026. The Lions have the offense to win the franchise's first Super Bowl , but now probably don't have the defense to even get to the big game. On the flip side, Tampa Bay has a Super Bowl-caliber defense, at least of late, but likely doesn't have the offense to make noise. So it's a fascinating matchup between the clubs Sunday from Ford Field.
No weather concerns indoors for the 1 ET kick on Fox. At -7 via DraftKings , Detroit is taking only 33% of handle but 64% of wagers. Heavy leans on Over 43.5, even though Bucs QB Baker Mayfield is in some question.
The Lions have had the offense to win the Super Bowl since 2024 but can't keep the defense healthy. That unit has totaled 429 games missed the past three seasons (including this one), most in the NFL. Hutchinson, linebacker Jack Campbell and secondary pieces Brian Branch , Kerby Joseph and Alim McNeill all have suffered major issues. And all are under 27 years old.
Hutchinson leads the NFL in pressures with 351 since 2022 and tops the team with 50 this season, second in the league. He was the +1100 third-favorite for Defensive Player of the Year but now is obviously off the board. It's the second season-ending injury in the past three years for Hutchinson, who played five games in 2024 before sustaining a broken tibia and fibula. I think that Lions team would have won the NFC that season if he were healthy.
Quarterbacks with time against this Detroit defense have succeeded big-time in 2026. Per ESPN: On unpressured dropbacks since Week 5, the Lions are 27th in defensive success rate with a completion percentage allowed over expectation of plus-3.1%, which is well above league average. Long story short: If they don't pressure the QB, they get torn up.
Campbell probably isn't returning this season, either, after a scary neck injury suffered on Nov. 1 against Minnesota. Joseph is expected to make his season debut Sunday, however. He has been on the PUP list because of a chronic knee injury that caused him to miss the final 11 games of last season. The other two secondary guys have been back.
That core five has missed 62 combined games since 2024, and all five have been on the field for just four of the team's 43 games – none of the past 38. In total, they have played together on just 3% of all Detroit defensive snaps in that span.
Despite that Hutchinson injury, the various sportsbooks didn't hit the Lions too hard because they did win the game easily against a good Patriots foe and are sitting at 7-2. Their +220 odds to win the NFC North and +870 to win the conference title for the first time are largely unchanged. Detroit did go from +1800 to win the Super Bowl to +2200. To make the playoffs, the team was -330 entering the New England game and is now -600.

As for Tampa Bay (3-6) as it comes out of a bye week, its only route to the postseason is surely to win the mega-weak NFC South as it sits just a game behind first-place Carolina, holds the current tiebreaker and hosts the Panthers on Monday in Week 12.
If Mayfield and that offense could be just league average, the Bucs should win the division, and they are +140 to do so behind the Panthers (+130). Tampa Bay leads the NFL in takeaways (21), rushing defense (79.1 YPG) and defensive EPA per game (10.7). It is the only club in league history to allow fewer than 80 rushing yards per game, have 15 or more interceptions and still be below .500 through Week 10.
That's mostly on Mayfield, as he has seven turnovers in his six games – he has missed a few with injuries. He's only the fourth quarterback in the past 10 seasons with 925 or fewer passing yards and three or fewer passing TDs in his first six starts of a season. This century, there have been 880 qualified QB seasons through Week 10, and Mayfield's -0.28 expected points added per dropback ranks fourth-worst among them. All-time bust JaMarcus Russell of the Raiders is one of a few QBs worse than Mayfield on that list at -0.44.
There are a lot of reasons for that, but the former Heisman winner is holding on to the ball too long. He's been sacked on 37.5% of dropbacks when pressured this season, the second-highest rate by a qualified QB through Week 10 in the past 10 seasons. Perhaps Mayfield is facing the perfect team on Sunday, then.
That's if he plays. Mayfield did suffer a foot injury in Week 9, and this week the Bucs added Cooper Rush to the practice squad and signed Easton Stick to the 53-man roster. NFL Network reported late Tuesday that Mayfield "seems to be trending" toward sitting out. Undrafted rookie Jalen Daniels, 1-2 as a starter, would get the call if Mayfield can't go.
