summary: Joe Burrow keeps the top spot, Patrick Mahomes is back in the top five and Jordan Love is one of the biggest fallers
full_text:
Quarterbacks are the most vital position in football. After all, they're the highest-paid players, and the past 13 NFL MVP award winners are, that's right, quarterbacks. While some quarterbacks are a byproduct of their offensive ecosystems, a select few elevate above their current circumstances to the ranks of the elite.
These rankings are fluid and designed to tell the story of each starting quarterback's respective rise and/or fall throughout the season. That's why some quarterbacks in this week's rankings rose as many as seven spots or fell as many as eight. Not in a vacuum, Patrick Mahomes would remain No. 1 for the foreseeable future and so on. He hasn't been in the top spot for some weeks now, given his torn ACL and others playing better ahead of him. However, that isn't set in stone, and Mahomes is certainly making a charge after his five-touchdown performance on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons.
So where do the league's biggest names line up entering the 11th week of the regular season? Enjoy the Week 11 edition of the 2026 NFL Quarterback Power Rankings:
author: Garrett Podell

title: Sorting 9 struggling franchises into tiers, from hopeless to hopeful: When will Jets end drought?
summary: At least one multi-year playoff drought will end in 2026, but others are only bound to get longer
full_text:
The last time the New York Jets made the playoffs was all the way back in 2010. Their 15-year postseason drought is the longest in franchise history and by far the longest active streak in the NFL . The Atlanta Falcons own the second-longest run without a playoff berth at eight years, and nine different teams own droughts of at least three seasons. Through 10 weeks in 2026, a couple of those squads appear poised to snap their dry spells. But others are destined to watch the postseason from home yet again.
Reasons for hope exist inside most of these downtrodden teams who have waited at least three years for a return to the Super Bowl hunt. Emerging or solidified franchise quarterbacks, superstar talent and renowned coaches are the best foundational pieces to own on the road back to competitiveness.
For the franchises that lack those puzzle pieces, however, the outlook is far bleaker.
Below are the nine teams with the longest postseason droughts sorted into tiers from hopeful to hopeless.
The two most aggressive sellers at the trade deadline are in the earliest stages of a rebuild. Yes, even the Titans , who started theirs back in 2023.
Tennessee whiffed on their first swing at a franchise quarterback when Will Levis did not work out, which essentially reset the clock on their rebuild. Then they made a second coaching change in two years by bringing in Robert Saleh, which amounted to another overhaul. The Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker trades this month moved a franchise legend and the NFL's most prolific defender at forcing interceptions and set the roster's talent back again. All the while, the product on the field has not improved one bit. Since Mike Vrabel's exit in 2023, the Titans have not won more than three games in a season. They are on pace for two this year. And while there are fun young weapons on the offense, it is still unclear whether Cam Ward is the answer at quarterback.
The Colts gutted their roster save for Jonathan Taylor , Sauce Gardner and Daniel Jones , and more moves could be on the way in the offseason. They have an opening at general manager, might be in search of a new coach in a couple of months, are devoid of talent at wide receiver and probably need to change things up at quarterback considering Jones' dreadful production in his first year back from a torn Achilles. This will get worse before it gets better. And on top of all that, they do not have a 2027 first-round pick.
Geno Smith and recently traded Jacoby Brissett are classic veteran bridge quarterbacks whose job is to keep their teams somewhat competitive until they draft their replacements. The Cardinals already moved on from Brissett and are taking a look at the future with Carson Beck , and he did not look the part of a future starter in his debut in Week 10. Both them and the Jets will shop for a signal-caller in the draft.
The quarterback Arizona selects will have an elite receiving tight end in Trey McBride , which will give that incoming rookie a premier safety valve as he gets his feet wet. If and when Jeremiyah Love gets and stays healthy, there is tremendous upside at running back, too. The Cardinals need to upgrade their receiving unit to aid their next quarterback, though. Decisions await on the other side of the ball, where Budda Baker and Josh Sweat remain locked in as two veteran leaders after the Cardinals elected to keep them at the trade deadline.
Years of mediocrity and the NFL's longest playoff drought helped the Jets stockpile young talent, so the quarterback they select might inherit an even better situation than the one in Arizona. The offensive skill positions are flush with rising standouts and established stars. David Bailey is a tremendous building block for the defense as the league leader in forced fumbles with five and a havoc-wreaker with 7.5 sacks as a rookie. The Jets just need to finally hit on a quarterback and ace the coaching hire that feels destined to come with Aaron Glenn on perhaps the hottest seat in the NFL.
Each of these teams own the same blueprint: A developing young quarterback who may be their long-term solution, at least one offensive star or superstar and enough promising or established tertiary weapons to keep them out of the league's basement.
The Saints have trailed at some point in all 26 games of Kellen Moore's tenure. That appalling reality does not instill much confidence that he is the right man for the job. A porous defense is largely to blame for this year's issues, as it ranks 29th in yards allowed per game, 26th in scoring and 23rd in EPA per play allowed. Between that and the musical chairs the Saints have played at running back, the positives that continue to come out of Tyler Shough and his receivers only go so far.
Las Vegas was among the most pleasant surprises of the season's first half, although the luster wore off in the weeks leading up to the Kirk Cousins trade. It was obvious in the first few weeks of the season that Klint Kubiak was an excellent hire and that if Fernando Mendoza delivers on his promise as the No. 1 pick, it will not take long for the Raiders to make noise. Brock Bowers ought to aid Mendoza's development, but they are still in desperate need of wide receiver help and must build around Maxx Crosby on defense.
The combination of Bijan Robinson and Drake London is a legitimate championship-caliber duo that the Falcons hope does not go to waste. Even some locked-in playoff contenders would gladly take Atlanta's skill position weapons over their own. The key for coach Kevin Stefanski is to mold Michael Penix Jr . into at least an upper-half-of-the-league quarterback and field a defense strong enough to maximize the elite playmaking ability on the more loaded side of the ball. That latter task got a little tougher when the Falcons traded Jessie Bates III , though.
Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury in Week 2 will always make this a "what could have been" season for the Giants . How much they accomplish in the second half of the campaign will determine how much excitement will exist for Year 2 of the John Harbaugh era when Dart returns to action.
Harbaugh is a strong candidate for Coach of the Year and continues to make the most of a rough situation without his starting quarterback — so much so that the Giants, even on the heels of a disappointing loss, are in the driver's seat in the NFC East. He could be set for a lengthy tenure in New York if everything goes according to plan. He and Joe Schoen will work together to add even more talent to this roster after the latter turned in a couple of highly fruitful drafts and loaded the squad with some of the league's most exciting young players like Malik Nabers , Abdul Carter and Arvell Reese .
This version of the Bengals is the one the franchise had to have envisioned when Joe Burrow led his 2022 team to the Super Bowl. It just took a few years to manifest. Now that it has arrived, Cincinnati might not just get back to the Super Bowl; it could win it.
Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and Chase Brown were never the problem. All the reasons behind the three-year playoff drought had to do with either injuries or the defense. In 2026, the stars have stayed healthy, and the commitment to fixing the defense has paid off. The Bengals spent all offseason trading for, signing and drafting impact players on their weaker half of the roster. Dexter Lawrence . Boye Mafe . Bryan Cook . Each of them, along with others, has taken the unit to a new level. Consistency still lacks a bit, but the highs are higher than at any other point during the Burrow era. If the defense peaks down the stretch, nobody will be able to keep up with the third-highest-scoring team in football.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Predicting full 14-team NFL playoff bracket heading into Week 11: AFC field seems set, Packers miss out
summary: For the first time this season, we have the same Super Bowl matchup two weeks in a row
full_text:
Heading into Week 11, the NFL playoff race is supposed to be heating up, but it might actually be cooling down, at least in the AFC.
Several things happened in Week 10 that make it feel like the AFC playoff field might be set. For one, Drake Maye went down with a potentially season-ending injury , and because of that, the Patriots (5-5) are now a long shot to make the playoffs. Also, the Browns pulled off a stunning comeback win over the Texans , putting Cleveland in firm control of a wild card spot.
According to our projection, the AFC's seven-team playoff field is all but set. So who's projected to get in? Glad you asked.
To help us figure that out, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season. There are 122 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated all of them. Not only did he project all eight division winners and the 14 playoff teams, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion.
With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.
The biggest win in Week 10 was probably the Browns' wild comeback victory over the Texans. With Cleveland's win, the Browns are now projected to get the seventh seed in place of Houston, who was there last week.
Here's the projected AFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. Bills (8-1) -- AFC East champion 2. Jaguars (7-2) -- AFC South champion 3. Bengals (7-2) -- AFC North champion 4. Chiefs (7-2) -- AFC West champion 5. Broncos (7-2) 6. Steelers (6-3) 7. Browns (6-4) JUST MISSED: Patriots (5-5), Texans (3-6)
BREAKDOWN: According to our projection, the AFC playoff field is basically wrapped up. That's right, we're only in Week 11, but our model feels pretty strongly that these will be your seven playoff teams. The model has given up on the Patriots because they just lost Drake Maye, the Ravens have been left for dead after losing to the Chargers , and even if the Texans somehow rebound to get to 10 wins, they're in a spot where they would lose almost any tiebreaker (they've already lost to the Bills, Bengals and Browns, so the head-to-head tiebreaker is out the window). They do play the Steelers in Week 13, and at this point, that's essentially a must-win game for Houston.
The addition of Kirk Cousins has caused a ripple effect in the NFC North. After watching Cousins lead the Vikings to a win over the Packers in Week 10, our computer now projects the Vikings will win the NFC North (the Lions were projected to win it before the Cousins trade).
Here's the projected NFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. 49ers (8-1) -- NFC West champion 2. Vikings (7-2) -- NFC North champion 3. Giants (5-3-1) -- NFC East champion 4. Buccaneers (3-6) -- NFC South champion 5. Lions (7-2) 6. Bears (7-2) 7. Seahawks (6-4) JUST MISSED: Packers (6-4), Rams (6-4)
The most interesting part of the NFC projection is that we have the Packers and Rams both reaching 10 wins but still missing the postseason. To add insult to injury, our projection has the Buccaneers (8-9) and Giants (8-8-1) both finishing at .500 or below, yet still getting in as a division winner.
AFC breakdown: The AFC wild card round would be must-see TV with two huge divisional showdowns. The Bengals just destroyed the Steelers in Week 10, and the computer has them once again winning in the postseason. The juiciest game in the AFC would come in Kansas City, where the Chiefs would edge the Broncos in a thriller. As for the other game, the computer is predicting a short playoff run for Cleveland.
NFC breakdown: We didn't see a single home team lose in the AFC wild card round, but in the NFC, things are much different, with the home teams going a combined 1-2. The NFC North sends three teams through to the divisional round, becoming just the fourth division in the Super Bowl era to pull that off. This round also sees the elimination of the Seahawks, which means the NFL will crown a new champion.
AFC breakdown: Our projection has the Bills beating the Chiefs, but I'll believe it when I see it. On paper, the Bills might have the better overall roster, but that never seems to matter when these two teams meet in the postseason. Patrick Mahomes is 4-0 all-time against Josh Allen in the playoffs, and if our projection is right, Allen's drought will finally end here. As for the other game, the Jags beat the Bengals in Cincinnati earlier this year, and our projection has the Jags earning the win again in Jacksonville.
NFC breakdown: We get total chaos in the NFC with two crazy games that end up going down to the wire. Kirk Cousins leads the Vikings to their first NFC title game appearance since 2017 while the 49ers edge the Bears in a thriller.
If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: three teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills, Jaguars and Vikings) and one team that hasn't won a Super Bowl in over 30 years (the 49ers' last title came in 1994)
We've been doing a projection every week since the start of the season, and here's a look at the projected Super Bowl each week.
For the FIRST time all season, our computer has projected the same Super Bowl matchup for TWO straight weeks. The Bills have been projected to win the Super Bowl for four straight weeks and that's mostly because the computer loves them. Our model gives the Bills an 18.27% chance of winning it all, which is incredibly high, especially given that no other team is above 11%.

title: Week 11 picks, best bets: Lowly Jets send Chargers back into loss column, Titans cover vs. Cowboys
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 11 schedule, including five locks against the spread
full_text:
You all remember the No. 1 rule about Fight Club, right? You don't talk about Fight Club.
There's a similar philosophy/mantra in the gambling space. You do not, under any circumstances, bring up the fact that you're on a heater, for fear of jinxing it. You simply don't acknowledge it, continue going about your business and pray that the good times keep rolling.
With that in mind, I'm not going to tell you that I went 11-3 (ATS and straight-up) over the Week 10 slate, which included a near-perfect 4-1 ATS record in my five locks of the week. And I'm certainly not going to highlight that I'm currently on a 26-3 moneyline run over the past two weeks, along with a 7-3 ATS mark on my locks.
Again, I'm NOT telling you this. Why would I? Nope. All we need to do now is roll up our sleeves, pick up our lunch pail and keep it moving into Week 11. Because there isn't much else to talk about.
Note : Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, Los Angeles ( Rams ), New England and Seattle are on the bye in Week 11.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
I think Dallas is one of those teams that plays up or down to their opponent. So while it may have gone toe-to-toe with the 49ers last week, I wouldn't be surprised in the slightest to see the 1-8 Titans hang around. In fact, I'm betting they will. Tennessee is a respectable 3-1 ATS on the road this season. Conversely, AT&T Stadium hasn't been much of an advantage for Dallas, as it is 1-3 ATS at home.
Over their last three games, the Titans offense has also been pretty solid, averaging 5.8 yards per play. That's the sixth-highest in the NFL over that stretch. A large part of that success has been thanks to the ground game, as they are averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The only team better than them is the 49ers, who just ran for 214 yards and three touchdowns against this Dallas defense in Week 10. The Cowboys' defense is showing no signs of improvement, as their 6.1 yards allowed per play are the sixth-highest in the NFL season. At the very least, the backdoor will be left wide open.
Projected score: Cowboys 30, Titans 23 The pick: Titans +8
Los Angeles finally got a win, snapping an eight-game losing streak to start the season and an 11-game skid dating back to last year (including playoffs). This moment in the winner's circle, however, will be short-lived. With Geno Smith reportedly avoiding a major injury , that only strengthens my faith that the Jets will take down the Chargers on Sunday. I assume Smith plays, and with him under center, the Jets have been solid.
Moreover, I thought New York's defense largely hung around against Buffalo last week before the wheels fell off in the second half. Justin Herbert is not Josh Allen , nor is Omarion Hampton James Cook, so the Jets' defense should be able to keep this offense in check for four quarters. New York also has the rest advantage after LA played in Baltimore on Monday night.
The Chargers have yet to record an ATS win (0-4) at home this season
Projected score: Jets 24, Chargers 20 The pick: Jets +3.5
The Jaguars are a freight train right now. Over their three-game winning streak, Jacksonville is averaging 38.3 points per game. For the season, they're averaging 6.0 yards per play (tied for fifth-highest in the NFL), a 46.8% conversion rate on third down (third-highest) and 8.7 yards per pass attempt (second-highest). Trevor Lawrence is playing at an MVP level, while running back Bhayshul Tuten is in the midst of a full-blown breakout. Over the winning streak, he's rushed for 221 yards and three touchdowns, while adding 80 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.
Meanwhile, Jacksonville's defense is about to get a boost this week as two of their trade deadline acquisitions (safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis ) are all set to make their debuts after Liam Coen gave them Week 11 off to get acclimated.
While New York does boast a defense that is allowing just 305.7 total yards per game this season (fifth-best in the NFL), the Jaguars feel like an entirely different animal to overcome. I also believe Jacksonville's defense, which is allowing 4.7 yards per play over the last three games (tied for fifth-lowest in the NFL), can contain a J.J. McCarthy-led Giants offense that still gives me pause.
When you look at the trends, the Jaguars have given bettors confidence to back them on the road this season. As the away team, Jacksonville is 3-1 ATS with a 9.5-point average margin of victory, the third-highest in the NFL.
Projected score: Jaguars 33, Giants 21 The pick: Jaguars -6
Fernando Mendoza actually played pretty well given the circumstances, in my opinion. The No. 1 overall pick was making his first career start against one of the toughest defenses in the NFL: the Seahawks . Naturally, he looked like a rookie quarterback at times, completing 17-of-29 for 143 yards, no touchdowns, and no interceptions. He was also sacked six times. That said, he showed some flashes, including a touchdown run on his first possession of the afternoon. While Mendoza has a bright future in front of him, his baptism by fire will continue in Week 11 as he and the Raiders travel to Denver to face a Broncos team that was on the bye in Week 10.
Denver is 3-0 coming off a bye under head coach Sean Payton, and its pass rush could prove to be the difference in this game and keep Las Vegas outside of the number. This season, Denver is second in the NFL in pressures (159) and tied for the ninth-most sacks in the league (26), according to TruMedia. At home, this feels like a recipe for Mendoza to be under siege early and often, allowing Bo Nix and the Broncos offense to simply take advantage of what has been a poor Vegas defense. Coming into Week 11, the Raiders are tied for the most points per game allowed (28.9) in the NFL.
Projected score: Broncos 27, Raiders 16 The pick: Broncos -10
There are a lot of big spreads this week, so we're naturally going to see some teams creep through the back door. I think New Orleans could be one of them. The Saints are tied for the second-most pass attempts per game (38.1) in the NFL this season. That number jumps to a league-high 39.5 when they're on the road. That should only continue in this matchup against Chicago as they try to keep up with Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams on the other side.
The Saints' passing attack is also getting a midseason boost with the return of first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson . Over the first two games of his career, the No. 8 overall pick has looked like the real deal, including an 11-catch, 80-yard outing last week in the loss to Carolina. Paired with Chris Olave , that's a nice one-two punch for Tyler Shough to get us to a cover. Speaking of covers, that's all New Orleans has done this season, as they're the only team in the NFL without an ATS loss on the road so far in 2026 (3-0).

title: Prisco's Week 11 NFL picks: Texans edge Colts on 'TNF,' Cowboys rout Titans, 49ers over Vikings
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road
full_text:
Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games .
I did that the past two weeks.
After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow.
The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark.
Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it.
Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around.
Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19
The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it.
The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers.
Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23
The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome.
Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout.
Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14
The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well.
Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13
Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close.
Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22
The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense.
Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24
Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big.
Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14
This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten .
Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17
This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it.
Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16
The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling.
Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30

title: NFL schedule flex: League moves Week 12 'Sunday Night Football' matchup, shifts afternoon games
summary: Patriots at Chargers is moving out of prime time
full_text:
The NFL is flexing its scheduling freedom, moving the Week 12 Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns matchup from 1 p.m. ET to "Sunday Night Football." The New England Patriots were originally scheduled to play the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium in prime time that week, but that matchup will now move to 4:05 p.m. ET.
Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars , which was originally scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET that week moves to 1 p.m. ET.
The Raiders-Browns matchup will feature Las Vegas's newest quarterback, Fernando Mendoza . The No. 1 overall pick took over after Vegas (4-6) sent Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings at the trade deadline last Tuesday, and Week 12 will mark the first prime-time matchup of his career. Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards in his first career start on Sunday, which came in a 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks .
As for the Browns, they moved to 6-4 last week following a remarkable comeback win over the Houston Texans . The 17-0 deficit Deshaun Watson and Co. overcame made it the second-largest comeback win at home in franchise history, while the Browns are now a perfect 4-0 in their home stadium for the first time since 1963. Cleveland currently holds the last wild-card spot in the AFC (No. 7 seed), behind the 6-3 Pittsburgh Steelers and 7-2 Denver Broncos .
The 5-5 Patriots are being flexed out of prime time following their disastrous 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. The team reportedly fears that quarterback Drake Maye , who suffered a lower-leg injury early in the game, could be sidelined for an extended period of time . The injury could force last year's MVP runner-up to miss the remainder of the season. New England's Week 12 opponent, the Chargers, actually just tallied their first win of the season on Monday night, defeating Jacoby Brissett's Baltimore Ravens, 23-20.
The NFL implemented this "flexible scheduling" rule in 2006. For "Sunday Night Football," they can flex up to two games between Weeks 5-10 and any week during Weeks 11-17.

title: Taxes hurt: Breaking down an NFL player's weekly pay stub and where all the money goes
summary: A pay stub included in the Chiefs receiver's bankruptcy filing shows how taxes, garnishments, union dues and an NFL fine can cut earnings in half or worse
full_text:
If you've ever wondered what an NFL player's paycheck looks like, we now know the answer thanks to Rashee Rice. The Chiefs wide receiver recently filed for bankruptcy , and as part of the court filing, he had to include a copy of his pay stub that he gets from the team each week.
The paycheck offers a rare inside look into where all the money goes for an NFL player. Rice is currently in the fourth and final year of a rookie deal that's paying him $1.635 million in base salary this year, but when it comes to his take-home pay, it's much more complicated than just looking at his base salary.
Like the rest of us, Rice has to pay taxes and he also has to pay his NFLPA dues. Not to mention, his paycheck is also being garnished to pay off several civil liabilities that he's facing.
For the week of Oct. 19-25, Rice got paid $43,353.08, but he only got to take home a small portion of that.
Let's take a look at where the money went.
Here's a look at one of Rashee Rice's recent pay stubs from the Kansas City Chiefs (via his bankruptcy filing). $43,353 in weekly earnings - $19,570 for taxes/SS/Medicare - $9,117 for garnishments, union dues, and fines ———— = $14,665 in take-home pay As of October 25, Rice has… pic.twitter.com/dNjtBJaEVi
It's certainly interesting to see how little Rice ends up taking home here.
After all the deductions were made, Rice's total net pay was $14,665.25. That means he only got to take home 33.9% of his paycheck. Most players don't have to deal with garnishments or fines, so let's take those out real quick. If Rice did NOT have to pay those two things, he still would have taken home only 52.7% of his paycheck ($22,860.96).
Another interesting thing about this pay stub is that you can see all the ways a player gets paid besides their base salary. For instance, Rice has been paid over $350,000 in performance pay along with a $75,000 workout bonus this year. Rice also earned $20,500 just for attending training camp. A player's salary only applies to games they play in, but they still do earn a stipend for training camp. Under the current CBA , veterans get paid $3,500 per week during training camp and this pay is equal for everyone, so Patrick Mahomes and Rice would make the same amount.
Although Rice is only making $43,000 per paycheck right now, that number will likely shoot up starting next year. The 26-year-old is in the final year of his rookie deal, and he'll definitely be cashing in this offseason, whether that's in free agency or signing an extension with the Chiefs.
author: John Breech

title: Texans' Azeez Al-Shaair reportedly facing surgery after move to injured reserve
summary: Houston's underperforming defense will be without one of its leaders for at least four games as Al-Shaair deals with a significant groin injury
full_text:
The Houston Texans are losing a key defensive piece for at least the next four games. Houston placed starting linebacker and team captain Azeez Al-Shaair on injured reserve, the team announced . Al-Shaair has been dealing with a groin injury that kept him out of Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns . The groin injury is significant enough that it requires surgery and he will likely miss more than four games, a ccording to the Houston Chronicle .
Over the next four weeks, Houston plays Indianapolis, the Baltimore Ravens , the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Washington Commanders . The Texans then close the season with a four-game stretch in which they play the Jacksonville Jaguars , Philadelphia Eagles , Green Bay Packers and Tennessee Titans .
Al-Shaair, a Pro-Bowler in 2025, has dealt with the groin injury all year, missing a pair of games with it so far this season. He has recorded 68 tackles, one tackle for loss, three quarterback hits and three passes defensed in seven games.
In Al-Shaair's absence, Jake Hansen will presumably see more snaps at linebacker (he played 66 of 68 defensive snaps against the Browns) while Henry To'oto'o will take over the green dot responsibilities of calling the defense, according to KPRC2 .
The Texans' defense as a whole has been one of the more disappointing units in the NFL in 2026, ranking 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed, and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces.
Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks this season, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. The Texans have also failed to force turnovers at the same rate as a year ago, with only 8.8% of opponents' drives resulting in a turnover (27th in the league) compared with 14.6% last season (fourth).
Those relative struggles have led the Texans to compile a 3-6 record despite C.J. Stroud and the offense showing significant year-over-year improvement. The Texans are now 2.5 games back of the No. 7 seed in the AFC and need to go on a strong run down the stretch of the season to have any hope of making the playoffs. And now, they'll likely have to do it without one of the leaders of their defense.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Jerry Jones says Cowboys 'talking about' change at defensive coordinator, their fifth in five seasons
summary: First-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker's defense allowed 584 total yards to the 49ers on Sunday, the most ever in a Dallas home game
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys may be on the verge of their fifth defensive coordinator in five seasons by the time the 2027 NFL season kicks off next year.
After having top-five and top-10 ranked defenses under Dan Quinn from 2021 to 2023, Dallas' defensive coordinator position appears to be cursed, possibly as cursed as Hogwarts' Defense Against the Dark Arts professor in Harry Potter. Mike Zimmer filled in as the last defensive coordinator on Mike McCarthy's Cowboys staff in 2024. Matt Eberflus floundered in his one season as DC on current Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer's first staff in Dallas.
Current defensive coordinator Christian Parker, the former Philadelphia Eagles defensive pass game coordinator who is in his first DC job at the age of 34, isn't performing much differently from Eberflus despite the Cowboys pouring in significant free-agent and draft capital into the unit. Dallas is 4-6 in 2026 with the No. 5 scoring offense (28.6 points per game) and the No. 30 scoring defense (28.2 points per game) in the NFL this season.
That is why Jerry Jones felt comfortable floating the idea of a change at Dallas' defensive coordinator position once again.
"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about that here, but we are talking about those things," Jones said Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday, via The Dallas Morning News .
In the team's 46-40 home loss against the San Francisco 49ers — the NFC's No. 1 seed — in Week 10, the Cowboys defense allowed 584 total yards, the most allowed in a home game in franchise history.
The 49ers also became the first team in NFL history with three touchdowns of 50-plus yards by players age 30 and older. San Francisco wide receiver Deebo Samuel , who will be 31 years old soon, ripped off a 70-yard rushing touchdown on an end-around play in which he was nowhere near getting touched. Running back Christian McCaffrey , who is 30 years old, totaled both a 66-yard receiving touchdown and a 74-yard receiving touchdown. McCaffrey's 66-yarder came on an all-out blitz from Parker that forced 37-year-old edge rusher Von Miller to cover the All-Pro running back.
Jones also made it sound like he has a lot of faith in Parker, and that the youngest defensive coordinator in franchise history just needs more time and/or seasoning to call plays. That's despite the Cowboys having the league's worst total defense (393.8 total yards per game allowed), run defense (154.1 rushing yards per game allowed), third down defense (48.8% third down conversion rate allowed) and the worst defense in terms of defensive expected points added (EPA) per play (-0.13).
"Everything about him would give you promise that he would be an excellent play caller. Everything," Jones said Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. "He has outstanding people skills, and communication and relationships with players. Those are key things now. They make a big difference. Some of the best coaches you'll ever see have had their turn and had to take another run on it in play calling."
Third down conversion rate allowed
Completion percentage allowed
Schottenheimer and Dallas' players may not hold the same faith in Parker at the moment. The Cowboys head coach was asked at his Monday press conference if the locker room still has confidence in Parker, and he didn't exactly leap to his defensive coordinator's defense.
"Still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer said on Monday. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of things that we need to clean up as a football team. We're taking a deep dive and looking at everything."
When directly asked whether he is considering a change at his defensive coordinator position, he did not offer a vote of confidence.
"I'm not saying that," Schottenheimer said when asked if a DC change was possible. "I'm saying we're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today."
author: Garrett Podell

title: Believeland? Why the 6-4 Browns are on track to make the NFL playoffs despite troubling numbers
summary: Cleveland is 6-4 despite a negative point differential, with Deshaun Watson delivering six game-winning drives and a resilient defense
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns traded their best player -- one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history, no less -- this offseason, nobody expected them to be any good.
When they named a starting quarterback who was feuding with his own fans and had been arguably the worst acquisition in pro sports history, nobody expected them to be any good.
When they opened the season with a 34-10 loss, the sentiment was the same as it had always been. "In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster , the Browns is the Browns," Mike Tomlin, the longtime coach of the AFC North-rival Steelers , said in his NBC debut .
Nine weeks later, the Browns are very much not those Browns. Cleveland is 6-4 after erasing a 17-point deficit in a crucial Week 10 win over the Texans . If the playoffs started today, the Browns would be in them as the AFC's No. 7 seed.
Teams are what their records say they are, but context is important, too. All six of Cleveland's wins have come by one score, tied with the Broncos for most in the league. Cleveland ranks 21st in point margin this season (-32). But even more than that ...
But, again, the record is the record. Just hear Todd Monken tell it.
"Isn't that cool? Isn't that awesome?" Monken said after the win. "I mean, holy shit. There's no other way to put it, man. You're 6-4 ... and our guys continue to fight, and we're 6-2 in one-score games. Says a lot about our guys, man."
It certainly does. Now, as the Browns hit their bye week, the question is whether they can sustain it.
The ability to win close games is a crucial one in the NFL, but relying on it too much can put you in a lot of trouble. The Browns have faced a lot of trouble this year; just re-read the third bullet point above.
But that's when Deshaun Watson has stepped in. His six game-winning drives are tied for most by any quarterback through a team's first 10 games since at least 1950 -- and that's despite him missing one game, too.
Some team-wide stats can convolute how a quarterback actually plays, but Watson has indeed taken his play to an absurd level on these game-winning drives.
Add that up, and that's 23 for 29 (79% completion percentage) for 254 yards, which is 8.8 yards per attempt. He made another big-time throw Sunday to set up Quinshon Judkins ' winning touchdown.
Harold Fannin Jr. down to the 5! HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GQL0DtQAaV
Watson has been, generally, average this season. He takes too many sacks, and the down-to-down accuracy is iffy at best. He has thrown just four touchdowns compared to seven interceptions. That combination can snowball, and it has in Cleveland's three losses with him under center. But let Cleveland hang around long enough, and Watson has proved to be excellent late in games.
"I wish we could find ways to pull it out a little bit sooner so we don't have to go through that," Watson said. "But, whatever it takes to win. Whatever it takes to stay on the winning side is the biggest thing."
When Watson and the offense struggle, the defense does enough to keep the Browns within striking distance. In all six Browns wins this year, their opponent has scored 24 or fewer points.
Cleveland has been excellent against the pass this year -- only the Vikings have a better defensive passing success rate -- and generally solid overall. The Browns can get gashed by the run and give up some big plays, but they also make enough big stops to hold on. The Browns are first in the percentage of plays that go for zero or negative yards and first in fourth-down conversion rate allowed. They're also eighth in red-zone touchdown rate allowed. Those are all vital for a team that can struggle to score.
When the Browns are trailing in the second half of games this year, they rank fifth in defensive EPA per play. On the season, they're 11th. Again: a unit coming up biggest in the biggest moments.
The Browns are just the sixth team since 2000 -- and the first since the 2017 Titans -- to have at least 6 wins through 10 games despite having a -30 or worse season point differential. Here's how those six teams finished:
6+ wins, -30 or worse point diff through 10 games since 2000
To narrow it down even more, only four teams since 2000 have had six game-winning drives in their first 10 games. Two of them -- the Browns and the Broncos -- are from this year. The other two are the 2016 Lions , who went 9-7 and missed the playoffs, and the 2003 Panthers, who went 11-5 and made the Super Bowl .
So, yes, these teams that outplay their point differential can and often do make the postseason. Furthermore, it's important to remember that none of those teams had the 14-team playoff. Right now, that expanded field is playing a crucial role.
That's the first piece of good news for the Browns. Another is that the AFC playoff race doesn't look especially cutthroat. The Patriots may not have Drake Maye again this season. Same for the Ravens and Lamar Jackson . The Browns' win over the Texans might be the nail in the coffin for 3-6 Houston, which has no room for error and now trails the head-to-head against Cleveland.
SportsLine projections have the Browns winning 9.4 games, seventh-most in the AFC and well clear of the closest competitor, the Texans at 8.0.
That leaves Cleveland with a 68% chance to make the postseason, per SportsLine calculations. The Texans and Patriots (19% each) are far, far behind.
Of course, nothing is set in stone. It's only been 10 weeks. Cleveland still has tough tests left, and the Browns have struggled against even some of the league's worst teams.
For now, this high-wire escape act is working, and the answer for "Can they keep this up?" is an unequivocal "Yes."
Unless one of the less-than-inspiring teams behind them makes a push, the Browns are on track to be, based on preseason expectations, of the most unlikely playoff teams of the 21st century -- a true credit to Monken, Watson and the entire organization.
And as Watson said Sunday, "Once you get in, anything can happen."
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Lions set to get key defensive player back in Week 11 in wake of Aidan Hutchinson injury
summary: Safety Kerby Joseph has missed the entire season with a knee injury sustained last year, but he is set to return to the lineup this week
full_text:
Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph is on the verge of returning to the lineup. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said during a radio interview on Tuesday that "the plan would be to get [Joseph] going this week" against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , according to The Detroit Free Press .
Joseph has been out the entire season with a knee injury sustained last year. He played in only the first six games of the 2025 season before being placed on injured reserve. Joseph dealt with the knee injury during the 2025 preseason and played through it early in the year, but he aggravated it and missed the remainder of the year.
The Lions' defense desperately needs the lift that Joseph can provide on the back end after losing star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season to a torn ACL suffered in the team's victory over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye on the first drive of the game and then injured his knee while celebrating the play.
Detroit's defense has played better of late after beginning the season looking like one of the worst units in the league. The Lions allowed at least 24 points in each of their first four games and at least 30 points in three of them. They also allowed at least 335 yards in each of those games and at least 445 in three of them. Since that point, they have yet to allow more than 21 points or 327 yards, and they have won five straight games.
It's probably no coincidence that they recently got defensive back Brian Branch back from his injury to solidify one of the spots in the secondary, which has helped limit opponents' ability to attack through the air. The Lions have been excellent against the run during that stretch, though, and their ability to wrangle opponents' run games may now take a hit with Hutchinson out. So, they need the lift that Joseph will provide on the back end to make up for it.
Detroit's schedule for the rest of the season includes a few tough tests, such as the division rival Bears twice and the Packers in the regular-season finale. However, it also provides some easier games against the Buccaneers (possibly without Baker Mayfield ), Falcons , Titans , Vikings and Giants . Joseph's return will surely help them navigate that slate, even if he has to ramp up to a full workload of snaps.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Why Derrick Henry and Ravens' rushing attack have collapsed without Lamar Jackson
summary: Henry scored twice but managed only 10 yards as Baltimore's ground game hit a historic low in its fifth consecutive loss
full_text:
If you simply looked at his touchdown total, you'd think that Derrick Henry had himself a night in the Week 10 finale. The veteran back once again barreled into the end zone multiple times, and even tied LaDainian Tomlinson for the most seasons with at least 10 rushing touchdowns (9) in NFL history. Not too shabby, right?
Well, when you zoom out of the mere touchdown total, you'll find Henry and the Baltimore Ravens ground attack managing just 16 total rushing yards amid a 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night. That led to Henry getting a bit testy in the locker room following the loss that dragged Baltimore to 4-6 on the season and its fifth straight defeat.
"What were they doing?" Henry asked when questioned about how L.A. was stopping them on the ground, via the Baltimore Banner . "Not letting us run the ball. We weren't efficient enough to run the ball. They were better on that side."
When asked whether it was more about the Ravens not executing or the Chargers doing a good job at stopping them, Henry said, "Everything. Just not doing a good enough job to be efficient in the run game. 16 total yards is a clear explanation."
Those 16 rushing yards are the third-fewest in a game in team history. They had zero rushing yards in the entire first half. As for Henry, he accounted for 10 of those 16 rushing yards on 10 attempts. When accounting for his five receptions in the loss, Henry averaged just 1.3 yards per touch, which is the fewest this season of any player (233 instances) that has had at least 15 touches in a game.
This lackluster ground attack on Monday night isn't a one-off for Baltimore. The run game has been virtually nonexistent amid this losing streak, which coincides with Lamar Jackson missing time due to an ankle and right thumb injury. Over the past seven games, Henry has logged zero 20-plus-yard rushes and has failed to have a 10-yard rush in three of his last four games.
During this five-game losing skid without Jackson, Henry has logged 81 touches for 246 yards. That 3.0 yards-per-touch average is the fewest of any player in a five-game span in the past five seasons (min. 80 touches), according to CBS Sports Research.
Again, this has a lot more to do with Lamar Jackson's absence than with Henry falling off. When you subtract Jackson from the equation, it takes the mystery out of Baltimore's running game. No defense fears the like of Tyler Huntley , Joe Fagnano or Jacoby Brissett pulling the ball from Henry and running it himself as they do with Jackson. That allows them to key in on Henry and the ground game even more, especially if they're struggling in the passing attack.
Here's a look at Baltimore's remaining opponents and how they are against the run so far this season:
The Ravens are 4-6 on the season and situated as the No. 10 seed in the AFC playoff picture, looking up at the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) and New England Patriots (5-5) in the wild card race. They are all looking to unseat either the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) or Cleveland Browns (6-4), who hold the No. 6 and No. 7 seeds entering Week 11.
If Baltimore can't find a way to rekindle their ground attack, their season may go by the wayside with it and eliminate any reason for Lamar Jackson to return from IR once his broken right thumb heals.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL Week 11 picks and score predictions: 49ers win Mexico City thriller over Vikings, Bengals stay hot
summary: We pick every Week 11 game as Joe Burrow draws an inviting matchup, the 49ers battle the Vikings in Mexico City
full_text:
I have made it 24 years without watching a single episode of "The Bachelor,"  but that streak might soon be coming to an end because an NFL quarterback has been chosen to star in the show.
Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman is this year's bachelor, and the only reason I'm mentioning that is that I'm not quite mentally ready to start talking about Week 11 yet. I just looked at the Week 11 schedule and what the NFL is giving us during the 1 p.m. window might be the worst slate of games ever.
There are seven games in the early window, and none of them will feature two teams with winning records facing off. Let's take a look at this schedule:
I would rather watch old episodes of "The Bachelor" than any of these games. That being said, I might watch the Cowboys game just to see if Jerry Jones fires everyone after his defense gives up 47 points to the Titans.
So will that actually happen? Let's get to the picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the Week 11 picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . In completely unrelated news, I'm in charge of the NFL newsletter here at CBSSports.com, which I'm only telling you about because it's the perfect gift for the holidays. If you want to buy someone a gift, but you don't actually want to spend money on them, just subscribe them to the newsletter. It's the gift that keeps on giving. All you have to do is click here and enter their email address .
For the second straight week, we have a team coming off a game in Europe facing a team coming off a bye. Last week, things worked out pretty well for the Bengals , but that feels like an anomaly. This game will mark just the seventh time in NFL history that a team coming off an international game has had to play a team coming off a bye, and uh, I have some bad news for everyone in Detroit: The team coming off the international game has gone 1-5, with the only win coming by a possessed Bengals team in Week 10 that got to host a Sunday night game at home for the first time in three years. There was no way the Bengals were losing.
However, I am worried about the Lions. For one, they just lost Aidan Hutchinson for the season to a torn ACL, and thanks to the injury, there's a 50% chance that Dan Campbell is going to ban his entire team from celebrating anything ever again.
Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF
Not only did they just lose their best defensive player, but it gets worse, because they now have to face the top rushing offense in the NFL. The Bucs are averaging 163.9 yards per game on the ground, which is 10 yards more than the next closest team. Tampa Bay has more rushing yards this season than the Bengals and Packers COMBINED.
I do not know if Baker Mayfield (foot) is going to play, but I'm not sure it matters, because the QB in Tampa only has one job and that's to hand the ball off. If Baker can't play, Jalon Daniels will, and if he can't play for some reason, the Bucs could probably just hold a fan raffle for the job.
Bucs: Can you hand the ball off? Fan: Yes. Bucs: OK, the job is yours.
There have only been three games this season where an NFL team has run the ball at least 49 times and the Buccaneers have two of them. With the Buccaneers coming off the bye, that means they're going to be well-rested and it also means that offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has had plenty of time to tear out every page from his playbook that has a passing play on it. The Bucs might run it 71 times on Sunday.
The good news for the Lions is that they've been one of the best teams in the NFL at stopping the run. They're giving up just 90.4 yards per game, which is the fifth-best number in the NFL, but that was with Hutchinson on the field. This week, they obviously won't have him.
The Lions are flying back from Germany; they just lost their best defensive player, and they have to face a Bucs team coming off a bye. Oh, and did I mention that NFL teams are a combined 13-3 coming off their bye this year? Because NFL teams are a combined 13-3 coming off their bye this year. And two of those three losses were by the Titans and Chargers , so I'm not even sure those count.
Not only do the Bucs have the best rushing attack in the NFL, but they also have the best run defense in the league, so this could be a long day for Jahmyr Gibbs . This game comes down to whether you trust Jared Goff to dice up Tampa Bay's defense, and, well, I'm the guy who made Goff my preseason prediction to win MVP this year, so I'm riding with Goff and the Lions here.
PICK: Lions 23-20 over Buccaneers
If there's any game in Week 11 that feels like a disaster waiting to happen, it's definitely this one. With the Jets and Chargers on the same field, I won't be surprised if the government declares SoFi Stadium a federal disaster area.
There's been no bigger disaster in the NFL this year than the Chargers. They hired Mike McDaniel to fix their offense and he somehow might have made it worse. When McDaniel was in Miami, one reason his offense worked so well is that he had two superstar receivers in Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle . He doesn't have anything near that in L.A., but he does not seem to realize that. McDaniel keeps doing things his own way, and as a result, the Chargers' offense is so bad it's almost painful to watch.
It's getting to the point where I feel like the Chargers' best offensive strategy would be to just not have an offense at all. I have no idea how that would work, but I have to think it would be an upgrade over what they're doing now. This team is averaging UNDER 180 passing yards per game, which shouldn't be possible when you have Justin Herbert as your QB.
Not to be outdone, the Jets have also been a disaster. Here's a quick synopsis of how things have gone for the Jets. Back on Feb. 24, Aaron Glenn said he would call plays on defense because it's one of his superpowers.
"To me, play calling is my superpower" Aaron Glenn on his decision to call plays on defense pic.twitter.com/FvHFYW97pK
As it turns out, though, he might have been wrong, and play-calling might actually be his kryptonite.
Aaron Glenn gave up play calling vs the #Bills — that’s really big of him. Called it his “super power” this offseason. He wants to call the game. To step back and be willing to give it to someone else, for the betterment of the team, isn’t something a lot of coaches are willing… https://t.co/ivYq4cnBca
Aaron Glenn saw Josh Allen coming up on the schedule in Week 10 and said "No thanks, I'm good. You're now in charge of calling play on defense, Brian."
So we have the Jets' broken defense going up against a Chargers offense that can't move the ball on anyone. I said this game feels like a disaster waiting to happen and that disaster might happen after the game. If the Jets lose here, the temperature on Aaron Glenn's hot seat will get so hot that I don't think the Fahrenheit scale can actually measure it. We might have to switch over to Celsius.
The Chargers stunned the Ravens on Monday night by rushing for a season-high 160 yards. Running the ball is literally the only thing the Chargers can do on offense, which might work in their favor here because the Jets can't stop the run.
The Chargers went into Week 10 with ZERO wins, so I feel crazy even thinking this, but this team might actually win two games in a row.
PICK: Chargers 19-16 over Jets

This game was originally scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET, but the NFL decided to move it to 4:25 p.m. ET, and we're celebrating that fact here at CBS Sports by sending "The NFL Today" crew to MetLife Stadium.

author: John Breech

title: Ranking the 50 QBs who have started an NFL game in 2026: From cellar-dwellers to gold standard
summary: Every quarterback to start an NFL game this season is ranked across 10 tiers, with Joe Burrow setting the gold standard
full_text:
So far, quarterback injuries and a revolving door of quarterbacks represent defining aspects of the 2026 NFL season. That number reached 50 quarterbacks in Week 10, which would be a staggering amount for an entire season.
So where do they all stack up? The rankings were broken down into 10 tiers, with three quarterbacks getting their own tier.
49. Carson Beck , Cardinals
46. Joe Milton III , Eagles
43. Justin Herbert , Chargers
Nobody wants to be here, but their performances have nonetheless left them in the basement. Of all the quarterbacks in this group, Herbert is the most notable given all the success he experienced during his first six seasons in Los Angeles.
Herbert hasn't been good, but it's not all on him. His supporting cast hasn't carried its weight, and the Chargers' coaching staff (especially Jim Harbaugh and OC Mike McDaniel) aren't on the same page.
If there's a silver lining for Herbert, it's that Peyton Manning had a similar season at a similar point in his career. Manning bounced back all the way to the Hall of Fame. We'll see how Herbert responds to this adversity.
42. Fernando Mendoza , Raiders
Mendoza gets his own tier for two reasons: he's had just one start, and that start was a mixed bag. Overall, it was a promising debut for the No. 1 overall pick.
Facing Seattle's "Dark Side" defense, Mendoza went 11 of 13 in the first half and scored the only touchdown before intermission on a 10-yard run. Mendoza was less effective in the second half as Seattle ratcheted up the pressure. He finished with 143 yards on 17 of 29 passing in a 21-13 loss.
41. Kyle McCord , Dolphins
40. Carson Wentz , Vikings
39. Baker Mayfield , Buccaneers
38. Jalon Daniels , Buccaneers
36. Shedeur Sanders , Browns
35. Gardner Minshew , Cardinals
34. Jameis Winston , Giants
33. Tyler Huntley , Ravens
32. Marcus Mariota , Commanders
31. J.J. McCarthy , Giants
Each of these backups experienced various levels of success.
McCarthy, traded from the Vikings to address New York's injury situation, is getting another chance (albeit temporary) to be an NFL starting quarterback. As was the case in Minnesota, McCarthy has shown signs of being a solid player in New York, but he still needs to work on his consistency, among other things.
Take last week, for example. McCarthy threw for 293 yards and a touchdown and made some plays with his feet, but he also threw an ugly interception that sealed New York's loss to Washington.
Daniels, the only rookie in this group, led the Buccaneers to their first win of the season, an upset in Dallas back in Week 5. A week later, he took Tampa Bay to overtime in an eventual loss to the Steelers .
Mayfield was included here because his performance this season is most in line with this tier. He threw just 14 combined passes in his two wins as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He made odd history in Week 8 by becoming the first quarterback since 1974 to win a start without completing a single pass.
30. Jacoby Brissett , Ravens
29. Kyler Murray , Vikings
28. Malik Willis , Dolphins
27. Michael Penix Jr. , Falcons
24. Sam Darnold , Seahawks
These quarterbacks have had moments of success this season, but those moments have often been overshadowed by shortcomings.
Hurts is dealing with something much bigger than football. He's been away from the team since blood clots were discovered following the Eagles' Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. The Eagles said at the time that Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and that he is expected to make a full recovery.
Murray is listed as a starter here, but there's a very good chance that, barring injury, he has made his final start for the Vikings. Minnesota's production with him under center just wasn't up to snuff.
22. Geno Smith , Jets 21. Drake Maye , Patriots
20. Deshaun Watson , Browns
18. Aaron Rodgers , Steelers 17. Bryce Young , Panthers
These guys aren't the first quarterbacks taken in fantasy football drafts, and for good reason: they don't consistently put up numbers. They are, however, above-average quarterbacks who once in a while show flashes of greatness, just not enough to be ranked higher.
Rodgers' production isn't close to what it once was, but he has continued to play good football (especially for a 42-year-old) while helping the Steelers get off to a 6-3 start. A big reason Rodgers hasn't had more success is Pittsburgh's lack of receiving weapons, a need that wasn't addressed at the trade deadline .
Nix had a slow start to the season, which was probably a byproduct of January's season-ending ankle injury. His play has improved in recent weeks, which is certainly good news for a Broncos team with Super Bowl aspirations.
Watson has struggled with his consistency and production from a touchdown standpoint (he hasn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5), but he's been good enough to win six of his nine starts. Each of Cleveland's wins featured game-winning drives led by Watson.
Maye's tumultuous season took a disastrous turn Sunday when he suffered a potentially season-ending ankle injury .
Each backup quarterback that has started a game this season has had various levels of success. None has been better than Lock, who is 3-0 this year as Seattle's starting quarterback. Lock's stellar play (he has had seven touchdowns, no picks, and has completed 73.1% of his passes) has led to rumblings about whether or not he should be the starter in Seattle moving forward .
14. Jayden Daniels , Commanders
13. Dak Prescott , Cowboys
12. Kirk Cousins , Vikings
Stroud has put up good numbers, and he is far from Houston's biggest problem. Houston had seven players miss Sunday's loss to Cleveland due to injury. Their running game has been largely non-existent, and the defense has underperformed all year.
Prescott continues to be one of the league's most prolific passers, but most of his production has come against bad teams or when the Cowboys were trying to catch up, as was the case during Sunday's loss to the 49ers.
Cousins' performance in Sunday's win over the Packers was nothing short of amazing. Just days after being traded from Las Vegas, Cousins threw a pair of scores and completed 67.7% of his passes while leading Minnesota to a 30-10 win. If Cousins keeps this up, the Vikings could very well win the NFL's hardest division, if not the Super Bowl .
Per usual, Daniels has been excellent this season when healthy. Dart was off to a strong start before an injury ended his sophomore season after just two weeks.
10. Lamar Jackson , Ravens
8. Matthew Stafford , Lions
Jackson was off to another strong start before a thumb injury derailed his season and the Ravens'. Williams missed three games earlier this season, and while his play has been mostly good, his production has been somewhat lacking (he has just three games with multiple touchdown passes this season). His four-pick performance in Chicago's Week 9 win over Tampa was a tough watch.
Stafford, the league's reigning MVP, has displayed remarkable resilience this season amid the Rams ' early losses and injuries to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams . He won't win a second MVP this season, but in some ways, Stafford's performance so far this season is just as impressive.
Stafford's predecessor in Los Angeles, Goff continues to play at a high level in Detroit. His success has led to continued success for the Lions, who are once again in the thick of the NFC North race.
6. Patrick Mahomes , Chiefs
5. Trevor Lawrence , Jaguars
All five of these guys have an MVP case.
Allen, the MVP front-runner for most of the season's first half, doesn't have as many touchdown passes (13) as his peers, but he does have a league-high 11 touchdown runs. He's also the catalyst for the Bills' 8-1 start.
Purdy has been rock solid all year for the 8-1 49ers, but it's fair to wonder whether his strong supporting cast will negatively impact his MVP chances. Regardless, Purdy is playing the best ball of his career and is a big reason why the 49ers are the cream of the NFC crop.
Love…

title: Cardinals hand Chiefs an infrequent gift
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals this weekend. The Chiefs are one of the best clubs in the AFC and one of four teams with identical 7-2-0 records. Which means they are a really good team.   With this game, Arizona is giving the Chiefs a rare occurrence on any team’s regular season […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: Isaac Seumalo #73 of the Arizona Cardinals drops back to block during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals this weekend. The Chiefs are one of the best clubs in the AFC and one of four teams with identical 7-2-0 records. Which means they are a really good team. With this game, Arizona is giving the Chiefs a rare occurrence on any team’s regular season schedule. RELATED: JORDAN BURCH LOST FOR SEASON The Cardinals are showing they are a hot mess and one of the worst teams in the league, currently at 3-7-0. Kansas City has the opportunity to play in this year’s AFC Championship Game the way they are playing. Five of their nine contests, the Chiefs have scored 30+ points. But there are obstacles on their schedule. That begins the week after playing Arizona. The Chiefs are on the road on Thanksgiving Day against the Buffalo Bills. Currently, the Bills are the AFC’s best team with an 8-1-0 record. They have a 3-1 home record and are the league’s highest-scoring team with 287 points. Needless to say, this is an important game for both the Bills and Chiefs. As the season begins to dwindle, both clubs are assured of making the playoff whether as a division winner or a lower seed. However, with these two clubs, the Number 1 seed in this year’s postseason just might be at stake. Here’s the rub: The Chiefs against the Bills on Thursday in a huge matchup is just four days after playing the Cardinals. Usually, this is a major issue. There isn’t time to have a player’s day off or have any meaningful practice sessions in order to get ready for the next opponent and gameplan. Not to mention the colossal matchup pitting Buffalo against Kansas City. The loser suddenly starts to backpedal and, in all likelihood, gets sent to the bottom of the playoff contenders, whereas the winner is king of the mountain. By playing the Cardinals first, the Chiefs have the opportunity to rest some starters in order to save them for the Bills, which also guarantees they won’t become injured. This is usually the norm in the final game of the season for certain clubs that are already in the playoffs and have nothing to gain with a win. Teams have been known to start their entire second team offensive and defensive units in contests such as this. But never during the meat of the schedule. It is very possible that Kansas City could run their starters in the first quarter, or even the first half, and then insert the second teamers for the remainder of the game. Arizona has been outscored 51-9 in their past two games. Their offense cannot run the ball, and are starting the third quarterback this year behind an offensive line full of Band-Aids and backups to backups. The team has scored less than 24 points in a game seven out of nine contests. Three games, less than 10 points. They have the seventh fewest scoring offense. The defense is tied for allowing the most points (289). Kansas City is 4–0 at Arrowhead Stadium this season and holds an average margin of victory of 15.8 points at home, the second-best mark in the NFL. However, it is not exactly about one team looking beyond this week’s opponent and thinking they are going to breeze by without trying. Playing their second teamers against what Arizona is putting on the field just might become a fair fight. Look at the Cardinals’ current starting lineup on offense compared to Week 1: QB3 RB2, RB3, RB PS WR4, WR5, WR6 TE1, TE2, TE IR RT1 RG1 C2 LG1 LT3 The entire Cardinals roster is a hot mess. Which is “Advantage Kansas City.”

title: 3 up and 3 down: The Midseason Edition
summary: The Atlanta Falcons have played roughly 60% of their games, so this is the perfect time for a midseason 3 up and 3 down to see whose stock has risen the most and who’s taken the biggest hit. Here’s the Week 10 edition. 3 up Drake London The touchdown numbers have taken a hit, but […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 15: Drake London (5) of the Atlanta Falcons breaks free of the Kansas City Chiefs defense during the Sunday afternoon NFL game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Kansas City Chiefs on November 15, 2026 at the Mercedes-benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons have played roughly 60% of their games, so this is the perfect time for a midseason 3 up and 3 down to see whose stock has risen the most and who’s taken the biggest hit. Here’s the Week 10 edition. 3 up Drake London The touchdown numbers have taken a hit, but don’t get it twisted, Drake London has been worth every penny. I know he had a drop in the Chiefs game, but that’s a rare occurrence for the wideout; it was only his second this season. This man has dealt with constant quarterback shuffling, bad offensive coordinators, and no consistent running mate, but he still gets the job done. Heading into the bye, London has the 7th-most receiving yards in the league, and his inaccurate quarterback is suppressing those numbers. He’s the best blocking receiver on the team, and you never have to worry about his effort. You’re always going to get the best version of him. Drake London adds to his HUGE night @ATLvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0nWsw3vuwJ — NFL (@NFL) September 25, 2026 Gervon Dexter Sr. Dexter was one of a handful of players who got an in-season extension , and he’s been living up to it. He’s second in pressures (30) on the team, the 5th most among all interior defensive linemen, and his 15.2 pass-rush win rate is 6th best for his position. He also has the second most sacks on the team. Acquired via trade right before the season, he had a lot to prove in this new environment but has fit well in this attacking front. He still needs work in the run game; he doesn’t handle doubles well, but he still has the 3rd most run stops on the team with 10. If he can keep improving that area of his game, he’ll be one of the best overall interior players in the league. Chris Lindstrom There may be issues on this offensive line, but Lindstrom is not one of them. In true pass sets, he’s only allowed eight pressures and one sack across 10 games. He’s also shown that he can play in this new scheme and be a weapon as a puller. Unfortunately, he’s playing next to arguably the worst run-blocking tackle in the league, and his former center, Ryan Neuzil, wasn’t a fit, making it even harder for Lindstrom to thrive. Doesn’t matter to Lindstrom; he’s shown up every week and done his job. The team needs to get him some help this offseason so he’s not doing it alone. Chris Lindstrom had one of the best performances of his career last night. He's doing it all in this revitalized run scheme. Elite at climbing to the 2nd level. Finally getting opportunities as a puller. Had multiple 2 for 1s & consistently moved the Saints DL off their spots pic.twitter.com/SNxddB0MIG — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 6, 2026 Honorable Mentions: Sydney Brown, Bijan Robinson, and LaCale London 3 down Michael Penix Jr It’s been a mixed bag for the quarterback, and that’s not what you want to hear when you’re auditioning for your future. At this rate, I am not confident he’ll get his 5th-year option picked up. There have been flashes of good quarterback play, but not enough to give anyone confidence he’s the franchise’s future. The Falcons need the quarterback that showed up to the 49ers game, not the one they’ve had since. While accuracy has always been an issue, Penix has done a good job of protecting the ball, but we aren’t seeing that this year. Lately, his good play doesn’t come until the game is out of hand. It also isn’t a good sign that in the 2/3 wins where he looked good, his backfield put up 200 yards on the ground. He isn’t elevating the offense, and he is cracking under pressure while facing it at the second-lowest rate (28.7%) in the league . Penix isn’t playing for his 5th year anymore; he’s playing for his job in 2027. If the team keeps losing, they may end up with the opportunity to grab a new quarterback or feel forced to spend more money than they’d like on the market. Off target, missing open guys, and putting the ball in harms way. It's hard to win football games and build any sort of momentum playing like this. pic.twitter.com/c7yiogOxmE — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 16, 2026 Divine Deablo A player many of us had hoped would become a piece for the future is playing himself out of Atlanta. Deablo has been bad out of the gate. His play recognition has regressed, and he looks like a shell of himself. He was dealing with a hamstring to start the season and is once again wearing a club. The team scratched him for the Chiefs game, and hopefully the bye week does his body some good. Unfortunately, injuries are a feature of his player profile. He’s missed time every year of his career with something, and you can’t commit significant dollars to someone who can’t stay on the field. AJ Terrell When cornerbacks fall off, they fall hard. This season had the makings of a special storyline with the addition of his younger brother ; now the Falcons have to handle this situation carefully to prevent any bad blood. There were some lapses before Terrell went on IR, but since coming back, he’s been a disaster. It’s one thing to get torched by Ja’Marr Chase; it’s another to get worked by Cyrus Allen, giving him his first touchdown of the year. There is no easy out of this contract; the best the Falcons can hope for is that he comes off the bye, looks serviceable, and gives them enough confidence to roll into 2027 for one last ride. Filthy route from Cyrus Allen 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/YNh2IdJZjU — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Dishonorable Mentions: Mike Hughes, Jawaan Taylor, and Olamide Zaccheaus The Falcons have seven games left, and everyone on this list has a chance to improve or lower their stock heading into the offseason. It ain’t over till it’s over, and this evaluation period will be critical in helping the Falcons build their 2027 roster. Who will you be keeping an eye on during the final stretch?
