title: 3 reasons why the Bengals will beat the Commanders on MNF, and 3 reasons they won’t
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals did it! They not only got revenge on their hated division rival for their Week 3 defeat, but they absolutely dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers from the first snap to the last. They won the game 38-18, and 15 of those 18 points were from garbage time scores. So even though the Bengals […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals did it! They not only got revenge on their hated division rival for their Week 3 defeat, but they absolutely dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers from the first snap to the last. They won the game 38-18, and 15 of those 18 points were from garbage time scores. So even though the Bengals won by 20 points, the game wasn’t even that close. Now they travel to Landover, Maryland, to face the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. The Bengals last played the Commanders in 2024, when Jayden Daniels and the Washington offense beat the Bengals in a shootout, 38-33. What will happen on Monday night? Here are three reasons the Bengals will win on Monday Night Football, followed by three reasons they won’t. The Bengals will win because…. They’re a better team from top to bottom. This is a fact. The Bengals have a more talented roster, and that more talented roster is playing at a higher level than the Commanders are likely even capable of. The Commanders’ offense has scored over 30 points just once this season, and that was in Week 3. The Bengals have scored at least 30 points in five consecutive games, and Joe Burrow is leading the pack for NFL MVP at this point in the season. And then there’s Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who have time to do their thing because the offensive line is doing a good job at protecting the quarterback. The Bengals scored seemingly at will on Sunday Night Football against a defense that has been playing good football over the prior month. The Commanders are talented—there isn’t a team in the league that doesn’t have talent all over their roster. But they’re not nearly as loaded as the Bengals. Nobody is. It’s not a tough matchup on the secondary. The Bengals’ secondary could use a little work, and the defensive front is really pulling a lot of the weight. However, for the second week in a row, the Bengals’ secondary will be matching up against a receiving corps that has seen better days. Terry McLaurin, the Commanders’ WR1, is on IR for the reason of the year, which means Washington’s top wide receiver is likely an over-his-prime Stefon Diggs. Similarly to their game plan against the Steelers, Al Golden will likely feel comfortable leaving his corners and safeties on islands against the Commanders’ receivers, allowing the defensive line and linebackers to focus on the run game and rushing the passer. The Commanders’ struggle against the pass. I mean, nobody does against the Bengals, right? The thing is, the Commanders are coming into Week 11 allowing the 10th most yards through the air in the league. Outside the Cowboys and Rams, though, the passing attacks of every team they’ve played have been mediocre at best. The Bengals have the most potent passing attack in the NFL. On top of that, the Commanders’ defense blitzes at the third-highest rate in the NFL. On Sunday night, the Steelers blitzed Burrow 12 times. Burrow went 12 for 12 for 186 yards. View Link The Bengals won’t win because….. There is such a thing as an emotional hangover. How many times have we seen a team blow out a rival one week just to lose to an inferior team the next week? It happens multiple times every season. The season is short—compared to the NHL, NBA, and MLB, it’s pathetically short—but it’s not short enough that the eventual Super Bowl winner can’t drop a non-conference game they should have won earlier in the season. Only one team has been perfect coast-to-coast, and the only team I remember being perfect in the regular season was the ‘07 Patriots, and we know what happened to them. The Bengals won the big one on Sunday Night Football, and as much as I’d love to see them go 8-2 for the first time since the 2015 season, it wouldn’t shock me if they looked like a different team on Monday. It just happens sometimes. Jayden Daniels could be a matchup problem. Do you remember when I said the Bengals’ secondary doesn’t have too tough a matchup on Monday Night Football? Well, even the worst receiving corps in the NFL can figure out a way to get open if the quarterback is able to extend the play. No corner can stay on a receiver’s hip for more than a few seconds. If the Bengals’ defensive line can’t put pressure on Daniels, it could be a big problem for the secondary. Daniels is one of the most athletic quarterbacks the Bengals will face all season long. If he gets out of the pocket, not only could he punish the Bengals with his legs, but he can buy time to find a receiver downfield. He’s perfectly capable of making any throw required of him, and if the Bengals can’t keep him in a pocket they can close around him, the secondary could have a long day. The Bengals’ opponent has a rest advantage…again. The Steelers were coming off their bye week and still lost to the Bengals, who were coming off an international trip. The Bengals absolutely overcame that situation, thanks to leadership from Zac Taylor and the rest of the staff that got the players from Cincinnati to Madrid and back without skipping a beat. Can they do it again? They’ll have an extra day, going from Sunday Night Football to Monday Night Football, but the Commanders will be coming off a Thursday Night Football game. This gives them 11 days to the Bengals’ 8. It’s not a huge difference, but sometimes it’s the little things that make big differences in NFL games. Why do you think the Bengals will win or lose? Sound off!
author: Jason Garrison

title: Buy or Sell: 15 hot takes on the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are on fire. They’re riding a five-game win streak, have the best offense in the league, Joe Burrow is playing out of his mind, and they just dominated the Steelers at home in front of a national audience. So, yeah. Things are pretty great right now in the Queen City. Below are […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are on fire. They’re riding a five-game win streak, have the best offense in the league, Joe Burrow is playing out of his mind, and they just dominated the Steelers at home in front of a national audience. So, yeah. Things are pretty great right now in the Queen City. Below are 15 hot takes from across the internet, and some I’ve whipped up on my own. I’ll share whether I’m buying or selling, but I want to see what you think. Sound off! Joe Burrow is going to win the 2026 NFL MVP. Burrow is playing lights out. He is responsible for at least four touchdowns in each of the last five games, and has been able to guide the Bengals to almost score at will since mid-October. He does have the best wide receiver duo in the NFL, but he’s putting the ball only where they can catch it, and he’s leading the best offense in the NFL. If things go this way, he’ll be a shoo-in. My take: Buy. If I were a betting man, I’d place a wager. The Bengals have the best offense in the NFL. Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been lights out. Against the Steelers’ vaunted defense, Burrow threw for 337 yards and three touchdowns. In the first half. At that point in the game, the Steelers only had 40 yards and mustered just three points. The game was over then and there. My take: Buy Bengals should be favorites to represent AFC in the Super Bowl They’ve come a long way since we were questioning what was going on in their back-to-back losses in Weeks 3 and 4. The defense still has some growing to do, though—especially the secondary. I think they’re close, and by the time the season comes to an end, hopefully it’s a yes. My take: Sell, for now Amarius Mims will be an All-Pro this season. Mims has taken 381 pass-blocking snaps, and he’s only given up six pressures (per PFF). He has the third-highest pass-rush efficiency and has been nothing short of the second coming of Big Willie Anderson. The Bengals have been able to leave Mims all alone on an island against some of the league’s best pass rushers, and he’s absolutely shut them down. My take: Buy Zac Taylor deserves serious consideration for Coach of the Year. He will be in the conversation because the Bengals are 7-2 and are among the small list of teams that can be considered true contenders. He flawlessly guided the Bengals through an international trip, and then brought them right back home to blow out the Steelers, who were coming off their bye week. That alone is pretty incredible. My Take: Buy Ja’Marr Chase is already the greatest wide receiver in Bengals history. Can it be that after just six seasons in the league, we can crown Chase as the greatest receiver in the franchise’s history? And to be clear, the Bengals have a long list of amazing wide receivers—it’s kind of their thing. Chase has 7,715 receiving yards, which is the third most in franchise history behind AJ Green (9,430) and Chad Johnson (10,783). He’s fourth in franchise history in touchdown receptions with 61, but the leader, also Johnson, has 66. It wouldn’t be surprising if Chase was the new record holder before we get to December. Chad is great, but…. My Take: Buy The Bengals don’t need a top-10 defense to win the Super Bowl. With the best offense in the NFL, maybe the Bengals’ defense only needs to be okay. Maybe they can be near the middle of the pack, or possibly even closer to the bottom than the top. As long as it’s not the worst, right? No, we’ve seen that movie. My Take: Sell Boye Mafe was Cincinnati’s best offseason acquisition. The Bengals signed Mafe for less than the Ravens were willing to pay Trey Hendrickson, and it has been a great decision, rivaling some of the top free-agent acquisitions they’ve made over the last dozen years. But while it was special, the trade for Dexter Lawrence was a generational thing. My Take: Sell The Bengals will finish the regular season with at least 13 wins. The best regular-season finish the Bengals have had was 12-4. They’ve done that four times in team history (2022, 2015, 1988, 1981), and 13 wins would set a new record. It would also possibly put the Bengals in contention for the No. 1 overall seed in the playoffs, meaning the AFC Championship Game will be played in Cincinnati (hopefully). My Take: Buy Tee Higgins would be a top-five receiver if he were another team’s WR1. I’m not going to spend too much time on this. It’s a yes. The only reason Higgins isn’t WR1 is he plays on the same team with the best wide receiver in the NFL. Think of him as the Cris Carter to Chase’s Randy Moss. My Take: Buy The Bengals will sweep their remaining AFC North games. This, I think, will come down to the Browns. The Ravens aren’t going to be able to overcome the injuries they’ve suffered, and it’s the Browns who are 6-4 that pose the biggest threat to the Bengals in the AFC North. They’ve had the Bengals’ number over the past few years, but that’s a monkey the team has been able to shed as of late. I don’t think Cleveland can keep up with Cincinnati’s offense. My Take: Buy The Bengals’ offensive line is the best it’s been in the Burrow era. Burrow has been one of the most hit quarterbacks since he was drafted in 2020, which is one of the reasons he’s spent so much time on the IR in his career. For the first time, he came into a season with the same five starters on the offensive line in front of him as he had the season before. And they’ve played like it. He has been able to operate from a clean pocket, or has at least had the time to step up to find a receiver. He has only been sacked 16 times, which is the sixth fewest in the league. My Take: Buy The Bengals will regret not making a bigger move at the trade deadline. Yeesh. The Bengals thrashing the Steelers on Sunday Night Football may not have completely washed away the bad taste in the mouths of fans created by the front office’s blunder at the trade deadline. Here’s the thing: The Bengals absolutely have the talent on their roster to win the Super Bowl. If they don’t, though, will we look back at the trade deadline as the reason why? My Take: Sell……. I hope Anything short of reaching the AFC Championship Game would make this season a disappointment. I came into the season thinking the Bengals needed to win at least one playoff game for me to be satisfied in the direction Taylor and his staff were taking the team, and anything short of that should result in his termination. My opinion on the matter has changed somewhat, though. They’re too good to win on Wildcard Weekend just to get bounced by a less-talented team in the divisional round. So yeah, not getting a chance to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl would be a big disappointment. My Take: Buy This is the best Bengals team in franchise history. The Bengals have been to three Super Bowls, and they’ve unfortunately lost all three. It’s difficult to even compare those three teams to each other because there were over 30 years between the second and third teams to reach the ultimate game. So it’s hard to compare this team to those teams too. They’re exciting, for sure. I don’t know if I can say they’re the best, though. Yet. My Take: Sell, hopefully just for now Now, discuss in the comment section. Do you buy or sell the 15 lukewarm-to-hot takes above? Sound off!

title: Bengals News: More big events coming to Paycor Stadium?
summary: The riverfront of the city of Cincinnati has undergone some major changes over the last 40 years. full_text: The riverfront of the city of Cincinnati has undergone some major changes over the last 40 years. From a series of parking lots between Paycor Stadium and Great American Ballpark to The Banks, the area between the two professional sports franchises’ respective homes has been transformed into a place people actually want to be. One major issue the city faces, though, is a lack of places to host large events. Sure they have Heritage Bank Arena, but it’s old and run down, and it just doesn’t have a very large seating capacity. The city and county could bring in a ton of revenue if they could attract some major events. Luckily for the denizens of the Greater Cincinnati Area, Hamilton County has begun the search for a partner to help bring major events to Cincinnati at Paycor Stadium. So that band you like that’s going to be touring in the next couple of years, maybe they’ll make a stop down on Pete Rose Way. “This is about maximizing the return on investment for the taxpayer,” Hamilton County Commissioner Denise Driehaus, according to the county’s website . “By attracting more events to Paycor Stadium, we can generate additional revenue while supporting jobs, tourism and local businesses.” Here’s what else is going on: NFL snubs Bengals’ red-hot offense and flexes AFC North rival into Week 12 primetime slot instead The league has flexed the Cleveland Browns’ Week 12 home game against the Las Vegas Raiders to “Sunday Night Football.” The move bumps the Los Angeles Chargers’ matchup with the New England Patriots out of the primetime slot. It’s time: This is finally the year Bengals star Joe Burrow wins his first MVP award For the first time in his seven-year career, the Cincinnati Bengals star quarterback has the inside track to winning his first NFL MVP award. The Bengals demolished the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night, 38-18. Bengals Release Uniform Combination for Week 11 Against Commanders The Bengals head to Washington for their third straight national game as they play the Commanders on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow’s Big Night and a Shut-Down Defense Earn Bengals an ‘A+’ Grade Against Steelers Burrow was money through the air, Ja’Marr Chase ran circles around Pittsburgh’s defenders, and the defense shut Aaron Rodgers down for three straight quarters. Cincinnati also pushed its winning streak to five games while climbing to 7-2. Zac Taylor’s squad now hits the road for a Monday Night Football trip to Washington.

title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly: Bengals get revenge vs. Steelers
summary: That’s how you answer a September loss. With first place in the AFC North on the line and the country watching on Sunday Night Football, the Cincinnati Bengals jumped on Pittsburgh early, led 24-3 at halftime and 31-3 late in the third quarter, and cruised to a 38-18 win at Paycor. Cincinnati is 7-2, has […]
full_text: That’s how you answer a September loss. With first place in the AFC North on the line and the country watching on Sunday Night Football, the Cincinnati Bengals jumped on Pittsburgh early, led 24-3 at halftime and 31-3 late in the third quarter, and cruised to a 38-18 win at Paycor. Cincinnati is 7-2, has won five straight, and sits alone atop the division. It’s hard to find much to complain about after a night like that, but we’ll try. Let’s get into it. The Good Joe Burrow, MVP front-runner. Burrow went 35-of-44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns with no turnovers, a 135.7 passer rating. He had 302 yards and three touchdowns by halftime. His 27 touchdown passes lead the NFL. He also became the second quarterback in league history with at least four total touchdowns in five straight games, joining Peyton Manning (2004). Ja’Marr Chase on the big stage. Chase had 11 catches for 231 yards, including 146 in the first half. That’s the most receiving yards by any player in a game this season, the fourth-most in Bengals history, and the fourth 200-yard game of his career. His 53- and 43-yard catches both set up touchdowns. Chase Brown, red zone weapon. Brown caught touchdowns from 2 and 4 yards out, his second career two-touchdown game, and finished with eight catches for 39 yards and 10 carries for 44 yards. Drew Sample (3 yards) and Dohnte Meyers (15 yards) also caught touchdowns, and Samaje Perine ran one in from a yard out. A first-half defensive clinic. Pittsburgh had 40 total yards and four first downs at halftime. Aaron Rodgers started 0-of-8 and didn’t complete a pass until late in the second quarter. By then, the Bengals had completed 21, which ties the most by one team before its opponent’s first completion since 1978. Boye Mafe (his team-leading 6.5th sack), Jonathan Allen and Myles Murphy each sacked Rodgers. History. Cincinnati has now scored 30-plus points in five straight games. That’s the longest streak in franchise history, breaking the old mark of four set in 1997, and no other NFL team has done it this season. The 66,860 fans at Paycor were the fourth-largest home crowd in team history. “The Dirty Work” Guys. Drew Sample, Samaje Perine, and Brown all did a number of things in this one. Sneakily effective receiving options, effective runs, and pass protection galore. Upon a rewatch of this game, Perine and Brown were seldom knocked down on first contact. The Beatdown on Primetime TV. How many times have we seen the Steelers impose their physical will upon the Bengals—especially under the brightest of lights? Cincinnati absolutely dominated their divisional foes in their own trademark way, dominating the trenches, and utilizing their amazing offensive weapons. And they did it with the nation watching. “Satisfying” doesn’t quite cover it. The Bad The streak is over. Evan McPherson opened the game with a 24-yarder, his 25th straight make, the longest active streak in the NFL. Then he pushed a 43-yard try wide right in the second quarter, his first miss of the season. He’s still 13-of-14 on the year, and nobody should panic, but it was a reminder that nothing lasts forever. I mean, let’s give him a pass—he has been outstanding this entire season. The run defense, still leaky. Pittsburgh ran for 102 yards on 23 carries, 4.4 yards per carry. That’s better than the last two weeks, but it’s still more than you’d like against an offense that couldn’t throw a lick in the first half. The Ugly The flags. The Bengals were penalized eight times for 80 yards, double Pittsburgh’s four for 46. Against a team that was already beaten, it didn’t matter. Against Kansas City, Buffalo and/or a playoff opponent, 80 yards of free field position will matter in a big way. The fourth-quarter fade. Up 31-3, the defense let Rodgers throw touchdown passes to DK Metcalf (22 yards) and Pat Freiermuth (27 yards), plus a two-point conversion. That was 15 points in about five minutes. It’s garbage time, sure, and the final margin was never in doubt. But it turned a historic beatdown into a 20-point win, and it’s a habit worth breaking before the games get tighter. That’s about as nitpicky as it gets. On a night that featured the best quarterback in the league and arguably the best receiver, the Bengals looked every bit like a contender.
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Week 10 awards from Bengals’ impressive win vs. Steelers
summary: A 38-18 Sunday night win over your biggest rival, a fifth straight victory, and sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Not a bad weekend in the Queen City. The stars were brilliant, and we’ll honor them. But a win like this also needs the guys who did the dirty work. Here are […]
full_text: A 38-18 Sunday night win over your biggest rival, a fifth straight victory, and sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Not a bad weekend in the Queen City. The stars were brilliant, and we’ll honor them. But a win like this also needs the guys who did the dirty work. Here are my nominees for Team MVP and Unsung Hero of the Week. Team MVP nominees Joe Burrow, QB. Burrow went 35-of-44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns with no turnovers, a 135.7 passer rating. He had 302 yards and three scores by halftime, before Aaron Rodgers had done much of anything. He’s now the second quarterback in NFL history with four or more total touchdowns in five straight games, joining Peyton Manning, and his 27 touchdown passes lead the league. If this was his MVP audition on national TV, he nailed it. Ja’Marr Chase, WR. Chase caught 11 of his 14 targets for 231 yards, 146 of them in the first half. That’s the most receiving yards by any player in a game this season and the fourth-most in Bengals history. His 53- and 43-yard catches both set up touchdowns. He didn’t score, but nobody had a bigger impact on the game. Boye Mafe, DE. Mafe hit Rodgers three times and sacked him once on a third down, pushing his team-leading total to 6.5 sacks. He was a big reason Pittsburgh had four first downs and 40 total yards at halftime. Unsung Hero of the Week nominees Demetrius Knight Jr., LB. Knight led the team with eight tackles, six of them solo, plus a pass breakup and a quarterback hit. On a night when the pass rush got the headlines, Knight was the one cleaning up everything underneath and keeping Pittsburgh’s short game in check. Jordan Battle, S. Battle was second on the team with six tackles. He added a tackle for loss and a pass breakup, and was all over the field in a secondary that held Rodgers to 15-of-29 passing, with both of his touchdowns coming after the game was decided. Drew Sample, TE. Sample caught three passes for 15 yards, including the 3-yard touchdown that put the Bengals up 10-0, his second career touchdown catch. As usual, much of his value came as a blocker, the kind of work that never shows up in a box score. Jonathan Allen and Myles Murphy, DL. Each had a sack. Allen’s, like Mafe’s, came on third down and ended a Steelers drive, and Murphy’s brought his season total to 2.5. Neither will make SportsCenter, but those drive-killers are why Pittsburgh couldn’t find any rhythm early. The offensive line. Burrow was sacked once all night against a Steelers front that usually lives in the backfield. That’s how a quarterback throws for 302 yards in a half. Dalton Risner hurt his left knee during the game, so keep an eye on his status this week. Your vote Who’s your Team MVP: Burrow or Chase? And who did the dirty work best on Sunday night? Make your case in the comments! And Who Dey!

title: Grading the Browns offense during their midseason bye week
summary: Describing the Cleveland Browns offense from last season is easy; to sum it up, it was abysmal. Top to bottom. From the offensive line, quarterback, skill positions, everything was bad. GM Andrew Berry spent the entire offseason rebuilding the entire unit. With the team entering their bye week, we will give a grade to the […]
full_text: Describing the Cleveland Browns offense from last season is easy; to sum it up, it was abysmal. Top to bottom. From the offensive line, quarterback, skill positions, everything was bad. GM Andrew Berry spent the entire offseason rebuilding the entire unit. With the team entering their bye week , we will give a grade to the 2026 Browns offense that was created out of all those moves. Browns roster, offense: What has changed? Everything. Last year, Cleveland’s offense was towards the bottom in every statistical category. Despite the young pieces with running backs Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson, tight end Harold Fannin Jr and a reliable veteran wide receiver, Jerry Jeudy, it didn’t have much success overall. The offensive line was older and less effective, and the quarterback play was below average. Berry spent the entire offseason rebuilding this offense. Fired head coach Kevin Stefanski; hired Todd Monken Traded for right tackle Tytus Howard, signed left guard Zion Johnson, center/guard Elgton Jenkins, drafted rookie left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber Drafted rookie wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston It was a lot of work, but Berry did what was necessary to improve one of the worst offenses in the league last season. Comparing the numbers from last year’s offense at the bye week to this year’s offense, you can see a stark difference, even if it still ranks in the bottom half of the league: Browns Offense pre-bye (last season) 31st in offensive EPA per play 32nd in offensive success rate 32nd in Dropback EPA/per play 13th in Offensive Rush EPA per play 32nd in Dropback Success Rate 31st in Rush success rate Browns offense pre-bye (2026 season) 23rd in EPA per play 23rd in Offensive Success Rate 22nd in Dropback EPA/per play 27th in Rush EPA/per play 20th in Dropback Success Rate 21st in total offense 23rd in Rush Success Rate Having better offensive personnel has something to do with the numbers looking better, but it is a night-and-day difference from last season. The one thing that the team lacked last season was generating explosive plays in the passing game, rookies Concepcion and Boston have changed that. Fannin has also been a part of a somewhat revitalized passing game, giving Cleveland something with those three in the skill position room. The one thing that the team has lacked for years is competent quarterback play. Going into the season, the Browns quarterback room was considered a major weakness. Granted, it still is because there is no long-term solution on the roster, but the room has some form of stability from an unlikely individual. Going back to the offseason, many believed that second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders would be the starter for the entire season. However, quarterback Deshaun Watson took the job despite his tenure in Cleveland not being what he envisioned. Many believed that Watson was done after how he lashed out at the fanbase after the second preseason game in which he was booed. Fast forward to now, Watson is playing better than he did in 2024. Head coach Todd Monken has something to do with that: #Browns HC Todd Monken on how Deshaun Watson has turned things around from the Bills preseason game where he called out fans who booed him: "When we met after that, it really wasn't about his physical traits; it was really where you are mentally and emotionally…'Did you get… pic.twitter.com/aAhPQt54Kh — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) November 16, 2026 Monken had an honest conversation with Watson, and it appears to have benefited the quarterback, and his play looks different than before. Playing with more confidence, better pocket presence, utilizing his legs, and showing signs of how he looked in Houston. Granted, Watson hasn’t been perfect, but the Browns have lacked competent QB play last year, and Watson is giving the team that now. In terms of the offensive line, the unit has been better than expected. Fano has been sensational. The same can be said for Barber. Johnson, whom Cleveland paid in free agency, has been better than people give him credit for. Jenkins and Howard have been the subject of criticism (unfair at times), but they are providing stability at their respective positions. What needs to improve? Two things come to mind: The running game hasn’t materialized this season. At times, it feels as if the running game is coming along until it reaches a roadblock. It could improve after the bye week or possibly next season. For the running game to work effectively, the offensive line has to be better, and the backs have to improve as well. Whether it’s opening up rushing lanes consistently or the running back having better vision, the running has to get better. The second thing is the slow starts, which have also been a common theme. It’s more of a recurring theme. The offense simply has to get out of the gate faster and not wait until the game is out of reach to start executing. Going no-huddle or tempo could be easy fixes, but the slow starts offensively have to stop. Grade Overall, the Browns offense has flaws, but this is a unit that is 10x better than last season. Competent QB play, quality talent at the skill positions, a competent offensive line, and a good offensive coordinator are all Cleveland needed. The QB position isn’t solved long-term, but overall this unit is competent and has made massive improvements from last year. Grade: C-, maybe a C How would you grade the Browns offense going into their bye week? Join the conversation! title: Cleveland Browns news: Been waiting 5 years for Sunday night!
summary: The NFL has decided that it is time for the rest of the country to experience the particular brand of football currently being played by the Cleveland Browns. On Tuesday, the league announced it was flexing Cleveland’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders on November 29 into the Sunday night primetime slot. The game will […]
full_text: (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The NFL has decided that it is time for the rest of the country to experience the particular brand of football currently being played by the Cleveland Browns. On Tuesday, the league announced it was flexing Cleveland’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders on November 29 into the Sunday night primetime slot. The game will mark the first time the Browns have been on Sunday Night Football in the regular season since Week 12 of the 2021 season, when they lost to the Baltimore Ravens. While no Sunday time slot has been particularly beneficial to the Browns in recent years, the primetime one has been especially thorny, as Cleveland is 2-11 all-time when playing on Sunday night. Although we would be remiss not to point out that the playoff beatdown of the Pittsburgh Steelers in January 2021 took place on a Sunday night. We will have plenty more about Cleveland’s history on Sunday night, as well as their history with the Raiders and much more about this year’s game in the days to come. title: Browns roster adds DLine help; once again, waive recent draft pick and injured DT
summary: Despite being on their bye week, not everything is rest for the Cleveland Browns. Not only do fans need to change their plans for the Browns next game, which has been flexed to Sunday Night Football for Week 12 against the Las Vegas Raiders, but GM Andrew Berry rarely takes a week off from making […]
full_text: Despite being on their bye week , not everything is rest for the Cleveland Browns. Not only do fans need to change their plans for the Browns next game, which has been flexed to Sunday Night Football for Week 12 against the Las Vegas Raiders , but GM Andrew Berry rarely takes a week off from making changes to the roster. On Tuesday, Berry made three moves with Cleveland’s roster: Claimed DE Jamree Kromah off waivers from the Miami Dolphins Once again waived TE Carsen Ryan off the 53-man roster Waived DT Elijah Chatman off the injured reserve list Despite being on and off the active roster, Ryan has played in nine of the Browns 10 games this season, with 126 of his 129 snaps coming on special teams. Kromah is in his first season in the NFL after going undrafted out of James Madison. He played two games for the Chicago Bears and two with the Dolphins before being waived this week. His NFL draft profile was as follows: Kromah posted impressive impact production in 2023 after playing a bigger role than he had in the previous four seasons between Rutgers and James Madison. He’s muscular with very long arms and might have the frame for additional weight to bump inside. Kromah features jarring pop in his hands but might lack enough fluidity and athleticism to capitalize on it as a pro. He’s an effort rusher who is unlikely to create enough consistent pressure to warrant rush-down snaps, but he does have a shot at making the back end of a roster as a base end or future 3-technique. Chatman’s move was reported by Cleveland’s radio announcer, Andrew Siciliano: Browns waive DT Elijah Chatman from injured reserve. — Andrew Siciliano (@AndrewSiciliano) November 17, 2026 In two years in the NFL, Chatman played 22 games for the New York Giants before landing on the Browns roster this offseason.

title: Cowboys have the perfect chance to bounce back against Tennessee
summary: The Cowboys dropped to 4-6 after a wild 46-40 loss to San Francisco, but Sunday brings a much more favorable matchup. Tennessee comes to Dallas at 1-8, having lost its last three games and allowed 40-plus points in consecutive weeks. The defense struggled badly against San Francisco, forcing a desperate comeback that fell short. Dak […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys dropped to 4-6 after a wild 46-40 loss to San Francisco, but Sunday brings a much more favorable matchup. Tennessee comes to Dallas at 1-8, having lost its last three games and allowed 40-plus points in consecutive weeks. The defense struggled badly against San Francisco, forcing a desperate comeback that fell short. Dak Prescott now has 2,724 yards and 21 touchdown passes this season. Tennessee has allowed 43 points to Cincinnati and 40 to Jacksonville in its last two games. This looks like another opportunity for Prescott and the offense to score heavily, especially after what George Pickens did against the 49ers. Pickens returned against San Francisco and immediately produced his best game of the season. He caught three touchdowns and finished with 145 receiving yards. Now Tennessee has to deal with Pickens alongside CeeDee Lamb, who already has 976 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. The Titans simply don’t have one receiver they can concentrate on stopping. The numbers between these two team’s offenses aren’t close. Dallas averages 28 points per game, fifth in the NFL. Tennessee averages only 18, ranking 28th. The Cowboys also average 368 yards per game compared with Tennessee’s 278. If Dallas gets into the high 20s or 30s again, Tennessee may struggle to keep pace. This is where having both Lamb and Pickens, along with players like Ryan Flournoy will come into play. Perhaps the most interesting statistic is time of possession. The Titans average only 25:12 with the football, worst in the NFL. That gives Dallas exactly what it needs after watching San Francisco control huge parts of Sunday’s game. Get Tennessee off the field and give Prescott, Lamb and Pickens as many possessions as possible. Tennessee has some serious injury issues and placed starting guard Peter Skoronski on injured reserve because of a hamstring injury. Linebackers Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton are dealing with injury, and wide receiver Carnell Tate has a big question mark on whether he’ll suit up this Sunday. Wan’Dale Robinson is going on injured reserve. The offensive line injuries should interest a Dallas pass rush that finally produced some numbers against San Francisco. They recorded five sacks against Brock Purdy, including four in the first half. Cam Ward is a talented young quarterback, but Dallas needs to make him uncomfortable behind a weakened offensive line. Tennessee’s rookie quarterback can be pressured into mistakes Ward has shown improvement, but he is still learning. Through nine games he has thrown eight touchdowns and six interceptions with an 80.7 passer rating. He threw another interception against Jacksonville on Sunday. Then there’s the past between these two teams. The Cowboys won the last time these teams met when they travelled to Tennessee in December 2022, coming away with a 27-13 victory. Now the Titans have to travel to AT&T Stadium while carrying one of the worst records in football and knowing they’ve lost four out of the last six meetings between these two teams.

title: Where does the Cowboys defense go from here?
summary: Coming into this season, the world had moderately low expectations for a Dallas Cowboys defense in the middle of a rebuild, paired with a first-time defensive coordinator. Given the offseason moves and what we saw in Oxnard, there was no reason things shouldn’t have at least been a little bit better than last season. If […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Coming into this season, the world had moderately low expectations for a Dallas Cowboys defense in the middle of a rebuild, paired with a first-time defensive coordinator. Given the offseason moves and what we saw in Oxnard, there was no reason things shouldn’t have at least been a little bit better than last season. If nothing else, it couldn’t possibly be worse for a defense that would have ranked 40th in 2025 if there were 40 NFL teams. Then 2026 hit us like a ton of bricks. The numbers The first-year Christian Parker defense ranks last in nearly every metric across the league. Dallas ranks last or near last in total yards allowed per game, rush yards per game, third-down conversion rate allowed, while also failing to contain explosive plays week after week. Despite possessing a top five scoring offense in the NFL, the Cowboys are just 4-6. While the offense isn’t without flaws of their own, the clearest reason for most losses comes down to a historically bad defensive performance. The Cowboys are once again on track to set all the wrong defensive records just one season after setting all the wrong defensive records. What’s going wrong This failure isn’t just a one year collapse. It’s the continuation of a multi-year slide that began after their peak during the Dan Quinn years where Dallas had a top five ranked defense in 2022 and 2023. Dallas has gone through defensive coordinators each year after the Quinn departure with Mike Zimmer, Matt Eberflus, and now Christian Parker. The front office spent the last year and a half spending draft capital, making big trades, and signing free agents to fix that side of the ball, yet the returns on investment are yet to be discovered. Parker, 34 and in his first defensive coordinator job is struggling to install a functional unit that won’t break down in tackling, communication, and scheme execution. While the pass rush has gotten significantly better since adding Mike Pettine to the staff, who is now taking over as the defensive play caller , the defense as a whole still suffers from an inability to execute the most basic functions of sound defense. The defensive line, including the edge group, plays undisciplined football. Setting the edge and staying disciplined seems to be something that the ends just simply aren’t interested in, as displayed by the Deebo Samuel reverse play against the 49ers. Quinnen Williams is the lone, consistent bright spot up front for the Cowboys. The secondary has been uneven with rookie Caleb Downs and Joey Porter Jr. playing the best amongst the group. Downs has hit some rookie bumps, as to be expected, but he’ll clearly be a good player in the NFL. Porter Jr. is a difference maker, consistently shutting down the short side of the field. But the gap between those two players and the rest of the secondary is too great to overcome. The floor of the players on the Cowboys defense appears to be too low and the first-year defensive coordinator has not done enough to raise it. They’ll play multiple quarters of, at worst, acceptable football. And then out of nowhere, the dam breaks thanks to a simple screen, blown coverage, or big run play. Dallas has simply been unable to put an end to this cycle week after week and it’s costing them games. Where it goes from here In the short term, there is no easy fix. The foundations have been laid and Dallas now turns the defensive play-calling duties to Mike Pettine in hopes of better gameday results. Dallas was heavily focused on improving the football intelligence and ability of the players on the defense, but are now looking to simplify the calls according to Brian Schottenheimer. With that in mind, there is still a more than small chance for the Cowboys to make the playoffs in 2026. The Giants schedule is hitting their tough stretch, while the Cowboys have a couple of easy games ahead. That may not mean much, however, as we’ve seen the Cowboys lose to bad teams like the Buccaneers and Cardinals, so they can lose to anybody. If the defense can clean up the most fundamental issues such as tackling and lane discipline, this team may stand a chance at winning the NFC East. If not, we’ll continue to witness struggles against even the worst teams in the league. For 2027 and beyond, the Cowboys find themselves in a tough situation to navigate. Salary cap restructures or cuts with DaRon Bland, Kenny Clark, Rashan Gary and others are looming. The biggest decision of the offseason may come down to Joey Porter Jr. versus George Pickens and who gets a new deal. Losing either player significantly hurts the ability on their respective side of the ball. Dallas will also have to make decisions on their coaching staff from the head coach down. The entire picture is muddy as the defensive rebuild continues, maybe even requiring another step back to properly build it out moving forward. Dallas spent significant resources in the middle of 2025 and in 2026 trying to remake the defense into a respectable unit this season. Unfortunately, the results have not matched the investment. With time running out of the season, the next several weeks will determine what happens with this coaching staff and how much rope the front office will allow them to course correct this year and beyond.

full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The shoe has dropped. After speculation ran rampant on Monday afternoon in the aftermath of words from Brian Schottenheimer and Jerry Jones it is now official: The Dallas Cowboys are stripping defensive coordinator Christian Parker from play-calling duties. Christian Parker will remain as Cowboys defensive coordinator but Mike Pettine, the senior defensive assistant, will call the defense on gamedays, sources tell me and @ByKimberleyA — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) November 18, 2026 It goes without saying that this is a rather seismic decision. Parker is in his first season with the Cowboys, obviously his first as their defensive coordinator, and it is his first season ever calling plays in general. Revoking that puts his future in doubt for the Cowboys, but that is obviously a discussion for another day. ESPN’s Todd Archer noted in his report of the news that Mike Pettine, senior defensive assistant, is set to call plays moving forward. This makes sense in the vacuum of the moment, but considering that Pettine joined the Cowboys only a month ago (after the Buccaneers loss and before the Packers game) it isn’t exactly the most organized operation at the moment. What do you think? Was this the right decision? Was it the least awful one? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Cowboys Week 11 opponent: A look at the 2026 Tennessee Titans
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are coming off one of the ugliest defensive performances in franchise history, but they’ll have an opportunity to get back on track against a Tennessee Titans team that is still searching for answers. Tennessee enters Week 11 at 1-8, sitting at the bottom of the AFC South and holding the No. 1 […]
full_text: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are coming off one of the ugliest defensive performances in franchise history, but they’ll have an opportunity to get back on track against a Tennessee Titans team that is still searching for answers. Tennessee enters Week 11 at 1-8, sitting at the bottom of the AFC South and holding the No. 1 spot in the projected 2027 NFL Draft order. The Titans are clearly in rebuilding mode under head coach Robert Saleh. They’ve struggled to put together consistent performances on either side of the ball, and their recent decision to trade defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker is another indication that the organization is looking toward the future. Still, this isn’t necessarily a game Dallas can sleepwalk through. Rookie quarterback Cam Ward has shown improvement, Tony Pollard remains a productive running back, and Tennessee’s defense has been surprisingly opportunistic when it comes to taking the football away. The Cowboys are 4-6 and desperately need a win, but after allowing 46 points to San Francisco, there are plenty of reasons to approach this matchup with caution. Cam Ward is showing signs of progress The Titans’ season hasn’t gone according to plan, but there are reasons for optimism surrounding rookie quarterback Cam Ward. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has experienced the growing pains that come with playing quarterback for a rebuilding team, but he’s starting to show why Tennessee invested so heavily in him. Through nine games, Ward has completed 63.8% of his passes for 1,714 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions. His 80.7 passer rating isn’t impressive, but he’s shown flashes of the arm talent and athleticism that made him the top selection. Ward’s most recent performance against Jacksonville was encouraging despite the 40-23 loss. He completed 28 of 39 passes for 231 yards and two touchdowns, while also throwing an interception. He directed five scoring drives and connected with running back Tony Pollard for a touchdown that kept Tennessee within striking distance. Ward has also contributed 151 rushing yards and two touchdowns this season. His mobility gives the Titans another option when plays break down, and Dallas has struggled to contain mobile quarterbacks and prevent explosive plays. There is still plenty of room for improvement. Ward has been sacked 14 times, and his six interceptions demonstrate that he can be vulnerable when forced to make difficult throws. Against Jacksonville, he threw an interception on a pass across his body, a decision that immediately put his defense in a difficult position. The Cowboys need to make him uncomfortable without allowing him to escape the pocket. After giving Brock Purdy and the 49ers far too much room to operate, Dallas needs a much more disciplined performance from its pass rush and secondary. Easy pass from Cam Ward to Daniel Bellinger for six JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/W4Lw36MZeM — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 An offense searching for consistency, with contributions from multiple players Tennessee’s offense has struggled to find its identity this season. The Titans are averaging just 18.6 points and 278.6 total yards per game, ranking 28th and 29th in the NFL, respectively. Their inability to sustain drives has been a major reason for their struggles. However, there are a few players Dallas needs to account for. Tony Pollard remains the focal point of the rushing attack. The former Cowboy has rushed for 628 yards and six touchdowns on 142 carries, averaging 4.4 yards per attempt. He’s also contributed 136 receiving yards and a touchdown, giving Ward a reliable option out of the backfield. Tony Pollard slips tackles for a 32-yard score! JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FPR0vlha2W — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Pollard is coming off a relatively quiet rushing performance against Jacksonville, finishing with just 33 yards on nine carries. However, he made an impact as a receiver, catching eight passes for 66 yards and a touchdown. The receiving corps is a collection of players who have contributed in different ways. Rookie Carnell Tate leads Tennessee with 413 receiving yards on 34 receptions, while Elic Ayomanor has added 290 yards and is averaging 16.1 yards per catch. Wan’Dale Robinson has caught 38 passes for 272 yards and three touchdowns, but he is going on injured reserve. Chimere Dike has contributed 140 receiving yards and a touchdown, while tight end Gunnar Helm has added 183 yards on 21 receptions. The Titans aren’t particularly explosive as a team, but they spread the ball around and have enough players capable of making plays to punish a defense that loses track of its assignments. The Titans defense can create turnovers, but gives up plenty of yards Tennessee’s defense has been one of the more inconsistent units in the league. The Titans are allowing 26.6 points per game and have surrendered approximately 391 total yards per contest, making it difficult for the offense to overcome the defense’s struggles, like the Cowboys. Their secondary has struggled. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per game, the most in the NFL. That’s an inviting matchup for Dak Prescott and a Dallas passing offense that has averaged 368.3 total yards per game. There is one major caveat, however: Tennessee knows how to take the football away. The Titans have recorded nine interceptions through nine games, tied for fifth in the league. They also have 21 sacks, putting them in the middle of the pack in that category. Defensive end Jacob Martin leads the team with 7.5 sacks, giving Tennessee a legitimate pass-rush threat. Linebacker Cedric Gray has also shown playmaking ability. With injuries affecting the Titans’ linebacker group, Gray stepped into a larger role against Jacksonville and recorded nine tackles and an interception. He has an opportunity to become an important part of the defense as the season progresses. Cedric Gray was the best player on the #Titans defense against the Jaguars, and he should play every defensive the rest of this season He's still an explosive downhill run fitter, high-end athlete with sideline-to-sideline range and sound in coverage. Communication shortcomings… pic.twitter.com/HtCazRJTlv — Drew Beatty (@IronCityFilm) November 16, 2026 The Titans’ recent performance against Jacksonville was a good example of the unit’s highs and lows. Tennessee intercepted Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter, but still surrendered 40 points and 459 yards. The Jaguars converted seven of 14 third-down opportunities, repeatedly extending drives and keeping the Titans’ defense on the field. For Dallas, the formula should be straightforward. Protect Prescott, take advantage of Tennessee’s vulnerable secondary and avoid giving the Titans opportunities to create turnovers. The Cowboys have the personnel to exploit this defense, but they cannot afford to become careless with the football. Can Dallas bounce back? On paper, this is a favorable matchup for the Cowboys. Tennessee is 1-8, ranks near the bottom of the league in both scoring and total offense, and has struggled to stop opposing passing attacks. Dallas, meanwhile, has one of the more productive offenses in the NFL, averaging 28.6 points and 368.3 yards per game. But the Cowboys have bigger problems than their opponent’s record can solve. The defense is coming off a game in which it surrendered 46 points, 584 yards and three touchdowns of at least 60 yards. Christian Parker’s unit has struggled to tackle, communicate and prevent explosive plays. Those problems won’t disappear simply because the opponent is Tennessee. Ward has shown enough improvement to take advantage if Dallas continues to make the same mistakes. Pollard is familiar with the Cowboys and can contribute as both a runner and receiver, while Tennessee has enough receiving options to test a secondary that desperately…

summary: The Dallas Cowboys were historically bad on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. Just when you think the bar can’t get any lower, the defense gives up 584 yards of offense—the most allowed at home in franchise history. That has raised questions about Christian Parker and his future with the team. Jerry Jones: Cowboys ‘talking […]
full_text: Tom Fox/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys were historically bad on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. Just when you think the bar can’t get any lower, the defense gives up 584 yards of offense—the most allowed at home in franchise history. That has raised questions about Christian Parker and his future with the team. Jerry Jones: Cowboys ‘talking about’ adjustment to Christian Parker’s role – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Does Jerry Jones foresee a change at defensive coordinator for the rest of the season? “We’re talking about that, but I’m not going to talk about it here,” Jones said. “But we are talking about those things.” Jones did not specify what a change could look like, but said that it would impact the coming week as the Cowboys prepare to host the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. “I think it would impact this week, but it certainly would be looking to the rest of the season at least,” Jones said. “And if anything, we did. And we shouldn’t do anything out here that doesn’t give us the best chance against the Titans. And that’d cover a lot of the future as well.” Cowboys Part Ways with 2nd Year Offensive Lineman, Sign Former Buccaneers Guard – Daniel Arwas, Heavy on Cowboys The Cowboys’ track record at developing mid-round offensive linemen takes another hit. “The Cowboys have waived OL Ajani Cornelius and signed OL Nick Leverett to the active roster from the practice squad.” DallasCowboys.com’s Tommy Yarish reported on Nov. 17. The roster move represents one of the cleaner one-for-one personnel swaps possible, with it very much being one versatile guard-primary offensive lineman in at the expense of another. Since being drafted out of Oregon back in April 2025, Cornelius has only participated on special teams and has yet to record a single snap on offense. Brian Schottenheimer, Cowboys ‘taking a deep dive, looking at everything’ on defense – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com It sounded like Brian Schottenheimer was still processing what he saw from his defense on Sunday. “I think we got beat pretty good in some man-to-man stuff last night,” Schottenheimer said. “The missed tackles is really what got us. We got to lower our target, we got to wrap up a little bit better, we’ve got to gang tackle a little bit better. Definitely some plays it should’ve been maybe 12, 14, 18-yard plays, and they ended up going for more than that. But in terms of simplifying, that’s definitely a potential solution that we’re talking about.” Despite exploring that as an avenue to switch things up defensively, Schottenheimer affirmed that he thinks his players believe in what they’re being coached to do. title: Cowboys rookie report: LT Overton makes an impact against San Francisco
summary: Forty points still wasn’t enough. Dallas lost 46–40 to San Francisco, with defensive breakdowns undoing another productive afternoon from the offense. For the rookies, LT Overton supplied a bright spot, Caleb Downs endured a difficult follow-up to his Indianapolis performance, and Jaishawn Barham received more playing time. But here is how each rookie fared this […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Forty points still wasn’t enough. Dallas lost 46–40 to San Francisco, with defensive breakdowns undoing another productive afternoon from the offense. For the rookies, LT Overton supplied a bright spot, Caleb Downs endured a difficult follow-up to his Indianapolis performance, and Jaishawn Barham received more playing time. But here is how each rookie fared this week, listed in draft order, and any undrafted players worth noting after that. Caleb Downs (65 defensive snaps| 10 tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended) Downs stayed involved throughout, but his tackle total disguises a difficult afternoon. His most costly moment came when Kaelon Black ran through his attempted tackle on a 25-yard touchdown. He also struggled to contain George Kittle in coverage. The effort and involvement were there, but Dallas needed cleaner tackling and fewer gains allowed from its first-round defensive back. Jaishawn Barham (21 defensive snaps, 20 special teams | 0 defensive tackles, 2 special-teams tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 QB hits ) Barham’s defensive workload increased considerably from his three snaps against Indianapolis, but the extra opportunity brought little recorded production. His two tackles came on special teams. He did break up a third-quarter pass intended for Deebo Samuel, although an accepted Dallas offside penalty erased the play. That was an encouraging moment, but he otherwise struggled to make his increased involvement count. Drew Shelton (5 offensive snaps) Shelton participated on special teams but received no offensive snaps. There was no pass-protection or run-blocking performance to evaluate this week. LT Overton (5 defensive, 26 special teams | 1 defensive tackle, 2 special-teams tackles | 1 TFL | 1 sack | 0 INT | 1 pass defended | 1 QB hit ) Overton made his limited defensive opportunities count. He brought down Brock Purdy for a three-yard sack late in the first half and added a pass defended. With just five defensive snaps, that was an impressive return, while two tackles showed his involvement on special teams. The sample was small, but his individual production gives Dallas a reason to consider more defensive work for him. Camden Brown (18 total snaps | 0 targets | 0 receptions | 0 receiving TD | 4 kickoff returns, 93 yards) Brown’s main contribution again came on kickoff returns, where he averaged 23 yards without breaking a long return. His six offensive snaps brought no targets. He also “recovered” a teammate’s fumble during the desperate final lateral play before subsequently “fumbling” himself, with Dallas retaining possession. It was another afternoon dominated by special-teams work rather than receiving opportunities.

title: Inside the Cowboys historic defensive collapse against the 49ers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost a game to the San Francisco 49ers. That’s not a shocker to anyone, as this Cowboys team has struggled all season, and the 49ers are the best team they’ve played so far, and by a good margin. Looking at their opponents, San Francisco is the only offense the Cowboys have faced […]
full_text: Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys lost a game to the San Francisco 49ers. That’s not a shocker to anyone, as this Cowboys team has struggled all season, and the 49ers are the best team they’ve played so far, and by a good margin. Looking at their opponents, San Francisco is the only offense the Cowboys have faced this year that is ranked in the top eight in scoring, now averaging over 31 points a game. In fact, the Cowboys haven’t fared well against offenses that average over 22 points a game. They’ve played five teams that average more than 22 points/game. Their record against those teams is 1-4. They’ve played five teams that average fewer than 22 points/game. Their record against those teams is 3-2. Clearly, playing decent offenses is not ideal for this Cowboys defense, so when they faced the NFC’s highest-scoring offense, it was a huge problem for a unit that has struggled immensely all season. Even so, it shouldn’t have been that bad. The defense gave up 584 total yards on the day. It was the most yards they have ever given up at home during their 67-year existence. The most ever is never good. The frustrating part about this game is that when you take a closer look, it’s easy to tell that the Cowboys never had a shot. The defense was just outmatched. It was like playing one of those games where you play against an older sibling, where they might toy around with you for a bit, only to flatten you when it’s time to get serious. The 49ers did that to the Cowboys’ defense. That doesn’t mean they were playing opossum at any point during the game. It’s just that whenever the 49ers found themselves in a crunch, they always had a go-to play where they knew they could take advantage of the Cowboys’ vulnerabilities. The Cowboys had several defensive breakdowns in the game, with multiple third-down letdowns and explosive plays. One of the most embarrassing plays came on the Deebo Samuel reverse play in the third quarter. When fullback Kyle Juszczyk went in motion, the entire defense was lured into a trance. Follow the Juice because that’s where the action goes most of the time. Only this time, the Juice wasn’t worth the squeeze. Sadly, the entire defense took the bait. It was crazy to see how many defenders continued chasing running back Kaelon Black. That left an entourage of blockers out in front of Samuel, leaving very little chance for the Cowboys to make a stop. Malik Hooker and Shemar James were the first to figure it out, but they were so far out of position that by the time they caught up, they were left gambling and taking poor angles. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was the last hope. He’s not the greatest tackler as it is, but he’s even worse when he’s washed out by multiple blockers. This one play shows how awful the Cowboys' defense is. Juszczyk goes in motion, trap set. Nobody recognizes Deebo swinging around. Defenders run themselves out of the play without a clue. Blockers heavily outnumber tacklers, and tacklers take terrible angles. Just pathetic. pic.twitter.com/qYISpQggww — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 16, 2026 In our game preview article , we mentioned that “Shanahanigans” would be an issue due to the Cowboys’ over-pursuing nature, and right on cue, they obliged. It was one of the poorest-defended reverse plays we’ve seen. Mental lapses are common for this defense, but more frustrating is when their effort is so lackadaisical. The touchdown run by the rookie Black was horrible for different reasons. It starts with Juice looping around with banana motion. He and wide receiver Jordan Watkins take on the outside defenders, leaving a nice hole for Black to run through. With no defenders to impede his path, Black gets a full head of steam and commits some terrible Big 10 rookie-on-rookie crime by running over Caleb Downs. Yes, that’s the Cowboys’ top draft pick being leveled, but in fairness to Downs, he squared up well. It’s just hard to defy physics when the running back comes plowing through with that much force. The rest of the Cowboys’ defense is sealed off from clever run-blocking that creeps to the second level. Cornerback Cobie Durant has one final chance to bring him down, but he gets run over like he’s not even there. It wouldn’t be a Cowboys game without a humiliating run-stop attempt against a team’s backup running back. This play is even more embarrassing. Juszczyk with the banana motion. He and Watkins take on the outside. Interior defenders are completely sealed off. Kaelon Black hits the hole and levels Caleb Downs. And he runs through Cobie Durant just for fun. Pathetic. pic.twitter.com/cDeJczzuIz — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 16, 2026 Getting their playmakers in space was the name of the game for the 49ers, and they did it often. They just meandered off to one side, got the defense to cha-cha-cha in that direction, and then boom, sealed off! On the quick pass to Samuel, the Cowboys’ defense was so out of position that their lone, helpless cornerback wasn’t even able to get a hand on him. When you go against a defense that lacks discipline, it's easy to find plays that work. All the skill players run to the left, the defense bites. Deebo has a convoy of blockers with only DaRon Bland to deal with. Bland is erased, Deebo waltzes in untouched. It's that easy. pic.twitter.com/5HUexZEuj9 — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 16, 2026 And then there were the two long touchdown passes to Christian McCaffrey. To be fair, McCaffrey is a handful all of the time, so game planning for him isn’t easy. The first touchdown catch was especially hard because the defense actually played well for 90% of the play. It was just hanging on for that last 10% that got them in trouble. McCaffrey was a sneaky sneakerton and, at the last second, leaked out into the secondary, and as soon as Brock Purdy saw that, it was over. The second touchdown was a harder pill to swallow for a couple of reasons. First, it essentially iced the game. Any hopes of a comeback were crushed. Second, in the defense’s biggest moment, they were once again escorted out of the play. It was a simple play for the 49ers, with all their receivers basically running away from where McCaffrey was, taking the defense with them. It was like Moses parting the Red Sea, only Kyle Shanahan was holding the staff, and it was the Cowboys’ defense that opened up for the easiest pitch-and-catch you’ll ever see. The first big touchdown to Christian McCaffrey was difficult to defend because Brock Purdy scrambled and extended the play. The second one, the Cowboys sold out with a blitz, and the 49ers schemed the defense completely out of the play. It was like shooting fish in a barrel. pic.twitter.com/jpgNn4AbcI — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 16, 2026 The Cowboys’ defense has been a problem all season, and the 49ers exploited every element of it. The same things keep happening, and they aren’t showing any sign of improvement. And it’s not going to get any easier with four of their final five games against offenses averaging over 22 points a game. This defense has fallen into troubling times with very little chance of escape.

title: 2026 NFL Week 11: Dallas Cowboys vs. Tennessee Titans
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are still in the mix. Laugh if you will (or maybe need to given the state of things), but the NFC East is within reach for the Cowboys despite their 4-6 record. You do reach a point though, where if you keep losing, that is no longer the case which means the […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are still in the mix. Laugh if you will (or maybe need to given the state of things), but the NFC East is within reach for the Cowboys despite their 4-6 record. You do reach a point though, where if you keep losing, that is no longer the case which means the Cowboys have to get things together this week against the Tennessee Titans. Sunday’s game and Thanksgiving Day right after offer an opportunity for the Cowboys. They are 4-6, can win this pair of games, and sit at .500 on Thanksgiving night with pecan (or pumpkin) pie and hope for luck around them. That wouldn’t guarantee anything, but it would certainly be a start. Tennessee has been down this season, but that sort of qualifier has not stopped other squads from taking care of Dallas this year. This game also will see Dallas taking on a former player of theirs in Tony Pollard, and you can just see him breaking off a 60-yard touchdown if you close your eyes. It will also bring one of last year’s players in Solomon Thomas, plus staffer Aaron Whitecotton, to town. Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Quinnen Williams, and Caleb Downs all have a lot to do to take the first step. If anyone has anything to do it is notably Brian Schottenheimer and Christian Parker. We will see what the game brings. title: 2026 NFL Week 11 Power Rankings: Cowboys drift towards irrelevancy
summary: Another week, another Dallas Cowboys loss. Things have been tough sledding for America’s Team as of late and as such the rest of the world is (rightfully) recognizing them to be as a Team You Cannot Believe In. We know this because of where the Cowboys continue to sit in power rankings across the internet. […]
full_text: Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Another week, another Dallas Cowboys loss. Things have been tough sledding for America’s Team as of late and as such the rest of the world is (rightfully) recognizing them to be as a Team You Cannot Believe In. We know this because of where the Cowboys continue to sit in power rankings across the internet. Early in the season there was some optimism, but as we approach Thanksgiving and sit on the heels of a shellacking from the San Francisco 49ers, reality must be faced. Let’s get to it. 1. Buffalo Bills (LW: 1) They are a consistently good team. It must be nice. 2. San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) Daddy made the kids eat the vegetables on Sunday. 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 3) Trevor Lawrence must be so grateful for Liam Cohen. If only. 4. Detroit Lions (LW: 5) The Aidan Hutchinson injury was brutal. It is hard to see how the Lions can withstand the NFC North race down one of their best players. 5. Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 7) Is this Joe Burrow’s season to win MVP? 6. Chicago Bears (LW: 6) Caleb Williams missed time, but he has the post-bye part of the season to make his own case. 7. Minnesota Vikings (LW: 13) Kirk Cousins is back and everything feels right again here. They are such an interesting team and situation. 8. Denver Broncos (LW: 8) Welcome back as well. 9. Green Bay Packers (LW: 4) It is hard to see how they could be the team in the division when they got wrecked by the Cousins-led Vikings in his return. 10. Seattle Seahawks (LW: 10) They are finding a way. That special teams play was incredible. 11. Los Angeles Rams (LW: 12) Another team who is making lemonade. 12. Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 14) It is hard to figure out what their ceiling is. But they are in the mix as always. 13. Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 11) Sunday night was a sobering loss. There is such a gap between them and the now divison-leading Bengals. 14. Cleveland Browns (LW: 20) This is one of the more unexpected parts of this season. Who would have thought? Cleveland! 15. New England Patriots (LW: 9) Part of the ranking here is that they are going to be without Drake Maye for a bit. They seem a little snakebitten. 16. New York Giants (LW: 15) For my money this is still the future NFC East winner. 17. Houston Texans (LW: 16) They had it on Sunday. I don’t know what the issue is. They are wasting such a great season from their quarterback. 18. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 17) Welcome back as well. 19. Carolina Panthers (LW: 23) They lead the NFC South, but I can’t imagine for how long. 20. Atlanta Falcons (LW: 18) Although I don’t think this team is a threat. 21. Dallas Cowboys (LW: 19) This team isn’t threatening anybody. 22. Washington Commanders (LW: 25) Don’t count Washington out of division talks, though. 23. Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 22) Fernando Mendoza looked decent in his debut. Time for him to figure out as much as he can so next season is when it all really starts. 24. Baltimore Ravens (LW: 21) It all feels like it is falling apart. 25. New Orleans Saints (LW: 24) Is Kellen Moore going to make it through this? 26. Indianapolis Colts (LW: 29) They won a game. Clearly the Cowboys beat a formidable group. 27. Arizona Cardinals (LW: 26) They have scored nine points in the two full games since playing the Cowboys and thriving in the second half and fourth quarter specifically. All field goals. No touchdowns. Unreal. Yet totally believable. 28. Miami Dolphins (LW: 27) They put up a bit of a fight at least. 29. Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 28) It is annoying how they are selling because they are good at this. 30. Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 32) A win! At long last! 31. New York Jets (LW: 30) Another lost year. 32. Tennessee Titans (LW: 31) How can anyone say with confidence that they won’t beat the Cowboys? ESPN : 20 (LW: 20) No movement. Non-QB MVP at midseason: DT Quinnen Williams Considering the porous nature of the Cowboys’ defense, it’s difficult to say a player on that unit deserves this honor, but that’s how well Williams has played. He leads the team with six sacks, the most for a Dallas defensive tackle in a season since 2017, and is second in QB pressures. Williams leads the NFL with 15 tackles for loss and is tied for fifth with three forced fumbles. He is doing everything he can to raise the level of play on defense. He just needs more help. — Todd Archer NFL.com : 18 (LW: 22) Know that I checked several times to make sure I wasn’t misreading. A rise of four spots. We knew the Cowboys’ defense couldn’t stop a nosebleed. We knew their offensive firepower represented their only chance of success. Dallas seemingly acknowledged this reality, too, with Sunday’s performance against San Francisco. This offense remains good enough (in most weeks) to keep the ‘Boys in the playoff hunt, but the defense won’t ever give them a real chance of winning anything significant without some changes. It just is what it is. USA Today : 22 (LW: 21) A slight dip. Christian McCaffrey > Christian Parker. But Dallas’ defensive breakdowns obviously go way beyond Sunday, when the Cowboys surrendered three TDs of at least 66 yards. Dallas has allowed at least one from 55 yards in each of its past three games. Yahoo : 22 (LW: 20) Further down we go. There’s not much more that can be said about the Cowboys’ defense. Even noted Cowboys fan Post Malone was absolutely fed up. After allowing 584 yards in a 46-40 loss to the 49ers, Brian Schottenheimer made perhaps his harshest comments on the team since becoming head coach. “I thought the second half was unacceptable,” Schottenheimer said, according to the team’s site. “Tackling was atrocious. We’re going to do a deep dive and see why.” It’s not like the Cowboys’ offense has been the 1999 Rams or anything: fifth in points scored, eighth in yards gained, fifth in EPA per play and sixth in DVOA. That still should be enough to win a poor division. The defense is ruining the Cowboys’ season, though DVOA still gives Dallas a 32.4% chance to win the NFC East. CBS Sports : 18 (LW: 18) Another hold. That defense is putrid right now. They bust coverages and the effort lacks at times. They just can’t stop anybody. The Athletic : 19 (LW: 17) Back down. Breakout player: Ryan Flournoy The third-year wide receiver, a sixth-round pick in 2024, has found a role even with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens getting most of the targets. Flournoy had six catches for 71 yards and a touchdown Sunday and is on the doorstep of a career year with seven games left. He has 38 receptions for 466 yards this season. ProFootballTalk : 24 (LW: 25) One last rise to close us out. It was a weird week with some teams needing to fall further down. The defense has gotten worse, not better.
