title: Broncos vs Raiders preview: Denver wants strong start post-bye week
summary: The Denver Broncos come out of the bye week on a five-game winning streak. They currently sit at 7-2, are in the hunt for the AFC West title and the top seed in the AFC. Even better is the week off should allow the Broncos to get players back from injury, especially on defense. All […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Courtland Sutton #14 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers with Bo Nix #10 during the first quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos come out of the bye week on a five-game winning streak. They currently sit at 7-2, are in the hunt for the AFC West title and the top seed in the AFC. Even better is the week off should allow the Broncos to get players back from injury, especially on defense. All of this to say Denver is in a great spot. Now come the hated Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The Broncos want to build on this great start to the season and carry the momentum over from the bye this Sunday against their rivals. Denver is a massive -10-point home favorite against the Raiders (4-6) at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the under at -115. Offensive Rankings Las Vegas : Tied for twenty-second in total offense (314.2 yards per game), 31st in rushing offense (70.7 YPG), 10th in passing offense (243.5 YPG), 10th in scoring offense (25.1 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (277.3 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (91.4 YPG), 25th in passing offense (185.9 YPG), 19th in scoring offense (22.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Las Vegas : Thirtieth in total defense (385.1 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (150.1 YPG), 23rd in passing defense (234.0 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (28.9 points per game). Denver : Twenty-seventh in total defense (355.0 yards per game), 24th in rushing defense (124.3 YPG), 20th in passing defense (230.7 YPG), ninth in scoring defense (20.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Sunday’s game. Just win, baby! (By starting fast offensively) The best way to put pressure on a rookie quarterback is to make the Las Vegas offense one-dimensional. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense can do their part by starting Sunday’s game fast offensively and finishing drives with touchdowns. We saw glimpses of this against the Carolina Panthers, with some deep shots early by Nix, but Denver had to kick a field goal on the opening drive. Replicate that this Sunday, but finish the opening drive with a touchdown. And then do it again. And then again. Add to the pressure that the Broncos defense will undoubtedly bring on the rookie QB. — Ian St. Clair Get after Fernando Mendoza Last week, Fernando Mendoza got his first career NFL start against a fierce Seattle Seahawks defense. Prior to Mendoza being a starter, the Raiders’ offensive line only allowed 11 sacks when Kirk Cousins was quarterback. Last Sunday, with the 2026 NFL Draft’s top pick under center, they gave up six to the Seahawks. If Denver wants to win the game, their defensive front seven has to dominate. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph needs to throw everything he can at the rookie signal caller and rattle him early and often. — Christopher Hart Keep feeding Jonah Coleman I don’t need to discuss numbers. Just look at how much better the offense is when Coleman gets his touches. Whether he’s running the ball or catching passes, he gives the offense a weapon that forces the defense to respect what Denver is doing in the trenches, thus opening up the opportunities for Bo Nix to push the ball downfield. — Adam Malnati Blow a team out for once I know, I know. It’s just not how this team is built. Every team gets a chance to beat the Broncos, but most of them fail to do so in the final minutes. Buuuuut, it would sure be nice to enjoy a good ol’ fashioned butt-whoopin’ type game — especially against the Raiders. — Tim Lynch Score more points than the Raiders The Broncos scored more points than the Panthers a few weeks ago and didn’t need to score any last week, because they were on a bye. Now, it’s Raiders week, and my key to the game is simple. Score more points than the Raiders. Denver is 7-0 when it does that and 0-2 when it does not. Using advanced analytics, I say the Broncos have a 100% chance to win on Sunday if they score more points than the Raiders. That is my key to the game! — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday’s game?

title: Midseason focus for Broncos is run blocking and 3rd-and-long coverage
summary: The Broncos have run the gauntlet of their schedule by and large at this point. Now, it is time for them to hone their game and improve in order to make a postseason run. I’m not taking anyone lightly, by the way. Every game is going to be hard coming down the stretch. Heck, even […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Alex Palczewski (63) of the Denver Broncos works out with Kage Casey (78) during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Broncos have run the gauntlet of their schedule by and large at this point. Now, it is time for them to hone their game and improve in order to make a postseason run. I’m not taking anyone lightly, by the way. Every game is going to be hard coming down the stretch. Heck, even the Los Angeles Chargers have found a way to win a game against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football . For the Broncos, my hope is that they spent some quality time during their bye week digging deep into the team’s inefficiencies: executing zone coverage on 3rd and long and run blocking. 3rd and long troubles One of the few nagging issues on the defensive side of the ball has been the number of longer 3rd downs they have given up conversions on. I’m not sure anything other than health is going to greatly improve this one. Getting Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones back will go quite a long way in this arena. The one thing that this issue points to in my mind is the lack of high-level talent behind our starters. No offense to any of the backup safeties or corners that have been playing. They have absolutely been giving it their all and doing an admirable job. That being said, the team has obviously been running a lot more zone schemes with the players playing off to minimize the damage down the field. The good thing about getting the depth players so many snaps is that it leads to teachable moments. They are going to be able to see in detail why they needed to move sooner, play closer, or react quicker. They will also get coached on how to read the routes being run to predict where they need to be at a higher level. Run blocking We’ve been pointing to their issues blocking all year long. It isn’t just one player, either. While we can all point to Ben Powers as the weakest link, the offense has had gaffes from every position group. If you want some excellent breakdowns on the woes of the run game, please check out Tyler Polumbus’ breakdowns . The first and most impactful change I think is possible is giving Alex Palczewski or Kage Casey (if he’s ready) the start at left guard. We need more steady blocking there, as it has been a weak point all season long, consistently. The next piece is just good old hard coaching about run blocking. I’ve seen wide receivers and tight ends blocking poorly. I’ve seen atrocious first steps from several linemen. It almost seems like the focus for the offense has largely been in the passing game. They need to up their game in getting their assignments blocked. The final piece to this is going to happen naturally when the team gets back Tyler Badie and RJ Harvey. Badie has been a phenomenal force as a blocker and has chipped in some good runs this season. Harvey returning adds a different challenge to defenses, especially the raw speed he brings to the table. I’m cautiously optimistic about the Broncos running game moving forward, if for no other reason than Sean Payton specifically mentioning it as a focus for improvement. Payton doesn’t spout nonsense about things like this. If he says it is a problem and a focus, it will be a focus until it improves. It is possible that it won’t improve without changes in players, but rest assured that will happen if that is what it takes. title: Should the Denver Broncos shake-up their starting offensive line?
summary: One of the things that has been irritating many of us this season has been specific areas of offensive line play. I have seen people call out poor performances by Mike McGlinchey and Luke Wattenberg, but the real problem fans seem to see along the offensive line has been from interior guard Ben Powers. Personally, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on against the Carolina Panthers during the first quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the things that has been irritating many of us this season has been specific areas of offensive line play. I have seen people call out poor performances by Mike McGlinchey and Luke Wattenberg, but the real problem fans seem to see along the offensive line has been from interior guard Ben Powers. Personally, I’ve seen him whiff on blocks and get turned around so frequently that I wonder if he is the primary reason Bo Nix has been quick to bail to his right as often as he does. It’s not much better in the run game either, which is a source of constant frustration when watching these games. Head Coach Sean Payton was asked about making changes to the offensive line and he seemed to downplay it a bit, but left the door open too. “I made sure to make a point about evaluating all assets of what we’re doing in our front in the offense,” Payton said on Monday. “So I want to make sure one story doesn’t lead to another. We’ll spend an inordinate amount of time looking at mid-season cutups where we’re at relative to scheme and personnel.” Frankly, I think they should make a change. If it gets a lot worse, then you can always change it back. I have nothing against Powers, but he has struggled and it is problematic for sustaining offensive drives. Making a change shouldn’t be so hard to do. And maybe there are other things I don’t see or cannot understand due to being on the outside looking in. If it’s not Powers, then its someone in there not doing a good enough job and a change is certainly warranted. What do you think: is Payton waiting too long to take action along the line? Broncos daily recap Broncos quarterbacks past and present, how does Bo Nix measure up? As Broncos fans, in our lifetime, we’ve had the absolute privilege of watching some of the best quarterbacks in football play for the Denver Broncos… and the frustration of having to watch the not-so-great struggle. Needless to say, Broncos fans know how to measure quarterback play, both good and bad, when they see it. All of the Bo Nix clips from ManningCast on MNF in Week 10 Peyton and Eli Manning brought in Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix for a visit on ManningCast last night as the Los Angeles Chargers notched their first win of the season against the Baltimore Ravens. NFL Power Rankings for Week 11: How did the Denver Broncos hold up over the bye? The Denver Broncos didn’t play last weekend, but a good chunk of prognosticators didn’t move them an inch up or or down in their weekly power rankings. Potent quotables Sean Payton On what changed with the anticipated trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley “Nothing changed. It was already stated. Everything was pretty clearly spelled out. I’m not going to get into the specifics. He’s a prospect we thought—and still do [think]—very highly of. It just didn’t work out and it’s not uncommon with trades. That’s kind of where it went, and I’ll leave it at that.” On his message to the team after the bye week and the areas of focus going forward “I think collectively, we just finished a team meeting talking about the improvement in certain areas where we feel like we’re going to have to be better at in this, call it, second half of the season. Specifically, I mentioned this last week, we need to block better on offense and we need to be in the right place. I thought we did an average job against Carolina, and I think that’s an area of focus relative to more consistency in our run game. Then there were some third-down, fourth-down-and-longs defensively that was an Achilles heel for us a year ago, and the other day became one. Those are just a few things.” On if there is a loophole in the trade process “I saw it all. There’s no loophole. It just is part of the trade process every step of the way.” On the inside linebacker depth and if there are opportunities for more players to get snaps “I don’t view it the same way you do. We’re going to play the starters and then guys that earn reps certainly will earn playing time. Yes, that’s all I could say to that.” On the process for handling travel issues with the nationwide flight stoppage “It’s not that complex. [Vice President of Player Development] Ray [Jackson] does a good job of just finding out who’s out of town, who may need assistance. I think he communicated several e-mails. title: NFL Power Rankings for Week 11: How did the Denver Broncos hold up over the bye?
summary: The Denver Broncos didn’t play last weekend, but a good chunk of prognosticators didn’t move them an inch up or or down in their weekly power rankings. It would seem those writers believe that the bye week shouldn’t change how they ranked those bye teams the week prior. The same cannot be said for all, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Courtland Sutton #14 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers with Bo Nix #10 during the first quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos didn’t play last weekend, but a good chunk of prognosticators didn’t move them an inch up or or down in their weekly power rankings. It would seem those writers believe that the bye week shouldn’t change how they ranked those bye teams the week prior. The same cannot be said for all, though, as the rest moved them down into the bottom half of the Top 10 for having the week off. One even leapfrogged the Kansas City Chiefs over Denver a week removed from losing to Denver. That’s how the cookie crumbles. Until this Broncos’ squad wins a Super Bowl, they will get no respect from media interests outside of Denver itself. I do like the overdog setup. Here’s how the Broncos are doing in this week’s power rankings around the web: NBC Sports – 4th The next time the Chargers play the Broncos, Sean Payton will tell Jim Harbaugh to stick his “loophole” up his poophole. ESPN – 7th The Broncos are the league’s foremost escape artists — six of their seven wins have come by one score — so we’re looking for an MVP from the defense who has closed out those contests. Linebacker Alex Singleton leads the league in tackles per game and run stop win rate, but Allen’s down-to-down relentlessness is the tone-setter for the group. He is second in the league in quarterback hits despite a double-team rate of 79.4% on his pass-rush snaps. Allen impacts almost everything happening around him. Yahoo Sports – 8th It’s hard to find an advanced metric that indicates the Broncos should be higher than this. They’re 14th in point differential, ninth in DVOA, 15th in net EPA as of last week and also a stunning 30th in yards per game on offense and 27th in yards allowed per game on defense. Their Super Bowl odds are tied for ninth best, for what that’s worth. But here’s why that doesn’t matter: Denver is 7-2 after stacking (close) wins and has the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL, via DVOA, after playing the hardest schedule to this point in the season. Here’s what Denver has coming up: vs. Raiders, at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers. That’s two playoff contenders (assuming Drake Maye’s injury sinks the Patriots) of eight remaining games. Like last season, the Broncos could end up with 13 or 14 wins and an army of naysayers wondering how good they really are. USA Today – 6th Their schedule, the league’s easiest down the stretch based on their remaining opponents’ collective winning percentage, suggests they should match last year’s 14-3 record. Fox Sports – 2nd The Broncos rode a five-game winning streak into the bye week and are holding onto this spot thanks to the way the 49ers had to hang on to beat the Cowboys. It also helps that the 7-2 Broncos have a really easy schedule over the next five weeks, maybe outside of their Black Friday game in Pittsburgh. They’ll get the Raiders twice, the Dolphins and the Jets, which should give them a great chance to pad their record. It could also give QB Bo Nix a chance to finally get on a long-awaited roll. CBS Sports – 5th Coming off the bye, they need to get better play in two areas: Passing game and run defense. If they do, they can make a deep playoff run. NY Times – 3rd The fourth-round rookie running back had 36 touches for 192 yards of offense in weeks 8 and 9. That ranked 17th in the league in that stretch. For the season, he’s averaging 9.8 yards per reception, and he could have a big day against a middling Raiders defense this weekend. What do you think of these power rankings? Share in the comments section below!

title: 6 Lions vs. Buccaneers thoughts after watching TB vs. Bears
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off a bye after a narrow loss to the Chicago Bears on “Sunday Night Football.” To get a sense of what the Detroit Lions could expect from the Buccaneers this week, I went back and re-watched that Buccaneers vs. Bears game and came out with six thoughts about this […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers carries the ball against the Chicago Bears during the third quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off a bye after a narrow loss to the Chicago Bears on “Sunday Night Football.” To get a sense of what the Detroit Lions could expect from the Buccaneers this week, I went back and re-watched that Buccaneers vs. Bears game and came out with six thoughts about this upcoming matchup. Pass rush very effective… when blitzing The Buccaneers were an absolute terror for Caleb Williams, forcing him into four interceptions and just a 59.5 completion percentage. And while they only sacked him once, Williams faced a total of 25 pressures. But the Buccaneers also had to be super aggressive to create that pressure. Per NFL Pro, they blitzed 63.4% of the time, second only to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9. Turns out for the season, they absolutely need to blitz to create pressure. For the season, the Bucs only have a 33.2% pressure rate (24th) and 5.0% sack rate (25th). But they may have found some answers with the blitz this past game. For the season, they still look like an ineffective blitzing team (28th in pressure rate when blitzing, 30th in sack rate), but with their highest blitz rate of the season vs. the Bears, they got home early and often. Bucky Irving is a dude Irving finished this game with 97 rushing yards, 4.9 yards per carry, and two touchdowns, but it was the manner in which he gained those yards that was particularly impressive. Per NFL Pro, he had 83 yards after contract. For the season, Irving ranks fifth in rushing yards after contact per game (65.9), 12th in yards after contract per rush (3.6), and leads the league with 16 broken tackles forced. He is a forced to be reckoned with, and the Lions will need to make sure they are tackling by committee on Sunday. The Bucs run game is inconsistent but strong No one runs the ball more than Tampa Bay, although that is admittedly skewed by Week 8, when Tampa ran the ball 56 times and threw it just three times in a monsoon. Still, I was mesmerized by just how versatile and diverse their run game was. They do under center, shotgun, zone, power, gap. They’ll try to run between the tackles, then hit you with a toss play. This graph is a pretty good indication of how they aren’t married to one kind of run, which speaks to the versatility of their decent offensive line ( top-10 per PFF ): Every team's run concept mix through Week 10: pic.twitter.com/5cK0tUTnge — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) November 17, 2026 But despite their strong running back and diverse scheme, the efficiency just isn’t what it should be. They’re ninth in rush EPA and ninth in success rate (43.9%). That’s certainly not bad, but it just seems like it should be better. Passing game has no identity Against the Bears, Baker Mayfield was just bad. He was inaccurate (-7.9% completion over expected) and he threw two interception. Aside from one deep ball connection with Tez Johnson, just about everything he completed was within 5 yards of the line of scrimmage. He hasn’t been helped by a weak receiving corps. While Emeka Egbuka still has WR1 potential, the Buccaneers were victimized by a pair of critical drops from second-year receiver Johnson. In short, it just looked like there was no chemistry between Mayfield and his receivers. For the season, the Buccaneers are just 30th in dropback EPA and 31st in dropback success rate. They could play Jalon Daniels this week, but he’s averaging just 5.1 yard sper attempt and has a 63.3 passer rating on the season. Interior offensive line could be a weakness With Jeffery Simmons aboard, the Bears were able to create a ton of havoc up the middle vs. Tampa, in both the run and in terms of pass rush. While at times it seems like Tampa is getting a ton of push up the middle, all three starting interior offensive linemen rank in the bottom half of the league in run blocking grade. Pass protection seemed like a bigger issue against the Bears, though. All three posted PFF pass blocking grades lower than 60, with left guard Ben Bredeson ceding pressure, center Graham Barton responsible for one sack, and right guard Cody Mauch posting a 52.1 pass blocking grade. While Detroit may be overmatched at the tackle positions—with Tristan Wirfs and Jake Goedeke at the top of their games, and Aidan Hutchinson out—Alim McNeill, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Tyleik Williams could be in line for big days. That secondary is balling While they were helped by a reinvigorated pass rush against the Bears, the secondary made everything difficult for Caleb Williams on Sunday night. Jacob Parrish is perhaps the most surprising of breakout players, as he is currently PFF’s No.4 graded cornerback in just his second year in the NFL. Opposite him, Zyon McCollum has 11 pass breakups (t-third in NFL) and four interceptions (t-third). And Tampa’s safeties Antoine Winfield Jr. and Tykee Smith are both ballers, as well.

title: Detroit Lions’ playoff odds: Postseason, division, Super Bowl probabilities
summary: The Detroit Lions are in a pretty darn good position through 10 weeks, sitting at 7-2 overall while currently holding the NFC’s No. 2 seed. They’re at the top of a competitive NFC North via tiebreakers, and you can see the full NFC playoff picture laid out here. But despite that 7-2 record, the Lions’ […]
full_text: Munich, Germany - November 15: Jared Goff of Detroit Lions gestures during the NFL match between New England Patriots and Detroit Lions at Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Mario Hommes/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Detroit Lions are in a pretty darn good position through 10 weeks, sitting at 7-2 overall while currently holding the NFC’s No. 2 seed. They’re at the top of a competitive NFC North via tiebreakers, and you can see the full NFC playoff picture laid out here. But despite that 7-2 record, the Lions’ path to the playoffs will not be a cakewalk in the final eight weeks of the season. Not only do they have four remaining divisional games, but the entire NFC conference is pretty competitive among the top-nine teams. For example, the ninth-ranked team in the conference—the Los Angeles Rams—are just two games behind Detroit at 6-4, and LA has won four in a row. The 6-4 Seattle Seahawks (eighth in NFC) have won three of their last four. So let’s take our first look at the Lions’ playoff odds—including their chances to win the NFC North, secure the conference’s top seed, and reach the Super Bowl—according to several analytical models. Postseason odds: NYT simulator: 79% RBSDM: 78% DVOA: 77.7% ESPN (FPI): 89.4% To hold a 7-2 record and have less than a four-in-five probability to make the playoffs shows just how competitive this division is. However, you’ll notice a pattern here: ESPN is curiously very high on the Lions compared to the rest of the models. I’m not exactly clear why, but I imagine it has something to do with having just the 16th-hardest remaining schedule, per their model. That’s among the easiest compared to the rest of the NFC contenders (49ers: 9th, Rams: 1st, Bears: 6th, Seahawks: 2nd, Vikings: 22nd, Packers: 5th). NFC North title odds NYT simulator: 24% (Behind Vikings, Bears) RBSDM: 26% (Behind Vikings, Bears) DVOA: 19.4% (Behind Vikings, Bears) ESPN (FPI): 33.1% (Behind Vikings) For all four models, the Vikings have the best odds to win the division, despite Detroit currently holding the top spot. Perhaps that’s because of their schedule. Perhaps that’s because they’ve already tallied an impressive 3-1 record in the division. The Bears are generally favored over Detroit as the stronger of the two teams, but they’ll have to overcome a brutal schedule ahead—and an o-2 record in the division. Meanwhile, every model has the Packers’ NFC North title odds below 3 percent, because they’re both two games back and have a 1-3 divisional record. NFC’s No. 1 seed NYT simulator: 10% RBSDM: 12% DVOA: 6.9% ESPN : 9% Though Detroit is just a single game behind the NFC West-leading 49ers—and San Francisco has a brutal schedule—Detroit has somewhere around just a 10 percent chance of earning a first round bye. But given the bye didn’t help the Lions at all in 2024, I doubt Detroit fans care much. Super Bowl appearance odds ESPN (FPI): 10.4% DVOA: 5.9% Yes, it’s weird to me, too, that ESPN gives the Lions a better shot to make it to the Super Bowl than to win the NFC’s top regular season seed. But I’ll take a 10.4% chance at this point in the season. DVOA is much more down on Detroit, seeing as they have the Lions ranked as the 13th best team overall .

title: Detroit Lions scouting report: Tampa Bay’s defense is dangerous
summary: After a trip overseas to Germany, the Detroit Lions return home to Ford Field to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Detroit comes in at 7-2, on a five-game winning streak with no signs of slowing down, and has become the top team in the NFC North. Both sides of the ball are humming, despite being […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Alex Anzalone #34 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers reacts during the third quarter against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a trip overseas to Germany, the Detroit Lions return home to Ford Field to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Detroit comes in at 7-2, on a five-game winning streak with no signs of slowing down, and has become the top team in the NFC North. Both sides of the ball are humming, despite being down star EDGE Aidan Hutchinson for the season with a torn ACL . Tampa Bay, meanwhile, is coming off a much-needed bye week after winning two of its last three games to improve to 3-6. While the record isn’t pretty, this team is better than it shows. They were without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for three weeks, and the team went 1-2 in his absence. Since he’s been back, the offense has improved, and the defense continues to play strong. Like Detroit, the Bucs still have a chance to win their division despite their record, as the NFC South continues to appear as the worst division in the NFL. Let’s take a deep look at the Bucs and how their 2026 season has been so far. Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2026 season thus far (3-6) Week 1: Lost to Cincinnati Bengals 33-27 Week 2: Lost to Cleveland Browns 23-19 Week 3: Lost to Minnesota Vikings 23-16 Week 4: Lost to Green Bay Packers 17-14 Week 5: Defeated Dallas Cowboys 24-16 Week 6: Lost to Pittsburgh Steelers 26-19 OT Week 7: Defeated Carolina Panthers 43-13 Week 8: Defeated Atlanta Falcons 16-0 Week 9: Lost to Chicago Bears 27-24 Week 10: BYE Offensive stats: As I mentioned earlier, Mayfield has missed time due to injury, and he hasn’t been as solid as he was last year, throwing for 922 yards, a 60.6 completion percentage, three touchdowns, and four interceptions. This follows a contract extension he signed with the Bucs for three years at $165 million. In his absence, backup rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels took over and was a mixed bag, throwing for 501 yards, a 61.2 completion percentage, three touchdowns, and five interceptions in the four games he played for Mayfield. While the passing game has had its woes, the running back spot has seen solid play from its starter, Bucky Irving. Irving has been having a solid season, rushing for 825 yards (fifth in the NFL), averaging 4.9 yards per carry and seven touchdowns. When the team needed to lean on him, he’s answered the call as the passing game has taken a step back. The wide receiver room seemed to have found its next star in Emeka Egbuka last year, but now that their other former star, Mike Evans, is gone, it’s been a rough go for the group. Egbuka is the leader with 31 catches for 278 yards and two touchdowns, but for the leader to be that low at Week 11 is shocking. Chris Godwin just doesn’t look like the same player he was before the injuries piled up, with 29 catches for 259 yards. The team has a young core outside of Godwin, and life without Evans has been rougher than expected. Tampa Bay just can’t seem to move the ball through the air, as they are in the bottom tier of multiple passing statistics. Part of the issue has been the quarterback play, but also the receivers struggling to get open. According to PFF, Tampa Bay’s receivers grade out to 59.2, ranked 31st, ahead of only the Los Angeles Chargers. The offensive line is ranked sixth in pass-blocking (73.7), so the blame can’t be put on them. Defensive stats: On defense, they’re one of the best units in the NFL, arguably better than the Minnesota Vikings. The pass rush isn’t as dominant, but it’s still a respectable front seven that teams can’t ignore. Linebacker David Walker leads the team with four sacks, with YaYa Diaby behind him at three. The former Lion trio of defenders—Al-Quadin Muhammad, Alex Anzalone, and A’Shawn Robinson—has four sacks combined. You also can’t ignore the beast at nose tackle, Vita Vea, who hasn’t had a big season, but is still a problem teams need to prepare for. Meanwhile, the secondary has played solid defense this year. Cornerback Zyon McCollum is tied with Anzalone with four interceptions and seems to be becoming a lockdown corner for this team. Second-year cornerback Jacob Parrish has been involved too, leading the team in pass deflections with 14 and has two interceptions of his own. This defense has dominated the turnover battle, with 21 takeaways, leading the NFL. They’ve gotten 16 interceptions and five fumbles. The entire defense picking off quarterbacks. It doesn’t matter where you throw the ball; anybody at any level can create a turnover through the air. You also have to respect the Bucs’ run defense. They’ve allowed the fewest rushing yards (712) and the third-lowest yards per carry (3.5), while only allowing three rushing touchdowns, the fewest in the NFL. They’ve contained the big plays, allowing only four 20+ yard runs, with the longest being for 31. Injury notes Key players ruled out : None Key players to monitor : QB Baker Mayfield (foot), WR Jalen McMillan (IR), WR Emeka Egbuka (foot), LB Yaya Diaby (knee) Wide receiver Jalen McMillan is on IR and can return, but odds are, with no practices in him yet, he will not play this week. Egbuka was questionable in Week 9 but played with a foot injury, so with the week off, we can see if there has been any improvement. Diaby didn’t play in Week 9 due to a knee injury, so like Egbuka, if the week off helps, Diaby could return on Sunday. The biggest story came up on Sunday: Mayfield suffered a foot injury against the Chicago Bears in Week 9, and his status this week is unknown. The Bucs signed quarterback Cooper Rush to their practice squad and elevated Easton Stick to their 53-man roster on Monday, which could be insurance if Mayfield can’t see the field on Sunday. Mayfield will be the biggest name to watch this week, and this team has played without him already this season, so it wouldn’t be something they haven’t dealt with before. The #Lions are up big in Germany right now then head back to Detroit to face the #Buccaneers . Right now, it’s unclear whether they’ll see Baker Mayfield, as sources say he’s dealing with a lower-leg injury suffered against the #Bears https://t.co/PJvIgW0idw — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 15, 2026 Biggest strength: Turnovers You’d think with the amount of turnovers the Bucs defense has generated this year, their record would be better than what it is. Unfortunately, even if you lead the NFL in turnovers, it doesn’t always guarantee success. Either way, what the Bucs are doing right now is impressive, and even more impressive is how versatile they are in generating these interceptions. Interceptions by position Cornerbacks – 6 Linebackers – 6 Safeties – 2 Defensive lineman – 2 View Link For a defensive lineman like Robinson to have as many interceptions as safety Tykee Smith is impressive. The Bucs are averaging 1.7 interceptions a game this season, and if they keep that pace up, they will finish with 30 interceptions. The last team to get 30 interceptions was the 2009 Green Bay Packers. While it isn’t close to the NFL record (hello 1961 San Diego Chargers with 49!), it’s still tough, and teams have to watch it when throwing the football. Biggest weakness: Wide receivers It’s a bit surprising to list this position as the team’s biggest weakness, but the evidence speaks for itself. The loss of Evans is bigger than the team expected, and while Egbuka is a good player to take on that WR1 role, he isn’t the same player as Evans. Egbuka had almost 1,000 yards last year as the number two option, but now that all eyes are on him, he isn’t getting that same kind of production. He certainly took advantage of having someone like Evans on the roster, but with most of the pressure on him, Egbuka seems to be struggling a little bit. Then you have Godwin, who’s taken a big step back due to all the injuries that have piled up over the past few…

title: Detroit Lions create practice squad spot, set stage for Wednesday roster moves
summary: The Detroit Lions announced on Tuesday that they’ve released defensive lineman Ben Stille from the practice squad, creating a vacancy on the 17-man squad ahead of their week of preparation for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Stille, a 29-year-old veteran defensive lineman, was a standout during training camp this offseason, but he failed to make the […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 13: Ben Stille #72 of the Detroit Lions walks off the field following the preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions announced on Tuesday that they’ve released defensive lineman Ben Stille from the practice squad, creating a vacancy on the 17-man squad ahead of their week of preparation for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Stille, a 29-year-old veteran defensive lineman, was a standout during training camp this offseason, but he failed to make the 53-man roster. He was quickly signed to the practice squad and got the call-up for Detroit’s Week 1 game, playing just nine defensive snaps. This move sets the stage for what will likely be a few roster moves on Wednesday. How the Lions will fill the practice squad spot remains to be seen, but it is certainly worth noting that on Monday, the Lions waived cornerback Nick Whiteside to make room for waiver claim DE Tyrus Wheat . On Tuesday, Whiteside cleared waivers, so if Detroit wanted to bring Whiteside back, there’s now a spot on the practice squad for that. Whiteside spent two months on the Lions’ practice squad earlier this year. On top of that, the Lions are expected to activate safety Kerby Joseph from the Physically Unable to Perform list to the 53-man roster on Wednesday, the final day of Joseph’s 21-day evaluation window. If the Lions don’t activate Joseph, he would be shut down for the year, but on Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell indicated that Joseph will not only be activated, but they expect him to have a significant role in Sunday’s game against the Buccaneers . “The plan is to get him going. I think we’re going to let him play,” Campbell said. It’s not clear how the Lions will create the roster spot for Joseph, but the easiest way would be to place Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL on Sunday.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Lions vs. Patriots Song of the Game: ‘Time’ by Pink Floyd
summary: The international excursion is officially over. The Detroit Lions return home from their trip to Germany with a better record than they left the States with, but it came at a cost. Will it end up costing them their season? Will they rally in the same way they did a couple of seasons ago? Only […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions goes down with an injury while celebrating getting a sack during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images The international excursion is officially over. The Detroit Lions return home from their trip to Germany with a better record than they left the States with, but it came at a cost. Will it end up costing them their season? Will they rally in the same way they did a couple of seasons ago? Only time will tell. Lions vs. Patriots Week 10 Song of the Game: “Time” by Pink Floyd Ticking away the moments that make up a dull day You fritter and waste the hours in an off-hand way Kicking around on a piece of ground in your home town Waiting for someone or something to show you the way Getting this out of the way from the jump: big stock down for social media last week. Opting out of the scrolling experience was a wise choice, but it took a couple of days to realize why last week felt like such a slog and a bummer. Avoiding socials was the only cure for the intense FOMO brought on by people’s constant stream of posting their good ol’ time in Germany. And if you made the trip, very happy for you—truly hope you had an unforgettable experience because it doesn’t get much more memorable than that, right? There’s no room to be envious, or else the overlords in this country are getting the exact kind of class dissension they want. For those who couldn’t make the trip, maybe one day you’ll be shown the way, financially, that affords you the opportunity to travel abroad and see the world and your football team in distant lands. Maybe one day you’ll be high enough up on the totem pole at your job and have the autonomy to leave your work and responsibilities behind for an entire week. There’s only one way to find out if you’ll get there, and it’s through; here’s to the next intercontinental trip. Tired of lying in the sunshine, staying home to watch the rain And you are young and life is long, and there is time to kill today And then one day you find ten years have got behind you No one told you when to run, you missed the starting gun Aidan Hutchinson’s injury, one that’s going to put an end to his 2026 season, is a harrowing reminder of the Lions’ window with their current core. By the conclusion of this season, he’ll have missed 20 games over the last three seasons, and who knows how much of his 2027 season will be compromised by rehab and training. He’s no spring chicken anymore—Hutchinson will turn 27 before the start of next season—and the (freak) injuries have put a sizable dent in the prime of his promising career. The hope is he’ll bounce back from this setback just like the last time, but the runway is getting shorter, and the clock is ticking—for both Hutchinson and this current iteration of the Lions’ core. 2022 doesn’t feel too distant, but the NFL’s clock measures days differently, and injuries only exacerbate its passage of time. The defensive core of players signed to extensions—Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Kerby Joseph, and Alim McNeill—rides on the hopes of Joseph’s knee and McNeill’s dominant (and entirely overlooked/under appreciated) season to keep the defense afloat for the rest of 2026. Not trying to be a “miserable piece of shit,” not trying to ruin anyone’s day, just looking at things in a relative way. Every year is getting shorter, never seem to find the time Plans that either come to naught, or half a page of scribbled lines Hanging on in quiet desperation is the English way The time is gone, the song is over, thought I’d something more to say Acknowledging the weight of Hutchinson’s absence isn’t an exercise in quiet desperation—it’s just the reality of how fragile things can be in the NFL. At 7-2, the Lions are still in the driver’s seat of their season, and we know Dan Campbell: the urgency inside Allen Park isn’t rooted in panic or desperation. The locker room’s perspective echoed a shared sentiment following Sunday’s win over New England: “It’s completely different,” McNeill said of the defense’s situation compared to 2024. “We went, what, 15-2? So we had a good year. This d-line is different. This defense is a lot different. I feel like it’s equipped a lot different. Hutch is Hutch. We have the pieces, and the puzzle pieces to put in the game to try and create that production. But I think this is a way different equipped d-line.” Hutchinson has faced the music, but this season isn’t over until the fat lady sings. McNeill and the rest of the defense still have something to say before anyone can write off the Detroit Lions. If you want to relive previous Lions seasons, you can find the playlists we curated below: 2016 , 2017 , 2018 , 2019 , 2020 , 2021 , 2022 . And if you want to read previous versions of our Song of the Game columns, you can find those here .
author: Ryan Mathews

title: NFL Week 11 power rankings: Despite dominating win, Lions fall following Hutchinson injury
summary: The Detroit Lions (7-2) are riding a five-game win streak and are coming off a dominating 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany. Their offense is firing on all cylinders, their defense is improving (they’ve allowed just 12.8 points against per game over the last four games), and they currently sit atop the […]
full_text: Nov 15, 2026; Munich, DEU; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell during the second quarter against the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions (7-2) are riding a five-game win streak and are coming off a dominating 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany. Their offense is firing on all cylinders, their defense is improving (they’ve allowed just 12.8 points against per game over the last four games), and they currently sit atop the NFC North because they’re 2-0 in divisional games, ahead of the Vikings (7-2, 3-1 in division), Bears (7-2, 0-2), and Packers (6-4, 1-3). While the Lions have been on an upward trajectory for over a month, they lost star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season in their last game, and the national media seems convinced it will be the Lions’ undoing. Of the eight national power rankings we track, the Lions fell in five, stayed level in two, and climbed in just one. When comparing the Lions’ ranking to those within the division, the Lions land at third in all but one ranking, with the Bears ahead on every list and the Vikings ahead on all but CBS Sports, despite the Lions holding a head-to-head victory over them just three games ago. So while the national pundits are dropping the Lions down their rankings and worrying over what could have been or where things go from here, Lions coach Dan Campbell refuses to discount this team despite their injury obstacles : Great answer from Dan Campbell. pic.twitter.com/kf3jR7zqyF — Colton Pouncy (@colton_pouncy) November 17, 2026 Let’s take a closer look at this week’s national power rankings. NFL.com: 8 (Previous rank: 7) From Nick Shook : Detroit’s offense is among the most consistent units in the NFL — save for Week 9 — and the team continues to enjoy improvement from the defensive side. The Lions only fall this week because of movement around them, although I am quite concerned with how they’re going to replace Aidan Hutchinson’s production. CBS Sports: 8 (Previous rank: 8) From Pete Prisco : The loss of Aidan Hutchinson with a knee injury could be a damning blow to this defense. The high-powered offense might need to score even more. Sporting News: 8 (Previous rank: 10) From Vinnie Iyer : The Lions are up to a five-game winning streak after starting 2-2. Amon-Ra St. Brown’s monster game in Munich reminds that Jared Goff has fully embraced an aggressive wide receiver-centric offense. The simplicity of the production has them flying under the radar a little to other NFC contenders. Sports Illustrated: 9 ( Previous rank: 6) From Connor Orr : I hate to knock the Lions down after a convincing win over the Patriots, but losing Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson may be a bridge too far for this team to recover from. I think the Lions are still good enough to limp into the playoffs, but can this offense score at a historic rate to make up for all the attrition? The Athletic: 9 (Previous rank: 8) From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall : Breakout player: Alim McNeill The sixth-year defensive tackle already has a career high in sacks (6.5) and quarterback hits (11), and the Lions are going to need him more than ever with Aidan Hutchinson out due to injury. Detroit proved again Sunday that its offense is Super Bowl-worthy, but the defense is 28th in the league in defensive EPA (minus-5.2 per 100 snaps). USA Today: 10 (Previous rank: 6) From Nate Davis : Barring another catastrophic injury, hard to envision a scenario where this team misses the playoffs. But it might be wise to begin conserving RB Jahmyr Gibbs’ touches, because he may need 30 per game in January if this team is going to make any kind of Super Bowl push. ESPN: 10 (Previous rank: 10) From ESPN Staff, excerpt from Eric Woodyard : Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Jahmyr Gibbs There’s a reason the Lions made Gibbs the NFL’s highest-paid running back over the offseason. And he has proved to be worth every penny after a phenomenal start to his fourth season as the team’s clear lead back. With 62 career touchdowns, the 24-year-old recently passed Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61) for the most through a player’s first four seasons in NFL history, per ESPN Research. His 1,384 scrimmage yards are the most a Lions player has produced through the first nine games of any season, and he has already scored 13 touchdowns. Yahoo Sports: 11 (Previous rank: 9) From Frank Schwab : The Lions’ season changed with the reported ACL injury to defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. They were already without linebacker Jack Campbell, arguably the second-best player on the defense, and Detroit lost its unquestioned star because of a sack celebration. That’s brutal. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum are capable vets and will fill in, but they’re nowhere near Hutchinson’s level. “Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy,” Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, according to NFL.com. The Lions won on Sunday without Hutchinson for most of the game to improve to 7-2, and perhaps they have enough wins banked to make the playoffs in what will be a difficult wild-card race. But their hopes of being a Super Bowl contender are likely dashed without their two best defensive players.
author: Erik Schlitt

title: Dan Campbell delivers epic answer on Lions’ injury frustration
summary: Ask any Detroit Lions fan, and they’ll tell you about the team’s incredibly unlucky streak when it comes to injuries. It’s not just the number of injuries the Lions have endured, but injuries to their star players. Aidan Hutchinson has now suffered two season-ending injuries. Jack Campbell’s neck injury could threaten his career. Brian Branch […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 13: Detroit Lions Head Coach Dan Campbell speaks to press during the Detroit Lions practice and press conference at FCB Campus on November 13, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Julia Beverly/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ask any Detroit Lions fan, and they’ll tell you about the team’s incredibly unlucky streak when it comes to injuries. It’s not just the number of injuries the Lions have endured, but injuries to their star players. Aidan Hutchinson has now suffered two season-ending injuries. Jack Campbell’s neck injury could threaten his career. Brian Branch tore his Achilles last December, Kerby Joseph has been dealing with a knee injury for over a year, and the Lions lost Alim McNeill to an ACL injury shortly after Hutchinson went down in 2024. As CBS Sports’ Doug Clawson pointed out this week, over the last three years, Hutchinson, McNeill, Joseph, Campbell and Branch have played on the field at the same time for just 3 percent of snaps —and haven’t all played together in over two seasons (38 straight games). On Tuesday, Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked if he ever feels frustrated for not having all of his defensive weapons at his disposal all at once. A bit perturbed by the question, Campbell offered a passionate response. “Yeah, well, I think there’s time where if you’re not careful, you lay in bed in night, and you start thinking about all the what-ifs. And at some point, you just become a miserable piece of shit,” Campbell said. “And I’m not going to do it. We’re not doing it. I refuse to look at it that way. “Does it stink? Yeah, it sure did in the moment. It’s time to move on. We have to. And what has happened with Jack Campbell, and with Hutch now, will not be in vain. We can’t allow it to. They got us to this point, and so what are we going to do about it, man? Are we just going to let it go to waste, or are we going to do something and pick up the slack?” Great answer from Dan Campbell. pic.twitter.com/kf3jR7zqyF — Colton Pouncy (@colton_pouncy) November 17, 2026 This reflects the team’s “next man up” mentality Campbell has preached since taking the job in Detroit. It’s what allowed the Lions to persevere when the Lions lost Hutchinson, McNeill, John Cominsky, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Carlton Davis—among others back in 2024. But now Campbell believes they are better prepared to endure the injury turbulence this year. “We are much better equipped than we were then,” Campbell said. “That’s the reason why we have the depth that we have in that room. We knew that was important. I mean, these are the things you learn over a six-year period; it’s how important depth is. And so, we feel really good about that room.”
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: UPDATE: Detroit Lions reveal workload for Kerby Joseph this week vs. Buccaneers
summary: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph has not played in a football game in 401 days, but it appears that counter will drop to zero this upcoming weekend. On his weekly radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket, Lions coach Dan Campbell said the expectations—barring any setback—is for Joseph to be activated from the Physically Unable to […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31) practices during OTAs at Detroit Lions headquarters and training facility in Allen Park on Thursday, May 30, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph has not played in a football game in 401 days, but it appears that counter will drop to zero this upcoming weekend. On his weekly radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket, Lions coach Dan Campbell said the expectations—barring any setback—is for Joseph to be activated from the Physically Unable to Perform list this week and play in Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. “Barring anything else here negatively—which there hasn’t been, he’s progressed nicely here—the plan would be to get him going this week. Get him going and get him into Tampa Bay and let him play,” Campbell said. Joseph has been dealing with a knee injury that limited his play early in 2025 and was eventually painful enough to cause him to miss the final 11 games of the season. Since then, Joseph has been working tirelessly to build enough strength and stability in his knee for the Lions to be comfortable enough to put him back on the field. The Lions returned him to practice three weeks ago, and they’ve been encouraged by his progress. “He looked a lot better than what I anticipated him looking (like),” Lions safety coach Jim O’Neil said a couple weeks ago. “So it was very encouraging. So now he’s gotta stack multiple days. He’s got to stack them, so today will be a big day for him, but he looked awesome yesterday at practice.” It’s unclear how much of a role Joseph will have upon his return, as the Lions have a pretty deep bench at safety. Not only did Brian Branch return to the lineup a few weeks ago, but veteran Chuck Clark has started to play better, and Detroit did just trade for former Jets safety Andre Cisco—who saw the field on defense last week in Germany. Regardless, it sounds like Detroit will have their All-Pro safety back in some capacity. UPDATE: During his Tuesday morning press conference, Campbell was asked how much they planned to play Joseph, and he said it will likely be more than Branch did upon his return (Branch played sparingly in the first half before most of the second half). “That’s why we started Kerby’s (clock) earlier. We were being very conservative with Branch and probably could’ve started him a week sooner than we did,” Campbell said. “But that’s why (with) Kerby, let’s start him a week earlier and if we had to park him for another week on the roster, we’d find a way if he wasn’t ready. But at least we got reps on him, we got reps, we got time. Is there a pitch count? Yeah, but not like what Branch had in his first game. So I think we’re going to be able to get a little bit more out of Kerby.” On top of providing an update on Joseph, Campbell noted that center Cade Mays (ankle) is unlikely to play this week, but he’s still very encouraged by how backup Juice Scruggs is playing. “I don’t see Cade being ready this week. There’s a chance, but I’m not putting all my eggs in that basket,” Campbell said. “And Juice has been doing a nice job for us. He’s playing really good football. That whole o-line played dang good football the other day.”
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit Lions stock report: 21 risers, 5 fallers against the Patriots
summary: The Detroit Lions’ offense got back to its overpowering ways with its first 30-plus-point scoring output since Week 5, despite not being entirely sharp. Meanwhile, the defensive resurgence continued, allowing only 10 points, although that comes with a grain of salt given the early-game injury to New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. Unfortunately, for the […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Amon-Ra St. Brown of Detroit Lions scores his teams first touchdown under pressure from Charles Woods of New England Patriots during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions’ offense got back to its overpowering ways with its first 30-plus-point scoring output since Week 5, despite not being entirely sharp. Meanwhile, the defensive resurgence continued, allowing only 10 points, although that comes with a grain of salt given the early-game injury to New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. Unfortunately, for the second victory in the last three weeks, the overall winning feeling was bittersweet, overshadowed by the potential season-ending loss of Aidan Hutchinson. The locker room again has to endure the perils of losing another defensive captain and one of its biggest difference-makers. His absence will place an even greater onus on the offense to perform at an elite level and help carry the team. Dan Campbell continued to echo confidence in the team’s plan to break this portion of the schedule into a four-game series, or quarter of the season, from traveling to Miami, to Munich, back home without a bye against Tampa Bay, and the final (turkey) leg coming on a short week as they host the Bears as their Thanksgiving guests. Halfway through, the team has executed well, handling its business on the business trip, with the old adage that defense travels living up to its billing. Just as importantly, Lions fans have flocked to take over both Hard Rock Stadium and now seemingly all of Munich. The resounding takeaway from the trip is the power of not just the Detroit Lions, but the fandom that’s part of the journey with them. With the Lions winning 35-10, their 25-point margin of victory being their largest since Week 2 against the Bears last season, and extending their winning streak to five games, the Week 10 stock report entails far more positive risers than fallers. Stock up: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB It’s getting to the point where Gibbs is almost a permanent fixture in the stock-up section, as he continues to barrel through a career season playing like a legitimate Offensive Player of the Year candidate. It’s impossible to leave him off after leading the Lions in both rushing and receiving yards. He notched the third-most rushing yards in a game in his career (153), the second-most receiving yards of his career (99), and the second-most yards from scrimmage (252) in a game in his career. Gibbs also recorded the second-most rushing first downs (9) in a game in his career. He now has six career games with eight or more rushing first downs, and half of them have come since Week 5. Not bad for a team that once went 70 consecutive games without a 100-yard rusher from 2013 to 2018. Gibbs was playing at a different speed than the Patriots’ defense, able to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge defenders with ease while displaying a fantastic feel for pacing and patience to set up his blockers, but also knowing when to floor it and explode through the hole. Both of his touchdown runs exemplified that perfectly. The team’s third touchdown drive consisted entirely of six Gibbs touches for 84 total yards, right after he and Sione Vaki nearly single-handedly marched the Lions from their own 3-yard line to set up the Isaac TeSlaa touchdown. Having days when the play design and offensive line allow him to get into a zone and take over games for different stretches will be remarkably valuable come the postseason. Stock up: Lions offensive line The big boys up front unexpectedly got muscled around by the Miami Dolphins’ defensive front last week, not long after the team let the Packers’ defensive front invade their side of the line of scrimmage. But the unit responded triumphantly with the return of Christian Mahogany to the lineup. Although they still had some squeaky wheels in pass protection early on, something they need to continue calibrating, they were dominant for the majority of the game. They consistently reset the line of scrimmage, displaced defenders, washed out defenders at the second level like a tidal wave, hit their targets on pulls, and gave Gibbs and Vaki rushing lanes to run through. They also gave Jared Goff stability in the pocket after the early leakage and were essential in the screen passing game. Most importantly, they started to reduce negative plays. Their stuff rate allowed was only 11.8%, the second-lowest of the season behind only the Jets game, a stark contrast to the 30.3% allowed against the Green Bay Packers. They also allowed a respectable 2.74-second time to pressure, helping the offense produce its second-highest EPA/play of the season (+0.25) and highest yards per play (7.3). It felt like a stepping-stone game in which both sides of the line, Penei Sewell-Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge-Blake Miller, continued to develop chemistry and complement each other on two-man blocking assignments, while Juice Scruggs maintained his exceedingly excellent level of play at the pivot. Sewell killing two birds with one stone, without even touching one of the defenders on Gibbs’ sweep touchdown, was an impressive feat that only he could pull off. Stock up: Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR It was far too fitting for Bavarian St. Brown to put on a show while in the spotlight in his mother’s native Germany. What was surprising was seeing him score multiple touchdowns from deep range, becoming the first Lions wide receiver since Marvin Jones in 2020 to score multiple receiving touchdowns of at least 25 yards in a game. In doing so, he also joined the illustrious company of Calvin Johnson and Herman Moore as the only Lions players in franchise history with at least 50 receiving touchdowns. St. Brown’s surprising explosiveness also led to him tying a career-high with 24.5 yards per reception in a game. Big-play St. Brown kicked off his fireworks show and set the tone with a wild-and-wacky, slip-and-slide 56-yard touchdown catch-and-run that was reminiscent of some of Golden Tate’s most thrilling plays as a Detroit Lion. He continued his smooth navigation on the greasy, yet firm, thin-grass surface by expertly swerving around blockers for a 28-yard zoom on a tunnel screen, finding an open lane on the Autobahn before getting a little help from his friends to push him over the edge. To fully maximize the Lions’ offense, St. Brown also added his trademark tough-nosed blocking effort and execution, once again proving just how valuable a team player he is. Stock up: Roger McCreary, DB McCreary is on his fourth defensive coordinator in his last four seasons, and the Lions were also breaking in new coverage principles to start the season. While McCreary was inconsistent early on, he may finally be settling in. The interception was a nice gift right into his breadbasket, but his pass deflection against DeMario Douglas, covering the full width of the field, was particularly impressive. On the day, he allowed only two receptions for 10 yards on four targets and a 16.7 passer rating when targeted. McCreary erased Douglas in coverage, a slot player who has been playing really good football recently. He did so while splitting time between outside cornerback in base personnel and the slot in nickel personnel. As he continues to get more comfortable in that Amik Robertson role, perhaps his best football is still ahead of him in the second half of the season. Quick Hitters Stock Up Sione Vaki, RB: One way to stay ahead of the sticks and mitigate negative plays is simply making sure Vaki gets some carries, as he plows through the hole and consistently falls forward. Jameson Williams & Isaac TeSlaa, WR: While the duo “only” combined for six catches on 12 targets for 69 receiving yards and a touchdown, they made some big-time catches, including TeSlaa’s spectacular, acrobatic end-zone grab…
author: Al Karsten

title: Why is Luke Butkus exempt from public criticism?
summary: Matt LaFleur has no problem criticizing the offensive line. He has no problems saying there are issues with how the offensive line is coached. He, like everyone else, knows the offensive line is a problem. So why is his offensive line coach exempt from criticism? Bring up the name Luke Butkus and suddenly the offensive […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - AUGUST 16: Green Bay Packers Offensive Line Coach Luke Butkus looks on before the NFL preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Indianapolis Colts on August 16, 2025, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Matt LaFleur has no problem criticizing the offensive line. He has no problems saying there are issues with how the offensive line is coached. He, like everyone else, knows the offensive line is a problem. So why is his offensive line coach exempt from criticism? Bring up the name Luke Butkus and suddenly the offensive line picture is rosy. “He was the same guy when we were rolling,” LaFleur said of Butkus after the Packers’ latest offensive line collapse. “I think it’s easy to pinpoint and point the finger, and everybody wants to pinpoint blame, but the blame can go to everybody. So it’s all of us in this together. Certainly it starts with myself, and then it goes to everybody else, and it’s coaches and players collectively.” According to LaFleur, then, it’s not Butkus’s fault, but it also is his fault, and it’s the players’ fault, and it’s the other coaches’ fault, and possibly the general manager’s fault. It might also be your fault, which is something I hadn’t considered before. I’ve been spending Packers’ gamedays just watching their offensive line get shredded and never once have I tried to do anything about it. I’m sorry. It starts with me. But why can’t Butkus be criticized? Why is it impossible that he’s part of the problem? I understand that LaFleur isn’t going to stand at the lectern and blast one of his coaches any more than he’s going to single out an individual player for post-loss criticism delivered through the media, but it’s insulting to our collective football intelligence that he won’t even entertain the question. That’s not hyperbole, lest we forget. After an embarrassing Thursday Night Football loss to the Atlanta Falcons earlier this year, reporters brought Luke Butkus up as a possible reason for the poor offensive line performance. LaFleur said “I’m not even going to respond to that.” Why? LaFleur is more than willing to criticize the coaching obliquely. After the Packers’ Week 1 collapse LaFleur said he and the Packers’ coaching staff have “got to find a way to get it done” regardless of who’s on the field. A few days after the Falcons loss, LaFleur directly criticized the offensive line’s fundamentals. “II think that’s where the majority of our focus will lie is in terms of our pass sets and how we’re passing off twists, how we punch,” he said. “All that stuff, it’s got to improve in a hurry.” That’s a particularly telling bit of criticism, because Butkus himself has identified improving fundamentals as one of the core aspects of his job. In 2025, Butkus was asked specifically what Jordan Morgan needed to improve to earn a full-time starting job, and Butkus responded that it was all about fundamentals — which he and the other coaches would work to help him improve. “So you’d better be good at technique, and that’s what we have to do constantly, be fanatics about working your technique and making sure if you’re letting defenders in your chest, you better be better with your hands,” Butkus said. “And that’s our job as coaches, help him with that.” Previous linemen have praised Butkus and offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich for helping them improve their fundamentals. The most pointed praise came from former Packers guard Jon Runyan. “Coach Steno, Coach Butkus, they make it so simple and it’s so easy to understand so that we go out there, we take everything they tell us from the film room onto the field and it’s just really easy to follow,” he said in 2021. “They just do a really good job of holding all of us to a really high standard and making sure that we know our stuff and they feel comfortable. They’re just doing their job at such a high level, it makes it a lot easier for us.” Why, then, are there repeated questions and concerns from the head coach about the offensive line’s fundamentals? It seems telling that the Runyan quote comes from 2021, when Adam Stenavich was a full-time offensive line coach and Butkus was merely his assistant. Both have been promoted since then; in 2022, Stenavich made the jump to offensive coordinator, while Butkus got the promotion to offensive line coach. Since then, it doesn’t seem like hyperbole to say the offensive line has been in a steady state of decline. Personnel plays a role in that; the Packers’ line is certainly less talented now than it was in the early Matt LaFleur era. But a coach’s job is to work with what he’s got, and many of the Packers’ early season struggles centered on Donovan Jennings and Jacob Monk, two players who had been in the Packers’ system for years. Both had several seasons of development under their belt, tutored all the while by Luke Butkus. If they weren’t ready to go when finally called upon, who’s to blame other than their position coach? The near-automatic response to LaFleur’s reticence to move on from struggling coaches is loyalty, but I’m not sure where that comes from in this particular instance. LaFleur and Stenavich go way back; Stenavich first worked with LaFleur as a practice squad member of the Houston Texans while LaFleur was a low-level assistant on Gary Kubiak’s staff. But there’s no such connection with Luke Butkus. He arrived courtesy of Nathaniel Hackett, with whom he’d worked for the Jacksonville Jaguars. His relationship with LaFleur began in 2019; it’s not like there’s some deep-seated relationship there. Maybe it’s just LaFleur’s general hesitance toward firing anyone rearing its head. Maybe there’s more going on behind the scenes than we’re seeing publicly. Maybe the second this season ends, Butkus will be out of a job. But for now, it seems like the man that should be getting rightly criticized — and in some cases, actually is facing some not-so-veiled criticism — is viewed as untouchable. In a season on the brink of total collapse, that’s hard to understand.

full_text: (Photo by Mitchell Layton/UFL/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Anthony Miller of UFL News Hub, the spring league has announced the top 120 players available in its 2027 draft, an event that will begin on Wednesday night in St. Louis. The first two rounds of the draft will be streamed on NFL Network (and the ESPN app) starting at 8 pm ET. The UFL has released their top 120 prospects for the 2027 UFL Draft that will be on Wednesday and Thursday. #UFL pic.twitter.com/BYvUu1Tz79 — Anthony Miller (@ByAnthonyMiller) November 17, 2026 Among these top prospects are six former Green Bay Packers players, who should be familiar to Packers fans. Each of the following players was a participant in the Packers’ training camp this year: QB Kyron Drones WR Kisean Johnson TE Luke Lachey TE R.J. Maryland OL Karsen Barnhart OL Dylan Barrett Drones was the Packers’ QB4 until a poor performance in limited snaps in the preseason opener led to his release. Johnson made big plays in the third preseason game, leading many to believe that he’d receive a practice squad opportunity that simply never came. Tight ends Lachey and Maryland both earned opportunities with first- and second-string units when the Packers were dealing with injuries at the position, before they were eventually let go with injury designations. Last season, 17 former Packers made final rosters for UFL teams . The UFL’s website lists Lachey as one of the top four tight ends in the talent pool and Barnhart as one of the top five offensive linemen available. The spring league has also replaced the Houston Gamblers and Birmingham Stallions this season with the Colorado Stampede and the Rhode Island Breakers, keeping the league at eight teams for 2027. Former Packers whose rights have been retained before the 2027 draft include: QB Jalen Morton (Columbus) RB James Robinson (Louisville) RB Ellis Merriweather (Colorado) RB Tyrion Davis-Price (Rhode Island) WR Kaden Prather (Louisville) TE Sal Cannella (St. Louis) OL Cole Schneider (Orlando) ED Keshawn Banks (Orlando) LB Michael Barrett (St. Louis) S Tra Fluellen (Colorado) S Trey Dean (St. Louis) Feel free to drop your full 15-round UFL mock drafts in the comments section.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Do the Packers have any reason for hope?
summary: Predicting the end of the Packers’ season is about the easiest take you can make right now. The 2026 Packers seem like a solved problem. Their offensive line is so bad that opposing teams have no reason to respect the run game and little reason to fear the passing game if they can get pressure […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers looks to pass against the Minnesota Vikings during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Predicting the end of the Packers’ season is about the easiest take you can make right now. The 2026 Packers seem like a solved problem. Their offensive line is so bad that opposing teams have no reason to respect the run game and little reason to fear the passing game if they can get pressure on Jordan Love, which, at this point, is about as easy as standing up and walking slowly forward as the Packers’ wholly inept offensive line flails their ineffective limbs in your general direction. That solved problem seems to indicate we know how the Packers will meet their demise. Either in the playoffs or, just as likely, before the postseason, the Packers will meet a team or series of teams that can exploit their incredibly obvious weakness and will beat them. They’ll either miss the playoffs or get bounced shortly after they begin. But what if that doesn’t happen? What if the Packers can hold off opposing teams just enough to give Jordan Love a chance to do what he needs to do? What if they actually can prove some resilience? What if they can get just healthy enough up front to put together an offensive line that keeps Love alive for a little while? That may not be entirely likely, but it’s not pie in the sky either. If they can get just good enough up front to make the line anything other than a total liability, maybe there’s a chance for this team yet. It’s not a huge chance, but if you’re looking for a reason for hope, it’s about all you’ve got. Otherwise we may just as well get the clock started on the offseason now. Packers DT Karl Brooks ‘doesn’t really have a weakness in his game’ | Packers.com Lost in an overall disappointing season, Karl Brooks is having a solid year. Long-lost Georgia O’Keeffe painting found in Manhattan closet sells for $4.8M | Associated Press All I ever find in my closet is clothes that don’t fit and junk my kids don’t play with anymore. title: NFL’s schedule shortchanges Packers, Rams over ‘bye week’
summary: For the first time in, well, maybe ever, the Green Bay Packers will have more rest between their next two games than they will get during their bye week. The NFL, in its infinite wisdom, has determined that it wants to claim the Wednesday before Thanksgiving as yet another special day for the league. Pro […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 8: Head Coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers walks to the field prior to the game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time in, well, maybe ever, the Green Bay Packers will have more rest between their next two games than they will get during their bye week. The NFL, in its infinite wisdom, has determined that it wants to claim the Wednesday before Thanksgiving as yet another special day for the league. Pro football’s schedule creep will never be over, not until the NFL finds a way to dominate every single day in the fall, and this is just the latest example. Unfortunately, the Packers (as well as the Los Angeles Rams) are the league’s guinea pigs for this next calendar expansion, with the two teams being set to play their Week 12 game next Wednesday night. Both teams have a bye in Week 11, ensuring that they do not have to play on a short week. That’s a good thing, right? Well, yes and no. It’s certainly untenable for NFL teams to play games with just two days of rest, which would have been the situation had the teams played a normal Sunday game in Week 11. Instead, with the Packers and Rams last playing on Sunday of Week 10 on November 15, they will have nine full days of rest before they face off on November 25. A Sunday-Wednesday sequence with an off week in between features 9 days of rest. That’s all well and good, but it’s the same as playing a Thursday Night Football game followed by a Sunday game the following week. Given the long grind of an 18-week NFL season, a few extra days of rest is certainly welcome. But having 9 days off between games is a significantly shorter break than the 13 days off that a team normally would get off for a full normal bye week. In fact, this sequence means that Packers actually get one more day of rest between their Weeks 12 and 13 games than they do between Week 10 and Week 12 with their “bye week” in between. Green Bay faces the New Orleans Saints on Sunday of Week 13, with that game taking place on December 6; that’s 10 full days of rest, effectively giving the Packers back-to-back mini-byes instead of a full week off. The Rams, meanwhile, have an even weirder setup. After 9 days of rest between Weeks 10 and 12, they have seven days off ahead of their Week 13 game, which is a Thursday Night Football matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. (The Chiefs, for their part, are in the night game on Thanksgiving Day, putting them on normal rest.) The Rams then get their extra mini-bye after that Thursday game, as they play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday afternoon in Week 14. Packers Rest Week 10-Week 12: 9 days Week 12-Week 13: 10 days Week 13-Week 14: 6 days (normal week) Rams Rest Week 10-Week 12: 9 days Week 12-Week 13: 7 days Week 13-Week 14: 9 days The Packers already had two mini-byes this season, having played a pair of Thursday Night Football games in the first half of the year. They did win both of the games that they played on extra rest — Week 4’s 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the 45-27 demolition of the New England Patriots in Week 9. Even after this strange stretch, the Packers will still have yet another long mini-bye awaiting them towards the end of the season. Green Bay plays their rematch with the Bears on Christmas Day — a Friday — before hosting the Houston Texans the following week on Monday Night Football. That sequence sets up yet another 9-day rest situation, equivalent to a Thursday-Sunday layoff.
