title: Stenavich on Packers’ starting offensive line vs. Rams: ‘I don’t know’
summary: Green Bay Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich, formerly the team’s offensive line coach, was pretty blunt with his criticism of the team’s offensive line this week. “I don’t think anyone up front had a good performance,” he said of the unit’s effort on Sunday. Stanavich, in a press conference on Tuesday, added, “We had some […]
full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich, formerly the team’s offensive line coach, was pretty blunt with his criticism of the team’s offensive line this week. “I don’t think anyone up front had a good performance,” he said of the unit’s effort on Sunday. Stanavich, in a press conference on Tuesday, added, “We had some pretty hard conversations yesterday.” The Packers’ staff met with players on Monday to “flush” the loss (in head coach Matt LaFleur’s words) before their players were given three off days as part of their split bye week . When asked about the team’s plan at guard, which has featured a rotating cast of characters week to week, Stenavich replied, “We got to evaluate what’s going on with everybody. I’m not going to tell you, one way or the other, because I don’t know.” He was later pressed on who the team’s best five were, if everyone was fully healthy. Stenavich responded, “I think we have a firm grasp on the best group, not necessarily the top five, but the top six, seven, and it’s all open to competition” So far, the Packers’ offensive line has played 13 players up front in 2026. Eight different line combinations have played at least 11 snaps together, while five of them have played at least 66 snaps together on offense. The most common line combination this year, so far, has been: Jordan Morgan, Laken Tomlinson, Sean Rhyan, Travis Glover and Anthony Belton. In total, that group has played 31 percent of the team’s offensive snaps, 189 total snaps. The only player who has been a full-time preferred starter to not miss action this year for the Packers’ line has been left tackle Jordan Morgan, easily the best player of the group in 2026. Injuries still loom, as there’s a question on whether or not Rhyan will be able to suit up, beyond just the question mark at guard — reps that have gone to Tomlinson, Glover, Aaron Banks and Kevin Zeitler this year. Stenavich wouldn’t discuss the Zeitler injury in the press conference, simply stating that Zeitler was “dinged up” in practice to the point where he couldn’t play on Sunday. He did confirm what LaFleur said this week: That the plan going into this week of prep was for Zeitler to start at right guard for the Packers. Glover ended up replacing Zeitler, instead of Banks — who is still on the injury report with two separate injuries. Banks was healthy enough to be active for the game, but he did not play a snap of offense. Even when the offense’s starters were benched in garbage time, the Packers’ starting line finished the game against the Vikings.

title: Tucker Kraft doesn’t look right
summary: The Green Bay Packers have had next to no luck with injuries for the better part of three years now, and that has even spilled into players who have returned to the field. After tearing his ACL halfway through an All-Pro-bound season, the Packers rewarded Tucker Kraft with a sizable contract extension after he returned […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have had next to no luck with injuries for the better part of three years now, and that has even spilled into players who have returned to the field. After tearing his ACL halfway through an All-Pro-bound season, the Packers rewarded Tucker Kraft with a sizable contract extension after he returned to the field this summer, inking him to a four-year, $75M extension with $26.5M in guarantees and about $34M in effective guarantees. Given Kraft’s fantastic production in 2025, the extension was well-earned, even with the caveat that 2026 may be a bit of a bump in the road returning from an ACL injury, and unfortunately, the bumpy road is what we’ve gotten. Even with the receiving room being more streamlined this year, even with the full breakouts of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson accounted for, Kraft has lost the “juice.” The star tight end is actually getting targeted at a marginally higher rate per game in 2026 than he did in his breakout 2025, but the results have been extremely disappointing. His catch rate has dropped from 73% to 66%, and his yards-per-target has plummeted by 40% to just 6.6. His yards-per-route-run is a career-low 1.3, even lower than his rookie season, and barely over half his rate last year. The first assumption, with the breakout of Watson and Golden as serious threats in both the intermediate and deep games, is that Kraft’s targets are different than they were in 2025, but he’s actually getting targeted farther from the line of scrimmage in 2026, with an air yards per target of 5.9 compared to 4.5 last season. That 5.9 mark would be the highest of his career. If Kraft is getting targeted a bit farther down the field in 2026, and Jordan Love is playing at perhaps the best level in his career, what is going on? Tucker Kraft looks like he’s had his powers removed from him by the Space Jam aliens. His ability after the catch is completely gone. In 2024 and 2025, he averaged over three yards after catch over expected per reception. This made him one of the very best players in the entire NFL with the ball in his hands. In fact, despite missing half the season last year, he finished thirteenth in total yards after the catch over expected, and led all qualifying receivers in YACOE per reception. In 2026, he’s basically average in this category, only averaging a measly +0.38 yards after catch over expected per reception. Every Kraft catch this year is gaining about three fewer yards after the catch than it did last year, all while he’s catching fewer of those targets. You would hardly be able to tell the difference between Kraft this year and a fringe-starting level tight end. Kraft has fewer YACOE than AJ Barner, Pat Freirmuth, and Brevyn Spann-Ford this year. He’s barely above Adam Trautman. Adam Trautman has six catches. The rule of thumb is that in returning from an ACL tear, the player won’t be back back for about 18 months post-op, and so that means we’re probably only going to get a mildly better version of Kraft for the rest of 2026, but as the Packers look to reload the offensive line this off-season to make a more serious run at contention in 2027, they’ll need the pre-injury version of Kraft back. They can’t afford to toss another albatross contract onto the Bako-Bewele, Wyatt, and Banks pile.

title: Packers add 2, drop 1 on Tuesday
summary: As expected, the Green Bay Packers signed receiver Coleman Owen back to the practice squad after he cleared waivers unclaimed on Monday. Owen was the first player the Packers have cut from the 53-man active roster this season, and they opened a practice squad spot on Monday by releasing defensive lineman David Blay Jr. Beyond […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As expected, the Green Bay Packers signed receiver Coleman Owen back to the practice squad after he cleared waivers unclaimed on Monday. Owen was the first player the Packers have cut from the 53-man active roster this season, and they opened a practice squad spot on Monday by releasing defensive lineman David Blay Jr. Beyond just that move, though, the Packers also made a change with their international exemption slot on the practice squad. Gone is kicker Lenny Krieg, who has been with the team this entire regular season. The team has added Haggai Ndubuisi, a defensive lineman from Nigeria, to replace Krieg. Ndubuisi, a former offensive lineman, has previously been on the rosters of the Arizona Cardinals, Denver Broncos, San Antonio Brahmas (UFL), Washington Commanders, New England Patriots, Houston Texans and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Earlier this season, he worked out for the Indianapolis Colts, Minnesota Vikings, Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders, prior to his visit to Green Bay on Monday. According to a source, Ndubuisi was measured at 6’7”, 323 pounds and had 36” arms at the IPP’s pro day back in 2023. He was active for the Texans in one game (Week 14) last season. Ndubuisi’s time in New England also overlapped with DeMarcus Covington’s time there. Covington, now the Packers’ outside linebackers coach/run game coordinator/assistant head coach – defense, was the defensive coordinator of the Patriots at the time. title: Packers Film Room: The Tucky Sneak adds a wrinkle
summary: Since his second year in the league, tight end Tucker Kraft has been something of a battering ram in the sneak game. Since 2024, the Green Bay Packers have used Kraft as the ball carrier in 8 sneak attempts: 3 times on 4th & 1, 5 times on 3rd & 1. He has converted 7 […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Since his second year in the league, tight end Tucker Kraft has been something of a battering ram in the sneak game. Since 2024, the Green Bay Packers have used Kraft as the ball carrier in 8 sneak attempts: 3 times on 4th & 1, 5 times on 3rd & 1. He has converted 7 of those attempts, for a Success Rate of 87.5%. The only time he has been stopped was on the 3rd & 1 play against the New England Patriots in Week 9 of this season. His longest gain came in the 2024 Wild Card game, picking up 8 yards on 3rd & 1. So it would make sense for the Packers to have a variation or two in their bag. We’ve seen a couple of nice ones over the past couple of years from other teams; who could forget Mark Andrews ‘ 35-yard TD scamper on 4th & 1 off a spin? So far, the Packers have kept it pretty vanilla. And why not? After all, an 87.5% Success Rate is exactly what you’re looking for in that situation. Take your battering ram and shove him into the line until he gets at least a yard. There’s not always a need to overcomplicate things. However, you need the occasional curveball. You don’t want the defense being able to load up in the middle of the line, but there are also explosives to be had if you can catch them out of position. That’s what the Packers did in the 1st quarter this past weekend. Down 3-0 with 8:52 remaining in the 1st quarter, the Packers were facing 3rd & 1 at the Vikings’ 44-yard line. They come out in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR), starting in an empty, condensed 3×2 look with Tucker Kraft [85] wide on the left. The Vikings have 4 men up on the line, with 3 linebackers set a few yards behind them. Kraft shifts under center, and it creates motion on the Vikings side of the ball. Eric Wilson [55] comes up to the line and moves the DT to his side over and Andrew Van Ginkel [43] leaves his spot over Matthew Golden [0] to get up on the line. Ivan Pace Jr. [0] starts moving towards the interior of the line as well. Everything is condensed to the middle, and the Packers are looking to play off that. At the snap, Kraft pitches back to Jordan Love [10], who rolls right. Chris Brooks [30] is shading out on the right side of the line. He’s acting as a personal protector for Love on that side. Golden slow-plays his release, then breaks on a corner route while Christian Watson [9] works as the trailer from the left. This is supposed to go to Golden. If Love throws this directly after he gathers the ball, he likely has Golden for a nice gain. However, Isaiah Rodgers [2] is playing as the boundary on that side. He’s initially held close to the line (in case of a Love scramble), but after Love is steered back inside by Van Ginkel, Rodgers breaks to the corner, taking away Golden. Love may think the throw to Golden would need to be behind him, and thus harder to corral. So Love sets and fires to Watson in the middle of the field. Watson does not appear to ever truly be expecting this ball. He looks like he’s slow-playing his release in the same way Golden does, but he never looks to hit a different gear or to break sharply and create a little more separation. Love finds him all the same, and the Packers pick up 15 yards and the 1st down. And if we’re opening up the floor for other ideas off of this, I humbly offer up the Fake Sneak/TE Pop. Albums listened to: Sister Ray Davies – Holy Island ; Phoebe Bridgers – Lost Weekend ; Hannah Cole – Switchbacks ; U2 – Carnaval De Luz

title: Week 11 Power Rankings Round Up: Packers come back down to earth
summary: Well, Green Bay’s matchup against Minnesota went about as badly as it could have, as the Packers fell 30-10. As it turns out, relying on Jordan Love to play at superhuman levels has its drawbacks. Love has answered the call at every turn and played admirably, all things considered, in Week 10, but it turns […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, Green Bay’s matchup against Minnesota went about as badly as it could have, as the Packers fell 30-10. As it turns out, relying on Jordan Love to play at superhuman levels has its drawbacks. Love has answered the call at every turn and played admirably, all things considered, in Week 10, but it turns out that football is a team game, and offensive line play is an important part of that team. As doom and gloom as Sunday was, there were some positives. J. Michael Sturdivant caught his first career touchdown, Kaleb Johnson showed some flashes when he had time to run, and Jordan Love finally drew a roughing the passer penalty, resulting in probably the loudest cheer of the day aside from the pregame flyover. It really has been a drastic swing of emotions for the green and gold faithful. There has been some really ugly football, some incredibly good football as we saw in New England, and then a swing back to really bad in Week 10. As much as people blame the offensive line, it truly was a team effort, or lack thereof. Green Bay’s defense gave up a touchdown on a 3rd and 23, Trey Smack missed another field goal, the line did let up 8 sacks, and the team coughed up 3 fumbles to go with a Jordan Love interception. In last week’s various Power Rankings, many had the Packers inside the Top 10, with Sports Illustrated having the team as high as the 5 spot in its rankings. One week later, Green Bay still remains in the top half of the league, perhaps as a testament to the strength of the Vikings. Or perhaps it is due to the Packers still finding themselves a playoff team, a true reminder that one game isn’t the be-all and end-all in the grand scheme of things. Thankfully, Green Bay will not lose this week, as the bye week is finally here. Every year, it seems like the bye week comes at the perfect time, but this year, that really rings true. It will be the shortest bye week in the NFL, as both the Rams and Packers will come off their respective bye weeks to play on Thanksgiving Eve a week from Wednesday. Josh Jacobs could be back, Micah Parsons should be back, and Kevin Zeitler will have another week to heal up and ramp up. So with the bye week here, let’s see where Green Bay stands around the league: NFL Power Rankings Entering Week 11: NFL.com: 10th NFL.com’s Nick Shook has the Packers as the highest mark on the collective lists this week, keeping Green Bay at the 10th spot, dropping 2 spots from the 8th spot. Shook writes: “We’re now entering the edge of the quagmire. Green Bay’s reliance on the explosive play became a weakness against Minnesota, as a lack of sustainable success contributed to its 20-point loss to the division rival. One might simply say the Vikings have the Packers’ number; I tend to think Minnesota merely exposed a weakness that might hold back Green Bay as it fights to remain in the playoff hunt in the toughest division in football. That’s not enough to knock the Pack out of the top 10, but it does shake my confidence in them.“ Fox Sports: 11th Sports Illustrated:12th USA Today: 12th The Athletic: 12th Yahoo Sports: 12th Bleacher Report: 12th ESPN: 12th Pro Football Talk: 13th CBS Sports: 13th Suffice to say, Green Bay is still viewed relatively favorably around the league. Despite falling 7 spots in Conor Orr’s rankings on Sports Illustrated, the Packers still hold the 12 spot in his metrics. So it certainly could be worse. Week 11 will kick off in a couple of days, and with Green Bay sitting idle on the bye week this week, they do not control whether they rise or fall. Enjoy the week of stress-free football!

summary: “I’ve never seen anything quite like this. full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - NOVEMBER 15: Cleveland Browns defensive end Isaiah McGuire (57) and Cleveland Browns cornerback Myles Harden (26) sack Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) during the third quarter of the National Football League game between the Houston Texans and Cleveland Browns on November 15, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images “I’ve never seen anything quite like this. Never…it’s crazy.” – Conor Orr, Heed the Call Podcast ”…this was Eagles-esque.” – Steve Palazzolo, Check the Mic Podcast “CJ [Stroud] got blame, protection plan for blame, run game got blame, receivers got blame, [Nick] Caley got blame, [Cole] Popovich got blame…there is not a single person that can watch that second half and think, ‘I did my job.’” – DJ Bien-Aime, Texans Cookout These are just some of the quotes from pundits, reporters, and analysts from around the league as they try to make sense of the Texans’ most recent, excruciating, 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns. If you had missed that game (or been wise enough to skip on watching), you may have thought that the world was crashing down on the Houston Texans Sunday afternoon, and that wouldn’t be far from the truth. This loss nearly guarantees Houston will not make the 2026 playoffs, pounding another nail into the coffin of one of their most ambitious seasons yet. Disappointment is something Texans fans have become accustomed to, but experiencing the air of hype surrounding this team deflate in just half of a season is a new low in the DeMeco Ryans era. In place of the hype, bitter feelings and debate about the team’s ability to make adjustments (or lack thereof) have filled the empty space. Texans guard Ed Ingram said he felt like there weren’t adjustments for the offense when it came to handling the pressure from Cleveland. pic.twitter.com/dWhevMAVOr — Cody Stoots (@Cody_Stoots) November 16, 2026 Asked Texans OC Nick Caley about the ongoing notion that they’re trying and why that even matters. The faith in the process despite results. Why he feels comfortable hanging his cap on his body of work. pic.twitter.com/6dffubsW0J — Landry Locker (@LandryLocker) November 16, 2026 As spectators of the team and hopeless bystanders to their games, our lack of agency in the performance of the Texans creates a sense of impending doom as the games go on and the losses pile up. As Battle Red Blog analyst Scott Barzilla stated in his Value of Things post this week, “It is like watching a car wreck in slow motion. You try to yell but nothing leaves your vocal cords. You just sit there in silence knowing what is going to happen.” That helpless feeling often manifests itself at first as casual frustration with the team and the coaching staff, then develops into resentment or ridicule as the season enters dire straits, and then finally, into pure exasperation as playoff hopes come crashing down. A failure this significant demands punishment – simple adjustments and a re-shuffling of game-day duties will no longer cut it for many in the Texans’ community; Now, with a 3-6 record, many are calling for firings. Some are even calling for the entire coaching staff to be dumped and for the Texans to just reset that entire section of their organization because of how unacceptable their current record is. How can you take a roster that went 12-5 and looked primed for a championship run just one year ago and drive them into the ground like this? More importantly, how are problems that have haunted this era of Texans football (penalties, hot-and-cold offense, poor offensive line) since 2023 still causing problems in 2026? The early successes of the Texans’ front office bought them time to address this issue, but stagnation year after year has now driven the community to a breaking point. Where do they go from here? It’s anyone’s guess, but chances are, we haven’t reached the lowest point of the season just yet. Regardless if shaking up the coaching staff in the middle of the season is the right decision to make, the fact this has become a popular refrain gives you an idea of how far Houston’s star has fallen in just two months. How far will that star fall in this week’s power rankings? Well, let’s find out: NFL.COM : 17. Houston Texans (3-6) (Last Week: 16) Well, just as the Texans’ unlikely turnaround from an 0-4 start was gaining steam, the Browns showed up to ruin it. Houston’s blown 17-point lead was a microcosm of what has plagued the team throughout this season, and while C.J. Stroud has enjoyed an excellent bounce-back campaign, his ineffectiveness for most of the second half Sunday was both disappointing and painfully familiar to Texans fans. This just might be what Houston is this year. – Nick Shook ESPN: 16. Houston Texans (3-6) Week 10 result: Lost to the Browns 27-24 Week 10 ranking: 17 Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge Will Anderson Jr . Despite the Texans’ defense regressing drastically from last season, Anderson is currently at the top of DraftKings’ odds for Defensive Player of the Year (+120). He has 39 combined tackles (21 solo, 18 assists), 10.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery. His sack total leads the league, and he’s tied for 12th among edge rushers with a 22.6% pass rush win rate. – DJ Bien-Aime SPORTS ILLUSTRATED: 20. Houston Texans (3–6) Last week’s ranking: No. 16 Last week’s result: lost to Browns, 27–24 This week: vs. Colts The Texans’ defense was a unit that preyed on its opponents by presenting pure simplicity at the line and then winning at every position. A year later, opponents like Todd Monken are looking at coverages from a year ago that are still being run and preying on that same simplicity. – Conor Orr BLEACHER REPORT: 22. Houston Texans (3-6) Last Week: 19 Week 10 Result: Lost at Cleveland 27-24 The Houston Texans’ season isn’t over just yet, but Sunday’s loss to the Cleveland Browns was a major blow. The Texans came out of their bye and delivered a convincing win in Week 9, albeit against the winless Chargers. Unfortunately, they were unable to build any momentum in Week 10. Instead, Houston blew an early 17-0 lead and slid further behind in the AFC South race. C.J. Stroud has played well enough to finally earn his second contract, but little else has gone well for the Texans this season. The defense continues to underwhelm, and running back Woody Marks (concussion) joined David Montgomery on the injured list on Sunday. At this point, the playoffs are an extreme long shot. – Kris Knox CBS SPORTS: 19. Texans (3-6) (Last Week; 19) The defense let them down in the loss to the Browns and now at 3-6 they have major problems in terms of the playoff race. They blew a 17-0 lead. – Pete Prisco USA TODAY: 23. Houston Texans (22): Elite defense? They’ve lost four games this season after surrendering a lead inside the final two minutes. – Nate Davis YAHOO! Houston was supposed to be one of the best defenses in the NFL. The Texans were second in EPA per play allowed last season. This season they’re 20th, despite having mostly the same personnel and coaches. While defensive success can fluctuate from season to season more than offensive success, the Texans’ decline is perplexing. If Houston finished just two of those five games, it would be above .500. “We have to play better — run defense, have to tackle better,” head coach DeMeco Ryans said, via Texans Wire . – Frank Schwab THE ATHLETIC: 23. title: Value of Things: Likely end game scenarios
summary: It seems that judging by the comments here and elsewhere that a number of fans have reached the point of no return on this team. We have also seen more than a few players express some frustration with how things have been going. Obviously, that does not mean there is a mutiny. That would be […]
full_text: Feb 28, 2023; Indianapolis, IN, USA; Houston Texans general manager Nick Caserio during the NFL combine at the Indiana Convention Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports It seems that judging by the comments here and elsewhere that a number of fans have reached the point of no return on this team. We have also seen more than a few players express some frustration with how things have been going. Obviously, that does not mean there is a mutiny. That would be irresponsible reporting at this point and would spill us into hot take territory. However, when seasons like this go south there are inevitable questions about who gets assigned blame and what happens to them? I think we can all agree that Nick Caley and Cole Popovich’s days are numbered. Is it even completely their fault? Heck, the team has had four late fourth quarter leads in one possession games and seen the defense give up the score every single time. I’d certainly understand anyone willing to give a pass to Caley and the rest of the offensive coaching staff. However, after watching what we watched on Sunday and coupling that with the horrible effort against the New York Giants, it seems that Caley really hasn’t grasped what would make this team a consistent offensive threat. That leaves two people clearly in the crosshairs and it seems amazing that either of these two would be here. I hate to look at one football game as changing everything, but the Browns loss in particular shows all kinds of issues that at least need to be talked about if not acted on. I clearly try to look at things rationally and logically, so there are four possibilities here. We will go in the order of most to least likely. Both Nick Caserio and DeMeco Ryans stay I know this is the least popular option on the board, but it is the most likely option. What would the justification be? Essentially, this pairing has been together for four seasons and they have been successful in three of them. So, this would be a bet on the fact that everyone deserves a mulligan and that both would learn from their mistakes and right this ship in 2027. Let’s ignore for the time being that Caserio has been on the job longer than that and has two other failed head coaching hires. Most people would consider that just the necessary time it took to fix Bill O’Brien’s mess. The roster is still in good shape and the cap appears to be in good shape as well. Yes, he did trade away some draft capital to get Marvin Harrison Jr. We will have to get to that in a minute when we look at the other possibilities. So, in essence this group would be hiring their third offensive coordinator and third offensive staff. We could editorialize beyond that, but those facts alone probably speak for themselves. Ryans stays and Caserio goes If it comes down to who has the most juice in the building it would have to be Ryans. For one, he has been there only the four seasons where Caserio has the extra two seasons to his name. That comes with the extra baggage of those decisions made before Ryans, but it also means he has had six years to get things like the offensive line right and failed to do so. I am not predicting a power struggle here, but if one occurs Ryans also has the advantage of being a franchise icon. In a game of finger pointing it becomes a battle between the team having good enough talent and not executing because of coaching and the team simply not having enough talent. It would be interesting to see how such an argument would play out. You could make a case either way and I certainly would argue both ways, but in this scenario we are simply listing what is most likely to happen. Caserio stays and Ryans goes This would mean that Caserio wins the power struggle over whether it was the talent or the coaching that went south. I actually would almost put this is the last option because I just don’t see it going down this way. There are just too many head scratching moves to make anyone buy an argument that Caserio isn’t the most culpable. Moreover, some of these choices were criticized at the time. Why did you have to trade draft capital to move up for Keelan Rutledge? Wouldn’t he have been there with your pick? Why did you trade a second rounder for Marvin Harrison when others were traded at the deadline for far less? Why in the hell are you drafting Marlon Klein at all much less in the second round? Was anyone else really going to draft him before the fourth round? Why are we going with the same buy a bunch of cheap guys on the offensive line for the third season in a row? That strategy didn’t work the two times before. Wasn’t Reed Blankenship one of the worst safeties in football in 2025? I could keep going, but you get the idea. I’m just not buying Caserio having more juice than Ryans. Both of them get the boot I think this would be the vote of most of the more vocal fans. Here’s the main problem with it: the Texans have never done this in their 25 year history. They’ve never sacked both at the same time. The closest would be Dom Capers and Charlie Casserly, but even they were separated by a matter of months. The secondary problem is a problem of classic overreactions. If you fire a coach and general manager every time you have a bad season you are going to have a revolving door at both positions. For these reasons, I just don’t see this outcome as likely. I imagine a good percentage of the fanbase would choose that, but I also wonder how much that fluctuates depending on the results of the most recent game. The Cleveland game obviously points to major coaching issues and if that continues this option could become more likely. The end result is likely that there will be some better games mixed in and therefore the emotions won’t be so strong. What is my vote? Honestly, I have seen quite enough of the Nick Caserio experience to last a lifetime. A part of my calculus on this is the fact that this is the first major failure of the Ryans era. He has never seen his defenses struggle like this even going back to his San Francisco days. He has been hit in the mouth and it is time for him to respond. Sometimes that takes an offseason to engineer. Having been a coach before, I know how hard it is to adjust when you are right in the middle of it. Caserio has tried the same thing over and over again and gotten the same result. He has gone cheap on the line. He has hired buddies for the coaching staff. These things have not worked, but he keeps going back to that well. I don’t think it is a good idea to cut coaches free just because they failed once. I think Ryans deserves a chance to fix it, but firing Caserio clearly puts Ryans on notice. He must hire an experienced coordinator and not go the first time coordinator route yet again. This might be where ownership steps in and forces a coordinator on him. Of course, that is just my opinion, I am sure you have some of your own and this is your opportunity to share them.
author: Scott Barzilla

title: The Day After the Day After: Houston Texans implode against the Cleveland Browns 27-24
summary: The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 10 A tale of two halves: Last week, the Texans came off the bye and flattened […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns scores a 5-yard rushing touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 10 A tale of two halves: Last week, the Texans came off the bye and flattened a then-winless Chargers squad. While Cleveland is objectively a better team than the LA Chargers, that Houston continued its momentum from last week was not surprising, but welcome for Texans’ fans. The squad scored on its first three possessions, with two Stroud TD passes and a FG. The defense held the Browns to only 34 yards and 0 points on their first three possessions (vs. 189 yards and 17 points for Houston). It did seem that Houston might be on another one of those late season rallies common in the Ryans regime. Then the Browns started making some plays, and the Texans started to stagnate a bit on offense. From up a dominant 17-0 start, Houston seemed lucky to get into the locker room up 7. Once the 3rd quarter commenced, it was clear that one team made some adjustments, and one did not. In particular, the Cleveland defense, a rather salty unit this season sans Myles Garrett, managed to bring more pressure against the Texans line and it threw off Stroud’s rhythm. While Cleveland only managed one sack, they did hold Stroud to only 2 of 5 passes for -2 yards passing (not counting the 9 yards lost on the sack) in that quarter. This was a bit surprising, given that Stroud has been one of the better QBs vs. the blitz, but Cleveland found something that the Houston offense could not effectively counter. Aside from the 5-play, 56-yard TD drive, Houston’s total offensive output in the 2nd half: 24 plays for -4 yards. The Critical Injury: In the 1st half, the Texans didn’t set the world afire in the running game, but Woody Marks did have 10 carries for 45 yards. That helped the Texans’ play-action game, which has been a critical part of Stroud’s success. While Marks would come in and out of the game in the 1st half, he did return for the 3rd quarter. On the 2nd drive of 2nd half, after Houston’s D forced a Cleveland punt, Marks had two carries for 5 yards. Unfortunately, that last carry saw Marks leave the game due to concussion protocol. This would have a marked impact on the Texans offense in a second half where the squad really needed all of the help it could get. After Marks left the game, the Texans ran the ball 6 more times on designed runs, for a mere 16 yards. Given the loss of Montgomery, the team looked to Marks to try to carry the running game. However, his injury history returned and now the squad will be even more short-handed in the running back stable with a quick-turn Thursday game coming up. An actual Texans’ Curse: The Texans might be the youngest franchise in the NFL, but they are old enough to have acquired their own curse, separate from the curse of being a pro football team in Houston. In 2012, the Houston Texans’ season ended with a double-digit loss at New England in the Divisional Round. The following year, the team cratered to 2-14, missing the playoffs. In 2016, the Houston Texans yet against returned to New England for the Divisional Round, only to once again lose by double-digits to the Patriots. The following season (2017), the Texans fell to 4-12. Last season, arguably the greatest team in Texans’ history fell in a double-digit loss to the Patriots in New England. Right now, the team sits at 3-6. If the trend continues, another losing record/non-playoff season for the squad. THE CRITICAL PLAY: 5:05, 2nd Quarter, 1st and 10, CLE Ball @ the CLE 29; Watson pass to Jerry Juedy for 65 yards to the HOU 6. In a game like this, you could point to any number of plays that would see the momentum flip. However, this play seemed like the one that would shift the strategic momentum of the game. After going up 17-0, the Browns managed to get on the board with a FG and their defense finally forced a Houston punt. The Browns sat with a long field ahead of them. However, the Cleveland O-line gave Watson the requisite time he needed to set his feet and uncork a deep pass. On a previous possession, the Texans allowed a Cleveland receiver to get behind them deep, but KC Concepcion could not make the catch. This time, Jeudy got plenty of steps on MJ Stewart and fried him on a long catch-and-run. The Browns scored on the following play and suddenly, the dominant 17-0 start fell by the wayside in a tight 17-10 duel. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 2-0: Watson’s record when he’s played against the Texans. I guess he can say he has never lost to his former team. The first time was back in 2022, right after he took the field after a near two season layoff. He did not look great, but the Texans were bad enough that it didn’t matter. He played better this game, so he could take a bit more pride in this one…such as it is. Watson wasn’t playing when Houston faced Cleveland twice in 2023, which saw Houston lose in the regular season but more than get their revenge in the Wild Card round. 9/81: Average number of penalties/penalty yards for the Texans in their losses: This is now an established feature of Ryans’ teams that they will likely commit a lot of penalties. In this game, 13 for 112 yards. Granted, you could quibble with the Lassiter penalty on Cleveland’s final drive to score the winning TD, but Houston committed plenty of mental mistake/dumb penalties to set themselves back. GAME BALLS: DE Logan Hall: With Danielle Hunter out, the burden of replacing his pressure was on all of the defensive line. Hall and Clowney at least answered that part of the task. Hall managed to log 2.0 sacks that helped keep Houston in the game when things started to shift momentum-wise. KR/PR Nikko Remigio: A wavier-wire pick for the team, he showcased some serious explosiveness in the return game. His opening kickoff return set up Houston’s first TD score, and the Browns were going out of their way to not kick the ball anywhere near his zip code. Remigio ended the day with 114 yards on 4 kick returns and 29 yards on two punt returns. Would have been near perfect, but he did have that one personal foul penalty. Cleveland Coach Todd Monken/Offensive Coordinator Mike Rutenberg: I suppose you could put all of the Cleveland coaching staff here, but Monken’s team has been a comeback squad all season, and he was steady in allowing the Cleveland team to weather a 17-0 deficit to secure yet another Cleveland comeback win. 1980’s “Kardiac Kids” Browns redeux, anyone? Major credit to Rutenberg, whose second half adjustments were perhaps the biggest factor in getting Cleveland back in position to win this one. SHOULD BE FORCED TO LISTEN TO DESHAUN WATSON NOT TAKE RESPONSIBILITY FOR HIS ACTION INTERMIXED WITH A SOUNDTRACK OF DEMECO RYANS TRYING TO UNSATISFACTORILY EXPLAIN WHAT IS GOING ON WITH THE TEXANS THE REST OF THE WEEK : OC Nick Caley: Few would be surprised that Cleveland, having been gashed something fierce by Houston to start the game would make some major adjustments to try to change things up. However, Houston’s offensive game plan seemed completely incapable of countering those changes. In particular, the Texans’ O-line could never quite get the blocking schemes situated to counter the Cleveland blitz. The Texans’ defense did at least show some ability in the 4th quarter to hold the Browns enough for the Texans to get out with a win. However, the offense reverted to the form we all know and despise. DB MJ Stewart: This is a game he would wish to purge from the memory banks. We already discussed his public incineration by Jeudy. However, later in the game, he surrendered yet another deep pass that set up another…

full_text: The Indianapolis Colts released their Wednesday injury report ahead of their week 11 Thursday night football game against the Houston Texans. The Colts did not practice yesterday but instead conducted a walkthrough. We conducted a walk-through on Tuesday. Today’s practice report for #INDvsHOU is only an estimation of a player’s participation if there was a practice. pic.twitter.com/GwmKMupIJz — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 17, 2026 The team decided to conduct another walk through for its Tuesday practice. Cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) missed both walkthrough so far this week. Gardner has reunited his calf after it had previously caused him to miss game time already this year. Gardner looks like a massive long shot to play Thursday night. Wide receiver Anthony Gould (toe) has been limited in both walkthroughs this week. Gould has been given a bigger role on offense rather than just his kick off duties, due to Josh Downs being traded. Gould still has a shot to play Thursday night. Tight end Will Mallory (hamstring) has missed both walkthroughs so far this week. With the Colts already putting Alie-Cox on injured reserve the team is thin at tight end behind Tyler Warren and Dre Ogletree. Mallory looks like a long shot to play Thursday night. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann (concussion) has missed both walkthroughs this week. Raimann suffered a concussion in last Sundays game and had to leave the game. With it being a short week Raimann looks set to miss this week due to concussion protocol. Raimann will likely be replaced my Luke Right Tackle Jalen Travis (knee) missed both walkthroughs this week. With the team set to already be down its left tackle it may also be down its right tackle too. The Colts may need to shift Matt Goncalves to right tackle again to help fill the void. Cornerback Charvarius Ward (knee) has missed both walkthroughs this week. Ward alongside Gardner look both set to miss Thursdays game against the Texans. The Colts look set to be mightily thin at corner this week.

title: Beating the Texans, would still be fun for the Colts.
summary: The fan base has accepted the fact that the Colts will be hunting, fishing, and vacationing, as soon as the regular season is over. When your final record only determines your draft position in the 2nd round of the draft, losses don’t bother you, but wins are not seen as “devastating” to the future of […]
full_text: The fan base has accepted the fact that the Colts will be hunting, fishing, and vacationing, as soon as the regular season is over. When your final record only determines your draft position in the 2nd round of the draft, losses don’t bother you, but wins are not seen as “devastating” to the future of the team. So instead of cringing at the thought of winning a meaningless game and blowing the chance to draft the QB of the future, it’s okay to still want beat a division rival. I can’t say that I like our chances, but there is definitely some smugness that I wouldn’t mind wiping from their faces…again. Why don’t I like the Colts’ chances? We often talk about the turnstile of QBs that have come through Indy since Luck retired and it would be hard for me to come up with one of them that I wouldn’t feel more comfortable with under center at this point in the season. Add to that, I can’t for the life of me figure out what Steichen is doing as a Head Coach. I think he is still filling his role as a Offensive Coordinator. At least it looks like he is still calling plays in between each spit, but I think bad press conferences is all he is contributing as a HC. I’m not letting Lou off the hook either, even though some individuals are proving their worth. I’m not sure why it took so long for Ade, CJ, and JTT to get regular reps, but it appears that is what each of them needed to succeed. The Fins would have scored 30, had they converted their 2 point conversion and a couple of makeable FGs. This was with a backup QB making his first start. But, our offense gave them 7, so it wasn’t all on them. I can’t fathom how anyone can’t see some of the havoc created when we blitz, but continue to hold that ace-in-the-hole until the hand is already lost. I thought the benefit of having “lock down” corners, was that we could send more pass rushers? I’m going to get some eye rolls here, but I’d like to make my case for keeping Jones as the Colts QB1 next year. Let me preface this by saying that he would not take another snap for me this year. Just as “historic” was used during last year’s early run, it can be used for DJ’s poor performance to date. I would have yanked him at halftime of the Jags game and am befuddled each time he returns to the field. He is not doing anything well and looks bad in the process. So why keep him? I blame the injury and I blame myself for thinking that he was not like others who have had the same injury. Duke medicine, fitted braces, and a will to show that last year’s success was not a fluke, was supposed to see him at 100% on opening day. Just because Cousins and Rodgers took a couple of years to be whole again, it wouldn’t mean that a younger Jones would need the same amount of time. Especially with what was being reported out of camp. Him not playing during the preseason, didn’t change my opinion. Now, at least in my humble opinion, he is not nearly 100%. He has no confidence in moving up, or around, in the pocket. I think that Flacco and Ryan may have been better at buying time than this version of Jones is showing. Without taking evasive action, he is settling for his first read or the closest outlet. Even the timing on that first read is bad and he seems unwilling to trust throwing before the break. So, while agree that he is stinking on an epic level, I don’t believe that it is because he stinks. The next GM and coach are going to meet with him, prior to making any designation concerning his roster status. Jones is going to lean on what he’s done well in the past, particularly the preparation factor. He’s a smart person, accepted to Princeton, so he will be able to digest anything that he is presented with. Even though the season will be far off, they will see him in the complex working. He will have 47 million reasons to remain a Colt and the Colts have a lot of cap space. I do not see other Free Agent QBs who inspires any confidence? The best case scenario would be packaging a pick with our #2, to move into the end of the first round, to essentially reach for someone not deemed to be first round material. Even if that was the case, you can’t believe that another rookie would be thrown to the wolves in year one, with the AR experience so fresh in our minds. We don’t have a #1 pick to offer in trade for a QB, so we would be getting what we paid for and I do not see a new administration having such a short-term philosophy. I like Jones, no matter how poor he is currently playing. I think his teammates like him as well, although I have had zero conversations with anyone who could confirm or deny this claim. I also think he could be the reason that our reset only lasts for one year. I can’t unsee what I saw last year. I understand that not all of the competition was upper half of the league, but we were good against the good teams as well. Just like many do not believe he is as good as he showed last year, I do not believe he is nearly as bad as he has shown this year. Give him a dedicated OC, without HC responsibilities and maybe a little freedom at the line of scrimmage. Get Pierce back to 100%. Spend on a bookend at WR and shore up the OL a bit. Maybe go big on a LT, then move Raimann to RT and let the interior stay in tact. In year two, Burks could become the slot that left in Downs. That was my soap box and I understand that very few are going to agree. A couple of other quick observations: Give Big Grove a few cracks on 3rd down or passing downs. He’s best at eating blocks, but he beats one-on-ones pretty consistently and could provide that middle pressure that we lack. Plus, in a season like this, let the veteran big man eat. How is Raimann escaping our wrath? Maybe it will kick in when he is making 90 million over the next three years? Should Jones be cut, Raimann will be the highest paid Colt next year, barring a high dollar free agent signing. I like seeing McGowen get more carries. He probably won’t house one, but he is showing how bad he wants it. As for who I’d put in for Jones? I guess I’d go Leonard. He could be a depth QB for some time, so give him more live game snaps. We choked the chance to do it last year, in favor of Rivers. By the way, congrats to him for landing a D1 coaching job, straight out of the high school ranks. AR would likely give us a better chance of winning, but he won’t be here next year, so go with the guy who will still be under contract at a really manageable price tag.

title: Jaguars Reacts Survey: Who is Jacksonville’s Midseason MVP?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. With a 7-2 record about halfway through the 2026 NFL season, the Jacksonville Jaguars are tied for third in win percentage (.778) and rank top three […]
full_text: Oct 6, 2025; Jacksonville, Florida, USA; Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) celebrates with wide receiver Travis Hunter (12) after a touchdown during the first half against the Kansas City Chiefs at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. With a 7-2 record about halfway through the 2026 NFL season, the Jacksonville Jaguars are tied for third in win percentage (.778) and rank top three in FPI and DVOA efficiency metrics. They lead the league in point differential (+125). The Jags are elite, and we all know their coaching staff plays a major part. But it’s always been players over plays. Trevor Lawrence has been Jacksonville’s best player this season. He’s on pace for 4,314 passing yards and 40 passing touchdowns — if the season ended today, it’d be the best in franchise history in terms of yards per attempt (8.8), passer rating (112.8), EPA per dropback (0.281), and dropback success rate (53.4%). It’s not a conversation. pic.twitter.com/UIOI94XVIo — Gus Logue (@gus_logue) November 18, 2026 Lawrence is the main catalyst of this team. Outside of the quarterback position, though, it’s a toss-up between a few guys for Midseason MVP. Two of this year’s stars had big cleats to fill. Ventrell Miller replaced All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd and currently leads his position in PFF grade; Bhayshul Tuten filled in for 1,000-yard rusher Travis Etienne and is on pace to score 15 touchdowns. DaVon Hamilton probably deserved to be an option for this survey. Walker Little deserves a shoutout for filling in more than admirably at left tackle. And Cam Little has been automatic. But this probably comes down to Parker Washington or Travis Hunter. Who do you think has been the Jaguars’ best non-quarterback so far this season? Who has been Jacksonville’s best player? Are you confident in the Jaguars? Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

The Week 12 rematch with the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, November 29, at EverBank Stadium will now kick off at 1 p.m. ET instead of the original 4:05 p.m. start. The game has also changed networks and will […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Travis Hunter #12 of the Jacksonville Jaguars intercepts the intended pass to Elic Ayomanor #5 of the Tennessee Titans during the first half of the game at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL, on Tuesday, announced an adjustment to a second Jacksonville Jaguars game in as many weeks. The Week 12 rematch with the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, November 29, at EverBank Stadium will now kick off at 1 p.m. ET instead of the original 4:05 p.m. start. Our Week 12 matchup vs. Tennessee is now scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 17, 2026 The game has also changed networks and will air on FOX rather than CBS, as originally scheduled. Giants’ Game Previously Flexed The most recent Jacksonville change came just last week , when the league announced that this Sunday’s Week 11 matchup with the New York Giants would move from 1 p.m. to 4:25 p.m. ET. That game, however, remained on its originally scheduled network – CBS. It also takes over the late national window, replacing the Steelers-Eagles game, which moved to 1 p.m. Both decisions are clearly meant to reward teams with both opponents still in playoff contention over those less impactful ones. Why the Titans Flex Makes Sense The Week 12 change is a pretty easy one to understand. Tennessee is 1-8 and currently holding the rights to the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, following Jacksonville’s 40-23 road victory in Nashville. Clearly, that makes the matchup a tougher sell for a prime afternoon window. The earlier kickoff in two weeks is surely still a frustrating adjustment for fans with pre-existing tailgating plans, though many may be grateful for the extra time following the Titans’ matchup. For those in attendance for the rematch, plan around the 1 p.m. start. Jacksonville now has two flexed games in a three-game stretch. Blame the Titans.

title: Rayuan Lane III named Jaguar’s 2026 Salute to Service Award nominee
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have officially named safety Rayuan Lane III as their nominee for the 2026 Salute to Service Award presented by USAA, recognising his outstanding commitment to supporting military personnel, veterans and their families. Now in its 16th year, the NFL’s annual award celebrates individuals across the league who go above and beyond in […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 05: Rayuan Lane III #25 of the Jacksonville Jaguars exits the field after an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on November 5, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars have officially named safety Rayuan Lane III as their nominee for the 2026 Salute to Service Award presented by USAA, recognising his outstanding commitment to supporting military personnel, veterans and their families. Now in its 16th year, the NFL’s annual award celebrates individuals across the league who go above and beyond in honouring the United States military community. Lane is a particularly fitting candidate, having combined his emerging NFL career with a commitment to military service of his own. A 2025 graduate of the United States Naval Academy, Lane was selected by the Jaguars in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Alongside his football commitments, he serves as a second lieutenant in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve. Since arriving in Jacksonville, Lane has become actively involved in supporting service members, veterans and military families throughout Northeast Florida, participating in several initiatives alongside the Jaguars and veteran-focused organisations. What is the NFL’s Salute to Service Award? Real recognizes real. The @NFL Salute to Service highlights the toughest roster on earth: the U.S. Armed Forces. pic.twitter.com/GjUObpfKfV — U.S. Army (@USArmy) November 16, 2026 Presented in partnership with USAA, the Salute to Service Award recognises members of the NFL community who demonstrate an exceptional commitment to supporting the military. Its reach extends beyond players, with coaches, executives, staff and former NFL figures all eligible for recognition. The award forms part of the league’s wider Salute to Service initiative, which aims to honour, empower and connect with active-duty service members, veterans and their families throughout the year. The selection process begins with one nominee from each of the NFL’s 32 teams. Fans can then vote for their preferred candidates, with the public vote helping determine the three finalists. A panel featuring representatives from the military community, the NFL and USAA ultimately selects the winner. Previous recipients include some familiar names from around the league. San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey received the 2025 award for his work supporting veterans through his Christian McCaffrey Foundation and its 23 and Troops initiative. Other recent winners include 49ers tight end George Kittle (2024), New England Patriots long snapper Joe Cardona (2023), former Washington head coach Ron Rivera (2022) and former Denver Broncos tight end Andrew Beck (2021). The award also recognises the contributions of people beyond the playing field. Previous winners include former Atlanta Falcons executive Steve Cannon, former NFL linebacker Donnie Edwards and (then) Baltimore Ravens head coach John Harbaugh. There is also a financial contribution attached to the recognition. USAA will donate $25,000 in the eventual recipient’s name to official aid societies representing all branches of the U.S. military, with the NFL Foundation matching that contribution through a further $25,000 donation to the recipient’s chosen military charity. Rayuan Lane’s commitment to the military community Naval Academy graduate @rayuanlanelll is proud to represent both the Marine Corps and the NFL ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AG0DrM2TkN — NFL (@NFL) November 11, 2026 Lane’s nomination is particularly meaningful because his connection to the military goes considerably further than supporting it from the sidelines. His involvement with the Wounded Warrior Project (WWP) has been a significant part of his community work since joining the Jaguars. He welcomed participants in the organisation’s Soldier Ride 250 to the Jaguars’ Miller Electric Center for dinner ahead of their cycling journey, providing an opportunity to connect with veterans and those who have experienced the physical and psychological challenges associated with military service. Lane also visited Wounded Warrior Project headquarters in recognition of the 25th anniversary of September 11, learning more about the organisation’s mission and the ongoing work it does to support wounded veterans and service members. His involvement has also extended to inspiring the next generation of military personnel. Lane has administered the Oath of Enlistment to future Marines during a Military Entrance Processing Station ceremony and visited Recruiting Sub Station Jacksonville Beach, where he shared his experiences and offered motivational advice to prospective recruits. He has also participated in physical training activities involving aspiring Marines and local high school students, helping prepare them for the demands of boot camp. Away from his own military responsibilities, Lane has continued to support the Jaguars’ Salute to Service programming, including a movie night recognising active-duty and retired military personnel and their families. It’s a commitment that carries particular significance for a player who understands the responsibilities of military service firsthand. How can Jaguars fans vote for Rayuan Lane? Congratulations to @rayuanlanelll on being named the @Jaguars nominee for the NFL Salute to Service Award! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/WdAy0D5JWd — KLUTCH Sports Group (@KlutchSports) November 10, 2026 Lane is one of 32 nominees representing their respective NFL franchises, with fans having the opportunity to help determine the award’s three finalists. Voting is open until November 30, 2026, with supporters permitted one vote per day for their preferred nominee. Jaguars fans can cast their vote for Lane through the official NFL Salute to Service Fan Vote . The three finalists are scheduled to be announced in January 2027, with the eventual recipient recognised at NFL Honors during Super Bowl week. For Lane, the nomination represents recognition of a commitment that began long before he arrived in Jacksonville. Balancing the demands of an NFL career with his responsibilities as a Marine Corps Reserve officer is no small undertaking, and his continued involvement with veterans, military families and future service members demonstrates that his dedication to the military community extends well beyond his playing career.

title: Patrick Mahomes found his deep ball again in Chiefs’ latest win
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 on Sunday to improve to 7-2 and tie the Denver Broncos for first place in the AFC West. The Chiefs offense suffered multiple big blows from injuries before and during the game, but they made up for it with their passing attack. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes had […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 on Sunday to improve to 7-2 and tie the Denver Broncos for first place in the AFC West. The Chiefs offense suffered multiple big blows from injuries before and during the game, but they made up for it with their passing attack. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes had a massive day, throwing for 348 yards on 22 completions, a 135.4 quarterback rating, and a whopping five touchdowns, the most he has thrown in a game since his most recent MVP season in 2022. Patrick Mahomes recorded his 50th career game with 3+ passing touchdowns on Sunday, and his seventh career outing with 5+ passing scores. Both are the most in the NFL for any player since 2018, and Mahomes' seven five-touchdown games are the fourth-most in league history. — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs_Matt) November 16, 2026 Mahomes’ monster day came from an onslaught of deep balls, multiple new weapons in the offense and well-timed protection sets from the offensive line. A week after Chiefs fans held their breath when he exited the field with a visible elbow injury, Mahomes played his best game of the season and instilled a reinvented attack. Connecting with Downs Josh Downs played only eight snaps on passing downs, but he made the most of them, and Mahomes made sure to find him. They call that efficiency pic.twitter.com/JWz2Fskepv — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 16, 2026 On four catches in five targets, he put up 53 yards and a touchdown, showing the route-tree diversity the Chiefs coveted when they acquired him. With a play-action look and an expanded pocket for Mahomes, Caliendo pulls, the middle of the field opens up for Downs, and Mahomes finds him for a 20+ yard gain. This look is as easy a layup as there is for Mahomes, and it was a great way to get Downs involved in a play that helped the offense move the chains. Later in the first half, Mahomes would find Downs for the pair’s first touchdown connection. The Chiefs sought a man-beating wideout before the deadline, and that is what they got in Downs. Out of a tight bunch, the Chiefs go with a post-wheel concept, with Downs releasing all the way from the inside. The deep safety follows Xavier Worthy on the post; meanwhile, Downs already has a space advantage on the corner due to his delayed release behind Worthy and Cyrus Allen. The corner squares up Downs, who slow plays it initially, but once he recognizes the safety go to the post, he plants and gets upfield in a hurry. Mahomes maneuvers the pocket and delivers a perfect back shoulder throw. Post wheel action with Worthy pulling the safety. Downs with the double move to win the outside. 15 with a dart. pic.twitter.com/XMkfs2JKK8 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 15, 2026 The pocket isn’t perfect, but with the front line walled off and the edge rushers running past him, he has time to step up and fire a bullet. Downs’ role will only grow in the coming weeks. Shots for Armstrong and Allen Downs wasn’t the only Chiefs wideout to find the endzone on Sunday. Mahomes connected with two of his newer wide receivers on big shots to the end zone, the first to Cyrus Allen. This play is a simple concept being run to a high level, and Allen runs a fantastic route to find the endzone. Only three Chiefs run routes on the play, but the stop-and-start move from Allen, Mahomes holds the safety to the middle with his eyes before firing it deep. With seven in protection, Mahomes has plenty of time to drop back and fires a dart to Allen, who easily took it in for six. Not every concept needs to be a complex equation; sometimes the best course is to let good players win snaps. Later in the game, Mahomes found Armstrong deep on a third down. On third down and one, the Chiefs run a roll-out look with receivers flooding one side of the field. Mahomes has time to throw shorter routes and convert the needed yard, but Armstrong has his man beat deep, and Mahomes knows it. With a little pump fake of his own, Mahomes holds the defensive end in place and buys time to roll and throw the ball deep. With a big rip, Mahomes fires the pass, and Armstrong locates it in the air and comes back to it. Mahomes lets it fly, and Armstrong is there to haul it in, likely securing himself more snaps and more targets moving forward. Finding Rice Rashee Rice didn’t find the end zone, but he led the Chiefs with 82 receiving yards on five receptions. Early in the game, Mahomes and Rice connected on their usual underneath looks, with Mahomes doing a great job to extend the pocket. These underneath throws have been the bread and butter for the Mahomes and Rice connection, but later in the game, Mahomes would finally give Rice a chance to show off his ball-tracking ability. Rice and Allen line up out of a stacked look, and on the snap both run vertical routes, with Allen going up the middle and Rice staying outside. The deep safeties go after Allen, but with leverage inside, Rice continues upfield vertically. In the pocket, Mahomes has to deal with pressure and can’t even fully step into the pass, and it doesn’t matter. With a flick of the wrist, Mahomes throws a bomb, and Rice does a phenomenal job tracking the ball and hauling it in for a big catch. Most of Mahomes and Rice’s big plays have come underneath and with YAC attached, so it will be interesting to see if the deep ball connections continue. The bottom line Mahomes must have heard the ADOT (Average Depth of Target) crowd this week, and he made it his mission to attack the Falcons vertically. This performance also came as he missed his starting right tackle and starting running back; right guard Trey Smith left the game with a concussion, and center Creed Humphrey missed snaps after being gouged in the eye. Mahomes is as good as ever, and while it is still to be seen if the deep ball can become a consistent threat in the Chiefs’ offense, the building blocks are now in place, and the chemistry between Mahomes and his receivers is coming into its own.
author: Caleb James

title: The Good and the Bad from the Chiefs’ win over the Falcons
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs won their seventh game of the season, 35-13, over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Let’s look at two things that went well and something that didn’t from the game: The Good Chris Jones against the run It’s been an up-and-down year for Chris Jones, particularly as a pass rusher. But […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs won their seventh game of the season, 35-13, over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Let’s look at two things that went well and something that didn’t from the game: The Good Chris Jones against the run It’s been an up-and-down year for Chris Jones, particularly as a pass rusher. But one thing about Jones is undeniable: he’s still a beast against the run. Jones still has enough juice to split an open gap, and he does it here, immediately forcing the running back to slow down and let pursue defenders come free to tackle Robinson. The longer Jones has played, the better he is at using his length to keep guys off his chest in the run game. He destroys Pro Bowl guard Chris Lindstrom by getting inside his chest with his length and not letting Lindstrom get any movement. Jones has shown more juice as a pass rusher the past couple of weeks, which is big. I still need to see Jones dominate against a more mobile quarterback before I believe he’s fully back, but the run defense and occasional moments of pass rush brilliance make Jones a critical part of the defense. The Good Everything about Emmett Johnson Emmett Johnson is an awesome rotational running back. In a game where the Chiefs didn’t have Kenneth Walker, it was up to Johnson to be the lead back. He responded with 22 carries for 101 yards and six catches for 70 yards and two receiving touchdowns. Johnson isn’t the most explosive in the run game because he lacks the high-end speed to get past the defense before they can tackle him. Johnson makes up that lack of explosiveness in the run game by being an explosive pass catcher. Johnson is too good at breaking tackles to stick linebackers on him in man coverage, and he is great in the screen game where he can get his legs moving in free space. Johnson is a really strong player for someone who is only 202 lbs. If you try to arm tackle him, he will run through the first tackle. He can even run through defensive linemen, as he does on this play. Johnson gives the Chiefs the ability to run more power runs, as they do here. It’s not that Walker can’t run these runs, but he’s so good on outside zone runs, and those runs give Walker more chances to get into open space and create big runs. Johnson isn’t going to do that as much, but he can run power runs and get 4-6 yards. Johnson is so good at hitting the brakes and cutting it back that he can access any gap created in the power scheme. Johnson might not be explosive in the 20+ yard range, but in the 0-10 yard range, he’s dynamite. It takes real juice to hit this jump cut inside and then bounce off a tackle to get 10+ yards. At Nebraska, Johnson did this fly-by move all the time. Johnson hits the brakes so well that guys consistently fall off of him or trip over themselves. He has an uncanny ability to stay on his feet on first contact. Johnson emerging as a real piece of the offense gives the Chiefs offense a very high floor. Walker has a chance to take any run to the house, and Johnson gives them another punch with his high-efficiency style. With Josh Downs in the picture as well, the Chiefs offense feels like it has enough to score with anyone. The Bad Chiefs giving up interior pressure The only thing I didn’t really like in this game was the Chiefs’ pass protection. They had some rough moments, but some of that was due to injuries. Trey Smith went out early, leaving two backup linemen on the right side. Mike Caliendo is bad in pass protection and not strong enough to keep Gervon Dexter from getting upfield. Joshua Ezedau is not great in space and gives up the corner here. Everyone kinda lost on this play. Suamataia gets pushed back, Caliendo and Ezedau lose the corner and Benson gives up space. Rough rep. Johnson played great in this game, but he did whiff on this pass-protection rep and let the linebacker get a free run at Mahomes. When Trey Smith gets back, the Chiefs’ pass protection will be better. We’ve seen three games with Caliendo playing for Smith or Suamataia, and all three haven’t gone well. The interior offensive line has to be healthy for the Chiefs to go on a run. They already have to compensate for their tackles in pass protection. They need their interior to be firm, and Caliendo can’t do that. The health of Suamataia and Smith is uber important down the stretch.
author: Nate Christensen

title: Week 11 AP NFL Power Rankings: A new team vaults to the top
summary: The contenders are beginning to separate themselves from the pretenders. It was an odd but interesting week of NFL action. Half of the games were decided by two scores or more. Several of these lopsided contests were divisional games, signaling the disparity between team quality within divisions. With over half the season in the books, […]
full_text: (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The contenders are beginning to separate themselves from the pretenders. It was an odd but interesting week of NFL action. Half of the games were decided by two scores or more. Several of these lopsided contests were divisional games, signaling the disparity between team quality within divisions. With over half the season in the books, it seems like two divisions are already effectively decided. In the AFC, the Bills and Jaguars have firm control over the East and South, respectively. In the West, it’s between the Chiefs and Broncos, while the Bengals appear to be the cream of the crop of the North. When looking at the standings, depending on who you ask, it looks like anywhere from nine to twelve teams have a realistic shot at hoisting the Lombardi in February. The rest of the league could win or lose on any given week, which is exactly what the league desires. Let’s take a look at how the Arrowhead Pride staff sees the league, one week away from Turkey Day. Biggest riser: Kansas City Chiefs +5 Biggest faller: Pittsburgh Steelers – 4 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Maurice Elston, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, Jared Sapp, and Matt Stagner . 1. San Francisco 49ers (2nd) The average age of the 49ers’ wide receiver corps is approximately 75 years old, but head coach Kyle Shanahan continues to put all his offensive weapons in position to succeed. 2. Buffalo Bills (1st) Why does the AFC East always feel so one-sided? For decades, the Patriots dominated the division with no credible threat. Now, it’s the Bills. I know the Pats won the division last year, but that now seems like a fluke. 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd) The Jaguars have a complete stranglehold on the AFC South. 4. Cincinnati Bengals (6th) This team looks very dangerous. Quarterback Joe Burrow is currently in line for his first MVP award. 5. Chicago Bears (4th) The Bears face the Saints off their bye week, one of only two “gimmes” (if there is such a thing in the NFL) left on their remaining schedule. We’ll find out if they deserve to be ranked this high. 6. Kansas City Chiefs (11th) It was so fun to see that swagger back in Patrick Mahomes. His best performance in several years? 7. Minnesota Vikings (7th) What a feel-good story. Kirk Cousins made his first start at quarterback for the Vikings, at Lambeau, where he last played for them and tore his Achilles three years ago. The Vikings have a Super Bowl-caliber defense and have a legitimate shot at the Super Bowl with competent quarterback play. 8. Denver Broncos (5th) They possess the easiest remaining schedule of any team in the NFL. 9. Detroit Lions (9th) Some of the worst luck in the NFL. To have your defensive leader and captain of the team tear his ACL when celebrating a sack is just brutal. 10. Seattle Seahawks (8th) The defending Super Bowl champions wouldn’t be in the playoffs if the season ended today. 11. Los Angeles Rams (13th) Complete domination without wide receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua simply comes down to excellent coaching. 12. Green Bay Packers (10th) Jordan Love was sacked eight times on Sunday. A quarterback has not been sacked that many times at Lambeau since the Ice Bowl. 13. Cleveland Browns (16th) One of the big surprises of the 2026 season. And a great rookie class with a promising future. 14. New York Giants (14th) Quarterback JJ McCarthy has shown enough to warrant another chance in the league—somewhere. 15. Houston Texans (17th) They screwed around at the beginning of the season and are now reaping the reward. 16. Pittsburgh Steelers (12th) The Steelers have been the exact same football team for what feels like eight seasons. I feel they are appropriately ranked right in the middle of the NFL. Mid. 17. New England Patriots (15th) The season is effectively over in New England. The defending AFC champions are likely missing the postseason. 18. Carolina Panthers (18th) Currently leading the NFC South, with a losing record. The winner of this division is going to cause a postseason realignment, aren’t they? 19. Las Vegas Raiders (19th) A respectable first start for quarterback Fernando Mendoza. And a really cool gesture for the fans to stay seated for his first career touchdown, in honor of Mendoza’s mother, who is wheelchair-bound due to multiple sclerosis. Respect. 20. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (21st) We’ll see if their passing attack looks any less anemic coming off their bye week. 21. Dallas Cowboys (22nd) The Cowboys donning a red, white, and blue stripe on their helmet might be the most pompous thing in all of sports. Get over yourselves and figure out your defense. 22. Atlanta Falcons (20th) The Falcons have a major quarterback problem. It doesn’t matter if you have a top wide receiver or running back when the quarterback position is underperforming. 23. Washington Commanders (25th) They saved their season on Thursday night. And because they play in the NFC East, they still have a chance. 24. New Orleans Saints (24th) Welcome to the NFL, Jordyn Tyson. 25. Baltimore Ravens (23rd) Pretty embarrassing to lose at home to the 0-8 Chargers. 26. New York Jets (26th) Geno Smith was injured on Sunday. Somehow this Jets’ season got even more depressing. 27. Arizona Cardinals (27th) The Chiefs have to take care of business this Sunday against another team they should beat. 28. Philadelphia Eagles (29th) There haven’t been any updates about quarterback Jalen Hurts in a while. If the Eagles continue to lose football games, it will be fascinating to see what they do at the quarterback position in the offseason. 29. Tennessee Titans (28th) They have to move on from Cam Ward in 2027, right? 30. Indianapolis Colts (30th) Colts fans resorted to the paper bag on Sunday. Given Daniel Jones’s performance—can’t say I blame them. 31. Los Angeles Chargers (32nd) “Who’s got it better than us? Almost everyone! “ 32. Miami Dolphins (31st) Despite the losses, it seems like the Dolphins have a credible head coach for the future. This doesn’t keep them from dropping to last in the rankings, however.
