The Chiefs turned in their best offensive performance in years with a 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds before […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! The Chiefs turned in their best offensive performance in years with a 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds before hosting the flailing Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Joel Thorman asks: How much playing time will Emmett Johnson see down the stretch if Kenneth Walker is healthy? When the Blogfather (who has done so much to advance my writing career at Arrowhead Pride ) submits a question, it goes straight to the top. This is really a hard one because the Chiefs have never had two top talents at running back simultaneously in the Andy Reid era. Isiah Pacheco and Jet McKinnon did have a nice timeshare in 2022, with Pacheco doing the first-down and second-down work and McKinnon coming in for obvious passing downs. However, Johnson does not have the pass protection chops McKinnon boasted to work in a pure pass-down back role. He also can rumble for much more damage between the tackles than McKinnon could in Kansas City. I will be surprised if Walker suits up against Arizona with a short week looming. But Johnson has too much talent to go back to a reserve role after he returns. The best thing the Chiefs can do going forward is put the two in a true timeshare, even if that is not what Walker signed for top dollar in free agency to do. The ability to keep both running backs fresh as defenses get tired is probably the best thing Kansas City can do for the offense. I expect Walker to sit against Arizona before probably returning to a bell cow role on Thanksgiving after what will likely be two heavy workloads for Johnson. When the schedule settles down, I expect the eventual 60/40 split favoring the veteran. 5crawfishdinners asks: How much time does a receiver really need to be productive in our offense? Seems we always hear how long it takes to learn our offense yet Josh Downs seemed to do pretty good with just one week of practice. Starting to think that’s just an excuse for receivers that just aren’t that good. I think too much is made of it. If a receiver has talent, he can get the system. Downs clearly knew what he was supposed to do in his limited work Sunday. Perhaps in a more competitive game, they would have gone to him more. When DeAndre Hopkins came to the Chief at the 2024 trade deadline, I believe he was in such decline that he simply could not take on the role Kansas City needed, no matter how spectacular his best moments looked. Even so, he caught eight passes for 82 yards and two touchdowns in his second game in red and gold. People also forget how quickly Kadarius Toney seemed to be working into the Chiefs’ offense when he arrived via trade in 2022 before (predictably) injuring his hamstring in his third game. His second game in Kansas City saw four receptions for 57 yards and a touchdown — ultimately his second-best offensive performance as a Chief. I don’t think it’s that the scheme is impossible to learn as much as Toney not having what it took to be an NFL receiver in any system and Hopkins facing a firm ceiling on how much he could handle. Downs is the best position any acquisition has had to really take off in season. Don’t be surprised if Downs is limited again in the game plan this weekend before seeing a very high weekly snap count starting in Buffalo. Swaf asks: Will Josh Downs take more of Xavier Worthy’s snaps moving forward? Downs will primarily do his damage out of the slot, where Worthy has only aligned on 22% of his routes. But the newest Chiefs receiver will probably have an effect on how much work is left for the third-year pro in a disappointing season. Truthfully, Worthy needs to look over his shoulder at rookie Cyrus Allen, who ran a perfect outside route for a deep touchdown Sunday — the type of play Worthy teased the potential for coming out of college. Downs taking work in the slot also led to Rashee Rice getting more downfield work on Sunday — and the player generally relegated to a gadget receiver reeled in a 50-yard reception in Atlanta. Obviously, it would be better for the Chiefs if Worthy was dependably making such plays and using his speed to truly take the lid off of defenses. But early on, the presence of Downs appears set to give Allen and Rice opportunities to do the job that Worthy so far has not been able to. I expect the Chiefs to give Worthy plenty of chances to get on track against the Cardinals. But if he turns in another game to forget, I could see his workload cut drastically in Buffalo. HychHype asks: I don’t want to be pessimistic but is what we’ve seen in the past two weeks more about who the Chiefs have played (Jets, Falcons) or are they finally rounding into form as they prepare to play the better teams (Buffalo, San Francisco, etc.). I hope it’s the latter, lol. I try not to overreact too much to wins or losses. There are several things that make me skeptical about how unstoppable the Chiefs looked in the second half against the Falcons. To start with, Atlanta had the misfortune of playing an international contest the week before and not coming home to the bye. In the week between returning from Madrid and facing the Chiefs, they traded starting safety Jessie Bates and center Ryan Neuzil. There were definitely times on Sunday the team looked like it was missing integral pieces of communication on both sides of the ball. However, a team can only play the competition in front of them. A significant criticism of the Chiefs, even in winning seasons, has been playing down to the competition. I expected one of the last two games to end up being a frustrating down-to-the-wire affair with Kansas City needlessly letting an inferior team hang around. Both times, the Chiefs pulled no punches and turned in dominant second halves. If they had done the same in Denver in Week 8, they probably would be 9-1, with the division all but wrapped up and the conversation about level of competition looking very different. We will see what they look like against some of the tougher teams coming up. However, we have also seen the Chiefs underwhelm in the regular season in such situations — only to come out on top of some of those same teams when the games matter in January. waye6589 asks: What does it typically take for Andy to fire an assistant coach like special teams coordinator Toub? The penalties, the lack of production, the onside kick, the lack of development, and the punt returner issue coming up again have to be making his seat warm. I believe Toub has reached a level of detrimental to the team not seen since Bob Sutton ran Kansas City’s defense. Nothing about the third unit inspires much confidence. It’s hard to have faith in anything but a chip-shot field goal attempt. The Chiefs have never seemed a threat on the new kickoff rule that Toub helped design. When a good return actually happens, a penalty call is the default expectation. I am not sure Kansas City’s front office has done Toub much help. They probably should have made the call above him by now simply to stop putting Harrison Butker out there for kicks. Also, the Chiefs have not added any college players with significant punt return experience — either via late-round pick or undrafted free agency — in the last few draft cycles. After a decade of talent such as De’Anthony Thomas, Tyreek Hill and Mecole Hardman in the return game, Toub has fielded far inferior options the past two seasons. That said, his coaching looks sloppy. He has not adjusted to how expensive Kansas City’s roster has become, which has left him unable to depend on the same players year after year as he once did. The Chiefs simply cannot afford the roster space to keep players like former (nominal) linebacker Dorian O’Daniel in-house to fill special teams with dependable talent. Hopefully, it does not take a playoff…

full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs hosted five players at the team facility for a tryout, according to the NFL Transactions Report. Tight end John FitzPatrick Defensive tackle Aaron Graves Defensive tackle Eric Johnson Kicker Matt Prater Defensive tackle J.R. Singleton The team also reportedly had former Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Fred Johnson at its facility, according to Jason Anderson of 810 Sports . The NFL’s daily report shows that the Chiefs signed tight end John FitzPatrick to the practice squad of the tryout group. E.J. Smith was also brought back to the reserve unit. However, later in the evening, the Chiefs’ website also listed Johnson as a third practice squad signing. Did i cause the Chiefs to update their transactions page? Fred Johnson is officially on Kansas City’s practice squad https://t.co/cH6n5PENVQ pic.twitter.com/qycc8UQXWw — Jared Sapp (@TrumanChief) November 17, 2026 Johnson is an eight-year veteran who started his career with the Cincinnati Bengals as an undrafted free agent out of Florida in 2019. He started eight games over three years, but the most time he has seen on the field has been the last four years with the Eagles. Johnson started in 14 regular-season games in 2024 and 2025; he also played in all four playoff games through beating Kansas City in the Super Bowl. He primarily lined up at right tackle (726 snaps) during that time, but he also played 419 snaps at left tackle. Earlier in his NFL career, Johnson spent a stretch of time at right guard. Fred Johnson changed the game IMO. A seasoned vet. Should’ve been in immediately after Lane. pic.twitter.com/qZol3JyzGs — O.J. Spivey (@OJPhilly) September 22, 2025 Among the other names the Chiefs tried out, the most notable is Prater, a two-time Pro Bowl kicker who last kicked for the Buffalo Bills at age 41 last year. He made 18 of 20 field goal attempts, missing one of his two attempts from over 50 yards and another from short range. He also missed three point-after attempts. It’s also notable that three defensive tackles were brought in. Graves most recently spent time on the Houston Texans ’ practice squad after a college career at the University of Iowa. Singleton spent last year on the Seattle Seahawks ’ practice squad and was waived after this preseason. But Eric Johnson — the former Missouri State Bear — is a four-year NFL veteran with 41 tackles, two tackles for loss and one sack in his career with the Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots . He hasn’t played since 2025 after spending time on multiple teams practice squads over the last year. title: NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Roundup: Chiefs inching towards top
summary: In Week 10 of the 2026 NFL regular season, the Kansas City Chiefs blew out the Atlanta Falcons to advance to 7-2. Let’s see how the national media reacted to it in this week’s sampling of power rankings: ESPN: 5 (Up from 6) Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Kenneth Walker III Walker has been a […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 10 of the 2026 NFL regular season, the Kansas City Chiefs blew out the Atlanta Falcons to advance to 7-2. Let’s see how the national media reacted to it in this week’s sampling of power rankings: ESPN : 5 (Up from 6) Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Kenneth Walker III Walker has been a blessing for the Chiefs’ offense, considering he has produced many of the team’s explosive plays since signing a three-year deal this past offseason. He has generated 1,044 all-purpose yards, and his 11 total touchdowns are already his career high for a single season. By being a stabilizing presence, Walker has helped quarterback Patrick Mahomes find his groove following his return from the most significant injury of his career. Walker missed Week 10 because of a groin injury. — Nate Taylor The Athletic : 4 (No change) Breakout player: Emmett Johnson With Kenneth Walker out Sunday, Johnson, a fifth-round rookie running back, had 22 carries for 101 yards against the Falcons, which was almost as much as he had in his first eight games combined. Johnson also has 20 catches this season for 307 yards. In general, it’s tough to pick a breakout player in Kansas City, where it feels like all the contributors have been around forever, but Johnson has been a meaningful addition. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk : 6 (No change) There’s nothing wrong with Patrick Mahomes’s elbow. — Mike Florio CBSSports.com : 6 (No change) The offense gets all the attention, but that defense is third in points allowed. Coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is proving how he is one of the best to do it. — Pete Prisco Yahoo! Sports : 6 (Down from 6) The Chiefs also didn’t do anything to “move down” in a thorough 35-13 win over the Falcons. The Vikings needed to be adjusted after seeing them play well with Kirk Cousins. At this point it’s fair to wonder if the Chiefs are being underrated, which is strange for a team that has been in the spotlight so much over the Patrick Mahomes era. There isn’t much evidence to suggest they should be higher. They’re eighth in DVOA. They’re sixth in Super Bowl odds. They’re sixth in offensive and defensive EPA. They’re clearly good, but are they Super Bowl contender good? A big piece of that answer could be Josh Downs. He had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown just five days after he was traded to the Chiefs. Xavier Worthy was shut out, and we can finally close the book on him making any meaningful impact. It’s just not going to happen. The Chiefs need something extra in the offense, and perhaps it’s Downs, who always seemed to have more potential and the Colts couldn’t unlock it. Mahomes had 348 passing yards and five touchdowns on Sunday and perhaps that’s a sign of a hot streak coming. — Frank Schwab USA Today : 9 (Up from 10) Wait, you thought RB Kenneth Walker III was the reason for their rejuvenation? LOL. — Nate Davis Sports Illustrated : 7 (Up from 9) Emmett Johnson is so freaky athletic in space and looks to be made of some bendable symbiote whenever someone tries to tackle him in space. So, another really fun development for people trying to stop the Andy Reid/Patrick Mahomes machine. — Conor Orr Sporting News : 3 (Up from 5) Patrick Mahomes ended his five-touchdown drought against the Falcons on Sunday with the Chiefs racking up 452 yards despite Kenneth Walker III missing his first game for Kansas City. They still had a 100-yard rusher in rookie Emmett Johnson. This offense is clicking like it hasn’t for four years. — Vinnie Iyer FOX Sports : 4 (No change) Patrick Mahomes is not going to be the NFL MVP, but he’s going to make people think about it, at least. On Sunday, he was missing his top weapon, RB Kenneth Walker III , yet he managed to put on an offensive show anyway. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns in a rout in Atlanta. And rookie RB Emmett Johnson had 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns, showing Andy Reid is committed to his backfield-heavy strategy whether Walker is there or not. They still feel like they’re just lurking in the shadows at 7-2. But everybody better start paying attention to the Chiefs soon. Next game: vs. Cardinals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET) Stat To Know : The Chiefs have now started 7-2 or better in four out of their past five seasons. Patrick Mahomes threw multiple deep touchdowns (20+ air yards) against the Falcons, his first game with multiple deep TDs since 2021. — Ralph Vacchiano

summary: The Chargers have given away the first overall pick after winning their first game of the season on Monday night. However, as current owners of the second overall pick, they’re still in a position to come out with amazing value on day one. In a new 2027 mock draft by ESPN’s Jordan Reid, the Chargers […]
full_text: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 31: Indiana Hoosiers wide receiver Charlie Becker (80) warms up prior to the start of a college football game between the Minnesota Golden Gophers vs the Indiana Hoosiers on October 31, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers have given away the first overall pick after winning their first game of the season on Monday night. However, as current owners of the second overall pick, they’re still in a position to come out with amazing value on day one. In a new 2027 mock draft by ESPN’s Jordan Reid, the Chargers end up trading out of the second slot with the Jets, which allows them to pick up an additional first-rounder. With the first of their two picks (No. 4), the Bolts still land a top receiver in Indiana’s Charlie Becker. Here’s what Reid had to say about the pairing: “The Chargers have been extremely disappointing this season, and their one-win start has exposed the need for more talent everywhere. That and the fact they already have a QB in Justin Herbert are why I had them trade out of No. 2 and add another pick. And we’ll use this first pick to get Herbert some help .” “ Becker is an excellent vertical threat who has 10 touchdowns this season (sixth in the FBS) and can also execute the short to intermediate levels of the route tree. He is tall (6-foot-4) and sure-handed (zero drops on 85 targets this season) with excellent body control and elite hand-eye coordination, allowing him to win in the air on long and contested catch opportunities. Becker would immediately become Herbert’s WR1. ” As for the 13th overall pick, Reid has the Chargers grabbing one of the best and most versatile offensive linemen in the class with Iowa’s Trevor Lauck, who can play both tackle and guard at the next level. “ After acquiring a pass catcher with their initial first-rounder, it’s time for the Chargers to give Justin Herbert some blocking help. Between the erratic health of tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt and the constant issues with the interior line, the Bolts have struggled to keep Herbert upright in the pocket. Lauck is a steady blocker who doesn’t have much flash but simply gets the job done, allowing just five pressures and zero sacks in 10 games this season. Scouts are mixed on where they see Lauck playing in the NFL, but that shouldn’t matter for a Los Angeles team that needs help across the entire line. ” What do you think of this potential draft haul for the Chargers? (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers finally did it. After 10 weeks and nine games into the 2026 season, Jim Harbaugh and the Bolts finally got their first win of the season by beating the Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night Football. It was the team’s most complete game of the season, which included zero turnovers from Justin Herbert and over 160 yards rushing. The win put the Chargers tied with the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins at 1-8. For the most parts, experts put either one of these teams at the very bottom, but the good news is that it is no longer a clean sweep by the Chargers! That’s something worth celebrating, right? …right? Anyhoo, here’s where the Chargers landed in this week’s power rankings after their first win! Pro Football Talk – #29 “John Harbaugh says hello.” – Mike Florio ESPN – #31 “ Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge Tuli Tuipulotu ” “ It’s hard to find value in the Chargers’ one-win debacle, but the defense has at least been passable. And there’s no doubt that Tuipulotu is the best player on that unit. The 2023 second-round pick has a team-high 22 pressures and is tied for the team lead with three sacks. His average run tackle comes after a gain of just 2.2 yards.” – Aaron Schatz CBS Sports – #31 “They climbed out of the cellar by winning for the first time Monday night against the Ravens. Can you believe it?” – Pete Prisco The Athletic – #31 “ Breakout player: Tré Harris” “The second-year wide receiver, a second-round pick out of Ole Miss, set a new career high in yards in a season Monday night after catching five passes for a career-high 86 yards. He now has 348 for the season. It took one sliding and reviewed catch to get there, but it helped the Chargers get their first win.” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff Bleacher Report – #32 “The Los Angeles Chargers finally have their first win. And while that one victory isn’t enough to get them out of the basement of these Power Rankings, it’s a start at least.” “After weeks of a backfield committee that was…let’s go with confusing, the Chargers handed the keys in the backfield back to 2025 first-round pick Omarion Hampton. In doing so the Bolts may have unlocked something—Hampton racked up 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries.” “After a brutal stretch in the schedule, things let up some going forward—not one of the Chargers’ next four opponents has a winning record.” “The 2026 season is lost—and has been for a while. But there’s an opportunity for the Chargers to build some momentum over the next month, even if all it nets them is a lower pick in next year’s draft. – Brad Davenport Yahoo Sports – #32 ‘‘The Chargers got the win they needed to avoid a lot of annoying 0-17 questions. Let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves; it was just one win, and on the whole, they’ve still been the NFL’s worst team this season. But give the Chargers credit for a good effort. They figured out how to make the Ravens one-dimensional. Baltimore had 16 yards rushing on 15 carries. That forced Baltimore to lean too much on quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was making his first Ravens start after being traded less than two weeks ago.” ‘‘It was also encouraging to see Omarion Hampton emerge with a 105-yard rushing day. Justin Herbert completed only 12 passes but he didn’t need to do much more because the running game was effective. Maybe the Chargers can build on their first win and have a respectable second half of the season.” – Frank Schwab

(Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers began the season with Omarion Hampton as their lead back, but the second-year runner lost two fumbles in as many games to start the campaign and that quickly led the Bolts to a three-headed committee for the next month-plus. In recent weeks, Hampton’s been garnering a larger share of the backfield touches, but Monday night’s performance was much more of what we all expected to be the norm week-in and week-out. Hampton carried the football more than 20 times and finished with 105 yards and a score, his first 100-yard game since Week 4 of last year. He looked strong, locked-in, and overall more comfortable as the game went on the more he touched the football. This success on the ground or Hampton also coincided with a shift in the run game, going away from zone and more into gap and power schemes. Per James Koh of 97.1 The Fan in Los Angeles, the Chargers ran zone 53 percent of the time from Weeks One through Nine, but that number dropped to just 38 percent against the Ravens. This was Omarion Hampton's first 100-yard rushing game since Week 4 of last year. Interestingly, the run game seemed MUCH more Harbaugh coded. Per @SumerSports WK1-9 LA ran zone 53% of the time, in WK10 just 38% — James D Koh (@JamesDKoh) November 17, 2026 The shift away from zone for Hampton has been discussed at length this season, noting his success in gap schemes dating back to his time at North Carolina. On one of his best runs of the night, the Bolts pulled left tackle Joe Alt across the formation to kick out a defender in the hole and Hampton cut right off his backside for a gain of 19 to begin the second half. Overall the Chargers ran for 164 yards on 34 carries, aided by Justin Herbert’s 51 yards off scrambles, to end the night averaging a strong 4.7 yards per tote. Is this the new recipe moving forward for the Chargers? I wouldn’t be shocked in the slightest, if so. And now for today’s links. title: Puka Nacua’s last season with the Rams? ESPN thinks maybe
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have had a decision to make with Puka Nacua since the beginning of the 2026 offseason, and the longer they hold off on his next contract, the more likely it becomes that the fourth-year receiver won’t get one from Les Snead and Sean McVay. Nacua is set to become a 2027 […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have had a decision to make with Puka Nacua since the beginning of the 2026 offseason, and the longer they hold off on his next contract, the more likely it becomes that the fourth-year receiver won’t get one from Les Snead and Sean McVay. Nacua is set to become a 2027 free agent and ESPN’s Dan Graziano speculated on Wednesday that the Rams could be too concerned with his off-field issues and/or his injury to commit to him like other teams have committed to number one receivers. Nacua didn’t get the big contract extension that Jaxon Smith-Njigba got last offseason, even though he was eligible. And the Rams don’t hold a fifth-year option on him for next year because he wasn’t a first-round pick. Nacua also made bad headlines with his off-field behavior in the offseason and could still face league discipline under the personal conduct policy. Plus, he’s banged up again. He missed two games earlier this season with hip and groin injuries, and he’s currently on IR with a knee injury that will cost him at least four more games (counting the one he missed Sunday) and possibly more than that. Nacua played all 17 games in his rookie season but hasn’t managed to do that since. He’s 25 years old and a brilliant player, but his play style makes you wonder about his longevity. All of that is to say: I could at least imagine a scenario in which the Rams let him hit free agency, or franchise him and listen to offers. Graziano didn’t get into the weeds of what a franchise tag would look like and how challenging that would be for the Rams given their slate of free agents in 2027. Graziano: Rams hope to get Puka Nacua (knee, toe) back around Week 14 – Week 15. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 11, 2026 What does a WR tag cost? OvertheCap.com is projecting a $30.9 million franchise tag for wide receivers in 2027. What that Means: The Rams would have to pay Nacua a fully-guaranteed $30.9 million salary in 2027 The Rams would have a deadline to either extend Nacua, pay him the tag, or rescind the tag The non-exclusive tag means Nacua could negotiate with other teams and if he signs with a team and the Rams don’t match the offer, the Rams would get two first-round picks from that team The exclusive tag means Nacua can’t negotiate with other teams The Rams could still trade Nacua to another team on the exclusive tag The Rams could still extend Nacua before the deadline, this would just buy them some time Paying Nacua a $30.9 million salary in 2027 seems exceptionally challenging for L.A.. The Rams only have one starting offensive lineman under contract — AJ Jackson — and only one recent draft pick who might be a contender to start — Keagen Trost — meaning that at best L.A. only has three starting offensive line positions to fill. They will have a hard time replacing anyone in the draft because the Rams don’t have a first-round pick and they’re not keen on starting rookies anyway. The Rams also have to make a decision on WR2, as Davante Adams is a free agent. There are plenty of other free agents, including Kobie Turner, Byron Young, and Ethan Evans. In fact, the Rams also need to pick a kicker and potentially invest more money in special teams next year. An extension for Nacua could carry a 2027 cap hit of roughly $10-$15 million. That makes a tag 2-3 times more expensive next year at a time when the Rams have to sign almost half of their important starters. A tag would be very difficult for the Rams to pull off. Rams placed WR Puka Nacua on injured reserve due to his MCL injury. HC Sean McVay has said he expects Nacua to miss “extended time.” pic.twitter.com/XAR4rutM0Q — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 13, 2026 Will Nacua be a free agent? I highly doubt it. The Rams would only get a third-round comp pick in 2028 if Nacua leaves in free agency. That’s not enough compensation for one of the NFL’s best players who is only going to be 26. It would be a mistake of absurd proportions. The Rams will figure something out with Nacua, most likely. Free agency is highly unlikely. But the longer the Rams make us speculate, the more speculation that will occur.

title: Next Rams game is the biggest one of the season
summary: The Los Angeles Rams face a massive game against the Green Bay Packers in Week 12. The winner of that game may end up making the playoffs while the loser will still have a chance, but it could all be for nought if the winner of Week 12 keeps winning. Both teams have so much […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams face a massive game against the Green Bay Packers in Week 12. The winner of that game may end up making the playoffs while the loser will still have a chance, but it could all be for nought if the winner of Week 12 keeps winning. Both teams have so much at stake, and both will be coming off of their bye weeks. Throw in that this game will be the first ever Thanksgiving Eve Game, and this could be one of the more memorable games of the year. There will be plenty to talk leading up to the game such as if the Packers high scoring offense shows up, or if the Rams defense gets after the offensive line for Green Bay. Will the Rams offense show up? Will Davante Adams play? Will Sean McVay beat Matt LaFleur for the first time? Plenty of storylines. Enjoy Week 11 and L.A.’s bye week. Week 12 is coming, and all that comes with it. What are the Rams’ playoff odds with 7 games remaining? (ramswire) “At the Week 11 bye, here’s a look at the Rams’ playoff odds across various outlets. The Athletic and ESPN give them below a 50% chance to make the postseason, while Next Gen Stats puts the Rams’ odds at 52%. Sportsbooks such as DraftKings and FanDuel still give the Rams a better than 50% chance to make it based on the latest betting lines. FanDuel: -116 (54%) The Athletic : 47% Next Gen Stats : 52% ESPN : 46% DraftKings: -144 (59%)“ Russell Wilson sends warning to rest of NFL about Rams’ playoff threat (sports.yahoo) “During Tuesday’s broadcast of “Set Hut,” with former NFL offensive lineman Kyle Long, Wilson claimed that the Rams are the last team opponents want to see make the playoffs in the NFC. With the club in the middle of a four-game win streak going into the bye, Wilson believes Los Angeles has a chance to make some noise in the second half of the regular season. “If you’re a team across the NFC, or the AFC, you don’t want to see the Rams sneak into the playoffs,” Wilson said… “So, this schedule here. Right, they got a tough schedule… I think the biggest thing for this schedule, as tough as it is; Week 11. “Look at Week 11. Guess what they have? Bye week,” Wilson continued. “Guess what that means? Puka Nacua gets a little bit of extra treatment. Davante Adams gets a little bit healthier. And then [the Rams] have really 14 days before they have to [play] the Green Bay Packers.” “Keep this streak alive!” | Quentin Lake Mic’d Up for the Rams’ Week 10 victory over the Cardinals (rams.com) “The ultimate hype man! Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake was Mic’d Up for the Rams’ Week 10 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Watch his interception cellys, listen in on his sideline jokes, and relive his defensive stops at State Farm Stadium.” Rams Power Rankings Round Up Week 11: LA Rises After Fourth Straight Win (sports.yahoo) “With their fifth straight win, the Rams are starting to put things together, even with a laundry list of injuries. Here is where they stand in the national power rankings. ESPN – No. 11 ESPN has the Rams nearly cracking the top 10, moving up one spot into the No. 11. One of the biggest breakout performers and a player that might now be on everyone’s radar is running back Blake Corum. Corum finished the day with 100 yards on 17 carries, and he continues to outpace fellow back Kyren Williams.“ How will Rams shuffle O-line after losing 3 players in last 2 weeks? (ramswire) “After Shelton and McMahon went down, the Rams moved Beaux Limmer from left guard to center, and inserted Bill Murray into the lineup at left guard. The question now is whether that will remain the approach moving forward. The good news is the Rams have options. Option 1: Bill Murray and Beaux Limmer The Rams could just roll out the same guys who finished Sunday’s game by plugging Murray in at left guard and Limmer at center. Clearly, they feel good about Murray after keeping him on the 53-man roster and making him active on game days, which can’t be said about some other backup linemen. But during the bye, the Rams could evaluate things more closely and decide whether Murray is the man for the job at guard.“ NFC West: Rams starting center, a UW product, out 4-6 weeks (sports.mynorthwest) “Los Angeles (6-4) has won four straight games, but has also lost several key players to injury. Myles Garrett missed seven games with a knee injury, while starting cornerback Jaylen Watson is out for the season with a shoulder injury. Defensive tackle Kobie Turner is expected to return from injured reserve this month, but Poona Ford is out for the season. The Rams are still expected to be without star receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua for the rest of the month. Nacua will miss at least three more games on injured reserve, while Adams isn’t quite ready to return from his hamstring injury.“ Rams Playoff Picture: What Will It Take to Make the Postseason? (si.com) “It’s not going to be easy for the Rams to make the playoffs . There’s a chance that both the Seahawks and Packers go 10-7. With that said, because of the Rams’ division record, the Rams likely wouldn’t hold the tiebreaker. If the Rams want to safely make the playoffs, they almost need to go 11-6, which would mean a 5-2 record over the next seven games. The Seahawks still have games against the 49ers, Panthers, and Rams on the road. They may not lose all three of those games, but those are potential losses. Home games against the Cowboys, Giants, and Rams could be challenging as well, but are winnable. For the Rams to make the playoffs, the Packers losing as many games as possible is the best path. Jordan Love is playing at an MVP level, but they remain inconsistent on defense and have injuries on the offensive line. The Packers come out of their bye week to play the Rams on the road before facing the Bills and traveling to Chicago. They finish the season at home against the Texans and Lions. However, the Texans and Lions games are winnable and they also play the Saints and Dolphins.“ Fantasy Football Film Room: Breaking down Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start, plus Rams’ backfield split (sports.yahoo) “Corum is the better rusher in my eyes, with nothing bad muttered about Williams. He is still a good rusher himself! The difference is just that Corum can hit the hole with an extra gear at this point. That wasn’t true when Corum was coming off collegiate injuries and was still developing his frame, but Corum looks more athletic in 2026 and the results are felt when he has a chance to break past the second level. Corum always had excellent vision and contact balance, which is why the Rams drafted him as a Kyren clone. Now he’s paired those valuable skills with starting-caliber athleticism.” When the Rams can expect every injured player to rejoin the active roster (ramblinfan) “The Los Angeles Rams have had too many injuries to count, including to key starters and superstars. title: The Rams’ season starts now
summary: The Los Angeles Rams dug themselves out of a 2-4 hole en route to 6-4. They put together a four-game win streak. On the surface it seems like their early season struggles have all been corrected. In reality, their last four opponents have a combined record of 11-26-1. It’s reasonable to look at the last […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams dug themselves out of a 2-4 hole en route to 6-4. They put together a four-game win streak. On the surface it seems like their early season struggles have all been corrected. In reality, their last four opponents have a combined record of 11-26-1. Cardinals 3-7 Chargers: 1-8 Commanders: 3-5-1 Raiders: 4-6 It’s reasonable to look at the last month’s schedule and conclude we really learned nothing about the Rams. Of course, they should be given credit for keeping losing teams losing. Who are the Rams following their recent rash of injuries? What happens when stiffer competition slows LA’s run game and they must rely on an inconsistent and short-handed passing attack? The defense has stymied offenses of late. What happens when they face the likes of Jordan Love, Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy, and Dak Prescott in the coming weeks? One thing is still true: the Rams have three lives left in the NFC playoff picture It will take 10 wins to make the playoffs. In other words, they cannot take more than three losses moving forward without leaving their destiny up to factors outside of their control. When looking on the horizon, LA’s season effectively starts out of their bye week. Week 11: BYE Week 12: vs Green Bay Packers Perhaps the single-most important game left. The Rams are competing directly with NFC West teams in the race for their own division, although the 49ers may be running away with it. They are also indirectly competing against the NFC North . This Wednesday night game is the perfect opportunity to ding Green Bay and bolster their own chances. It carries significant playoff weight. Week 13: vs Kansas City Chiefs Unimportant in terms of the NFC tiebreakers, although the Rams really cannot afford to use one of their remaining three lives this early. Week 14: at San Francisco 49ers Can LA avenge their Week 1 loss where they looked enitely unprepared to play. Week 15: vs Dallas Cowboys Dallas can light up the scoreboard. It will be a tough test for the defense. The offense may need more production than simply grounding the game out on the ground in order to keep pace. Week 16: at Seattle Seahawks It’s tough closing the season out with the Seahawks in two of the final three weeks. The silver lining is that winning both matchups would effectively eliminate Seattle and reinforce LA’s destiny. They must take care of business or they could be left on the outside looking in. Week 17: at Tampa Bay Buccaneers Week 18: vs Seattle Seahawks

full_text: Myles Garrett requested a trade from the Cleveland Browns so that he could go somewhere with a chance to win a Super Bowl, and now the Los Angeles Rams have worse playoff odds than his former team. After 10 games and more than halfway into the season, the Rams have 46% playoff odds according to ESPN’s FPI metric. The Browns have a 59% chance to make the playoffs. Chance to reach the playoffs, according to ESPN's FPI! The Browns and Texans are big beneficiaries of the Drake Maye injury. pic.twitter.com/zu2J003QAg — Seth Walder (@SethWalder) November 17, 2026 In the NFC, the four division winners would be: 49ers Vikings Buccaneers Giants New York has worse playoff odds than L.A., but they are in the NFC East so there isn’t any competition. Except for the Cowboys, who are right on the Giants’ tail. That doesn’t help the Rams, however. The top three NFC teams for wil d card spots would be the Lions, the Bears, and the Seahawks. L.A. isn’t far behind Seattle, just 49% to 46%. Their playoff fates could be decided in Week 16 and Week 18, when the two teams face each other. The Rams have the toughest remaining strength of schedule, by some metrics. The Rams have completed their slate of preseason games. Their real season starts a week from Sunday. What is this Broncos remaining schedule lol? pic.twitter.com/Ay2Zgc3QGA — Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) November 17, 2026 However, in the AFC, the Browns are 6-4, which is already more wins than they had in either of the past two seasons. Cleveland beat the Houston Texans on Sunday and their favorable schedule continues after the bye week with a matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders and rookie Fernando Mendoza. Although the Browns have two games left against the Bengals, Cleveland’s remaining schedule could allow them to win 10 games this season. Pretty ironic for a historically awful team that traded its best player to the Rams — and the best player they got in return, Jared Verse, has zero sacks and isn’t doing much to help. Perhaps where the Browns went right and the Rams went wrong was not in the trade, but in the draft: Cleveland drafted receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, both of whom are having standout first seasons in the NFL. Imagine if the Rams had drafted even one of them. With Drake Maye out for the rest of the season, the Patriots are unlikely to make the playoffs, opening the door for the Browns, who are currently in the seventh seed in the AFC playoff picture. They are followed by the 5-5 Patriots, then the 4-6 Raiders and Ravens. If Cleveland beats the Raiders and Ravens when they meet later this season, they’re almost guaranteed to make the playoffs. The Rams are not. They’ll have to beat the Packers when they return from the bye week. Green Bay traded for Micah Parsons at the start of last season and we see where that’s gotten them. Perhaps not every trade for a edge is something that to rush into.

title: Highs and lows of Fernando Mendoza’s starting debut for Las Vegas Raiders
summary: Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start in the Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 10 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks was a tale of two halves. In the first half, he completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards, with both incompletions being throwaways, and had five rushes for 21 yards and a touchdown. According to Sumer Sports, […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start in the Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 10 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks was a tale of two halves . In the first half, he completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards, with both incompletions being throwaways, and had five rushes for 21 yards and a touchdown. According to Sumer Sports , that resulted in a total EPA of 6.56, an EPA per play of 0.328 and a 55 percent success rate — pretty good numbers. However, the second half was a different story, going six-for-16 with 53 passing yards and one rush for one yard to post a negative 13.49 total EPA, negative 0.642 EPA per play and a 14.3 percent success rate. For the entire game, the No. 1 pick completed 17 of 29 passes (58.6 percent) for 143 passing yards, along with six rushes for 22 yards and a touchdown. That netted a negative 6.93 total EPA, negative 0.169 EPA per play and a 34.1 percent success rate. For more context, Pro Football Focus credited him with a 66.7 percent adjusted completion percentage (accounting for the two throwaways and one drop), a slightly below-baseline (60.0) 59.8 passing grade and a slightly above-baseline rushing grade (65.2) to sit at a 62.2 overall mark. While the numbers above help paint part of the picture, let’s dive into the tape to see the full story. Another boot with a free rusher Sees LB drop to take away the deep crosser (Nailor) Dumps it to Heyward to get 5 on 2nd & 6 pic.twitter.com/NwQQKXuGbn — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 To help get the rookie going, Klint Kubiak dialed up bootlegs on Mendoza’s first three throws. The clip above is the third one and is a great decision by the quarterback. His first read is to see if the go route from the outside receiver is available for a one-on-one opportunity. However, the Seahawks have that covered with the corner underneath and the boundary safety on top of the receiver to execute the Cover 2 side of the Cover 6 call. Mendoza’s next two options are either tight end Michael Mayer, who runs a chip release into a curl route, or wide receiver Jalen Nailor on a crossing/drag route. The MIKE linebacker is all over Mayer to take that away, and the WILL linebacker turns to ROBOT and help the corner against Nailor. Meanwhile, fullback Connor Heyward is working across the formation to sell the run fake and run a flat route. Heyward gets contacted by the edge rusher, who ends up getting pressure on Mendoza. However, Mendoza does a good job of going through his reads, finding Heyward and throwing around the free rusher to dump it to the fullback, who picks up five on second and six to set up a third-and-short situation. This isn’t a sexy throw by any means, but it’s a good process to put the offense in a favorable third down situation. The Natty play/TD run QB draw, great job setting up Spencer Burford's block to score pic.twitter.com/Ib95orsSYx — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 Here, we’ll get a look at the touchdown run that got Allegiant Stadium rocking and is eerily similar to the run the Indiana product had to win the National Championship over Miami last January. It’s third and 10 as the Raiders come out in an empty formation where the Seahawks respond with a five-man box and both safeties deep pre-snap. That’s the perfect look to run a quarterback draw into, and Mendoza sells it well by taking a drop with his first step and eyeing wide receivers Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker post-snap, keeping the safeties in the end zone. Then, he takes off and does a great job of setting up left guard Spencer Burford’s block by getting downfield and pressing the five-yard line. That allows Burford to position himself between the linebacker and ball carrier. Finally, Mendoza shows off some impressive vision to see the field safety overpursue, cut back to the other hashmark and put the ball in the painted area. Best throw he had of the game Slant-Flat concept is covered Bails out of pocket with pressure up middle Can settle and hit White earlier, but eventually finds him on sideline for 22-yarder pic.twitter.com/5DKWS8PVlt — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 If the previous clip was the No. 1 pick’s best play of the game, the clip above is the best throw he made on the afternoon. Seattle starts with a two-high look pre-snap before rotating the boundary safety into the hook-to-curl area to play Cover 3. That takes away the curl from Nailor on the curl-flat concept. Maybe Mendoza can hit Mayer on the flat route, but the linebacker manages to avoid the pick and stay on top of the route. So, that’s a fine decision to hold onto the ball. But the problem is that the pocket starts to break down with Trey Zuhn III getting bull-rushed by Byron Murphy II. Mendoza manages to get out of trouble, but he can settle down and pick his eyes up at the 10-yard line instead of continuing to scramble. That would have allowed him to find slot receiver Cody White earlier — who is wide open on the corner route with a coverage bust from Devon Witherspoon — and hit White with some room to run. Regardless, Mendoza eventually finds White and delivers a strike on the run for a 22-yard gain near the sideline. Missed read/opportunity on the 4th & 1/1st & 10 debacle Boundary S rotates down to play Cover 3 Tucker beats press coverage and has a step on the CB for an explosive play but Mendoza doesn't let it rip Scrambles for 1 yard instead pic.twitter.com/w85mF2BoIC — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 This is where things started to get a little messy for the rookie, as the play above comes with about a minute left in the second quarter. Mendoza had a few missed opportunities for explosive plays in the game, with the one above being the biggest. The Seahawks show a two-safety coverage pre-snap but rotate into Cover 3 with the boundary safety spinning down. Since the Raiders are in a three-by-one formation, the boundary corner is locked in man coverage against Tucker, the Silver and Black’s best deep threat. Tucker beats press coverage and has a couple of steps on the corner, while the field or deep safety isn’t in a position to help the corner on a pass outside of the numbers. Mendoza gets to Tucker in his progression but doesn’t pull the trigger. Maybe left guard Spencer Burford losing control of Murphy discouraged the quarterback from letting it rip, but he has enough time and a clean enough pocket to make that throw. Instead, Mendoza opts to scramble and only picks up one yard. To be fair, this was the play that had the 4th and 1/first and 10 confusion (see the markers on the field and the scorebug on the top of the screen). So, maybe that played a factor in his decision, but this was certainly a missed opportunity. Sack, great blitz design by Macdonald OL and FB step strong with PA fake while WILL, MIKE & CB blitz weak Creates a numbers advantage for the defense and attacks 2 rookies (Mendoza & Washington) Mendoza's lack of feel for pressure shows up too pic.twitter.com/P9QP8rFx6O — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 Part of the reason Mendoza had such a low EPA is that he took six sacks on the afternoon. That was the result of some great play calling from Seattle’s defensive mastermind/head coach Mike Macdonald, and the rookie quarterback’s subpar feel for pressure. This is a perfect play call by Macdonald. Vegas runs a play-action pass where the entire offensive line and the full back work left to sell the run fake, while running back Mike Washington Jr. inserts into the protection scheme on the right edge. Meanwhile, Seattle slants the defensive line to the strong side of the formation as the MIKE and WILL linebackers blitz, on top of the cornerback coming off the edge. So, the Seahawks end up with a numbers advantage, where the Raiders have three blockers (Zuhn, right tackle DJ Glaze and Washington) to account for four pass-rushers (the edge, two linebackers and the corner). Also, Mendoza’s back is turned to the defense, and Kubiak calls…
author: Matt Holder

title: Fernando Mendoza’s shaky starting debut primary focus for Las Vegas Raiders in Week 11 NFL Power Rankings
summary: Fernando Mendoza’s starting debut for the Las Vegas Raiders has come and gone, and ‘shaky’ feels like an appropriate way to describe it. Mendoza was sharp in the first half but then struggled to decipher Mike Macdonald’s pressure looks and the Seattle Seahawks’ defense in the second, leading to the Raiders struggling to move the […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza’s starting debut for the Las Vegas Raiders has come and gone, and ‘shaky’ feels like an appropriate way to describe it. Mendoza was sharp in the first half but then struggled to decipher Mike Macdonald’s pressure looks and the Seattle Seahawks’ defense in the second, leading to the Raiders struggling to move the ball and ultimately losing the game . To be fair, that’s expected from a rookie quarterback against the league’s top-ranked defense, and the No. 1 pick’s performance is the primary topic of discussion surrounding Las Vegas in the Week 11 NFL Power Rankings roundup. Sports Illustrated 19. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 20 Here’s a column on the Fernando Mendoza debut and the question that’s been bothering me: If the Raiders were going to wait on playing Mendoza, why change their minds with the Seattle Seahawks on the schedule? — Conor Orr This is ironic because Orr was one of the many people pounding the table for the Silver and Black to trade Kirk Cousins. I don’t think that it was ever the plan to have Mendoza’s first start against the Seahawks, but John Spytek got the trade offer for Cousins that he was looking for ahead of the deadline. Sure, Aidan O’Connell could have played instead. However, Klint Kubiak and Co. were going to have to rip the band-aid off eventually. Look at it this way: Mendoza probably won’t face a tougher opponent than he did last week, so it’s all downhill from here! NFL.com 21. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 21 The Fernando Mendoza era officially began with an exciting opening touchdown drive. That was it for the day’s Silver and Black entertainment. The Raiders’ limitations were on full display against the Seahawks in the second half, in which they had -17 offensive yards prior to a late field-goal drive. I expect this offense to eventually find a groove with Mendoza after clearing this brutal stretch of games played against Seattle, Denver and Cleveland. — Nick Shook While what I said above is true, the Seahawks are the best defense Mendoza will face this season, it’s not like the Broncos and Browns are cakewalks. Those two rank 13th (-0.05) and 10th (-0.06), respectively, in defensive EPA per play, according to Sumer Sports . That being said, Denver does give up the sixth-most yards per game ( 355.0 ), meaning the rookie could build some confidence by being able to move the ball on Sunday. The Broncos do a really good job of buckling down in the red zone, though, ranking ninth in points per game allowed (20.7) despite giving up so many yards. Bleacher Report 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 17 Fernando-mania has officially arrived in Las Vegas. And for a moment, it appeared that Fernando Mendoza’s first start was going to be a magical one—Mendoza led the Raiders to a touchdown on his first drive. But the first NFL start for any quarterback is usually bumpy—even the first overall pick. And sure enough, for much of the rest of the game Mendoza looked like a first-year quarterback. He wasn’t terrible, and the loss of tight end Brock Bowers to an ankle injury most assuredly didn’t help matters. But Mendoza looked confused at times and held the ball too long, taking six sacks. The reality is that when the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins, they essentially white-flagged the 2026 season. It’s less about winning now than developing the team’s franchise quarterback of the future. In that respect, hanging around against the defending Super Bowl champions has to be at least somewhat encouraging. — Gary Davenport Davenport’s assessment of Mendoza looking confused and holding onto the ball too long is on point. It started toward the end of the second quarter, when Macdonald really ramped up the exotic pressure looks. That led to the rookie having the fifth-longest average time to throw (3.22 seconds) of the quarterbacks who had at least 22 dropbacks in Week 10, per Pro Football Focus . To be fair, even veteran quarterbacks have a tough time deciphering the Seahawks’ pressure packages. For example, Patrick Mahomes’ highest ATTT came in Week 7 against Seattle and was very similar to Mendoza’s at 3.17 seconds . That’s also the only game Mahomes has been above the three-second mark this season. ESPN 22. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 21 Non-QB MVP at midseason: TE Brock Bowers Bowers has played on another level in his third season. Until Sunday’s loss, which he had to leave early because of an ankle injury, he had seven straight games with 70-plus receiving yards. He has also recorded at least 100 receiving yards in three contests. Bowers’ season is even more impressive when factoring in how a lot of his production has come from being lined up on the outside. He has run 96 routes from the outside, totaling 27 catches for 409 yards and four touchdowns on 36 targets. — Ryan McFadden We’re shifting gears to the tight ends here, and it’s hard to argue with McFadden’s logic. Perhaps the biggest ringing endorsement for how valuable Bowers is to the Raiders is that the offense was completely inept last week after he left the game. Even if he isn’t getting targeted, the ‘football robot from heaven’ changes the entire coverage plan for defenses to help get other receivers open. Luckily, he’s considered day-to-day because the No. 1 pick really needs the offense to have its best player on the field to have success moving forward. The Athletic 20. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 20 Breakout player: Michael Mayer As tempting as it is to just give this to Fernando Mendoza after the rookie quarterback’s debut as a starter, we’re going with the fourth-year tight end. Mayer already has career highs in yards (404) and catches (41), and his role is only going to grow after Brock Bowers left Sunday’s game with another ankle injury. — Josh Kendall, Chad Graff Kendall’s/Graff’s logic is correct here, in theory. Mayer should have a bigger role without Bowers in the lineup. However, the former’s numbers are actually much better when he’s on the field with the latter this season. According to Sumer , Mayer has run 88 routes without Bowers and logged 15 targets, 11 catches and zero touchdowns for 0.78 yards per route run and a 17 percent rate of targets per route. With Bowers on the field, Mayer’s target rate is about the same (17.2 percent), but his yards per route run more than doubles at 1.69 with 198 routes, 34 targets, 30 receptions, 335 receiving yards and a touchdown. That reinforces the point above about how the two-time Pro Bowler makes life much easier for his teammates, even if they technically play the same position.

title: Fernando Mendoza era off and running
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a home 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Denver Broncos. Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick made his starting debut […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a home 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Denver Broncos. Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick made his starting debut in Week 10. He started great, scoring a touchdown himself on the ground on the Raiders’ first drive and the Raiders scored a field goal on his second drive. It got rough after that as Seattle adjusted. Mendoza was sacked six times. He completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards. He did have some moments where he showed his poise and accuracy. In the end, it was a rough day for Mendoza, but he showed the game wasn’t too big for him and he will continue to grow. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick played every defensive snap as usual. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick made his third straight start and he looks entrenched as a starter. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick played just nine defensive snaps after playing extensively in the previous two games. He did spell Eric Stokes when he was briefly injured. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played 29 percent in Week 10 after he played 34 percent of the snaps in Week 9 after playing 60 percent in Week 8. He had eight carries for 23 yards against the Seahawks. He is averaging 3.8 yards a carry. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was inactive for the ninth time in 10 games. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick started fir the fifth time, but he played just 40 percent of the snaps and struggled at times. It will be interesting to see how much he plays at Denver. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick was a healthy scratch for the third straight game.

title: Third time’s a charm; Dolphins sign new kicker to replace Zane Gonzalez
summary: Last week, the Miami Dolphins worked out two kickers amidst Zane Gonzalez’s struggles regarding the conversion of field goal attempts — a pretty important task for kickers in the National Football League. Despite impressive days from Ben Sauls and Daniel Carlson, Miami decided to roll with Gonzalez last Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. That decision […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Daniel Carlson #10 of the New Orleans Saints looks on during the third quarter against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, the Miami Dolphins worked out two kickers amidst Zane Gonzalez’s struggles regarding the conversion of field goal attempts — a pretty important task for kickers in the National Football League. Despite impressive days from Ben Sauls and Daniel Carlson, Miami decided to roll with Gonzalez last Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. That decision came back to bite them in the tuchus … big time. In a game in which the Dolphins lost by just two points, Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point try. Those gaffes cost the team the game, and the kicker his job in Miami, leaving general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan, to go searching for his third player at the position during the 2026 NFL season. On Tuesday, the Dolphins signed Carlson to their practice squad — giving the team roster flexibility while being able to call up the kicker to their active roster on game days three times before being required to sign him to their 53-man squad. Carlson — a 9-year veteran — has played for a number of teams in his career. His most recent stint was with the New Orleans Saints. However, Carlson was released earlier this season after going just 8 for 12 on field goal tries in 7 games played. For his entire career, Carlson has made 233 tries on 271 attempts — good for an 86% average. For the sake of comparison, Gonzalez has a career field-goal conversion rate of 79.6%. Our first opportunity to find out if Sullivan has finally found his kicker will take place when the Dolphins travel to Highmark Stadium this Sunday to take on the Buffalo Bills.

title: The Hits Keep On Coming: Dolphins’ Jordan Phillips Suffers Season-Ending Injury
summary: The Miami Dolphins’ defensive line suffered another major blow Tuesday, with defensive tackle Jordan Phillips becoming the third member of the unit to suffer a season-ending injury in the span of two weeks. ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reported that Phillips suffered a torn biceps during Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts and will miss the remainder […]
full_text: The Miami Dolphins’ defensive line suffered another major blow Tuesday, with defensive tackle Jordan Phillips becoming the third member of the unit to suffer a season-ending injury in the span of two weeks. ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reported that Phillips suffered a torn biceps during Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. The Dolphins subsequently placed Phillips on injured reserve. The Dolphins lost veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler to a ruptured biceps in their Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions. Zeek Biggers suffered a knee injury against Indianapolis and will undergo season-ending surgery to repair the lateral meniscus in his right knee. With Sieler, Phillips, Biggers and Grant leading the way, the Dolphins have climbed to 10th in the NFL in total defense and 10th in rushing yards allowed per carry. Those rankings could take a significant hit with three of the four players now sidelined for the remainder of the season. Phillips, a fifth-round selection in the 2025 NFL Draft, had emerged as an important piece of Miami’s defensive line. The 22-year-old appeared in all nine games this season, recording 28 tackles and a tackle for loss while playing approximately 60 percent of the team’s defensive snaps. His importance to the defense went beyond the statistics. Phillips had become a reliable run defender, occupying blockers and allowing Miami’s linebackers to make plays. He was expected to take on an even larger role following Sieler’s injury, with head coach Jeff Hafley previously identifying him as someone who needed to step up and provide leadership to the defensive line. Instead, Miami will have to move forward without all three of its most heavily used defensive tackles. With Phillips and Biggers joining Sieler on injured reserve, the Dolphins are left with Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. as their primary defensive tackles. Miami promoted Jordan Jefferson from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday and also signed former Dolphins defensive tackle Matthew Butler and Chris Smith to the practice squad. The timing of these injuries couldn’t be much worse. Miami travels to Buffalo in Week 11 to face a Bills offense averaging more than 150 rushing yards per game, with James Cook among the league’s leading rushers. The Dolphins will need their remaining defensive linemen to find a way to replace the production of three players who had become central to their defensive success.

title: The Phinsider turns 20
summary: Today marks the 20th birthday for The Phinsider. This site, started by Matt Infante on November 18, 2006, has become a huge community of Miami Dolphins fans as we all ride the roller coaster that is this team. The site has been here through the eras of Nick Saban, Cam Cameron, Tony Sparano, Todd Bowles, […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 29: A closeup view of the Miami Dolphins logo on a sweatshirt prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 29, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Today marks the 20th birthday for The Phinsider. This site, started by Matt Infante on November 18, 2006, has become a huge community of Miami Dolphins fans as we all ride the roller coaster that is this team. The site has been here through the eras of Nick Saban, Cam Cameron, Tony Sparano, Todd Bowles, Joe Philbin, Dan Campbell, Adam Gase, Brian Flores, Mike McDaniel, and now Jeff Hafley. It has seen Daunte Culpepper, Joey Harrington, Cleo Lemon, Trent Green, John Beck, Chad Pennington, Chad Henne, Tyler Thigpen, Matt Moore, Ryan Tannehill, Jay Cutler, Brock Osweiler, Ryan Fitzpatrick, Josh Rosen, Tua Tagovailoa, Jacoby Brissett, Teddy Bridgewater, Skylar Thompson, Tyler Huntley, Quinn Ewers, Malik Willis, and Kyle McCord start at quarterback. (Yes, there have been 22 different starting quarterbacks in The Phinsider’s 20 years.) The Dolphins are 150-184 over the 20 years of the site. The site launched during Nick Saban’s final year, immediately weathered the 1–15 nightmare of 2007 (saved only by Greg Camarillo), and then celebrated the 2008 Wildcat revolution and AFC East title under Tony Sparano and Chad Pennington. We lived through Cameron Wake’s walk-off safety on Halloween night in 2013, the “bullygate” scandal, Jay Ajayi’s back-to-back 200-yard rushing games in 2016, and, of course, Kenyan Drake’s touchdown in the Miami Miracle in December 2018. We debated “Tank for Tua”, cheered the 2022–2023 offensive track meets featuring Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, marveled at dropping 70 points against the Denver Broncos in September 2023, and now navigate the rebuild under Jeff Hafley in 2026. We have been through a lot together over the last 20 years. Infante, in 2011, took a look back at his goals when he founded the site. He wrote: I essentially planned on using this platform as my outlet, my escape, from grad school work. Hell, we all know that this football team drives us friggin’ mad most of the time. So I figured writing about the week to week and year to year disappointments of the Dolphins would be very good therapy. Living up in New Jersey, there obviously aren’t many Dolphins fans to vent with. So I thought that the platform SBN was providing me would also help me cope with the annual frustration that we all have come to expect out of this team by interacting with a few Dolphins fans. Never in my wildest dreams did I think that “a few Dolphins fans” would turn into the community that we’ve all built here. We’re now talking about a Miami Dolphins community that has just under 7,000 members now. The way this community came together was something I never expected. I took over the management of the site in July 2011. I originally thought I would be a temporary placeholder, getting the site through that season before handing it over to someone else as a permanent replacement for Infante. I am not a writer and never thought I would do something like this. Now, 15 years later, I am still here because of you, and I’m so thankful for your support of the site and the community we have built, and the opportunities that have come with it. From Infante founding the site in 2006 to the powerhouse it is today, we have seen the platform evolve over the years, with changes to the site’s look and new ways for you to interact. We have explored videos and podcasts. We have added polls, daily live chats, and more. And we have grown through all of it because of the sheer staying power of the community. Generations of Phinsider readers have bonded over traditions that often felt bigger than the regular season itself: NFL Draft live threads, debate-heavy mock draft seasons, free agency trackers, 53-man roster cutdown threads, and the legendary game-day live threads where hundreds of comments fly per quarter. As The Phinsider turns 20, I truly want to thank you for being the best Dolphins community on the internet. Thank you for reading, commenting, sharing, and discussing. Thank you for the FanPosts, FanShots, and Feed posts over the last 20 years. Thank you for caring about the site, for moderating yourselves, and for looking out for your fellow Dolphins fans. Thank you to all of the fans of other teams who have come to The Phinsider and become members of the community, adding insights about other teams, and maybe some fun-filled trash talking. And, a huge thank you to everyone who is and has been part of the author team on the site. I can never fully express how appreciative I am of each of you. Thank you to everyone just for being here. What brought you to The Phinsider? What made you stay? And what is your favorite memory from the site’s first 20 years? Here’s to the next 20!

title: Tuesday Miami Dolphins Thoughts With The Earl
summary: This game really depends upon your outlook for the season.  If you are a “get the first draft pick at all costs” person, then you like this outcome.  If you want to see a win and positive development, this was a horrible outcome.  It was another of the “close, but no cigar” games the Dolphins […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Michael Taaffe #16 of the Miami Dolphins intercepts a pass during the second quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images This game really depends upon your outlook for the season. If you are a “get the first draft pick at all costs” person, then you like this outcome. If you want to see a win and positive development, this was a horrible outcome. It was another of the “close, but no cigar” games the Dolphins have played this season. Here’s what I saw. THE DEFENSE HAD A MIXED REVIEW In previous games, there was a tradeoff between the offense and defense over which would show up. In this game, the offense was expected to be worse than the defense, with a backup QB getting his first-ever NFL action. However, the Dolphins still couldn’t go a game without some form of tradeoff. In this matchup, it was a tradeoff between the pass defense and the run defense. The Dolphins allowed a completion percentage over 70% and had a run defense that allowed less than 4 yards per carry. The pass defense had its best performance of the season. They held Danny Dimes to 50% completion and a 4.9 YPA average. They picked him off twice, one of which was returned for a TD. They allowed a passing TD and a couple of big plays but were solid in coverage. In a shock to everyone, the Dolphins allowed more rushing yards to TE Tyler Warren (3) than receiving yards (1). Warren was held without a catch until the 4th quarter and was a complete non-factor. Unfortunately, while the Dolphins pass defense stepped up covering the one receiving threat the Colts had, the run defense couldn’t stop the other threat the Colts posed. The Colts rushed for 172 yards on 34 carries, 106 of those yards coming in the 1st half on 19 carries. That’s a 5.6 YPA allowed. They improved a little in the second half, allowing 66 yards on 15 carries and a 4.4 YPA. But on the final drive, they allowed 12 yards on 2 carries that finished off the game. Just once, the team needs a complete performance on both sides of the ball. Now they need a complete performance on both sides of the ball. I will give them some due credit. They limited the Colts to 17 offensive points and were hamstrung by a limited offense, but the run defense was the backbreaker in this game. With the injuries mounting on the DL, I don’t know how they can fix it. SPECIAL TEAMS WAS UNACCEPTABLE We’ll get to the obvious problem in a moment. Bradley Pinion had 3 punts for 134 yards, with a 55-yarder. That’s an average of 44.7 overall and 39.5 on the other two punts. Indy’s punter had 6 for 290, averaging 48.3. The league average is 47.5. Miami still allowed too many yards in the kick return game. They had the 15-yard penalty on Louis, though I won’t complain about penalties since the total was lopsided in Miami’s favor and that penalty was ultimately inconsequential. It is still unacceptable, though. I said on Friday that the Dolphins simply aren’t good enough to win without winning in the margins. This is a young team working to find its identity. They come to work every day and put it all on the line every game. This isn’t the 2024 or 2025 Dolphins with players obviously checking out and Tua laughing on the sideline or Hill taking himself out of a game. This is a bad team playing like they are trying to get the top seed in the AFC. When the kicker, the second oldest player on the team, shanks not one, but two FGs and misses a PAT as the icing on the cake, that is a level of terrible that cannot be measured. After I watched the game and went to bed thinking of all I planned to say about how he cannot remain on the team if the coaches wanna keep the locker room, the Dolphins made my job easier and waived him on Monday. So that is a non-issue now. And I’ve seen the tweets about how the misses keep the tank alive and all that. But I cannot stress enough how not only is tanking a bad idea in general, but you really only tank for a QB, and the 2027 QB class is buns. They are bad. It’s an elevated class due to absences and wouldn’t be considered top prospects in a class like 2018 or 2020. I would love for the Dolphins to get Jeremiah Smith as much as any other fan. But this team is NOT trying to lose. They aren’t playing like they are trying to lose. They are talent deficient, but they aren’t tanking. So when you play as hard as they do and the veteran kicker can’t do the basic requirement of putting the ball through the uprights, then a message needs to be sent, and it was. THIS AND THAT Kyle McCord’s play will be dissected by many others, so I don’t want to get deep into it. I thought he played ok. I thought he played like a player getting his first NFL snaps. His performance isn’t worth getting worked up over one way or another. I said in Friday’s post that a healthy Willis wins this game by 2 scores, and I still believe it. But McCord played well enough for the Dolphins to get a win against another equally terrible team and was let down. The next step will be to see what, if any, level of improvements can be made. The run game has disappeared, and it probably won’t come back for a while. I tried to watch to see how much Indy loaded the box, but I didn’t truly keep track. Indy is a bad team, but Miami will face some good teams coming up; teams with solid to great defenses. My guess is they will load the box and force McCord to beat them. Having Meyer in there instead of Brewer hurt as well, but the OL can only do so much. The good news for the RBs is they were involved in the passing game. All three RBs were targeted 9 times with 8 catches for 62 yards, including the 4-yard loss for Kaytron Allen. If the RBs can contribute in the pass game, then the offense can function about as normally as we can expect. Even with the drop-off, Gordon is still on pace for a 1000 yard season. Caleb Douglas was invisible for most of the game but stepped up late. He will continue to be a force. Washington had the play of the game IMO with the one-handed catch down the sideline. He continues to improve in getting separation and being a factor in the offense. The TD throw was nice also. The TEs were invisible, and that’s a concern. I like Dulcich, and he has potential, but he is playing his way off the roster for 2027. The passing defense stepped up as I mentioned, and its leaders are two rookies. Michael Taaffe logged his 3rd INT this season, and Chris Johnson got his 2nd in consecutive weeks. It should have been his 3rd in 4 weeks, but that Jets WR fell down and they said Johnson interfered. He was a ballhawk in college, and it is showing up now. There are 17 players in the league with 3 or more INTs and only 7 with more than 3. Taaffe has the instincts to be around the ball a lot. His development going into the rest of this season will be interesting to watch. Regarding the kicker position, I would not be opposed to the Dolphins adding a young player – an undrafted rookie or second-year player – to fill the position. Vets are what they are, and while they offer some reliability, I’m all for giving a young player a chance to make his mark. They probably won’t because, well, they are trying to win games. But if they swing and miss with young players, at least they tried. If they get a hit, that’s something they can build on moving forward. I SAID WHAT I SAID Circling back to the opening paragraph, I am not a fan of losing games for a draft pick. I want the Dolphins to win. This game was frustrating because they had it and gave it away. They lost by the margins and lost the game. Unfortunately, this was the last win on the schedule for a while. Unless McCord magically turns into Tom Brady in the next few games, the Dolphins are looking at 1-16. They host the Jets in 2 weeks, but I don’t like that matchup with McCord. They host the hapless Chargers in week 16, and if Willis is back healthy, they’ll have a good…
