title: What Are the Chances of the Vikings Getting “Flexed” the Rest of This Season?
summary: Now that we’re into the second half of the 2026 NFL season, the potential for games to get “flexed” into different time slots has increased. Yesterday, as there were rumors that the Week 12 matchup between the Minnesota Vikings and the Atlanta Falcons at U.S. Bank Stadium might get flexed to Sunday Night Football that […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: A general exterior view of U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that we’re into the second half of the 2026 NFL season, the potential for games to get “flexed” into different time slots has increased. Yesterday, as there were rumors that the Week 12 matchup between the Minnesota Vikings and the Atlanta Falcons at U.S. Bank Stadium might get flexed to Sunday Night Football that week, the league decided to move the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Cleveland Browns to that spot instead. You read that correctly. . .the league moved a game between Cleveland and Las Vegas into a prime time spot, moving a game between the Los Angeles Chargers and New England Patriots out of that spot. So, with Week 12 no longer a possibility, do the Vikings have any other potential chances of being moved into a prime time slot for the rest of the season? Let’s take a look. To briefly review the flex scheduling rules, games can be flexed to Sunday Night Football with 12 days notice between Weeks 11-13 and with 6 days notice between Weeks 14-17, to Monday Night Football with 12 days notice between Weeks 12-17, and to Thursday Night Football with 21 days notice between Weeks 13-17. Basically, time is running short for the league to move games around, particularly if they want to move them to Thursday night. With that, here we go. Week 13: Panthers at Vikings, currently scheduled for 3:25 PM Central on CBS Sunday Night Football : Texans at Steelers Monday Night Football : Cowboys at Seahawks If the league is going to move this matchup into one of those two prime time spots, we’re going to know by this time next week, as it’s the last week that requires 12 days notice before moving a game into either of those spots. (The Sunday night requirement drops to 6 days starting in Week 14, as outlined above.) On top of that, the league has a couple of other matchups they’d likely find more attractive than Panthers/Vikings, such as Jaguars/Bears and Bengals/Browns, depending on which matchups the networks are protecting. Week 14: Vikings at Patriots, currently scheduled for Thursday Night Football Sunday Night Football : Bills at Packers Monday Night Football : Steelers at Jaguars The league would have to make the decision by tomorrow if they wanted to move Vikings/Patriots off of Thursday Night Football because of the 21-day notice requirement. The issue there is that two of the most potentially attractive matchups are already in prime time slots for that week. Chiefs/Bengals and Rams/49ers are both set for the late window on FOX in Week 14, and I don’t know if FOX can protect both of those games or not. If they can’t, one of those could be a possibility. Again, if it’s going to happen, we’ll know by tomorrow. Week 15: Lions at Vikings, currently scheduled for Sunday Night Football Yeah, the league isn’t moving this one. Week 16: Commanders at Vikings, date and time currently TBD Thursday Night Football : Texans at Eagles Sunday Night Football : Jaguars at Cowboys Monday Night Football : Giants at Lions Week 16 could get a little tricky. Vikings/Commanders is one of four games (along with Buccaneers/Falcons, Bengals/Colts, and Panthers/Steelers) that is currently set to, potentially, be a part of a Saturday doubleheader on the NFL Network. The two games from that group that aren’t selected for that Saturday, according to the footnote on the NFL’s schedule page for Week 16 , are eligible to be played on Thursday night. . . or on Sunday afternoon. . . or on Sunday night. . . or on Monday night. It’s Thunderdome out there in Week 16, kids. If both the Texans and Eagles continue to struggle, that Thursday night matchup might be one the league is looking to move off of for a prime time spot. But whether or not they move that Vikings/Patriots game out of the Week 14 spot could play a role in that, too. Lot of ins, lot of outs. . .lot of strands to keep in the dude’s head. The Week 16 matchups are supposed to be determined “immediately after Week 14,” so we’ll see how that works out. Week 17: Vikings at Jets, currently scheduled for noon Central on CBS Thursday Night Football : Ravens at Bengals Sunday Night Football : Eagles at Niners Monday Night Football : Texans at Packers I’m not going to spend a whole lot of time on this one. I just don’t think the league is going to put Vikings/Jets into a prime time spot for any reason, honestly. Week 18: Bears at Vikings, TBD As the league has done for the last few years, the schedule for Week 18 won’t be known until Week 17 is pretty much completely in the books and we know which matchups are going to carry the greatest playoff implications/drama going into the final week of the season. So, should we worry about the Vikings potentially getting their schedule changed over the second half of the season? It doesn’t look like it, honestly, but the league could give us a surprise. The biggest surprise would be moving the New England game off of Thursday Night, but if that’s going to happen, we’ll know about it by tomorrow because of the timing requirements.

title: Vikes Views: Which WR will Step Up in Jordan Addison’s Absence?
summary: Minnesota Vikings WR 2 Jordan Addison is expected to be out for the next several weeks. It hasn’t been the most productive season for Addison, but he has played a lot of snaps. Those snaps, along with new QB Kirk Cousins, will provide a big opportunity for someone to step up in Addison’s absence. Who […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Minnesota Vikings WR 2 Jordan Addison is expected to be out for the next several weeks . It hasn’t been the most productive season for Addison, but he has played a lot of snaps. Those snaps, along with new QB Kirk Cousins, will provide a big opportunity for someone to step up in Addison’s absence. Who do you think is most likely to take advantage of the opportunity? Tai Felton Felton received the most opportunity against the Packers, playing 86% of the offensive snaps. He had 33 yards with 3 receptions on 5 targets, including a nice 24-yard back shoulder catch to set up an Aaron Jones TD. He also had a couple of pre-snap penalties (false start and illegal shift). Jauan Jennings Jennings missed the game due to a calf strain. He’s expected to return this week. He only has 6 receptions on 10 targets this season for a total of 54 yards. Myles Price Price had 49 yards on Sunday, including the beautiful 38-yard TD on a rope from Kirk Cousins. He only played 48% of the offensive snaps, but was able to outgain Felton on the day. He caught all four passes thrown his way. Vikings TEs TJ Hockenson is expected to return soon, and potentially this week. Gavin Bartholomew filled in nicely with three catches on four targets for 36 yards and an easy TD this past week. There’s a chance the lack of production at WR continues and Kirk favors the big guys over unproven WRs.

title: Vikings Debriefing: Daily Norseman Week 10 Postgame Roundtable (A 30-10 win over the Packers)
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 10 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off easily their most complete effort of the season — a 30-10 dismantling of the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. So be honest….DO YOU LIKE THAT? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 04: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates against the Miami Dolphins in the fourth quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Vikings defeated the Dolphins 15-10. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 10 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off easily their most complete effort of the season — a 30-10 dismantling of the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. So be honest….DO YOU LIKE THAT? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle for a minute — get your initial thoughts out about the Vikings beating the Packers in Week 10, 30-10. Brandon Warne : The Vikings went out and had a ‘belt-to-ass’ performance against their biggest rival, completing a sweep with — for my money — their two most impressive/intriguing games of the season. If the Vikings can average 20 points per game with Cousins the rest of the way — they scored 20-plus just three times entering last weekend, and just twice since the opener — this is a damn scary squad. Christopher Gates : Few things in Vikings fandom are more satisfying than watching our favorite team slap the Packers around for sixty solid minutes. There really wasn’t a point in this one where it didn’t feel like the Vikings were fully in control, which was surprising given the trajectory that these two teams came in on. The Packers came off of a 45-point performance against New England the previous week, while the Vikings were coming off of the Monday Night disaster against Buffalo. But after the Packers fumbled on their first possession, it seemed like the Vikings grabbed on to this one and weren’t going to let go. Kirk Cousins provided the sort of quarterback play this team hasn’t had all season, and it let the defense catch a breather after a couple of weeks of being overworked. Warren Ludford : I was a bit surprised by the extent of the blowout. I wasn’t confident before the game when I saw the inactive list. But as the game went on, I realized again how bad the Packers OL is and how that completely compromises their deep ball game, which is what they do. I was pleasantly surprised that Cousins could move the offense and convert 3rd-and-longs. Craig Williams : My initial feeling is excitement. I don’t think the team has looked this much like a legitimate contender since the NFC Championship Game season. Cousins isn’t a top-tier quarterback, but he’s more than good enough to get this offense moving. For the first time all year, it feels like the Vikings have all three phases working in the same direction. I can’t wait to see what the offense looks like once T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison are back in the lineup. Shawn C. : Ecstatic. Given the unique circumstances of Kirk Cousins returning midweek, midseason, to the very place where his first tenure with the Vikings ended, this was the most satisfying regular-season win I can remember. The fact that it was against the Packers was the icing on the cake. Sam Buegler : Man, that was so much better than I hoped – the first half especially. I got nervous during the second half, but the defense held strong, and we got just what we needed out of Kirk to wind down the clock and seal the deal. ————— Question 2: Who was your Vikings MVP? BW : I have the benefit of seeing everyone else’s answers, so I’m going to zig when everyone else zags and say Dallas Turner. He was literally unblockable — not that it seemed like Green Bay put up much resistance — and is making a lot of those Jared Verse conversations look pretty silly right about now. Let’s get this guy signed up long term, please and thank you. CG : Even with the incredible defensive performance the Vikings put on…it has to be Cousins, doesn’t it? After eight games of watching Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz do…whatever, exactly, it was that Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz were doing…seeing Cousins do the little things on offense and move the chains consistently was exactly what this team needed. Throw in the fact that he did it with one full practice and with no Jordan Addison, no T.J. Hockenson, and no Jauan Jennings available, and it gets even more impressive. He was hitting guys like Myles Price, Tai Felton, Gavin Bartholomew, whoever the Vikings were making available to him. As the Vikings get those weapons back and Cousins gets more reacclimated to the offense, things should only get better. WL : Kirk Cousins has to be the MVP despite the defensive dominance. He made the offense work again. CW : Everybody is going to pick Kirk Cousins, and rightfully so. I’m going with Eric Wilson. He was asked to wear the green dot and fill Blake Cashman’s role against a division rival in a big game. That’s not an easy assignment. Wilson stepped up, led the defense, and was all over the field. That’s exactly what good teams need from their depth players. SC : Cousins is the easy answer, given the palpable excitement and enthusiasm for his return. But I definitely want to give a shoutout to Levi Drake Rodriguez, who recorded 8 pressures and 2 sacks. With all the playmakers showing up on defense this season, LDR often gets lost in the shuffle. He was front and center on Sunday. SB : I am going with Myles Price, since I assume someone else will choose Kirk. 4/4, 49 yards, a TD, and averaging 12 yards per catch is exactly what we needed with JA and TJ out. It was fun to watch him start to thrive with Cousins, and I am hoping to see more of him moving forward. ————— Question 3: Who was your Vikings LVP? BW : Outside of a couple of boneheaded penalties early, it’s really hard to isolate anyone who played poorly. Christian Darrisaw doesn’t seem to have the same juice as last year and PFF, for what it’s worth, didn’t particularly enjoy the work of the team’s safety trio of Josh Metellus, Harrison Smith and Theo Jackson. But trying to find an LVP feels like a real stretch here — in a good way. CG : Man, it’s really hard to find a least valuable player after a performance like this. I guess Jay Ward had a dumb penalty on the kickoff that followed the Vikings’ first field goal that gave the Packers good field position. Honestly, that’s probably about the best I can do there. I just can’t remember any other plays from the game where I shook my head and said, “Wow, that was really bad.” I can’t remember who got beat in coverage on the Packers’ one touchdown, but it wasn’t egregious enough for me to single anyone out, I don’t think. WL : Hard to pick a LVP, but I’ll go with Jay Ward for his personal foul early in the game on special teams that gave the Packers good field position near midfield. You can’t give up cheap yards like that with extracurricular activity on special teams. Especially on the road. CW : Surprise pick: Christian Darrisaw. He just hasn’t looked like himself this season. After allowing six sacks entering the game, he gave up two more against Green Bay. That’s eight sacks allowed already, which is a career high. The Vikings won comfortably, so it gets overlooked, but they’ll need better play from one of their highest-paid offensive linemen moving forward. SC : No one really stood out. But if I’m forced to pick someone, I guess it’s CB James Pierre, who probably had the weakest game in an otherwise exceptional season so far. Not worried at all. SB : LVP is a hard category to give out on a week when we crush the Packers. I am not going to single out a particular player, but I will say that the team needs to clean it up when it comes to flags. The reffing crew was calling them tightly, but 7 penalties for 75 yards needs to be fixed. It felt like that was what kept the Packers alive at points, so if we can get rid of those and still perform like we did yesterday, we will be in fantastic shape. ————— Question 4: How much has the Kirk Cousins acquisition changed your outlook for this team? How many wins did you expect them to finish the season with…

title: Notes on the Vikings-Niners Showdown in Mexico City
summary: The 7-2 Minnesota Vikings head to Mexico City later this week to take on the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers in what could be a showdown for the top seed in the NFC postseason tournament in primetime on Sunday Night Football. The 49ers currently hold the top seed, while the Vikings at 7-2 hold the 5th […]
full_text: The 7-2 Minnesota Vikings head to Mexico City later this week to take on the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers in what could be a showdown for the top seed in the NFC postseason tournament in primetime on Sunday Night Football. The 49ers currently hold the top seed, while the Vikings at 7-2 hold the 5th seed as the 7-2 Lions have the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Vikings for the division lead, but have a tougher remaining schedule- including facing the Cousins-led Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium. The Bears also stand at 7-2, but the Vikings have the head-to-head tiebreaker over them and the Bears have the toughest remaining schedule of all. The 49ers have some tough games left after the Vikings as well, facing their division-rival Seahawks and Rams along with a road trip to Kansas City. So, whichever team loses on Sunday night will have a tough time finishing a game better than the winner, which they would need to do to gain the top seed. Preparation The game is taking place at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, which is a high-altitude location 7,352 feet above sea level. That’s over 2,000 feet higher than Denver, for comparison. The thin air in such high altitude presents issues for players, who can become fatigued and dehydrated faster and potentially develop altitude sickness before their bodies are able to adjust to the altitude. The 49ers and Vikings are taking different approaches, both of which have their pros and cons. The 49ers flew straight from Dallas, where they played on Sunday, to Colorado Springs where they will spend the week training at an Air Force Academy location that is about 700 feet lower altitude than Mexico City. The idea is that they will have the week to adjust to the altitude. They did this in a previous game in Mexico City in 2022 and won the game- beating Arizona 38-10. The downside to this approach is that most experts say it takes at least two weeks to adjust to high altitude, rather than just one, and players could suffer altitude sickness while they practice during the week in Colorado. The Vikings, by contrast, are remaining at their training facility in Eagan and will fly to Mexico City on Saturday. The positive of this approach is that they can sleep in their own beds and practice in their state-of-the-art facility all week. But the downside is that they won’t have as much exposure to high-altitude. Update: the Vikings installed a high-altitude chamber at their facility in Eagan to get players used to working in high altitude. The risk is that they could potentially develop high altitude sickness that effects their performance. However, experts say that altitude sickness doesn’t really kick-in until 2-4 days after living in high-altitude conditions. There are other things teams can do to prevent the fatigue and dehydration that comes from playing in high-altitude such as a more carb-heavy diet and drinking more electrolytes leading up to and during the game, and having oxygen available for players on the sideline so they can recover between drives. Apparently the Vikings will have Tyler Williams, head of their training/sports science staff talk with the media this week about their preparation for playing in high-altitude. Mexico City is in the central time zone so there is no need to adjust to the time difference. The 49ers played in Australia week one and spent a week there ahead of time to get used to the time difference. Their opponent, the Rams, did not and did not play well, costing them the game. Preparing for high-altitude is different than time zone differences, however, or a 15-hour plane trip. Both teams are planning to fly to Mexico City on Saturday. Shanahan vs. Flores The key matchup in the game will of course be the #1 49ers offense vs. the Vikings #1 defense. It’s interesting that 49ers head coach and de facto offensive coordinator Kyle Shanahan has never beaten a Brian Flores defense going back to Flores time as a head coach in Miami. It’s a total of just three games, and Flores’ scheme has evolved over that time, but nevertheless noteworthy: 9/15/2024: Vikings 23, 49ers 17. 10/23/2023: Vikings 22, 49ers 17. 10/11/2020: Dolphins 43, 49ers 17. It’s interesting that in each game, Flores’ defense held the Niners to 17 points. But of the three games, the 2023 game at U.S. Bank Stadium may be the most relevant. Kirk Cousins was quarterback for the Vikings in that game, while Brock Purdy was quarterback for the Niners. The Niners had the #3 offense and defense that year, and were 5-1 going into the game while the Vikings were 2-4 after suffering a rash of turnovers early in the season. The Vikings were without Justin Jefferson that game and had Alexander Mattison at running back. The Niners had pretty much the same key players then as now. McCaffrey and Kittle (and Aiyuk) offensively and Bosa, Warner, Greenlaw, and Hargrave and Lenoir on defense (along with Chavarious Ward). The Vikings were able to get off to an early lead, capped by a touchdown catch by Addison where he ripped the ball away from Ward- who had earlier ripped the ball away from Addison for a turnover. The 49ers were able to cut the Vikings lead to 6 points with 13 minutes left in the fourth quarter, but the Vikings were able to mount a lengthy drive ending in a missed field goal, while Purdy threw an interception to end one drive and another to end the game. Cousins managed to throw for 378 yards despite not having Jefferson and was not sacked during the game- although nearly so a couple times. Purdy was only sacked once. But the 49ers had three giveaways in the game while the Vikings only had one. Comparing that game to now, Purdy is more comfortable and experienced in Shanahan’s scheme now, but the Vikings defense then seemed pretty tame compared to now. It was before Cashman and Van Ginkel, Dallas Turner, and Jalen Redmond. The Vikings also had Akayleb Evans at cornerback in that game. But in the most recent matchup, early in 2024 with Sam Darnold quarterback for the Vikings and a more aggressive version of Flores’ defense, Brock Purdy was sacked six times but still threw for over 300 yards. Darnold had 268 yards passing- a big chunk on the one 97-yard bomb to Jefferson early in the game. The 49ers had Deebo Samuel but not McCaffrey. However, Jordan Mason- then with the 49ers- had a big game rushing. Turnovers were even at two a piece (the Vikings’ both in the red zone), but the Vikings also had a blocked punt that led to their first field goal. The Vikings also had a goal line stand early, denying the 49ers points after a failed 4th and goal from the 1. Neither team had much success in the red zone. In both Vikings games, the Vikings got off to an early two-score lead, the 49ers were able to narrow it going into the fourth quarter, putting the game in reach with plenty of time remaining, but the Vikings ended up with a longish drive that bled the clock while the defense prevented a 49ers comeback in the time remaining. It will be interesting to see how the 49ers and Brock Purdy handle Flores’ defense this time around- and how Flores decides to handle the 49ers offense. In the last matchup the 49ers had a lot of quick game options- and they still do- which could make Flores hesitate a bit more with his blitz packages. The 49ers have McCaffrey, Kittle, Keenan Allen, Brandin Cooks, and Deebo Samuel as potential quick game targets. Unclear if Mike Evans will be back for this game, but Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans would travel to Colorado to join the team there and see what he can do in practices. In any case, Flores and the Vikings defense will need to have answers for the 49ers quick game to go with blitz packages. And they do, it’s just that the Niners have a lot of weapons. I could see the Vikings blitzing more situationally, but part of the beauty of what the Vikings are doing with their pressure packages is that there’s always at least a 50% chance of a blitz on any down and the packages are so varied that it’s difficult to…

title: Daily Norseman Reacts Survey: A Different Border Battle Awaits
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Vikings fans and fans across the country. It’s time for our SB Nation Reacts survey for this week, everybody! Time for us to, once again, take the pulse of the readers of the […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates scoring a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Vikings fans and fans across the country. It’s time for our SB Nation Reacts survey for this week, everybody! Time for us to, once again, take the pulse of the readers of the best damn Minnesota Vikings website on the internet to figure out how everyone’s feeling about our favorite football team. We’ve got two questions for you this week, one of which is the same question we ask every week: Do you think the Vikings are heading in the right direction? And boy howdy. . .what a difference a week makes, eh? The Vikings are coming off of the completion of a season sweep of the Packers, Kirk Cousins has given the offense a new lease on life, and they’re getting ready to play the game of the year (of the week) as they head to Mexico City to face off against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday Night Football. It sure does feel like this team is heading in the right direction, doesn’t it? Speaking of that big matchup south of the border, that’s the focus of the other half of our survey for this week, specifically how you think this one is going to turn out. full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 15: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a pass tying a Minnesota Vikings record for a 97 yard touchdown play while Ji'Ayir Brown #27 of the San Francisco 49ers defends during the game against San Francisco 49ers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 15, 2024 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. After half of a season of offensive struggles, the season appears to have turned around with the return of Kirk Cousins at quarterback for the purple. Cousins helped lead the team to their highest point outpout of the season in Green Bay and, more importantly, helped keep the offense on the field to allow the defense to have a rest rather than having to stay on the field for extended stretches. The Vikings’ #1 defense responded by registering eight sacks and forcing three of the team’s four turnovers in the victory. title: Vikes Views: Nincompoop of the Week: Week 10 – Vikings at Packers
summary: The Minnesota Vikings dismantled the Green Bay Packers, 30-10. Even in a 20-point blowout at Lambeau Field, somebody still earns the crown. Let’s take a look at who was a Nincompoop this week. Packers Offensive Line The Vikings defense is going to make a lot of offensive lines look bad. The Packers offensive line was […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Head coach Kevin O’Connell of the Minnesota Vikings hugs head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers after the game at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Vikings defeated the Packers 30-10. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings dismantled the Green Bay Packers, 30-10. Even in a 20-point blowout at Lambeau Field, somebody still earns the crown. Let’s take a look at who was a Nincompoop this week. Packers Offensive Line The Vikings defense is going to make a lot of offensive lines look bad. The Packers offensive line was also missing a few key players. However, there are no excuses for what happened on Sunday. There were plays where four or five Vikings were in the backfield almost immediately. Jordan Love had no chance on seemingly half of his dropbacks. The eight sacks allowed were the most surrendered by any team in the NFL this season. Matt LaFleur One of the reasons the Vikings were able to generate so much pressure was the Packers’ game plan. The Vikings defense is susceptible to the run game, yet Green Bay never seriously tested them. Maybe that’s because the Packers have one of the worst rushing attacks in football. They had some success when they ran the ball, but they abandoned it way too early. When your quarterback is getting battered and you keep asking him to throw deep, the results shouldn’t be surprising. Tai Felton If it wasn’t for his 24-yard reception, Felton would have contributed negative yards to the offense. Two pre-snap penalties from a receiver already struggling to find his rhythm didn’t help matters. Tai has just 99 yards in 26 career games. Felton didn’t do anything obviously wrong, he’ll just need to do a lot more if he wants to remain a regular part of the offense. Packers Special Teams An early missed field goal, numerous penalties, and a late fumble on special teams didn’t help the Packers’ chances on Sunday. They were sloppy from start to finish. On a day when the Vikings’ special teams unit was nearly perfect, Green Bay’s special teams played a major role in the team’s downfall. Christian Darrisaw Not a name I ever expected to put on this list. Darrisaw allowed another two sacks on Sunday, bringing his total to a career-high eight sacks allowed this season. The Vikings finally have competent quarterback play again, and the last thing they need is their franchise left tackle allowing defenders free shots at Kirk Cousins. Darrisaw is struggling to regain his form after a few injury-plagued seasons. My vote goes to Matt LaFleur. I’d probably go LaFleur, Pack OL, Darrisaw, Pack Special Teams, and Tai Felton if I had to rank them.

title: Drake Maye injury: Everything we know about the Patriots QB’s status
summary: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due […]
full_text: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due to what was later announced as an ankle injury. Shortly after the game, information was scarce but the first bits and pieces have started to come in. Based on everything we know, here is what we can say about Maye and his injury situation. What happened? The Patriots started Sunday’s game against the Lions with the ball, and actually moved down the field relatively well; it took them only eight plays to get from their own 25-yard line to the Detroit 3. Once there, however, things started to fall apart. Two penalties bookending an incomplete pass set up a 3rd-and-goal from the 13-yard line, and that play turned into a disaster for the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson easily got around left tackle Christian Elliss, and dragged Maye down from behind and he was climbing an increasingly collapsing pocket. Along the way, the two-time Pro Bowl edge came down on Maye’s right ankle. He did get up under his own power, but Maye showed a noticeable limp while making his way toward the sideline. Once there, he received attention from the team’s medical staff and afterwards headed into the blue medical tent. When he emerged, still clearly hobbled, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was already getting ready to enter the game. Maye slowly walked back to the locker room shortly thereafter, and initially labeled questionable to return by the team. Midway through the second quarter, he was downgraded to out. What do we know about the injury? Neither head coach Mike Vrabel nor any of his teammates were able to provide an update on Maye’s status during their post-game media availability. “Obviously, he wasn’t able to finish the game, so we’ll have to get some more tests run and we’ll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has,” Vrabel said at the podium. “I know that it was a low leg injury. I don’t know the exact details of it but I know he couldn’t go back in. … He couldn’t function. Couldn’t play. Couldn’t run. Couldn’t do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute, or function at that level.” Left tackle Will Campbell, who briefly occupied the blue medical tent before Maye went in, gave some more information in the postgame locker room. “I talked to him,” Campbell told MassLive’s Mark Daniels. “He’s in good spirits and just waiting to hear more information about what it is, and just told him I love him and praying for him and he’s going to be fine. He’s a fighter. Whatever comes his way, he’s going to attack it full head of steam and come back better.” The Patriots will fly back to the United States on Sunday, with some follow-up testing expected to take place after the team’s arrival on Monday. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Initial reports suggest that Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that might keep him out for the remainder of the season. For the Patriots, this is very much the worst-case scenario. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] The Patriots are concerned that Maye suffered a fractured ankle against the Lions. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Drake Maye did not travel back to the United States with the rest of the Patriots, per head coach Mike Vrabel. “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.” [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If indeed diagnosed as a fractured ankle, Drake Maye would “almost certainly” be out for the rest of the season, according to a report by Ian Rapoport. [UPDATE 11/17/2026] Appearing on local radio, Patriots safety Kevin Byard said that Maye was “probably out for the season.” What does it mean for the Patriots? “Any time your starting quarterback goes out and is not able to return, there are questions,” safety Kevin Byard told the media after the game. The questions mentioned by Byard are manifold in the direct aftermath of both the injury and the contest as a whole. Information about severity or a potential recovery timeline is limited, which in turn also limits the avenues the Patriots might have to explore in the immediate or long-term future. What we do know is that for however long Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito will be the top quarterback on the depth chart with third-stringer Behren Morton backing him up. DeVito completed 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each after entering the Lions game midway through the first period. DeVito described his and the offense’s performance after he took over for Maye as “not good enough.” The next chance to improve upon it will come after the Patriots’ upcoming bye, with a Sunday Night game versus the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. New England will not start its on-field preparation for that game until a few days beforehand; the team will return to its usual in-game schedule following the bye. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If the injury is indeed as significant as believed, here is a rundown of how it would impact the Patriots moving forward.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Drake Maye injury update: Patriots teammate drops hint about QB’s outlook
summary: If you were holding out hope that Drake Maye would still return this season, it might be time to adjust your expectations. For the first time since the New England Patriots starting quarterback suffered an ankle injury on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, one of his teammates has commented on the severity of the ailment. While […]
full_text: If you were holding out hope that Drake Maye would still return this season, it might be time to adjust your expectations. For the first time since the New England Patriots starting quarterback suffered an ankle injury on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, one of his teammates has commented on the severity of the ailment. While not asked directly about the injury or any recovery timelines, Kevin Byard did drop a hint about how long Maye might be out. “Our quarterback’s out, and he’s probably going to be out for the rest of the season,” Byard told WEEI’s Rich & Ken on Tuesday. Byard’s statement echoes earlier reporting about the injury . Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle on the opening drive against the Lions, an injury that necessitated him undergoing additional treatment in Germany and flying back to the United States later than the rest of the team. While no official statement has been released by the team on his status, head coach Mike Vrabel mentioned on Monday that Maye being available coming out of the Patriots’ upcoming bye was not expected. That statement plus Byard’s and the reports available start painting a clear picture: anything but the 24-year-old missing the remainder of the 2026 season would be a positive surprise. If that is indeed the case, Tommy DeVito is expected to take over as New England’s starting quarterback. For Byard, the backup quarterback will not be the only one in the spotlight, though. “The reality of the situation is that we have to get behind ‘Tommy Two Chains’ at the end of the day,” he pointed out. “We’re all going to have to do more, myself included. Everybody has to play better around our quarterback. This is honestly before Drake was injured, but we have to play better around our quarterback. We have two choices: we can rally behind this guy or we can pack it up. This is just where we are right now in the season.” Coming off back-to-back blowout losses, the Patriots are entering their Week 11 bye with a 5-5 record and on the outside looking into the AFC playoff picture .
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots vs. Lions snap counts from Week 10
summary: Halfway through the 2026 season, the New England Patriots’ trade for wide receiver A.J. Brown is not looking good. The 29-year-old has appeared in only four games so far, catching just 11 passes for 128 yards. Injuries have been the main reason for his lack of production, with ankle and knee issues seemingly derailing any […]
full_text: Halfway through the 2026 season, the New England Patriots’ trade for wide receiver A.J. Brown is not looking good. The 29-year-old has appeared in only four games so far, catching just 11 passes for 128 yards. Injuries have been the main reason for his lack of production, with ankle and knee issues seemingly derailing any momentum he had built during training camp. On Sunday against the Detroit Lions, he picked up another ailment: Brown left the game in the late third quarter because of a hamstring injury and did not return. On the day, he therefore played only 28 of 59 snaps (47%) and registered two receptions for 27 combined yards. It was the latest in a string of disappointing outings for a player acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles for two draft picks, including a first-round selection in 2028. “I thought he had a good week of practice. He was into it. I think he had a drop and then came back and made a big catch for us there, and unfortunately wasn’t able to finish the game,” said head coach Mike Vrabel about Brown on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday. “A.J. had a good week of practice, was excited about trying to help us win. We knew that he was going to be on a limited basis, wasn’t going to take 95% of the reps. I thought we were headed in the right direction there, but unfortunately we’ll have to see how he comes out here in the next couple days.” Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 35-10 loss . Offense Total snaps: 59 | Time on the field: 25:30 | * denotes starter LG/C Greg Van Roten* (59; 100%), RG Matt Pryor* (59; 100%), WR Mack Hollins* (54; 92%), C Jared Wilson* (53; 90%), LT Will Campbell* (53; 90%), QB Tommy DeVito (49; 83%), RT Morgan Moses* (45; 76%), WR DeMario Douglas (38; 64%), TE Eli Raridon* (37; 63%), TE Hunter Henry* (33; 56%), WR A.J. Brown* (28; 47%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson* (26; 44%), RB Corey Kiner (25; 42%), WR Kyle Williams (23; 39%), RT/FB Caleb Lomu (15; 25%), FB Reggie Gilliam (13; 22%), QB Drake Maye* (10; 17%), RB Lan Larison (8; 14%), WR Efton Chism III (8; 14%), LT Marcus Bryant (6; 10%), LG Andrew Rupcich (6; 10%), TE Cameron Latu (1; 2%) The Patriots offense saw the entire game and season changed after one drive. Starting quarterback Drake Maye hurt his ankle on a third-down sack, with initial reports indicating a fracture that likely would end up sidelining him for the rest of the season. On Sunday, this meant Tommy DeVito entering the game in his place and trying to build on the success the offense has had on its opening series. He couldn’t: the Patriots ended up scoring only once in 10 competitive drives with him at the helm, while Detroit pulled away further and further. The time on the field is a reflection of New England’s offensive ineptitude, and it ultimately led to the team mixing and matching its personnel. Backups such as Lan Larison, Marcus Bryant and Andrew Rupcich saw increased opportunities with the score getting out of hand. That said, there are still a few notable takeaways from the game. The Patriots opted to insert Greg Van Roten at left guard in his first game back from a stint on injured reserve, despite him having played only one in-game snap at the position in the previous six seasons. Van Roten also served as the backup center, snapping to DeVito during warmups and moving there when the O-line rotation started. Rhamondre Stevenson, who had suffered a knee injury the previous week versus the Packers, played 26 snaps in a clearly reduced role. The game script likely also contributed to his usage, same with tight end Hunter Henry. Defense Total snaps: 71 | Time on the field: 32:10 | * denotes starter CB Christian Gonzalez* (64; 90%), CB Marcus Jones* (64; 90%), LB Christian Elliss* (62; 87%), S Kevin Byard III* (62; 87%), S Craig Woodson* (57; 80%), LB Robert Spillane* (48; 68%), DT Milton Williams* (46; 65%), ED Elijah Ponder* (45; 63%), ED Gabe Jacas (44; 62%), ED Dre’Mont Jones* (36; 51%), CB Charles Woods* (34; 48%), DT Cory Durden* (32; 45%), DT DaQuan Jones (30; 42%), DT Joshua Farmer (27; 38%), DT Leonard Taylor III (24; 34%), LB Darius Muasau (23; 32%), DT Christian Barmore (22; 31%), S Jaylen Reed (20; 28%), LB Namdi Obiazor (9; 13%), CB Karon Prunty (9; 13%), S Mike Brown (9; 13%), LB Erick Hunter (7; 10%), CB Channing Canada (7; 10%) Christian Barmore was the subject of speculation before last week’s NFL trade deadline, but he did not get moved when all was said and done. However, he might as well have been: one week after playing a season-low 39% of snaps, he was on the field for only 31% against the Lions. Five other interior lineman surpassed his snap total of 22. Even considering how the game went and the fact that the Patriots are using him as a package player first and foremost, that number is surprisingly low. At this point in time, it appears that Milton Williams and Cory Durden are the clear 1-2 at the position. That said, Sunday’s game showed that the group as a whole needs improvements at the position: Detroit ran over New England at will, in large part because of its ability to reset the line of scrimmage. Speaking of low snap totals, Robert Spillane finished with a 68% playing time share. The team captain, who typically plays close to 100% of snaps any given week was banged up late in the first half and later exited the contest due to an illness. In his place, Darius Muasau took over as the top off-ball linebacker and on-field signal caller wearing the green dot on his helmet. His 23 snaps (32%) are a new season-high. As was the case on offense, the Patriots also managed to give their lesser-used personnel some opportunities on Sunday. Karon Prunty and Channing Canada replaced Christian Gonzalez and Marcus Jones late in the game, while Mike Brown entered the field in place of Kevin Byard. Namdi Obiazor and Erick Hunter also saw some action at linebacker. Brown back in the offensive mix, Kyle Williams spent time with the kickoff returners again during warmups. In the game itself, however, the second-year wide receiver was not used in that capacity; Corey Kiner and Lan Larison were the designated returners, with Marcus Jones handling punts. The core special teamers appearing on all four return and coverage teams consisted of seven players: Darius Muasau, Namdi Obiazor, Mike Brown, Cameron Latu, Erick Hunter, Lan Larison and Karon Prunty. Among the players appearing on three units was fullback Reggie Gilliam, who lined up on kickoff return, kickoff coverage and punt coverage in his first game since being activated off of injured reserve. Not all of it was by choice — *cough* Tommy DeVito *cough* — but most was. At least that means some experience for guys who typically are not getting a lot of it. full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Fans enjoy the pre-match atmosphere before the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The league expressed it’s confidence in the Patriots recovering from their two-game blown-out streak, by removing them from the Week 12 Sunday Night Football lineup in favor of Raiders at Browns. Did you get that? A Patriots game has been replaced by the Raiders and Browns. In the immortal words of Dunder Mifflin’s Michael Scott, “Well, well well, how the turn tables…” The experts not only turned the Pats in the rankings after last week’s debacle of a game, but dumped them on their head. New England now sits at 20th and could conceivably fall lower after the Bye week, depending on the results of Week 11. With Drake Maye out, my guess is that the team will move forward with the quarterbacks on their roster: Tommy DeVito and the backup’s backup, Behren Morton. The coaching staff has two weeks to figure out how to stanch the bleeding on both sides of the ball. Maybe some of the walking wounded will heal up enough to contribute. I still think this team can potentially still win some games, even as banged up as they are. The Chargers (Week 12), Jets (Week 16) and Dolphins (Week 18) are still bad enough to be beatable. We’ll see. My expectations have dropped lower than the rankings, but I still want to watch to see how Mike Vrabel and his men handle the situation. GO PATS!! [-2] 16th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): It feels like the wheels are coming off . [-2] 17th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Rhamondre Stevenson. The six-year veteran is one of the NFL’s best pass-protecting running backs, which has exceptional value when defenses have blitzed quarterback Drake Maye. Stevenson’s stat line isn’t eye-popping — 403 rushing yards, two rushing TDs, 27 catches, 259 receiving yards and two receiving TDs — but his determination to play through a knee injury in Week 10 reflects his team-first approach. On a team with few clear-cut candidates for this honor, that stands out . — Mike Reiss [-3] 19th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): Getting drubbed by the Lions was bad enough, but the news that QB Drake Maye might be lost for the season with a fractured ankle is the real kiss of death for this battered, star-crossed team. This season has been both sad and predictable. Everyone knew the defending AFC champs would struggle with a much tougher schedule. Mike Vrabel’s offseason scandal put a big cloud over the Patriots, too. Then their injury luck ran out in a very big way. This bye is much needed. But they’ve lost three of four, are sitting at .500 (5-5), and can see the Bills, Vikings and Chiefs staring at them on their December schedule. They may not think it’s over, but it is. Stat To Know : With Drake Maye on the field, the Patriots averaged 6.00 yards per play and posted a 52.3% success rate, scoring 24 touchdowns on 545 plays. Without Maye, they only averaged 3.06 yards per play and posted a 37.3% success rate, scoring two touchdowns on 67 plays . [-4] 20th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): The Drake Maye injury has them way down here. They look done. Even with him, they weren’t playing great . [-8] 21st – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): The Patriots took a big drop in the rankings and it might not be far enough. Drake Maye suffered what the Patriots fear is a fractured ankle, per ESPN. At the very least he’ll be out a while and the most likely outcome seems to be that his season is over. That turns the offense over to Tommy DeVito. It has been a long time since he had a few decent games as a rookie for the Giants in 2023 and became a fleeting cult figure. He looked entirely overmatched Sunday after Maye left the game. He had 81 yards on 24 attempts against a bad Lions defense. It’s hard to see how the Patriots keep their season afloat without Maye, unless DeVito somehow plays way better than he did Sunday or the Patriots find some very unexpected help off the street . [-7] 21st – Ian Glendon (Full Press Coverage): New England was routed 35-10 by Detroit and lost Drake Maye to an ankle injury reportedly feared to be a fracture. Tommy DeVito struggled to revive the offense, and the Patriots have lost three of their past four. Until Maye’s status is clearer, New England’s playoff outlook is precarious . That sounds like the perfect long-term project for a CEO head coach who is not responsible for calling plays on either side of the ball . [-8] 23rd – Nick Shook (NFL): The Patriots’ defense is bad. Drake Maye is out for the foreseeable future. A.J. Brown has suffered his third injury of the season. Everything is going poorly for the Pats, who simply aren’t a good football team right now . [-8] 24th – Nate Davis (USA Today): Let’s hope the NFL gets flex-ible in short order, given three of the Pats’ next four games are scheduled to occur in prime time. Mayeday indeed . Before those expectations are proven accurate, however, they will have to go up against a schedule that looks significantly more challenging than last year’s. Unsurprisingly, […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are entering the 2026 NFL season as reigning AFC champions and a realistic team to once again compete for a conference title and the Super Bowl. Before those expectations are proven accurate, however, they will have to go up against a schedule that looks significantly more challenging than last year’s. title: Patriots QB targets after Drake Maye injury include Will Levis, Jimmy Garoppolo
summary: Following a potentially season-ending ankle fracture suffered by Drake Maye, the New England Patriots could find themselves in the quarterback market. Head coach Mike Vrabel indicated Monday that making an external addition wasn’t currently the plan, backing quarterbacks Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton. However, reports suggest the Patriots could explore outside options during their bye […]
full_text: Following a potentially season-ending ankle fracture suffered by Drake Maye, the New England Patriots could find themselves in the quarterback market. Head coach Mike Vrabel indicated Monday that making an external addition wasn’t currently the plan, backing quarterbacks Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton. However, reports suggest the Patriots could explore outside options during their bye week. Most likely, any addition would fill the No. 3 quarterback role, with DeVito and Morton expected to receive increased practice reps throughout the week. That addition could come from another team’s practice squad or the free-agent market. However, with the Patriots sitting at 5-5 and potentially still eyeing a playoff spot , perhaps more aggressive options are worth exploring. Here are five quarterbacks who could be potential fits moving forward. Jimmy Garoppolo The Patriots’ second-round pick in 2014 is the most notable free agent currently available. Garoppolo did not sign with a team this offseason after playing just 84 offensive snaps for the Los Angeles Rams over the past two seasons as Matthew Stafford’s backup. That means his last extensive action came in 2023 under Josh McDaniels in Las Vegas. In six games, Garoppolo completed 65.1% of his passes for 1,205 yards, seven touchdowns and nine interceptions. The 35-year old has more experience in the Patriots’ offensive system than any available options, but has struggled to stay healthy and produce consistently in recent seasons. Bailey Zappe Another former Patriot, Zappe overlapped with Vrabel in Cleveland during the 2024 season, when the head coach served as a personnel consultant. Zappe started just one game that year after making eight starts for New England across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He went 4-4 as a starter where he gave rise to the infamous Zappe Fever among Patriots fans. Zappe also spent time with the Kansas City Chiefs before beginning this season on the New York Jets’ practice squad. The Jets released him in late September and he has remained unsigned. Will Levis Drafted by Vrabel and the Tennessee Titans with the 33rd overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Levis spent one season playing under the coach before his departure. Levis went 3-6 in nine starts as a rookie and was eventually benched the following season before the Titans selected Cam Ward with the No. 1 overall pick. Levis missed all of last season after undergoing shoulder surgery and now resides on the Jets’ practice squad, meaning the Patriots would need to sign him to their active roster. Derek Carr The veteran quarterback retired ahead of last season, citing injuries to his right throwing shoulder. However, Carr has left the door open to a potential comeback if the right opportunity presents itself with a Super Bowl contender. While Carr has spoken highly before of Vrabel, his final season under Josh McDaniels in Las Vegas in 2022 ended poorly, which may not make New England that special situation. Still, his familiarity with the offensive system and extensive starting experience would make him an option if he were willing to return. Dorian Thompson-Robinson Another quarterback who was with Vrabel in Cleveland during the 2024 season, Thompson-Robinson started two games for the Browns that year. He now resides in the UFL, where he is expected to serve as Rhode Island’s starting quarterback next season. The 27-year-old struggled during his NFL opportunities, but his athleticism could make him an intriguing option for the Patriots to handle scout-team duties and provide depth at the position.

title: Patriots margin of error ‘basically at zero’ after loss to Lions
summary: Even though they are still 5-5 and only one spot outside of the playoff picture, the New England Patriots’ season is at a crossroads. Injury questions with none more consequential than Drake Maye’s are one part of it, but so is the performance on the field. The Patriots are heading into their Week 11 bye […]
full_text: Even though they are still 5-5 and only one spot outside of the playoff picture , the New England Patriots’ season is at a crossroads. Injury questions with none more consequential than Drake Maye’s are one part of it, but so is the performance on the field. The Patriots are heading into their Week 11 bye off a two-game losing streak, with neither of the contests particularly competitive. The message coming out of the locker room is therefore clear: get it together, or else. “We have a seven-game stretch that we have to – the margin of error is basically at zero,” said safety Kevin Byard after the Patriots’ 35-10 defeat at the hands of the Detroit Lions on Sunday. “We have to find a way to string some wins together. We have to start playing together as a team, and it’s going to start in practice. Honestly, I feel like we had a great week of preparation this week. We’re just searching for answers right now.” The Patriots did not stand a chance against the Lions in Munich over the weekend. While one could play the “what if” game in regards to Maye exiting the contest after one series, fact is that neither the offense nor the defense looked particularly capable of, or at times even interested in, putting up a fight. The end result was jarring. Not only were the Patriots out-scored by 25 points, they also were out-gained by a whopping 343 yards. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs by himself put up more yards (252) and touchdowns (2) than all of New England’s offense did — despite playing just 69% of Detroit’s offensive snaps. Long story short, this was a total collapse. It was also one the team needs to quickly put behind itself in order to move forward. Unsurprisingly, head coach Mike Vrabel was trying to instill a fresh mindset right after the game. “We’re 0-0,” he said during his post-game presser. “We’re heading into a bye. We have to get some things fixed and changed and corrected, and figure out ways to win as opposed to what we’re doing right now, which is not giving ourselves enough of a change.” The first step in that process is making sure the locker room stays united, even though Maye reportedly missing extensive time will make for a challenging environment. For Byard, one of the team’s captains, doing so will not start by any raw-raw gestures but with the performance put forward every day. “We have to perform better,” he said. “Bottom line in this league, talking, motivational speeches, getting guys up on the sideline, it means nothing if we’re not playing well. We’re not playing connected as a team. We’re not playing complementary football. I would have bet my paycheck today that we wouldn’t put that performance out there that we did today. It just sucks right now. We are in a bit of a slump, injuries are piling up. It’s all type of things. But, obviously, going to a bye week, I’m going to take some time off, take my mind off of things and try to recharge.” The Patriots as a whole are in need of that. Whether they come out improved on the other side will be up to them, even though the circumstances are difficult.

title: Travis Etienne Jr. looks to find his footing against Bears
summary: Travis Etienne Jr. returned to action for the New Orleans Saints this past weekend, but his first game back did little to change the team’s run game issues. After missing five games with a hamstring injury, Etienne finished the 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers with eight carries for 14 yards and three receptions for […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 13: New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. (3) cuts back to gain more yardage and a first down during the Detroit Lions versus New Orleans Saints game on Sunday September 13, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Travis Etienne Jr. returned to action for the New Orleans Saints this past weekend, but his first game back did little to change the team’s run game issues. After missing five games with a hamstring injury, Etienne finished the 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers with eight carries for 14 yards and three receptions for 20 yards. It was a quiet afternoon for the running back, who had been expected to provide a boost to an offense that desperately needs more production from its backfield. The Saints couldn’t get much going offensively, and Etienne averaged just 1.8 yards per carry in his return. Still, there is reason to believe he can become a more productive part of the offense as he gets further removed from the injury. Before going on injured reserve, Etienne had rushed for 128 yards on 30 carries through his first three games with New Orleans. He also added 11 receptions for 51 yards. His ability to contribute as both a runner and receiver gives the offense another dynamic playmaker, but the Saints have to get him into a rhythm. The Saints will need more from that group when they travel to face the Chicago Bears next week. Etienne should have a better opportunity to settle into his role after getting his return to game action out of the way, although the workload and production will certainly need to improve. His return alone was not enough to fix New Orleans’ rushing attack against Carolina. The Saints need the version of Etienne they expected when he invested in him this offseason. A stronger performance against Chicago would be an important step toward giving the offense a more dependable run game and making his return meaningful.

title: Saints vs. Panthers: The good, the bad, and the ugly in Week 10
summary: The Good: Jordyn Tyson The Saints rookie wide receiver caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in just his second career game. He made a great diving catch over the middle to move the chains and also had some tough catches in traffic. Had this been his first game, he would have tied the […]
full_text: The Good: Jordyn Tyson The Saints rookie wide receiver caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in just his second career game. He made a great diving catch over the middle to move the chains and also had some tough catches in traffic. Had this been his first game, he would have tied the record for most receptions in a debut since the AFL-NFL Merger in 1970. Tyson played 45 snaps on Sunday compared to just 18 last week and looks to be fully integrated into the offense now. The Bad: Rushing Offense and Defense The Saints rushing attack once again produce a lackluster performance on Sunday. Tyler Shough was the leading rusher for the second time this year with just 25 rushing yards. Running backs Travis Etienne Jr, Audric Estime, and Alvin Kamara ran 17 times for just 24 yards. The Panthers are far from a good run defense, as entering the game on Sunday they were allowing an average of 133 rushing yards per game which was one of the worst marks in the NFL. The Saints have no variety in their offense and have no ability to sustain drives if the passing game is shut down. Compare that to the Panthers who were able to run the ball consistently with Chuba Hubbard. The Panthers did not turn the ball over and won the time of possession battle thanks to their commitment to the ground game, something the Saints have not been able to do all year. The Ugly: The entire first half The Saints are the worst first half team in football. They have trailed in every first half this season, and once again failed to do anything at all on offense until the middle of the third quarter. They turned it over three times (including a turnover on downs) and punted twice. Their deepest drive into Panther’s territory ended at the 25-yard line when they gained 9 yards on 1st down and then ran the ball three times for no gain, no gain, and -1 yards resulting in a turnover on downs. All this while the defense held Carolina to just 7 first half points makes it even worse. This has been a problem in every game under Kellen Moore in the last two years. This must be fixed otherwise this coaching staff may be shown the door.

title: Giants-Jaguars matchup: Jacksonville defense will look familiar
summary: The New York Giants return to action in Week 11 when they take on the Jacksonville Jaguars.. The 5-3-1 Giants enter the game as 5.5-point underdogs at home against the 7-2 Jaguars, per FanDuel. The Giants are coming off of a frustrating, and potentially significant, loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 10, while the […]
full_text: The New York Giants’ offense huddles before a play. | Getty Images The New York Giants return to action in Week 11 when they take on the Jacksonville Jaguars.. The 5-3-1 Giants enter the game as 5.5-point underdogs at home against the 7-2 Jaguars, per FanDuel . The Giants are coming off of a frustrating, and potentially significant, loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 10, while the Jaguars are riding a 3-game winning streak that features performances of 42, 33, and 40 points. The Giants are entering the toughest stretch of their schedule, and this game is believed to be an early litmus test to see if they have what it takes to hang with the best the NFL has to offer. The last time the Giants were significant underdogs, they responded by outplaying the Houston Texans and delivering a stunning upset following a bad loss to the Saints. Can the Giants’ offense respond to the loss to the Commanders and keep pace with one of the most prolific units in the NFL? Stats that matter The Jaguars’ scheme The Jacksonville Jaguars aren’t a team the Giants see all that often, and this is the first time they’ve faced off with Liam Coen as head coach and Anthony Camponile calling the defense. So with that in mind, the best place to start is with an overview of the type of defense the Giants will be facing. And in that, the Jags are more familiar than we might have expected. In fact, the schedule makers have done the Giants a low-key favor by making this game after the Eagles and Commanders. That’s because Camponile has spent time under both Vic Fangio and Brian Flores and runs a hybrid defense that incorporates elements of both schemes. The Jaguars run a high rate of Cover 3, Cover 4, and Cover 6 shells, much like the Eagles. And like Fangio, Camponile likes to use sophisticated coverage rotations to move between looks and shells after the snap. As we’ve seen with the Eagles and Fangio’s various acolytes around the NFL, the sophisticated rotations are a good way to both limit explosive plays and help create pressure passively. The rotations help confuse quarterbacks and keep the ball in their hands, giving pass rushers time to work. At the same time, the use of stunts, twists, and simulated pressures confuses blocking schemes and wastes blockers, creating advantageous match-ups elsewhere. The Jaguars start the above play in a classic Cover 4 shell, but walk a safety down to cover the slot just before the snap. Combined with the field-side cornerback (bottom of the screen) taking inside leverage, that clues us that they’re actually playing a Cover 3. The Jaguars respect the Texans’ play-action, with a fifth defender coming downhill to gap out the potential run, while the second level defenders freeze. The play design is also able to hold the free safety, keeping him from getting to the vertical route in time. The play is a big gain for Houston, but only because the protection holds up and C.J. Stroud is able to layer the ball over the trailing defender and put it where only Nico Collins can make the play. The Jaguars’ blitz rate is on par with the “Fangio Adjacent” defenses in the NFL at just 23.7% (10th-lowest). But when Camponile he does blitz, he uses similar structures as Brian Flores. Flores builds the blitz into every aspect of his defense, showing heavy pressure to gap-out the offense in the run game while creating uncertainty as to which defenders are — or are not — rushing. This play shows the other side of the Jaguars’ defense. There’s significant milling around the line of scrimmage, with all but three defenders crowding the tackle box. It’s almost impossible to know at the snap who’s rushing, who isn’t, or what coverage is even being called. They ultimately drop into a split-field coverage and there’s an opportunity for an explosive play down the sideline. However, the pressure and confusion force the ball out on the hot-read before Ward has a chance to see the open man down the field. Can J.J. McCarthy stay explosive? One of the biggest aspects the switch to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback has been unlocking the explosive elements to the Giants’ passing game. That could be significant in this game because, as Gus Logue of Big Cat Country tells us , the Jaguars have been hurt by explosive passes in the past. They’re currently the sixth-worst defense in the league in defending explosive passes (+0.82 EPA/play), despite playing the likes of the Indianapolis Colts, Baltimore Ravens, and Tennessee Titans over the past three weeks. None of those teams are offensive juggernauts this year, and while that doesn’t mean the Jaguars are a paper tiger (no pun intended), there might be an opportunity to exploit. Right now, McCarthy leads the NFL with an average of 10.4 air yards per pass while still having a good-enough completion percentage of 64.7. For context, Joe Burrow has a completion percentage of 66.4 percent, but is only averaging 7.4 air yards on his passes. And while some of McCarthy’s aggressiveness downfield has been due to third-and-long situations, he’s still been very willing to attack downfield. QB Time To Throw & Average Depth Of Target over last 6 weeks pic.twitter.com/uM5O6Fxqle — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) November 17, 2026 The Giants have speed on their offense to threaten defenses vertically. Malik Nabers is the Giants’ go-to receiver down the field, but they’ve also used Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields to attack the perimeter. They’ve also recently begun using Jalin Hyatt as a “sacrificial X” receiver, sprinting down the field to force defenses to respect the vertical aspect. McCarthy has attempted deep passes to Hyatt twice now, each time just failing to connect for a big play, and it could be worth going to that well again. The Giants don’t want to live on deep, low-percentage throws. Doing so will keep their offense volatile and unsustainable. However, they’re going to need to be as aggressive as possible in this game to score touchdowns. Not only do questions (or outright concerns) about placekicker Dominic Zvada remain, but the other side of the ball sees a Jaguars’ offense that is among the best red zone offenses in the league, going against a Giants’ defense that’s one of the league’s worst in the red zone. The Giants can not force their defense to try and win the game single-handed, which means hitting their explosive plays whenever they can get (or create) the opportunity. Run the ball, or at least simulate a run game The Giants have done much better running the ball since getting Cam Skattebo more involved. Skattebo had a career day against the Houston Texans in Week 7 and ran well against the Commanders after returning from his hamstring injury, with a combined 202 yards and three touchdowns in those two games. The Giants should remain committed to their identity as a running team. However, they should also be willing to extend the running game if they aren’t finding room around the line of scrimmage with the arrival of Jordan Davis and Davon Godcheaux on the Jaguars’ defensive front. Skattebo had 121 total yards against the Texans, and 122 total yards against the Commanders, which includes a combined 41 receiving yards. Skattebo, Devin Singletary, and Gregory Desrosiers all have upside (in different forms) as receiving threats out of the backfield. And while the Jaguars’ blitz packages could frustrate their pass protection as well as running game, there could be opportunities to use the backs to replace the blitzing defenders and keep the offense on schedule. Using their running backs as receiving threats is also a potentially useful deviation from their usual tendencies. The Giants love to use 22-personnel packages with two backs and two tight ends on the field. Personnel usage by team has a few major outliers: – Raiders: lowest 11 and highest 12 personnel rates in the league – Rams: Most 13 personnel by 11 points – 49ers/Chargers/Dolphins: 2-back sets galore, especially 21 personnel – Giants: 22 personnel on 19% of plays,…

title: ‘5 questions’ about the Jacksonville Jaguars: Is it Super Bowl or bust?
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars will be the best team the New York Giants have faced this season when the teams meet on Sunday. Let’s learn more about the Jaguars in this week’s ‘5 questions’ segment. Gus Logue of SB Nation’s Big Cat Country provides our answers. Ed: The Jaguars, obviously, went all-in to improve the roster […]
full_text: The Jacksonville Jaguars will be the best team the New York Giants have faced this season when the teams meet on Sunday. Let’s learn more about the Jaguars in this week’s ‘5 questions’ segment. Gus Logue of SB Nation’s Big Cat Country provides our answers. Ed: The Jaguars, obviously, went all-in to improve the roster at the trade deadline. After going 13-4 a season and being that aggressive at the deadline, has this become a year where anything less than a Super Bowl appearance makes the season a disappointment? Gus: At this point, anything less than a Super Bowl victory would be disappointing for the 2026 Jaguars. The new regime has been “strategically bold,” making aggressive and unorthodox moves to bolster a well-balanced roster that already boasts a great quarterback and an even better coaching staff. Jags fans appreciate that the team is genuinely trying to win it all, especially after so many seasons in the gutter, rather than letting this opportunity slip by. Jacksonville’s moves at the trade deadline do fall in the “win now” bucket but I wouldn’t necessarily categorize it as an “all-in” approach. The Jaguars will be contenders for the next several seasons — not just for 2026. Ed: If I gave you the option of taking Trevor Lawrence or any other current quarterback in the NFL, would you keep Lawrence? If not, who would you take? Gus: I would definitely take Patrick Mahomes. A few other quarterbacks can match his playmaking ability from both inside and outside the pocket, but nobody does it like him in clutch moments. Josh Allen and a healthy Lamar Jackson would probably still clear Lawrence, but if I were tiering quarterbacks, I’d have a “Zeus” category for Mahomes, an “Olympians” category for Allen, Jackson, Lawrence, Joe Burrow, Drake Maye, and Caleb Williams, and maybe a “demigods” tier for guys like Jaxson Dart and J.J. McCarthy who have shown special flashes but aren’t yet considered football deities. I have zero qualms with how Lawrence is playing the position right now. Ed: If you could take one player off the Giants’ roster and put him into Jacksonville’s lineup, who would it be? Why? Gus: The idea of Malik Nabers in Liam Coen’s offense makes me salivate, and the thought of Arvell Reese in Anthony Campanile’s defense gives me goosebumps. I might’ve said Jevon Holland before Jacksonville traded for Jessie Bates III last week. Andrew Thomas would probably be the responsible choice. But I will go with Abdul Carter, who would arguably provide the most game-changing plays for Jacksonville. Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker already occupy the starting edge positions, and the team is looking forward to second-year pro B.J. Green II returning from injured reserve, but another pass rusher could not hurt. Once the team starts seeing elite quarterbacks each week in January, it’d be handy to have a guy like Carter. Ed: Tell us about one offensive and one defensive player Giants fans should be paying attention to on Sunday? Gus: On offense, look out for Parker Washington. This kid isn’t just a fun little success story as a former sixth-round pick who first carved out a role on special teams. At least not anymore. Washington has blossomed into a borderline top-10 NFL wide receiver and the unquestioned engine of Jacksonville’s offense. The Penn State product will be more widely recognized in the tri-state area after this weekend. On the other side of the ball, look out for fourth-year linebacker Ventrell Miller. The former Gator has filled in wonderfully after offseason 2025 Pro Bowler Devin Lloyd departed in the offseason. Miller plays like a missile against the run. Ed: What is the Jaguars Kryptonite? On offense? Defense? If the Giants are going to win the game, how and what do they need to attack? Gus: The Jaguars’ biggest weakness is its offensive line. It’s been a “good enough” unit for most of the season, but the teams that pose the biggest threat to Jacksonville are those with a dominant front four that controls the line of scrimmage. If you can shut down the Jaguars’ running game and constantly heat up Lawrence, you’ll have a shot. On defense, the Jaguars allow the lowest EPA/play on short passes (-0.23) and the fifth-lowest mark on intermediate passes (-0.1), but they rank sixth-worst against deep passes (+0.82). Bates was brought in to help clean that up, and Travis Hunter gets better every week, but Jacksonville has to do a better job of limiting explosive passes — even if they’re not allowing many such attempts in the first place. The Jaguars have the horses to contain Cam Skattebo but they should be wary of Nabers and New York’s front seven.

full_text: Nikko Reed with the Chargers. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants are reportedly signing cornerback Nikko Reed , who was dropped from the 53-man roster on Monday, to their practice squad. Reed takes the place of running back Eric Gray , who was released from the practice squad on Tuesday. Reed, 23, was signed off the Los Angeles Chargers’ practice squad on Sept. 19. He played in three games for the Giants, exclusively on special teams. He made one tackle. Reed was cut on Monday when the Giants signed veteran special teams player and defensive back Tavierre Thomas off the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad. Gray was a fifth-round pick by the Giants in 2023. He played in 34 games for the Giants over three seasons, with 31 carries for 79 yards rushing, 2.5 yards per attempt. Gray was released when the Giants cut their roster to 53 players before the season started, but was re-signed to the practice squad two weeks ago.
