title: 5 NY Giants-Jacksonville Jaguars storylines: Time to step up in class
summary: The calendar says mid-November, and the New York Giants are playing meaningful games at this time of year for the first time since 2022. Let’s look at some of the storylines for Sunday’s matchup at MetLife Stadium against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Entering the heavyweight division When the two teams line up on Sunday, it will […]
full_text: The calendar says mid-November, and the New York Giants are playing meaningful games at this time of year for the first time since 2022. Let’s look at some of the storylines for Sunday’s matchup at MetLife Stadium against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Entering the heavyweight division When the two teams line up on Sunday, it will mark the first time this season the Giants will look across the field at a team with a winning record. The 6-4 Los Angeles Rams are currently the only winning team the Giants have faced, but the Rams were 0-1 when the teams met. Los Angeles won that game, 28-6. The Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart seven plays into that game, so perhaps that blowout is not indicative of how the Giants stack up. Five of the Giants’ final eight games this season are against teams with winning records. Whether they win on Sunday or not, how competitive the Giants are might tell us a lot about how well or how poorly the remainder of the season might go for the NFC East division leaders. Kick return merry-go-round Gunner Olszwewski was expected to be the Giants’ primary punt and kickoff returner. Only, he suffered a torn Achilles in training camp. Braxton Berrios got that spot, and suffered a season-ending foot injury after four games. Along came Charlie Jones. This week, after some ball security issues, out went Jones. The Giants have also lost Tryone Tracy, who has been their best kickoff returner, for a few weeks with a hamstring injury. They have tried Devin Singletary on kickoff returns, but he doesn’t really have the speed to succeed in that role. They have tried rookie Gregory Desrosiers, but he fumbled a return last week against the Washington Commanders. Now, along comes Xavier Gipson as the replacement for Jones. Gipson is in his third tour with the Giants, though he has never played a game for them. He has career averages of 9.1 yards returning punts and 25.9 yards returning kickoffs. That’s good. His 12 fumbles in 163 career touches, one every 13.6 touches, is bad. Jones had become an adventure in recent weeks. The Giants felt they had to try something different, but there is no guarantee that Gipson will be any better. One thing to watch: As the games get more important, might the Giants use starting cornerback Deonte Banks on kickoff returns? Banks was fantastic in that role last season, averaging 32.7 yards on 19 returns, including a 95-yard touchdown. He was, however, only a part-time defensive player last season. Now, he is probably the Giants’ best cornerback. ‘Hold on to that ball, Petey!’ That is one of the famous lines from the movie ‘ Remember the Titans ’. Holding on to the ball is something the Giants need to learn how to do. The Giants have 17 fumbles in nine games. Only the Green Bay Packers, who have played 10 games, have more with 18. The Giants and 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers average a league-worst 1.9 fumbles per game. It should be obvious that the Giants are going to have a difficult time beating top-tier teams if their ballcarriers keep putting the ball on the ground. By the way, the National Weather Service says there is a 40% chance of rain in East Rutherford, N.J. on Sunday. Adventures of the right hashmark Giants’ owner John Mara has a fair amount of power in league circles. Can he use it to push through an emergency rule change that placekickers get to choose which hashmark they kick from on field goals as well as extra points? Dominic Zvada and the Giants’ playoff hopes would appreciate it. By now, it has been well-documented that all six of Zvada’s missed field goals this season have come from the right hashmark . In all seriousness, the Giants need to hope Zvada has that issue figured out by Sunday. Turn up the heat, Dennard Giants’ defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has been throwing caution to the wind and dialing up the heat in recent weeks. Three times since Week 4, Wilson has called for the blitz on more than 50% of passing downs. Only once in that stretch has he blitzed less than on 40% of passing downs. Overall, NextGen Stats has the Giants blitzing on 40.6% of passing snaps. Only the Minnesota Vikings (a ridiculous 72.3%), Tampa Bay Buccaneers (43.9%), and Washington Commanders (42.1%) have blitzed more. This shapes up as one of those weeks when dictating to Jaguars’ quarterback Trevor Lawrence seems like a good idea. title: NY Giants news: Giants playoff paths, possible Kayvon Thibodeaux return, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants hit the practice field for the first time this week. Cowboys’ futility keeps Giants in control of NFC East despite division loss | New York Daily News The Giants have eight games remaining. Winning half of those games […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants hit the practice field for the first time this week. Cowboys’ futility keeps Giants in control of NFC East despite division loss | New York Daily News The Giants have eight games remaining. Winning half of those games should be good enough to win the division. But three of their next four are daunting: They’ll host the Jaguars, visit Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts (3-7), return home to face the 49ers (8-1) and then fly to the Pacific Northwest to take on the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4). If Harbaugh’s Giants can split those games and enter the home stretch at 7-5-1, they should feel good about their ability to close out the NFC East and return to the playoffs for the first time since 2022. If they only win one of those four, however, December and January will grow very uncomfortable in East Rutherford, N.J. The Giants will host the Cleveland Browns (6-4) on Dec. 20. They’ll travel to the Detroit Lions (7-2) for Monday Night Football on Dec. 28 after Christmas. Then that will set up a Jan. 3 road game at Dallas that might end up deciding the entire division, before finishing up by hosting the sorry Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) in Week 18. Giants have given up the second-most DPI yardage Defensive Pass Interference Penalties MIN is still sitting at ZERO – not a single DPI called against the Vikings this season. pic.twitter.com/gNBnjRmacW — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) November 16, 2026 NFL Power Rankings: Stacking all 32 teams for Week 11, plus non-QB MVPs | ESPN.com Non-QB MVP at midseason: TE Isaiah Likely . Likely has had success with Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy at quarterback. He has already set a new career high with 575 receiving yards. The Giants’ offense wouldn’t be nearly as good if he wasn’t their first free agent signing. Likely has also been incredibly consistent, with at least 50 receiving yards in six games and just one drop. That, as well as Likely’s team-high seven touchdowns, are the differentiators that put him ahead of wide receiver Malik Nabers for this honor. NFL Week 10: The highest-graded player at every position | PFF Safety: Ar’Darius Washington, New York Giants: 89.9 PFF overall grade, 54 defensive snaps. Washington earned an 89.9 PFF overall grade in a 24-21 loss to the Commanders, the best among the 82 safeties with at least 16 defensive snaps. He allowed three catches on six targets for 11 yards while recording one interception and one pass breakup. Jaguars’ Trevor Lawrence is about to give Giants their biggest test | NJ.com Are the Giants ready for Trevor Lawrence? Sunday’s nationally televised Jaguars-Giants showdown at MetLife Stadium presents a huge challenge for coordinator Dennard Wilson’s Giants’ defense: Lawrence, one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. He is third in the league in passer rating, one spot behind the 49ers’ Brock Purdy and two spots ahead of the Lions’ Jared Goff. Serby: J.J. McCarthy has proven he’s more than just a backup by keeping Giants’ hopes alive | New York Post The NFL backup quarterback is what Bill Parcells liked to call a hold-the-fort guy. J.J. McCarthy has provided enough evidence for John Harbaugh and Giants fans to believe that he is considerably more than a hold-the-fort guy. He has so far been a steal of a fifth-round pick who has given Harbaugh and the fanbase hope that he can be a raise-the-fort guy with a ceiling high enough to capture the Giants’ first division title since 2011. Ranking the 50 QBs who have started an NFL game in 2026 | CBSSports.com 15. Jaxson Dart, Giants; 31. J.J. McCarthy, Giants; and 34. Jameis Winston, Giants. McCarthy, traded from the Vikings to address New York’s injury situation, is getting another chance (albeit temporary) to be an NFL starting quarterback. As was the case in Minnesota, McCarthy has shown signs of being a solid player in New York, but he still needs to work on his consistency, among other things. Take last week, for example. McCarthy threw for 293 yards and a touchdown and made some plays with his feet, but he also threw an ugly interception that sealed New York’s loss to Washington. A way-too-early look at potential Giants draft targets: How determined is NY to upgrade at RB? | The Athletic Wayshawn Parker, Utah (Day 2 target) Brugler: A bouncy athlete, Parker is averaging 6.2 yards per carry this season and has scouts excited about his NFL potential. He has outstanding reaction quickness with the awareness to find his blocks, allowing him to stack his cuts as he weaves through traffic. Aside from his running ability, the Giants will love his impact on passing downs, both as a receiver and blocker. Mark Fletcher, Miami (Day 2-3 target) Brugler: Parker would be more of the quick, elusive option at running back, while Fletcher is the big, physical bruiser. The Giants already have that bruising style with Skattebo, but Harbaugh might be drawn to a back like Fletcher, who will remind him stylistically of the superstar he had in Baltimore: Derrick Henry. The Miami back is also stout in pass pro and serviceable in the screen game. It was a game the Giants could (and probably should) have won, but instead they squandered opportunities at the end of the game. So instead of […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images It’s safe to say that Week 10 didn’t go as planned for the New York Giants. The Giants lost 27-24 to the Washington Commanders in a crucial divisional game. It was a game the Giants could (and probably should) have won, but instead they squandered opportunities at the end of the game. So instead of being 6-2-1 with a comfortable lead in the division heading into a tough stretch of games, the Giants are 5-3-1 and Washington (3-5-1) has the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants. The good news for the Giants is that the Dallas Cowboys (4-6) couldn’t quite come out on top in a shoot-out with the San Francisco 49ers. That loss maintained the Giants’ lead over their closest division rival as we enter the second half of the season. So with that in mind, we want to know which team Giants’ fans think is the biggest threat to the Giants in the division. The Cowboys have a better record than the Commanders, and there’s still the Week 17 game between the Giants and Cowboys. That game could be for the division. On the other hand, the Commanders have the tiebreaker and a much easier schedule down the stretch. It’s possible they could go on a run and catch the Giants. title: The NY Giants have multiple paths to the playoffs
summary: The New York Giants had the postseason clearly in their sights in the dysfunctional NFC East…until they let victory slip through their hands against the Washington Commanders last Thursday evening. Now they have made life more difficult for themselves. If you experienced the Tom Coughlin era, you’ll probably remember that this is nothing new. Let’s […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach John Harbaugh of the New York Giants reacts during the second quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Giants had the postseason clearly in their sights in the dysfunctional NFC East…until they let victory slip through their hands against the Washington Commanders last Thursday evening. Now they have made life more difficult for themselves. If you experienced the Tom Coughlin era, you’ll probably remember that this is nothing new. Let’s take a little trip down memory lane: 2007: In Week 14 the Giants beat the Eagles at The Linc 16-13 to get to 9-4 and put the playoffs clearly in their sights. The the next week they laid an egg at Giants Stadium, losing to Washington 22-10. Not until Ahmad Bradhsaw’s 88-yard TD run as the snow started to fall late in the game in Buffalo the following week did the Giants clinch a playoff spot. 2011: In Week 14 the Giants won in Dallas 37-34 when Jason Pierre-Paul blocked the Cowboys’ last second field goal attempt to get to 7-6. Next week, at home against Washington, the Giants were embarrassed by a 4-9 Washington team at home, 23-10. Not until Victor Cruz’s 99-yard TD reception to spark a win against the Jets and a final week 31-14 win over the Cowboys for the division title did the Giants clinch a playoff spot. It just seems to be in the Giants’ DNA to play poorly against Washington. Now we’re three years and running that the Giants haven’t beaten them (coinciding with the arrival of Jayden Daniels). Anyway, that’s in the rear-view mirror, and the question is whether the Giants can bounce back as they did in 2007 and 2011 to get to the playoffs anyway. No one sees the Giants as a Super Bowl contender (more on that in a minute), but as 2007 and 2011 showed, you never know. Unlike those seasons, the 2026 Giants are in the driver’s seat in the NFC East even after their loss. Unfortunately, the wins have all been against losing teams and they now face a stretch of some of the best teams in the NFL. What are their chances of reaching the post-season, and which games have the most leverage on their chances? To answer that we’ll use The Athletic’s NFL playoff simulator . The simulator gives the current chances of each team making the playoffs, as a division champion or wild card, and allows the user to see how individual games affect your team’s chances. Let’s play with the possibilities. Let’s get one thing out of the way right away: The Giants will not make the playoffs as a wild card this season: The Giants’ chances of winning the division and making the playoffs are identical, as they are for every NFC East and NFC South team. The Eagles are out of the picture. The Giants’ chances to win the Super Bowl, however, are effectively nil at this point. How does each remaining game affect the Giants chances? Some matter more than others, but at this point they’re all fairly important: Obviously the Dallas game in Week 18 is their highest leverage game because it could directly decide the division champion. The differences among the other games are all about the NFL tiebreaking critieria. For a two-team tie these are: Let’s look at a few scenarios. Beating the Jaguars this Sunday would be big, increasing the Giants’ playoff chances from 61% to 76% according to the simulator without considering any other games. A loss however drops their odds to almost 50-50. Fear not – a win the following week over the downtrodden Colts would get them back to two-in-three playoff odds. The figure below shows the odds with me having selected the coming two games in black: Now let’s consider the brutal reality that the 49ers and Seahawks are next on the schedule. Not that either team is unbeatable – the 49ers had their hands full with Dallas last Sunday and the Seahawks are having a post-Super Bowl hangover. Still, the Giants will be clear underdogs in both games barring injuries to multiple key players on either team. So assuming two more losses: Three losses in the next four weeks, making it four of five defeats for the Giants, only reduces the playoff odds to about even. Why? It’s because the Cowboys have their own gauntlet to run. After presumable gimmes against the Titans and Eagles in the coming two weeks, they face the Seahawks, Rams, and Jaguars after that, before playing the Giants and Commanders in their final two games. And that’s the key: Even if the Giants stink up the joint in the coming month, the odds are that they still face the Cowboys in Week 17 with the division title on the line. So what is the Giants’ most important game? Actually, it’s coming up right after Jacksonville. The Giants absolutely must beat the Indianapolis Colts, who are in disarray after injuries, trading several of their best players, and Daniel Jones’ carriage turning into a pumpkin in his second season as a Colt. If they don’t, and they lose those other games as well: Even then, all might not be lost if the Cowboys play to form because of their tough December schedule. Let’s imagine that the Giants beat the surprising Cleveland Browns in Week 15, lose to a tough Detroit Lions team the week after, and then take care of business in Dallas and at home against the Eagles in the season finale: In this desultory performance scenario the Giants weather a five-game losing streak, only win three more games, and still have a 72% chance to win the division at 8-8-1. That’s almost as high as the 76% chance they’d get just by beating Jacksonville this Sunday. Beating the Jags and the Colts increases their chances to 85%, and that only drops to 77% if they lose to the 49ers and Seahawks as expected: All in all, I would say that the second scenario I presented above (lose to JAX, SF, SEA, beat IND) is the most realistic outcome for the coming month. That means that there are decent odds that it’s a coin flip by late December whether the Giants will make the playoffs, and it will all come down to that last month. It could have been so much better if they’d beaten Washington even once, never mind twice as could have happened. Still, things could be worse. You could be a fan of a team that only won its first game of the season on Monday night, or a fan of the team they beat that jettisoned its former head coach and may watch him in the playoffs while they stay home. (By the way, if the Los Angeles Chargers run the table they have a 52% chance to sneak into the playoffs.) Talk is cheap, though. Beating Jacksonville would be worth more.

Chase Brown’s receiving skills were on display; he caught eight passes for 39 yards with two touchdowns, and Ja’Marr Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards. The Bengals defense dominated Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers. The final score, 38-18, Bengals. The Bengals have now won five games in a row. No. 7 —Denver Broncos (6-2) | (5th) 📉 2 spots The Broncos had a bye in Week 10. Patrick Mahomes threw for 343 yards and 5 touchdowns, one to new arrival Josh Downs. The Falcons didn’t stand a chance at home – 35-13 Chiefs. No. 9 — Detroit Lions (7-2) | SAME Detroit beat up the Patriots in Munich. Jared Goff threw for 303 yards with three touchdowns ( and two picks ), while Jahmyr Gibbs gained 153 yards on the ground ( 7-yard average!) with a pair of rushing touchdowns. Detroit suffered a terrible loss with Aidan Hutchinson going down after a sack celebration in the first half. Still, the defense didn’t have to do much against the Tommy DeVito-led Patriots’ offense. Lock had some DOTs to Jaxson Smith-Njigba, who secured eight of ten targets for 171 yards with a touchdown. Seattle travels to San Francisco in two weeks. No. 11 — Green Bay Packers (6-4) | (10th) 📉 1 spot Green Bay was dominated by the Vikings’ defense, which forced FOUR Green Bay turnovers. The Packers still can’t run the football, and the heater that Jordan Love was on found its solution in Brian Flores’ defense. No. 12— Los Angeles Rams (6-4) | (14th) 📈 2 spots The Rams beat up the Carson Beck-led Cardinals. 34-6. Blake Corum rushed for 100 yards, and Ronnie Rivers had 81 yards on 15 straight runs to conclude the game. Los Angeles wasn’t threatened in this game; their defense forced three turnovers and sacked Beck five times. No. 13 — Cleveland Browns (6-3) | (16th) 📈 4 spots Cleveland is now 4–0 at home – first time since the 1960s! Houston took a big 17-0 lead but Cleveland rushed for three touchdowns and stayed resilient against a potent Houston offense. Cleveland won the game, 27-24 in the final minutes. Cleveland is a good, well-coached football team. No. 14 — New York Giants (5-3-1) | (12th) 📉 1 spot The Giants hosted the Commanders on Thursday Night Football, and they couldn’t find a way to win a tight game after Dennard Wilson’s defense forced two interceptions and a turnover on downs in the fourth quarter. Despite 293-yards from J.J. McCarthy, and another epic performance from Isaiah Likely, the Giants could not secure the win, allowing the Commanders to hang inch closer to the top of the NFC East. title: The Jets Need To Reimagine Their Running Back Usage
summary: I’ll start this article with a shameless pat on the back. Despite me getting numerous things wrong throughout the years (likely more wrong than right), one thing I’ve been very happy to see develop is the breakout of Braelon Allen. Now, for those who know my opinion on the matter, you know I’ve been pretty […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 09: Breece Hall #20 and Braelon Allen #0 of the New York Jets warm up prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers during the NFL Preseason 2025 game between New York Jets and Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on August 09, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ll start this article with a shameless pat on the back. Despite me getting numerous things wrong throughout the years (likely more wrong than right), one thing I’ve been very happy to see develop is the breakout of Braelon Allen. Now, for those who know my opinion on the matter, you know I’ve been pretty vocal about Allen’s potential and what he could end up being. It was rooted in a pretty simple theory: Allen is too strong, big, and fast to fail. If I had to get into a bit more detail, I could talk about how Allen possesses great contact balance, is light on his feet, showcases strong vision, and does all of this while being extremely young (he was 17 as a true freshman and just 20 when he entered the league). One of the few positive developments for the Jets this year was just how effective Allen was when Breece Hall was injured. Look at some of these snaps just the week prior to Breece’s return: Braelon Allen explosive runs vs Raiders pic.twitter.com/slf2ppAp0c — Omari Brown (@OmariiBrown) November 2, 2026 Come on, this is some good stuff. However, like most things with the Jets, it got complicated once Breece Hall returned. What would be a great problem to have for certain teams, two good players at the same position who complement each other well, has already become a big-time headache for the Jets. How does the staff utilize the skill sets of Breece Hall and Braelon Allen effectively? How can they both contribute as difference-makers to this team while still getting enough opportunities? Now, it’s a small sample since Breece Hall has come back (only two games), but I’m going to make my case as to why the early usage split doesn’t make much sense to me. Usage From a distance, I think everyone is probably in agreement that, simply put, Braelon Allen has flashed more as a runner this year. Before we even get to the stats, I think I could get most people to agree with that just from watching the two play. Allen fits your typical profile of a heavy-usage back. He’s big, has good vision, can break tackles, and rarely gets tackled for a loss. Breece is a bit different. Down by down, he’ll leave you with some inconsistencies. He’s heavily reliant on his breakaway speed, but that also makes him incredibly effective in the open field. He’s got a history of turning small gains into explosive ones. A stat I remember from this offseason really reminds me of this. Since 2020, there’s only been one player with 3+ 50-yard runs and 3+ 50-yard receptions in that time frame: Breece Hall. But now, let’s take a look at some of the rushing stats from this year. We’ll use a few metrics from Next Gen Stats that help demonstrate how Allen has been significantly more impactful as a down-to-down runner. Here are some of the metrics we’ll be looking at: Efficiency (EFF): Rushing efficiency is calculated by taking the total distance a player traveled on rushing plays as a ball carrier, according to Next Gen Stats, and dividing it by the rushing yards gained. The lower the number, the more of a north-south runner the player is. 8+ Defenders in the Box (8+D%): On every play, Next Gen Stats calculates how many defenders are stacked in the box at the snap. Using that logic, this metric calculates how often a rusher sees eight or more defenders in the box against them. Average Time Behind the Line of Scrimmage (TLOS): Next Gen Stats measures the amount of time a ball carrier spends behind the line of scrimmage before crossing it, measured to the nearest tenth of a second. TLOS represents the average time behind the LOS on all rushing plays where the player is the rusher. Rushing Yards Over Expected (RYOE): The difference between actual yards gained and expected yards gained (Actual – Expected). This uses player tracking data, including the position, speed, and direction of the runner, blockers, and defenders at the moment of handoff, to calculate how many yards an average running back would gain in that exact scenario. A positive number means the runner created yardage beyond what the blocking and defensive alignment provided. Rushing Over Expected Percentage (ROE%): Also tracked as Carries Beating Expected (%), this measures the share of a runner’s carries that gain more yardage than the NFL Next Gen Stats Expected Rushing Yards model predicts. While total RYOE can be skewed by a single massive breakout run, ROE% highlights down-to-down consistency. Now, let’s compare: Breece Hall: 77 carries, 265 yards, 3.4 AVG 4.8 EFF 2.79 TLOS -31 RYOE 32% ROE Braelon Allen: 128 carries, 638 yards, 5.0 AVG 3.41 EFF 2.72 TLOS 118 RYOE 52% ROE So, what do these stats tell us? A few things. For starters, they show that Breece has been significantly less of a north-south runner than Braelon Allen has. Hall actually has the 5th highest EFF in the league, showing that he’s traveling a lot of distance on plays without getting much to show for it. That also shows up in his RYOE and ROE numbers. He ranks in the bottom 10 in ROE%, something Hall has historically struggled with due to his home-run running style. He’s actually performed worse than what would be expected from an average back and that’s shown with the -31 RYOE. To Breece’s credit, he’s normally better than this. He may have been hampered by the injury earlier this year. Again, he has a tendency to make up for some of these inconsistencies with a handful of explosive runs. But the numbers this year have been pretty telling. Allen, though, has been quite frankly terrific. He’s top 8 in RYOE and yards per carry this year. He hasn’t showcased the historic explosiveness that Hall has, but Allen actually ranks #1 in the league in ROE%. That shows that Allen is rarely leaving yards on the field. He doesn’t have the home-run ability Hall has, and probably never will, but if you need a workhorse back who consistently churns out positive yards, keeps the offense above the sticks, and prevents the team from getting into bad situations, there legitimately hasn’t been a better back in the NFL at that this year than Allen. But the running back position isn’t just about running. We also have to consider how each back performs on passing downs. From a pass-protection perspective, there’s not a ton to glean from the numbers. Hall has historically graded decently in most metrics. He’s never been great, but he’s usually around average by PFF grade and ranks 19th out of 60 backs this year. He’s not a liability. Allen, quietly, has been great in this regard according to PFF. In an extremely small sample last year, his grade would have been good enough to finish as a top-2 back. This year, he ranks 6th in PFF grade. Based on what we’ve seen over the last season and a half, it’s probably fair to say Allen is a well above-average pass protector. Now, what about receiving? This is where Hall has the clear advantage, both in the stats and on film. Let’s take a look: Breece Hall: 17 catches, 18 targets, 195 yards 2.71 Yards Per Route Run 6 Missed Tackles Forced 8 First Downs Braelon Allen: 20 catches, 24 targets, 108 yards 0.68 Yards Per Route Run 6 Missed Tackles Forced 6 First Downs What does this data show? Hall is far, far better as a pass-catcher. And while the yards per route run number will likely normalize (it’s better than 95% of NFL wide receivers right now), Hall has consistently been a more than effective pass-catcher throughout his career. His career yards per route run is 1.59, a very good pace for a running back. For context, Jahmyr Gibbs sits at 1.56 yards per route run in his career. Christian McCaffrey and Alvin Kamara, probably the two best backs in recent memory at catching passes out of the…

title: New York Jets News: ‘Sham’ Search Process? NYJ Can’t Mess it up This Time Around
summary: The New York Jets have solicited advice from nearly everyone on planet Earth when hiring head coaches this century. That has included The 33rd Team, Charley Casserly, and do you remember that one time when Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning made a phone call to seal the deal for Adam Gase? Great times. […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - OCTOBER 21: Quarterback Peyton Manning #18 of the Indianapolis Colts talks on a telephone to coaches sitting overhead as he looks on from the sideline during a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Heinz Field on October 21, 2002 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The Steelers defeated the Colts 28-10. (Photo by George Gojkovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets have solicited advice from nearly everyone on planet Earth when hiring head coaches this century. That has included The 33rd Team, Charley Casserly, and do you remember that one time when Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning made a phone call to seal the deal for Adam Gase? Great times. That can’t happen in 2027. Make no mistake about it: the Jets will be looking for a new head coach in a matter of months, but in all of those other situations, they lost the battle before it ever began. Stop relying on people outside of the building. Put your big boy pants on and make a decision for yourself. Who is the right man for that job? Darren Mougey. Woody Johnson has called Mougey “The General” this offseason when referencing him to fans. He has spoken highly of him and believes the team is going in the right direction because of Mougey. Put him in the driver’s seat for this search and allow him to vet the candidates. ESPN New York’s Jake Asman called the latest Jets HC search a “sham” on the “Jets Collective” podcast. “Woody Johnson put Mike Tannenbaum, Rick Spielman, and The 33rd Team in charge of vetting candidates. Liam Coen is a UMass alum, Mike Tannenbaum went to UMass, and again, I work with Mike, so I’m comfortable saying this to his face. We’ve had many battles on the air and off the air, but if [the] Coz reporting is right that they got the intel wrong on Liam Coen, it’s another indictment of just this sham of a search process that led to Aaron Glenn.” J-E-T-S! title: Christian Parker loses play-calling as Cowboys’ defensive coordinator
summary: Back on October 13, we noted how Christian Parker seemed to be getting Sean Desai’d with the Dallas Cowboys bringing Mike Pettine in as a defensive assistant. That prophecy has now fully come to fruition with Parker losing play-calling duty to Pettine. It’s not hard to understand why the Cowboys are making this move; Dallas […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Back on October 13, we noted how Christian Parker seemed to be getting Sean Desai’d with the Dallas Cowboys bringing Mike Pettine in as a defensive assistant. That prophecy has now fully come to fruition with Parker losing play-calling duty to Pettine . It’s not hard to understand why the Cowboys are making this move; Dallas has the worst defense in the NFL. They just allowed 46 points and 584 yards in a home loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The Cowboys are looking for a spark that can get them pointed in the right direction with the NFC East crown still within reach. The Desai change famously didn’t work well for the Eagles in 2023. Their defense was even worse under Matt Patricia. But the Cowboys don’t really have any room to go but up from here. On one hand, it’s funny to watch the Cowboys scramble like this. On the other hand, it’s unfortunate that Parker — a contributor to the Eagles’ Super Bowl LIX victory — is floundering and now being publicly embarrassed by being demoted. It would probably be more respectful for the Cowboys to fire him as opposed to keeping up this charade where he’s the defensive coordinator in title only.

summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Baun is currently tied with Fred Warner as the NFL’s fifth-highest graded linebacker by Pro […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 08: Zack Baun #53 of the Philadelphia Eagles sacks J.J. McCarthy #18 of the New York Giants during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 08, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Zack Baun is allowing just a 77.6 passer rating when targeted this season, which is slightly below his 79.2 mark from his All-Pro season in 2024. Baun is currently tied with Fred Warner as the NFL’s fifth-highest graded linebacker by Pro Football Focus. He’s a rare bright spot in this dark campaign. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL Week 10: 32 teams, 32 observations – PFF Philadelphia Eagles. Among the 84 linebackers with at least 10 targets this season, Zack Baun has the second-highest forced-incompletion rate at 18.5%. He has five forced incompletions on 27 targets. Eagles Film Review: What to make of Makai Lemon so far – BGN I wanted to use the bye week to get a better idea of what the Eagles have in Makai Lemon. So I went back through every target from the first nine games, hoping to see how his rookie season was developing. By the end, I was probably more frustrated with the offense than I was when I started. Evaluating a first-round receiver when almost everything thrown his way is a hitch, a quick out, or an underneath crosser is incredibly difficult. At times, this felt like an Eagles’ offense disaster compilation, with Lemon unfortunately involved. His production has improved. After 18 catches for 127 yards through six games, he caught 19 passes for 185 yards and a touchdown over the next three. However, the bigger question for me is how much more he can offer. The Eagles have given us a pretty clear picture of the role they want him to play right now. They have given us far less evidence of what he could become. All statistics in this article are courtesy of Fantasy Points Data Suite. I liked Lemon as a prospect because he looked like a good football player with a fairly high floor. I still see that. I also questioned his explosiveness and whether he could become a really good receiver. Halfway through his rookie season, too many of those questions remain unanswered because his usage has been so boring. NFL Week 11 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we’re hearing – ESPN Quarterback Joe Milton is poised to start his second consecutive game for the Eagles offense, which is coming off a bye week. The Eagles haven’t announced this but the signs are pointing to Milton from what I’m hearing. Whispers of a Tanner McKee return persisted after Milton took seven sacks and lost a fumble in the team’s Week 9 loss to the Giants. But Milton has owned up to missing protections, and he should be more well-versed in them due to extra preparation time off the bye. Also, Milton has the mobility to help a struggling rushing attack. Three practice squad players around the NFL the Eagles should consider poaching – PhillyVoice 2) Michael Trigg (24), TE, Cowboys (6’4, 240). Trigg is a playmaker who had 50 catches for 694 receiving yards (13.9 YPC), and six TDs for Baylor in 2025. He finished third in the nation among tight ends in receiving yards. He’s a smaller tight end at 6’4, 240, but he has a wide catch radius because of his massive wingspan, which should also help him as a blocker. […] He also fights for every yard after the catch and is a surprisingly good route runner. I thought Trigg could go as high as Day 2 in the 2026 draft. Instead, he went undrafted because of character concerns. Longtime Cowboys beat Clarence Hill noted a couple weeks ago that Trigg is a developmental player “on and off the field.” If his off-field issues are workable, Trigg makes sense as a guy you can add to the roster, and then he’s yours all offseason to determine if he’s worth the effort in 2027 and beyond. But there’s no question that he has talent. Roob’s bye week stats: It’s awful but we do have Makai Lemon and Dallas Goedert – NBCSP FIRST TIME EVER: The Eagles are averaging 4.29 yards per play and allowing 5.37 yards per play. This is the first time in franchise history they’ve gained under 4.3 yards per play and allowed over 5.3 yards per play through nine games. The 4.29 is their worst on offense since 1999. Steelers WR Roman Wilson trending towards playing vs. Eagles – Behind The Steel Curtain The 84th pick in the 2024 NFL Draft has already posted a career high in receiving yards this season with 188 in five games played. Wilson had emerged as a downfield threat for Rodgers and one of the Steelers’ best man coverage beaters before his injury. Wilson’s return should provide a boost to the Steelers’ passing game that has been lackluster for several weeks now. NFL Fantasy 2026 Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em: Defenses for Week 11 – NFL.com START — STEELERS DEFENSE/SPECIAL TEAMS. Over their seven-game losing streak starting in Week 3, the Eagles have allowed the third-highest pressure rate (42.8%) and fifth-most sacks per game (3.4), while scoring a league-low 14.3 points per game. Pittsburgh’s D/ST is a top-tier play once again in Week 11. Quinyon Mitchell is consistent in his consistency – PhiladelphiaEagles.com Cornerbacks in the NFL must be able to maintain focus to play at a high level week in and week out, a harder task than it seems. A player they are covering may only be targeted four times in a game, meaning cornerbacks spend the vast majority of their snaps matching a receiver’s routes without ever seeing a pass come their way. Yet, Quinyon Mitchell never seems to let his guard down. “He can shut down one side of the field and that makes my job easier because I know he is going to do what he’s supposed to do,” safety Andrew Mukuba said of his teammate. “It gives me that opportunity and ability to just roam around and be able to make plays.” After playing right outside cornerback all season, the first-team All-Pro shadowed a receiver for the first time this year in Week 9 against New York. His assignment? Giants Pro Bowl pass catcher Malik Nabers. Mitchell lined up against Nabers on 80 percent (24 of 30) of the star receiver’s snaps, only allowing two catches for 7 yards while in coverage despite Nabers coming off four straight 100+ receiving-yard games. What makes him such a tough matchup for receivers? “He’s very confident in himself,” wide receiver Darius Cooper said. “He’s very strong and his ball skills are increasing as well. But I think his main attributes are his confidence in himself, his strength, and he has good feet as well.” Eagles Autism Foundation staff shine on game day – GMA ABC News’ Will Reeve visits Lincoln Financial Field to meet neurodivergent employees helping make Philadelphia Eagles game days special through the team’s commitment to autism inclusion. Chiefs sign former Eagles offensive lineman to practice squad – Arrowhead Pride Fred Johnson is an eight-year veteran who started his career with the Cincinnati Bengals as an undrafted free agent out of Florida in 2019. He started eight games over three years, but the most time he has seen on the field has been the last four years with the Eagles. Johnson started in 14 regular-season games in 2024 and 2025; he also played in all four playoff games through beating Kansas City in the Super Bowl. He primarily lined up at right tackle (726 snaps) during that time, but he also played 419 snaps at left tackle. title: Eagles Film Review: What to make of Makai Lemon so far
summary: I wanted to use the bye week to get a better idea of what the Eagles have in Makai Lemon. So I went back through every target from the first nine games, hoping to see how his rookie season was developing. By the end, I was probably more frustrated with the offense than I was […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images I wanted to use the bye week to get a better idea of what the Eagles have in Makai Lemon. So I went back through every target from the first nine games, hoping to see how his rookie season was developing. By the end, I was probably more frustrated with the offense than I was when I started. Evaluating a first-round receiver when almost everything thrown his way is a hitch, a quick out, or an underneath crosser is incredibly difficult. At times, this felt like an Eagles’ offense disaster compilation, with Lemon unfortunately involved. His production has improved. After 18 catches for 127 yards through six games, he caught 19 passes for 185 yards and a touchdown over the next three. However, the bigger question for me is how much more he can offer. The Eagles have given us a pretty clear picture of the role they want him to play right now. They have given us far less evidence of what he could become. All statistics in this article are courtesy of Fantasy Points Data Suite . I liked Lemon as a prospect because he looked like a good football player with a fairly high floor . I still see that. I also questioned his explosiveness and whether he could become a really good receiver. Halfway through his rookie season, too many of those questions remain unanswered because his usage has been so boring. If you want to see the video with analysis of all targets, it’s available on my Patreon here ! Have a little spoiler of my favorite route of his… Strengths Footwork and deception in short spaces Lemon’s best trait as a route runner is how quickly he can change direction and sell his routes using his whole body. A receiver can have quick feet, but good defensive backs aren’t simply staring at his feet. The shoulders and torso have to help sell the route. Lemon has several examples where a subtle body fake gets the defender leaning before he plants and breaks away. His movement in tight spaces looks very natural. He can threaten one direction and get into another without making the whole process look labored. 11) I haven't been impressed with Lemon, but this was the play that reminded me of what he can do. He thrives when he can find space in the middle of the field. Hurts does a good job of finding him. The Eagles need this relationship to develop because they need Lemon to start… pic.twitter.com/Ai8RMiqalm — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 29, 2026 The fourth-down slant against the Cowboys might be my favorite example of his season. He hesitates briefly on the release before selling the vertical stem, getting the cornerback into a position where he has to respect the possibility of Lemon continuing downfield. Then Lemon breaks inside. The separation comes from making the defender react to a believable threat before changing direction. It is a really clean win. Top of the screen — sudden & explosive release and route from Makai Lemon on what was his final catch of the night. Tough after the catch, as well. Ballplayer. pic.twitter.com/nCxc8rzJdv — Ryan Fowler (@_RyanFowler_) October 27, 2026 I particularly liked that play when comparing it with an earlier route against Travis Hunter vs. the Jaguars. On that rep, Lemon takes a hard outside step, but he doesn’t close enough to make Hunter feel threatened vertically. Against the Cowboys, Lemon does a much better job of making the release and stem look like the beginning of a vertical route. The opponents are different, so it isn’t a perfect comparison, but his improved route-selling is encouraging. The Giants game provides another lovely example of route detail. Lemon angles his stem slightly, suggesting he might continue inside, then works upfield and gets the defensive back to turn. Once the defender’s eyes move away, Lemon uses that blind spot to create separation as he breaks back toward the football. He adds a little physical contact to help himself, then gets his feet organized and catches away from his body. That is proper receiver play. Awareness against zone coverage Lemon understands how to find space against zone. Settling between defenders sounds straightforward until you watch receivers who keep running themselves into coverage. There is a difference between occupying an open patch of grass and adjusting a route as the defenders move. Lemon already shows some of that understanding. One of my favorite examples comes against the Jaguars. He initially threatens to cross the field, recognizes the linebacker dropping into the space around him, and adjusts back away from that defender. Simply stopping would make him easier to close on. Continuing across would take him toward coverage. Lemon finds a way to remain available, and Jalen Hurts delivers the ball where he can extend and catch it. He creates a usable throwing window, then gives the quarterback room to place the ball slightly outside his frame. Another example later in the target reel shows him working toward an out route but recognizing he is already free. He doesn’t need to keep racing toward the sideline and potentially bring himself closer to the outside defender. He can throttle down, turn, and present a target. Those little decisions are valuable, especially in an offense that has made completing passes look painfully difficult at times. 8) Do you know what? For a first start after just getting here, I still thought Milton did some things well. Obviously, it wasn't great, and it was never going to be in this system, but he showed off his arm talent downfield. This is a dime. Good pocket movement to subtly shift… pic.twitter.com/Ces1YINbQn — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 10, 2026 He is averaging 1.20 yards per route run against zone compared with 0.49 against man. At this stage, I feel more confident in his ability to recognize and use space than in his ability to consistently defeat every type of individual matchup. Catching away from his frame Watching all the targets together made this strength really obvious. Lemon repeatedly extends his hands away from his body and catches the football cleanly. He can reach behind himself, get down to a low throw, or turn and secure the ball while moving. This catch from Makai Lemon is going to be one of the most impressive ones he makes all year pic.twitter.com/2IGBKbKLBn — Fran Duffy (@FDuffyNFL) November 9, 2026 There is a catch vs. the Titans that is a good example. The ball arrives behind him, and he has to adjust before taking contact. Against the Panthers, he sells an inside route before breaking out against a defender with outside leverage. The coverage makes that a difficult route to win, and the throw doesn’t make his life especially easy either. He still finishes the catch. The two drops against the Giants need a mention, and I will get to them. But I came away from this exercise feeling positive about his hands overall. There are too many catches away from his frame, including through contact, for me to suddenly decide that catching the football is a weakness because of the final game before the bye. Toughness and awareness through contact Lemon takes some absolute shots in this target reel. He keeps making himself available over the middle anyway. I don’t see a receiver whose routes become hesitant because he knows a safety or linebacker is coming downhill. The Cowboys game, in particular, asks a lot of him physically, and he keeps competing through it. What I like is that his toughness includes some awareness of how to protect himself. His touchdown vs. the Cowboys is a good example. Lemon knows the hit is coming. He secures the ball and turns his body so that he can absorb contact without charging straight into it. A smaller receiver needs to make those adjustments. Being willing to take a hit is valuable; understanding how to finish the…

title: Eagles sign Jaydon Blue to the roster (once again), add practice squad DT
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. JAYDON BLUE Here’s a recap of Blue’s transactions with the Eagles: The Eagles have been reluctant to play Blue on offense thus far; the former Dallas Cowboys draft pick has only logged […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 08: Philadelphia Eagles running back Jaydon Blue #30 runs the ball during the game between the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles on November 8, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: RB Jaydon Blue was signed from the practice squad to the active roster. DT Leki Fotu was signed to the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. JAYDON BLUE Here’s a recap of Blue’s transactions with the Eagles: September 1 — Signed to the practice squad October 17 — Signed to the roster October 20 — Waived from the roster October 22 — Signed to the practice squad October 28 — Signed to the roster November 10 — Waived from the roster November 16 — Signed to the practice squad November 17 — Signed to the roster The Eagles have been reluctant to play Blue on offense thus far; the former Dallas Cowboys draft pick has only logged eight offensive snaps this season. And all of those came during garbage time in the Eagles’ loss to the Washington Commanders. In addition to theoretically providing running back depth, Blue has been serving as the Eagles’ kick returner. But he’s only logging 22.3 yards per return, which isn’t good. It’s a little curious why the Eagles signed Blue to their practice squad yesterday only to sign him to the roster one day later. Why not just sign him to the roster in the first place? Regardless, Blue is back on the roster. Assuming Saquon Barkley suits up and Will Shipley returns from injured reserve , the Eagles will have Blue as their third running back option. Until they inevitably cut him again down the road. LEKI FOTU Fotu had a tryout with the Eagles on Monday. Here’s what we wrote at the time: The 28-year-old Fotu is a 6’5”, 330 pound defensive tackle who’s made 26 starts in 66 career games played from 2020-2025. With the Eagles trading Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Birds have a need for more nose tackle depth. Fotu can help to fill that role, be it on the practice squad or the roster. Fotu is here to help fill practice reps and provide depth should the Eagles need him on game day.

title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 11 Edition
summary: Now that Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 08: Zack Baun #53 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates sack with Dallas Goedert #88 Ty Robinson #95 against the New York Giants during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 08, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. ( Here’s a link to last week’s version .) BLG’S WEEK 11 POWER RANKINGS 1 – Chicago Bears (Last Week: 1) – The Bears return from their bye to host the Saints. That game is certainly winnable; they’re 11.5-point home favorites. Despite this, Chicago has THE most difficult remaining strength of schedule in the NFL. They’re going to be majorly tested down the stretch. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) – The Niners own the Cowboys. They’re 5-0 in their last five meetings against Dallas … while averaging 32 points per game. For that much, Eagles fans can appreciate this team. 3 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 3) – The Bills are really good. They’ve also been fortunate to face the following quarterbacks in recent weeks: Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer, and Cade Klubnik. 4 – Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 4) – So much for any concern about Patrick Mahomes’ health; he threw five touchdowns and zero interceptions in KC’s most recent win. 5 – Detroit Lions (LW: 5) – Don’t sleep on the Lions. They’ve won five in a row and they’re 2-0 in division games. By contrast, the Bears are 0-2 in NFC North action. Unfortunately, they did take a major hit with Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending injury while celebrating a sack. 6 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 6) – The Jags are riding a three-game winning streak. Their average margin of victory in this stretch is 25 points. They’re looking tough to beat and they have the NFL’s fifth-easiest remaining strength of schedule. 7 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 7) – Are we sure Drew Lock shouldn’t be the full-time starter? He’s 3-0 and has a 125.6 passer rating this year. Sam Darnold is at 79.5. 8 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 8) – Joe Burrow is currently the betting favorite for MVP at +100. The dude is on fire. He’s above Josh Allen at +350 and Brock Purdy at +400. The Bengals are also now the No. 1 NFL team by DVOA. 9 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 9) – So far, so good on Kirk Cousins’ return to Minny. Given how strong their defense is, the Vikings needed mere competency at quarterback and it seems like they got it. 10 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 10) – After starting the season 2-4, the Rams have rebounded to win four straight … albeit against lesser competition. They’re probably better than their 6-4 record indicates . 11 – Denver Broncos (LW: 11) – The Broncos return from their bye to host the Raiders. It’s the first meeting of these two AFC West teams this season. Denver is favored by 9.5 points at home. 12 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 12) – We’ve entered a weird stretch in this week’s power rankings where all the teams above this mark did not lose in Week 10 … and five of the following six teams did. So, that’s why there’s little movement here. Anyway, the Packers deserve to be bumped down for a decisive home loss to Minny. They seem less ready to hang with the elites. 13 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 14) – Fernando Mendoza wasn’t particularly sharp in his NFL debut, which was to be expected going up against a tough Seattle defense. We’ll see if he can show up bigger against the Broncos in Week 11. 14 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 15) – A blowout loss to Cincy dropped the Stillers to second in the AFC North. Aaron Rodgers isn’t inspiring much confidence at the moment. 15 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 19) – Todd Monken has earned Coach of the Year consideration. The Browns entered this season with a projected win total of 5.5 games. Cleveland erased a 17-point deficit against Houston to pick up their sixth win of the season on Sunday. 16 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 16) – We shouldn’t let this dreadful Dallas defense (46 points and 584 yards allowed!) distract us from talking about how Dak Prescott is an elite garbage time stat padder. 17 – New York Giants (LW: 17) – The Giants had a chance to effectively wrap up the NFC East by beating Washington at home. They failed to do so. It’s possible they’ll still win the division anyway … but they’ll be kicking themselves if they don’t. 18 – New England Patriots (LW: 13) – The Pats’ season is probably over with Drake Maye going down. A.J. Brown is also hurt … again. We’ll see if this group has any resiliency before totally writing them off. 19 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 20) – The Bucs return from their bye to play in Detroit. Tough matchup for Tampa … but they’ll be rested while the Lions are coming off international travel. 20 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 21) – It was a narrow win for the Panthers but they beat the Saints to put themselves on top of the NFC South … with a 4-5 record. For all the jokes about the NFC Least, at least their division leader isn’t under .500. 21 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 18) – Oof. Baltimore’s quarterback situation obviously isn’t ideal but you’ve still gotta find a way to beat the winless Chargers while at home. Instead, the Ravens are slipping out of the AFC playoff picture. 22 – Washington Commanders (LW: 26) – Give the Commanders credit: Thursday was a must-win game for them to keep their season alive … and they out and beat the Giants. I’d argue that the result was more about New York blowing it than Washington asserting themselves. Nevertheless, the Commies are alive … and face the NFC East’s easiest remaining strength of schedule. Not impossible that they make a run. 23 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 22) – No team is worse at running the ball. They’re not going anywhere at this rate. The Saints today had the third-worst rushing success rate for any team in a game this season. 23 carries for 49 yards (2.1 YPC). Their longest run by an RB was 5 yards. On the season, the Saints rank 32nd in rushing success rate. — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) November 16, 2026 24 – Houston Texans (LW: 23) – Any chance of the Texans coming back to win the AFC South is over now after Houston choked away a 17 to 0 lead in Cleveland. Just not a team that deserves to be taken seriously. 25 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 24) – We’ve seen enough to say that Michael Penix isn’t the answer. The Falcons need a new quarterback in 2027. 26 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 25) – Carson Beck logged a 38.4 passer rating in his NFL debut. That’s rough. 27 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 31) – The Colts were competitive against Dallas in Week 9 and beat the Dolphins in Week 10. That’s not much. But it’s more than nothing. 28 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 27) – They lost to Indy. 29 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 32) – No longer do the Chargers hold the NFL’s longest losing streak! The Bolts are on the board. They’re also favored in their next two games: vs. NYJ and vs. NE. Can you say … winning streak?! 30 – New York Jets (LW: 28) – Make that five straight losses for the J-E-T-S. The last two have been blowouts, too. Aaron Glenn’s seat is only getting hotter. 31 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 29) – The Eagles’ bye was one of the most enjoyable weeks of their season. They return to host the Steelers as 4.5-point home underdogs. We’ll see if the time off actually helped at all or if the Birds will continue to struggle. 32 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 32) – The Titans are currently projected to have the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. It’d be their second No. 1 overall pick in three years.

title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Eagles 7-round simulation, Version 1.0
summary: The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season is all but over and the most exciting thing for the team is the future. Now rich with draft picks in the 2027 and 2028 drafts, the Birds are entering a rebuilding period after a four-year stretch of being one of the league’s best teams. There are many questions regarding […]
full_text: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 07: CJ Carr #13 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish looks to pass against the Miami Hurricanes during the first half at Notre Dame Stadium on November 07, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season is all but over and the most exciting thing for the team is the future. Now rich with draft picks in the 2027 and 2028 drafts, the Birds are entering a rebuilding period after a four-year stretch of being one of the league’s best teams. There are many questions regarding the coaching staff and quarterback, but there’s no question the Eagles need to get younger and more athletic at practically every position. It’s early, and much will change about the Eagles 2027 NFL Draft outlook, but here is a picture of what it could look like right now with their projected 10 draft picks. Using the PFF Mock Draft Simulator with their draft board and not making any trades. 1.05: Jeremiah Smith, Wide Receiver, Ohio State: Jeremiah Smith is the best receiver prospect to come out of college since Julio Jones and AJ Green. Getting him with the fifth overall pick would be a coup. He would enter the league as a top 10 receiver and make a formidable pass catching corps with DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon. 1.26: CJ Carr, Quarterback, Notre Dame: It’s very hard to envision a scenario where Jalen Hurts comes back to Philadelphia. It’s not impossible, but it feels highly unlikely given a multitude of factors. If he leaves, the Eagles will look to a deep quarterback class to hit the reset button. CJ Carr doesn’t have the most experience, but he has all the tools to be a high level passer in the NFL. He is smart with a big arm and good mobility. He will need patience in development, but his upside is very high. 2.37: Carter Smith, Offensive Tackle, Indiana: The Eagles have needs everywhere, and the offensive line is high on the priority list. Carter Smith is a highly experienced blocker who could take over day one at right tackle next year as the Eagles try to fill Lane Johnson’s shoes. 3.97: Sahir West, Edge Defender, UCLA: Sahir West is a bit of a tweener who has played all over the UCLA defensive line, dominating wherever he lines up. In the NFL, he may benefit from dropping some weight and becoming a true edge player where his motor and first step could make him a dangerous presence on rebuilding defense. 4.104: Zabien Brown, Cornerback, Alabama: Riq Woolen is a free agent after this season. The Eagles need another perimeter cornerback. Zabien Brown might not be a day one starter, but he has the athleticism to eventually compete for snaps on the outside. 5.142: Nate Frazier, Running Back, Georgia: The Eagles will need to prepare for a post-Saquon Barkley era. Age and injuries have caught up to the lead back and Philly will need to rejuvenate their offensive backfield this spring. Nate Frazier is an easy evaluation with his strong running style and great burst. He’s not a game changing back, but he can be a chain mover in the right offense. 5.150: Eli Finley, Tight End, Louisiana Tech: It’s unclear if Eli Stowers will be the guy the Eagles wanted. I hope he does, but the team still clearly needs some more tight end depth anyway. Eli Finley is a great receiving tight end who can really give them some quality youth at the position. 5.153: Tobi Osunsanmi, Edge Defender, Indiana: Tobi Osunsanmi is one of the biggest breakout players in the country this season. After years at Kansas State, Osunsanmi has emerged as one of the best pass rushers in college football. His track background combines with a hellacious motor to make him tough to block at the FBS level. Do his athletic tools translate? He would be a great day three flier. 7.224: Rod Moore Junior, Safety, Michigan: Rod Moore is a rangy, albeit undersized safety on the back end of the Michigan defense. He has some great coverage skills, but leaves some to be desired as a run defender. The Eagles safety situation right now is not great and some swings on high upside athletes makes a lot of sense. 7.238: Griffin Wilde, Wide Receiver, Northwestern: Griffin Wilde really strikes me as a player who will outplay his draft position. He is hidden away on an unconventional Northwestern offense, but he does big things every week for the Wildcats. He is big bodied, athletic, and sure handed. He could immediately push for snaps on an Eagles team in desperate need of pass catchers. Loading…

title: Eagles News: The MVP of Philadelphia’s season thus far
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! You know you’re not in a good place when the punter is the MVP. Do you agree with this pick of Braden Mann? Or would you go with another player? From an entertainment standpoint, Howie Roseman has a case as the […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 23: Braden Mann #10 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! You know you’re not in a good place when the punter is the MVP. Do you agree with this pick of Braden Mann? Or would you go with another player? From an entertainment standpoint, Howie Roseman has a case as the MVP since the Cam Jurgens and Jordan Davis are two of the more exciting moments of the season. Or you could go with Jalen Hurts since he was a big reason the team won the only two games they did and have looked very lost without him. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL Power Rankings: Stacking all 32 teams for Week 11, plus non-QB MVPs – ESPN 28) Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Non-QB MVP at midseason: P Braden Mann. Mann has been called on more than any other punter, which is what happens when your offense leads the league in three-and-outs by a healthy margin. But he has been nails for the most part. Mann has an NFL-best 22 punts inside the 20-yard line and only two touchbacks. His 86-yard boot in Week 9 against the Giants was the second-longest punt since 2000. And no, it is not a good sign when your punter is your first-half MVP. 12 takeaways from NFL Week 10 – BGN As for the team that Eagles fans should prefer to win the division, assuming it’s not going to be Philly? I previously felt like the Giants were the answer to this question because I can see them beating their chests about barely winning a bad division and overestimating how close they are to being serious contenders. But I actually think Washington might be the preferable choice. Maybe the Commanders keep Dan Quinn and put too much stock into coming back to win the NFC East, only to then struggle again in 2027. What do you think? NFC East Mixtape VOL. 207: Is Washington a real threat to win this? – NFC East Mixtape Week 10 has come and gone for the NFC East and the only team to emerge from it with a win was the Washington Commanders. They still have some work to do, but can they realistically win the division? Washington took down the New York Giants and they now have some difficult questions to answer. Difficult questions is the perennial state of the Dallas Cowboys, especially after their horrific loss to San Francisco on Sunday, yet they somehow remain mathematically relevant in the divisional race. RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss it all on the latest NFC East Mixtape. You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! Week 11 odds: Steelers open as favorites vs. Eagles – Behind The Steel Curtain The Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since October 24, 1965. Their last victory came before the Super Bowl era, the Penguins were founded, the Pirates won their last two World Series titles, and NFL and AFL merged. Pittsburgh needs a win to keep pace with the Bengals and hold off the Cleveland Browns, who are making a charge in the AFC Wild Card race. The Steelers look to prevent a snowball effect after a crushing Cincinnati loss that could be the turning point of the 2026 season. Eagles ‘soft tank’ roadmap for the remainder of the 2026 season – PhillyVoice 5) Get a head start on a plan for the 2027 coaching staff. Jeffrey Lurie and Howie Roseman are going to have to decide which coaches are out after this season, and which coaches they would like to retain. Of course, the biggest decision will be whether or not to move on from head coach Nick Sirianni. A few weeks ago, we laid out the argument for both sides , and in my opinion, there’s a stronger case for moving on. The last time the Eagles fired a head coach was after the 2020 season, when Doug Pederson was unable to survive a 4-11-1 record. That situation was a little different in that the Eagles didn’t decide to fire Pederson until after the season had ended, when Pederson wasn’t amenable to other changes within his coaching staff. If the Eagles are going to move on from Sirianni, they should probably already know by now. And if that is the intent, they’ll be in a unique position — relative to past firings, anyway — where they can formulate a head coaching search plan well in advance of the actual firing of the current head coach. I have no inside information here, but I would be stunned if early conversations on potential replacements aren’t already underway. Eagles Draft Talk – Iggles Blitz QB Drew Mestemaker – Oklahoma State – The Eagles have a big decision to make about Jalen Hurts future. Is he the QB for 2027? Do they sign him to an extension? We’ll see how that plays out. They could decide to go for a QB at 5 because you don’t often get a shot to draft that high. The QB could sit for a few years if needed. Mestemaker leads an explosive offense at OSU and he’s had a terrific season. He is a good athlete who can make some really impressive throws. Questions by position as Eagles return from 2026 bye week – NBCSP Coaching: Will Nick Sirianni survive this season? This season has been ugly. The Eagles won their first two games and have now lost seven straight. Sure, they lost Jalen Hurts for the season and have dealt with countless other injuries, so it has been a weird year. Maybe Jeffrey Lurie looks at the situation and gives Sirianni a mulligan. After all, Sirianni has been to the playoffs five times, to the Super Bowl twice and won it all to cap the 2024 season. That wasn’t that long ago. But we have also seen Lurie fire a Super Bowl-winning head coach and explain that it wasn’t because Doug Pederson deserved to get fired; he moved on in 2021 because he thought it was in the best interest of the franchise. So Lurie has to look at this situation and determine if the best thing for the franchise is to run it back with Sirianni in 2027. And if he does that, who are his coordinators? It’s hard to imagine Sirianni getting fired before the end of the season, so those are all fair questions for January. In the interim, let’s just see if the players continue to fight for Sirianni and his future. Are the Eagles, Howie Roseman entering the quarterback wilderness without Jalen Hurts? – PHLY Eagles Let’s assume the answer to both of those questions is yes. Wouldn’t another year spent trying to maximize Hurts with a rebuilt offensive line and quite possibly a different coaching staff give you about as much of a chance to find a “franchise quarterback” in Hurts as drafting the second or third quarterback prospect available this year? The Eagles also have plenty of draft capital in 2028 and 2029 with a real chance that the likes of Mestemaker, Manning, Mensah, and Co. will actually feature in a draft class, although it’s no given that draft capital will actually allow them to get in position for a highly touted prospect. All of this to say, the Eagles may be entering the quarterback wilderness whether they like it or not. But the notion that they should do so willingly or with enthusiasm loses sight of how difficult it may be to actually replace the most accomplished quarterback in franchise history. Colts sign CB Johnathan Edwards to active roster from practice squad; sign WR Samori Toure to practice squad – Colts Toure, 6-1, 196 pounds, has played in 23 career games (two starts) in his time with the Philadelphia Eagles (2026), New Orleans Saints (2025), Denver Broncos (2025), Chicago Bears (2024-25) and Green Bay Packers (2022-24). full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images After giving up 406 passing yards versus the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, it seems the Steelers have some interest in bolstering their secondary. On Tuesday, the Steelers worked out veteran safety Jordan Whitehead, NFL writer Aaron Wilson reported. #Steelers worked out Jordan Whitehead and Nazeeh Johnson — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) November 17, 2026 Earlier in the day, Pittsburgh reportedly worked out former Chiefs cornerback Nazeeh Johnson , which Wilson also reported. The team also officially signed former Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers safety AJ Finley to its practice squad. Although Whitehead has never been on the Steelers, he should be a familiar name as a former Pitt Panther in college. Whitehead has also been linked to the Steelers a number of times, including visiting the team in July earlier this year. Whitehead last played in 2024, when he started 12 games for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, recording 79 total tackles and two passes defensed. He suffered a season-ending injury that year after suffering a serious neck injury in a car accident. He was cleared to resume his football career in July . A fourth-round pick in 2018, the 29-year-old has appeared in 105 career NFL games, starting 101, with 11 total interceptions.

full_text: (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed former Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers safety AJ Finley to their practice squad, the team announced today . Finley signed with the Chargers in 2023 as an undrafted free agent out of Ole Miss, where he would go on to appear in 12 games as a rookie. He was waived in November, 2024 and immediately picked up by the Seattle Seahawks. Ever since, he has been on the Seahawks practice squad, appearing in four games in 2025 and three games in 2026. In 29 career games, he has 19 tackles and one forced fumble. Pittsburgh has been thin at safety all season due to the ongoing injury issues with DeShon Elliott, who missed Week 10 after hurting his knee in warmups. That has left Jaquan Brisker, Robert Spears-Jennings, and Jalen Ramsey in a hybrid role as the only safeties at the Steelers’ disposal. Let us know what you think in the comments .
