title: Which team will win the NFC East in 2026? – survey
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Commanders fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: With the season just past the halfway point, we’re continuing to ask the standard confidence question […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 20: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders looks to pass during a game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Commanders fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: With the season just past the halfway point, we’re continuing to ask the standard confidence question each week; that is, “Are you confident the Commanders are headed in the right direction?” We’ve been asking that question weekly from September to December for many years. The Commanders are fresh off of a huge ’gotta have it’ win over the Giants on Thursday Night Football. With their overall record standing a 3-5-1, and the division record at 2-2-1, after 9 games, there seems to be a renewed sense of of possibility growing around the Commanders fan base, though there is a long way to go before the 2026 season can be deemed a success. Any hope that Washington has for reaching the playoffs this season rests in a come-from-behind division championship, which remains a possibility in a struggling NFC East. However, with the victory over the Giants on Thursday and the Cowboys loss to the 49ers on Sunday the hill just got a little less steep. Washington sits 2 games back of New York, and sits just behind the Cowboys in the current standings. Dallas has played 10 games, and, with a 4-6 record has one more win and one more loss than Washington. What makes this race so interesting is the remaining schedule for the 3 prime contenders for the NFC East crown. The Giants face a particularly tough schedule, with games against the Jags, Niners, Seahawks, Browns & Lions looming. Since New York is the only team that Washington can tie with, and since the Commanders hold the first tie-breaker against the G-men, the challenge for Washington is to get 2 more wins in the final 8 weeks than the Giants. If the two teams finish with the same record, the burgundy & gold come out on top. Washington actually has to have fewer losses at the end of the season than the Cowboys to beat them out for the division title. That’s the case right now, with the ‘Boys having 6 losses compared to Washington’s 5. As with the Giants, Washington simply has to match the Dallas win total at the end of the season to be ranked higher. Thus, if Dallas wins 4 of its remaining 7 games to finish 8-9, the Commanders would only need to win 5 of their remaining 8 games to top the Cowboys by finishing with an 8-8-1 record. Likewise, if Dallas wins 3 games, Washington would need 4 wins to surpass the Silver & Blue in the standings. If you think the Commanders can go 5-3 in the final 8 games while Dallas goes 4-3 and the Giants go 3-5, then Washington should be your pick. In a scenario like that, the Week 18 game in Landover against the Cowboys could potentially determine which of these three teams gets to hang the division banner for the ‘26 regular season. But with 8 weeks left, literally anything could happen. We want to know what you think. So, in today’s second question, we ask you to predict which team — New York, Dallas or Washington — will win the NFC East title for 2026. full_text: The Commanders have opened the 21-day practice window for running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt to return off injured reserve, the team announced on Tuesday afternoon. Washington’s practice week formally starts on Thursday, which will be the first time he’ll hit the practice field after being placed on IR with a groin injury. Croskey-Merritt had been battling the injury since training camp, and Washington chose to shelf him rather than trying to manage the injury from week to week, allowing him to heal properly. RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt has returned to practice and his 21-day window has been opened pic.twitter.com/ouJ0GuU4br — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 17, 2026 That should bring some explosiveness and big-play ability back to his game — one that had been inconsistent in the most recent games he played prior to his injury. Croskey-Merritt has 21 days to be activated off IR. If he’s unable to come back, the running back will be done for the season. There’s hope, though no guarantee, that he’ll be able to play on Monday against the Cincinnati Bengals . That would provide Washington’s run game a real lift after struggling with efficiency during his absence. Croskey-Merritt would add a more physical presence to the rushing attack, which has featured Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler over the past few weeks. summary: With 2:20 remaining in the fourth quarter, the Commanders were trailing 17-21. Their attempted comeback drive had stalled out at their own 45 yard line.  On 4th and 2, they took one last shot at extending the drive for a win. Jayden Daniels’ pass to Chig Okonkwo was intercepted by Ar’Darius Washington.  It was his […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 12: Ben Sinnott #82 of the Washington Commanders scores a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on November 12, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images With 2:20 remaining in the fourth quarter, the Commanders were trailing 17-21. Their attempted comeback drive had stalled out at their own 45 yard line. On 4 th and 2, they took one last shot at extending the drive for a win. Jayden Daniels’ pass to Chig Okonkwo was intercepted by Ar’Darius Washington. It was his second pick of the season. His first had ended the Commanders’ previous possession. I had decided to “work from home” to watch the game, which started at 11:15 am in my time zone. That was looking like a poor choice. I thought the game was over and, with it, the Commanders’ season. Judging by the comments on the live game thread, I wasn’t alone. Then we got a little reminder of what it was like watching the Commanders play in 2024. The defense held the Giants to just 7 yards on the next set of downs, capped by Sonny Styles catching J.J. McCarthy from behind for a 2-yard loss on 3 rd and 3, at the two minute warning. Five plays and 55 seconds later, Jayden Daniels connected on a short pass with Stefon Diggs, who ran it in for the go-ahead score, with 1:05 remaining. Daronte Jones’ defense applied pressure on the Giants’ final drive, which stalled out on the Washington 48 yard line. And Rasul Douglas sealed the victory by intercepting an attempted bomb to Malik Nabers with 34 seconds on the clock. This season, the Commanders have demonstrated the ability to play good teams close, and even beat them. They have also demonstrated the ability to lose to bad teams. The clutch play on both sides of the ball in the final two minutes on Thursday night reminded fans that when this team locks in, they can beat anyone. The victory against the Giants pulled the Commanders within two wins of the leaders in the second-weakest division in the league, and gave them the benefit of the head-to-head tiebreak. They have 8 games remaining to at least pull even with the Giants and fend off the 4-6 Cowboys. Five of their 8 remaining opponents have losing records, including their last remaining divisional opponent. With the comeback win against the Giants, the Cardiac Commanders kept their playoff hopes very much alive. Can they sustain the momentum against the visiting 7-2 Bengals? The Commanders’ biggest issue this season has been playing with consistency. If they can start the game like they finished against the Giants and maintain that level of play through four quarters, then they absolutely can. But that kind of consistency has been elusive. There were positive signs in Thursday night’s win which might be built on to help establish consistent winning football down the stretch. The franchise QB demonstrated that he’s still got resilience in the face of adversity, Stefon Diggs showed that he’s still capable of explosive plays, Ben Sinnott flashed elite productivity in limited opportunities, the offensive line bounced back from a shocking performance against the Rams, Sonny Styles flashed elite potential in all phases on defense, the secondary continued to gel with all its players healthy, and Daronte Jones found the formula to generate pressure through the fourth quarter against a solid offensive line. As we await the Monday night matchup with the Bengals, let’s have a look at who lined up where, who stepped up and who stepped out of bounds at exactly the right time in what might prove to be the pivotal win of the Commanders’ season. Technicalities: Stats were sourced from the official NFL gamebook via NFLGSIS, Pro Football Reference (PFR), Pro Football Focus (PFF) and ESPN’s total QBR. In cases where advanced stats are scored differently, I have chosen preferred providers (eg. QB pressures – PFF, yards before contact – PFR). Where differences in advanced stats result from judgment calls (eg. Coverage yards allowed, broken tackles) I have gone with a modified consensus approach. When there is fundamental disagreement between sources, the stats won’t be reported. Minor differences between sources that support the same conclusion are reported. If advanced stats are reported without attribution of source, it means there was consensus. As always, official NFL stats override conflicting data from other sources. BIGGEST PLAYS OF THE GAME These plays had the largest impact on teams’ scoring potential within a drive, as judged by Expected Points Added (EPA). Threshhold: EPA = +/- 2.25 Biggest Plays for Commanders Q4, 1:05, 3 rd and 4 at NYG 32, Jayden Daniels pass complete short middle to Stefon Diggs for 32 yards, touchdown. EPA 4.39 Q3, 7:05, 3 rd and 1 at NYG 31, Jayden Daniels pass complete short right to Antonio Williams for 31 yards, touchdown. EPA 4.13 Q1, 4:08, 4 th and 4 at WAS 15, Dominic Zvada 33-yard field goal no good. EPA -3.0 Q3, 4:13, 2 nd and 12 at WAS 19, J.J. McCarthy pass complete short right to Malik Nabers for -1 yards. Malik Nabers fumbles (forced by Frankie Luvu), recovered by Jeremy Reaves at WAS-20. EPA -3.88 Biggest Plays for Giants Q4, 8:24, 3 rd and 7 at NYG 34, J.J. McCarthy pass complete deep middle to Isaiah Likely for 66 yards, touchdown. EPA 6.83 Q1, 6:14, 3 rd and 7 at NYG 45, J.J. McCarthy pass complete short left to Cam Skattebo for 34 yards. EPA 3.28 Q3, 6:49, 1 st and 10 at NYG 27, J.J. McCarthy pass complete deep left to Malik Nabers for 37 yards. EPA 2.44 Q4, 9:07, 4 th and 2 at NYG 31, Jayden Daniels pass incomplete short middle intended for Stefon Diggs (defended by Ar’Darius Washington). EPA -2.4 Q3, 14:13, 2 nd and 11 at WAS 20, Jayden Daniels sacked by Shelby Harris for 14 yards. EPA -2.84 Q4, 5:30, 1 st and 10 at NYG 24, Jayden Daniels pass deep left intended for Chig Okonkwo is intercepted by Jevon Holland at NYG 2 and returned for no gain. EPA -3.5 OFFENSE There were 4 penalties called on three offensive players this week. Jayden Daniels completed 23/33 passing attempts (69.7%, ADOT 6.2 yds) for 249 yds, 3 TDs and 2 INTs, with 2 balls dropped by receivers. Prior to this game, JD5 was the only QB with more than 100 passing attempts and no interceptions. As a crude metric of how well QBs protect the ball, I calculated turnover opportunities (interceptions + fumbles) as a percentage of passing attempts. After the Giants game, JD5 had 1.9% turnover opportunities, the third-lowest figure among starting QBs after C.J. Stroud and Dak Prescott at 1.8%. Drake Maye, Baker Mayfield and Justin Herbert brought up the rear, all over 6%. On the ground, JD5 contributed 11 rushing attempts for just 28 yds (2.5 Y/A) and 2 first downs. While that effort tied for his lowest rushing average of the season, his 54.5% success rate was his 4 th best in 7 games. Daniels was flagged in the third quarter for his fifth delay of game penalty this season. To his credit, he was clapping for the ball to be snapped on the play. While he wasn’t perfect, his play was good enough to get the win. JD5’s 52.2 Total QBR ranked 14 th among starting QBs in Week 10. Rachaad White had 11 carries for 47 yds (4.3 Y/A) and 4 first downs (54.5% success rate). He averaged 2.7 yards before contact/attempt, a little above average for RBs this season. White also caught 1/2 targets for 5 yds, with 1 drop. Austin Ekeler made 9 rushing attempts for 26 yds (2.9 Y/A) and 3 first downs, with 2 broken tackles. He averaged just 1.2 YBC/att, yet still managed a team-leading 55.6% rushing success rate. Ekeler also caught 4/4 targets for 26 yds. Robert Henry had 2 carries for 4 yds. Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets (10), receptions (6) and receiving yards (83), but not reception rate (60%, ADOT 5.7 yd). He was one of three Commanders with a receiving TD. title: 2027 NFL mock draft: Reid's midseason first-round predictions for all 32 picks
summary: Which NFL team could land Drew Mestemaker? Who needs Chris Cole, Ashton Hampton or Jamari Johnson? Jordan Reid projected first-round picks for 2027 -- and a trade.
full_text:
Now that the NFL trade deadline has passed and we're in the second half of the 2026 season , it's a great time to look ahead to the 2027 NFL draft .

 Some teams whose playoff hopes are mostly dashed are already fully into the process of evaluating prospects for the draft, which will take place in April in Washington. So why not take our own look at how that draft might turn out?

 This latest mock draft factors in a combination of what NFL teams need, my evaluation of production and tape from the 2026 college football season , and conversations I've had with trusted scouts and evaluators. Of course, things will change between now and April -- players will move up and down the board or exit the class entirely by returning to school -- but this is how I see things currently.

 The draft order obviously is far from set, so I based this 1-32 on what the order would look like if the season ended today. There have already been six trades in Round 1, and I actually pitched a seventh that could make sense.

 How many quarterbacks will make Round 1? Here are my full projections for all 32 first-round picks.

 Note: Underclassmen are marked with an asterisk. 

 

 

 1. Tennessee Titans  (1-8) 
 Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State* 

 Smith is  the best player in this draft, and as the first wide receiver to go No. 1 since 1996 (Keyshawn Johnson), he would allow the Titans to continue to build around quarterback  Cam Ward , the No. 1 pick of the 2025 draft. How  special  is Smith? He has drawn comparisons to some of the best wideouts of the past quarter century -- including Calvin Johnson, Larry Fitzgerald and Julio Jones -- by NFL scouts.

 Smith's 131.7 receiving yards per game ranks second in the FBS, and he continues to thrive despite Ohio State's quarterback issues . Speaking of the Buckeyes, the Titans could reunite Smith with fellow wide receiver  Carnell Tate , Tennessee's first pick in 2026. Smith's rare combination of size (6-foot-4 and 225 pounds), speed and power gives him early All-Pro potential and makes him the type of player Ward and the Titans need to further improve their offense.

 
 

 Projected trade: Jets package two first-rounders to move up 
 The Jets have three first-round picks, so I have them sending Nos. 4 and 13, along with a 2028 third-rounder, to the Chargers for the No. 2 selection. New York originally acquired the No. 13 pick in a trade with the Cowboys for defensive tackle  Quinnen Williams .

 Could this move finally allow the Jets to select their quarterback of the future?

 
 

 2. New York Jets  (via projected trade with 1-8 LAC ) 
 Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State* 

 Mestemaker has progressed from a walk-on who didn't start in high school to my top QB in this class. The Jets have used the past three drafts to establish an offensive base, selecting bookend tackles ( Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou ), wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr.  and tight end Kenyon Sadiq in Round 1. Along with star wideout  Garrett Wilson , they make New York an ideal landing spot for a rookie signal-caller.

 Mestemaker excels at pushing the ball down the field, with his 21 completions of 20 or more yards this season ranking eighth in the FBS. His decision-making is inconsistent at times, but Mestemaker is young (he's in his first season as a Power 4 starter) and has the tools to transform the Jets.

 

 
 

 3. Miami Dolphins  (1-8) 
 Colin Simmons , Edge, Texas* 

 After drafting 13 players last year, the Dolphins have a foundation of young talent on their roster. Now, Miami needs a star, which Simmons could be on defense. He is arguably the top pass rusher in this class and one of the best in the FBS at generating pressure off the edge. His 10.5 sacks are third most in the country despite him missing two games because of injury . His 20.5% pressure rate ranks fifth in the FBS, and Simmons' powerful hands let him set a violent edge in run defense.

 Pairing Simmons with 2024 first-rounder  Chop Robinson  would give the Dolphins an explosive pass-rush duo for defensive-minded coach Jeff Hafley.

 
 

 4. Los Angeles Chargers  (via projected trade with 2-8 NYJ ) 
 Charlie Becker , WR, Indiana* 

 The Chargers have been extremely disappointing this season, and their 1-8 start has exposed the need for more talent everywhere. That and the fact that they already have a QB in  Justin Herbert  are why I had them trade out of No. 2 and add another pick. And we'll use this first pick to get Herbert some help.

 Becker is an excellent vertical threat who has 10 touchdowns this season (sixth in the FBS) and can also execute the short to intermediate levels of the route tree. He is tall (6-foot-4) and sure-handed (zero drops on 85 targets this season) with excellent body control and elite hand-eye coordination, allowing him to win in the air on long and contested catch opportunities. Becker would immediately become Herbert's WR1.

 
 

 5. Philadelphia Eagles  (2-7) 
 Dylan Stewart , Edge, South Carolina* 

 This season has been a disaster for Philadelphia, but it allows the Eagles to get an elite edge-rushing talent. Stewart is a toolsy and explosive player who has the unique ability to bend around the corner and wreak havoc in the backfield. The 6-foot-5, 250-pounder hasn't had consistent production in college, but his tools and flashes of potential are tantalizing and reminiscent of  Brian Burns  coming out of Florida State . Stewart will have to answer questions during the predraft process about his production and an in-season suspension , but he's an ideal talent for the Eagles to draft and develop behind  Jonathan Greenard , Nolan Smith Jr.  and Jalyx Hunt .

 
 

 6. New York Jets  (via 3-7 IND ) 
 Leonard Moore , CB, Notre Dame* 

 Now that the Jets have traded up to take their quarterback of the future, they could select my No. 1 defensive prospect in this year's class here. Moore's 8.6% target rate is the lowest among all FBS corners this season, and he has allowed only seven completions in eight games. Moore is one of the most consistent cover guys in the country and has the length (6-foot-2, 197 pounds) and ball skills to be a shutdown corner in the NFL. He could start right away at outside corner for New York.

 
 

 

 7. Arizona Cardinals  (3-6) 
 Jordan Seaton , OT, LSU* 

 The Cardinals desperately need to add help in the trenches, and Seaton is an upper-tier athlete who is very polished in pass protection. He has allowed only one sack and four pressures this season on 344 pass-blocking snaps. He is more than capable of mirroring and matching edge rushers, though he needs to get stronger and improve his anchor and drive strength. But Seaton would be a plug-and-play starting option at either tackle spot opposite  Paris Johnson Jr. , who will be on his fifth-year option in 2027.

 
 

 8. Atlanta Falcons  (3-6) 
 CJ Carr , QB, Notre Dame* 

 With  Michael Penix Jr.  struggling to find consistency in Year 3, the Falcons could once again be convinced to use the No. 8 pick on a QB -- like they did three years ago with Penix , especially since the Falcons' front office and coach have changed since making that selection. Atlanta has plenty of skill-position talent (RB  Bijan Robinson , WR Drake London , TE Kyle Pitts Sr. ) that could enable a young QB to thrive immediately.

 Carr is an instinctive passer who consistently has answers and has already been given considerable autonomy in Notre Dame's offense. He doesn't have the high-end traits of some passers in the class (picture a more mobile Kirk Cousins ), but he is polished in many of the skills that are essential to playing the position.

 
 

 9. Houston Texans  (3-6) 
 Zereoue Williams , OT, Utah 

 "I could see him making a rise similar to  Kolton Miller " is a text that a scout sent me after watching Williams earlier this season. Miller was drafted No. 15 in 2018 by the Raiders, and Williams could be taken even higher. He is already 24 years old, which is part of why he is receiving some…

title: NFL Week 11 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we're hearing
summary: What are people around the league saying about Fernando Mendoza? Could changes be coming in Dallas? And what now for New England? Here's the latest intel.
full_text:
Week 11 of the  2026 NFL season  is here, and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 First, what are people saying about last weekend's much-anticipated first start for Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza ? What did he show against the Seahawks and what does it tell us about the rest of his season? Then, what are we hearing on the Cowboys' struggling defense and any potential changes on the horizon? What about the Patriots and their sudden downturn in the aftermath of Drake Maye 's injury? And finally, who are the most interesting 2027 free agents and what is the early intel on them?

 It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 11.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Mendoza's debut | Cowboys' defense 
 Patriots' concern | 2027 free agents 
 Fantasy advice  | More notes, intel 

 
 

 What are people around the league saying about Fernando Mendoza 's debut? 
 Graziano: They are saying he looked the part and that the moment didn't look too big for him. And that is really what you're looking for if you're starting a rookie No. 1 pick in Week 10 against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks' defense .

 Mendoza obviously has work to do on pre-snap diagnosis and other aspects of the job at this level, but he's not the first quarterback to not see Devon Witherspoon coming on a blitz, and he won't be the last. He clearly offers something with his legs that Kirk Cousins does not at this point, and he made throws outside the numbers that people view as a sign the offense can evolve with him at the helm.

 Fowler: People I spoke with saw flashes. Playing Seattle is an arduous task. But Mendoza used his legs to escape congestion, completed passes to 10 different receivers and navigated an offense that was without star tight end  Brock Bowers for much of the game. The Seahawks eventually overwhelmed him. He missed a few blitzes and took six sacks. He missed some throws, particularly to the left side of the field. But as one personnel evaluator noted, the game didn't look too big for him and he kept his eyes downfield, whether in the pocket or on the move. The arm strength and mobility are obvious, and those can be assets to the Raiders' offense in the coming weeks and into 2027.

 

 While Cousins probably would have started another week had he stayed, Mendoza was making enough progress behind the scenes that he was going to play soon enough. And he did enough to at least validate that promise.

 Graziano: He did, and it will get better. This is quite similar to the situation Eli Manning had as a rookie with the Giants in 2004, when veteran Kurt Warner started the first half of the season and Manning took over midway through. One key difference is that Warner remained on that Giants team for the rest of the season, whereas Cousins is no longer there to be a sounding board for Mendoza. So that's something to watch. But the Raiders have been extremely deliberate about Mendoza's development program, and while yes, his first start came a few weeks earlier than they had planned, they believe he's ready enough. And Sunday's debut didn't cause any fresh concern that I can detect in that building.

 It doesn't get a lot easier, with Denver and Cleveland in the next two weeks ahead of the Raiders' bye, but Mendoza has something, and people are excited to see more. It's no coincidence that the NFL flexed that Week 12 Raiders-Browns game into primetime on Tuesday.

 Fowler:  This is a challenging three-game stretch for a young quarterback. In order for him to survive it, the Raiders must find a way to run the ball more efficiently. How a Klint Kubiak-run offense ranks last in yards per rush at 2.9 is shocking to me, even with the transitional state of the offensive line. The Raiders' backs have a combined two rushing performances of more than 60 yards --  Ashton Jeanty  (102) in Week 1 and  Mike Washington Jr . (83) in Week 8. That's it. Running the ball well is a staple of the Kubiak system, and if the Raiders are to properly support Mendoza, they must find a way to manufacture explosive plays on the ground.

 The rest should come into focus. "Mendoza is a good fit for Klint [Kubiak's] offense," an NFC offensive coach said. "I thought he did well when facing live bullets."

 

 
 What's next for the Cowboys and their major problems on defense? Could they shake things up? 
 (Update: On Wednesday morning, the Cowboys made a playcalling change , and the below text has been updated to reflect that.)

 Fowler: The big shake-up would be changing coaching personnel on defense and based on public comments coming from the Dallas brass this week, it feels like everything is on the table when it comes to defensive coordinator Christian Parker's status. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer and owner Jerry Jones have been noncommittal about Parker. On Wednesday morning, the Cowboys did make a change and gave playcalling duties to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. Parker was formerly a Pettine understudy in Green Bay.

 In talking to people in Dallas, they believe firing coaches wouldn't solve much. Parker is a good young coach. It just hasn't worked out thus far. The personnel on defense, though improved on paper from a year ago, still isn't great and is clearly a year away. Yes, it looks bad --  Christian McCaffrey running untouched upfield twice is a hard image to shake -- but the Cowboys have already tweaked the defensive lineup earlier in the season. Plus, it's tough to make wholesale changes, in part because Dallas is very much alive in a weak NFC East.

 Graziano: Agreed. And I believe that's the way the Cowboys see it, too. Jones made some comments on the radio Tuesday  hinting about possibly changing defensive playcallers, and Dallas ultimately went that route. But this is very much not an ownership group that likes to make in-season coaching changes, so they would consider it a drastic step to move on totally from Parker now. Also, if Schottenheimer is concerned about his own job security at the end of this season, throwing a second defensive coordinator overboard in two years might not be the best way to project that he has everything under control.

 

 Fowler: The Titans and Eagles are on the schedule over the next two weeks. That could be a stretch for Dallas to get things right, though Cam Ward is improving in Tennessee and that game is hardly a gimme. Playoffs or not, the Cowboys will have serious work to do in the offseason to replenish the defense ... again. Defensive tackle  Quinnen Williams is worth building around. He's having a strong season as one of the lone bright spots on that side of the ball. But the Cowboys will need help at all three levels. There are not enough standouts. And they have just four picks in April's draft to change that.

 Situating the futures of corner Joey Porter Jr . and wide receiver George Pickens is critical. Franchise-tagging one of them could risk losing the other, and cornerback is a major need for the team, even with Porter in the lineup. Dallas was brimming with confidence defensively coming out of camp, and the good feelings dissipated early in the season. This is going on two years of bad defensive football.

 Graziano: It makes you wonder if the organization needs to take a broader look at the way it scouts, acquires and develops defensive talent. The Cowboys seem to need a more coherent overall plan, which admittedly is tough when you change defensive coordinators every year. Since Dan Quinn left to coach the Commanders, they have cycled through Mike Zimmer, Matt Eberflus and now potentially Parker. The criticism of Eberflus last season was that he didn't coach to the specific abilities of his players enough and wasn't flexible in making scheme changes to reflect the players' strengths and weaknesses. But things are worse on that side of the…

title: NFL Power Rankings: Stacking all 32 teams for Week 11, plus non-QB MVPs
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 11? We made our 1-32 list and picked the non-quarterback MVPs for each roster.
full_text:
When the NFL Honors awards ceremony takes place the Thursday before  Super Bowl LXI , it's almost guaranteed that the player who accepts the MVP award will be a quarterback. Former Vikings running back Adrian Peterson (2012) is the only non-QB to be named MVP since 2010, and only three non-QBs have won in the 21st century.

 But what if quarterbacks were disqualified from winning the award? In addition to our weekly 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick the non-quarterback MVP for each team at midseason. Which defenders and skill players deserve love for what they've done this season?

 To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a couple of highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Patriots' trip to Munich could not have gone any worse, as they left Germany with a two-game losing streak and without quarterback Drake Maye ( ankle injury ). That caused them to tie for the biggest fall of any team in our Power Rankings over the past week (three spots), and Maye could be out for the season if his ankle is fractured. New England is 1-3 in its past four games, with all of its losses coming to NFC North opponents. 
 The Browns are in the top 15 of our rankings for the first time this season after another comeback win -- this time against the Texans . Cleveland quarterback  Deshaun Watson  has conducted a winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime in all six of the Browns' wins. Watson joins the Cowboys' Troy Aikman (1990) and Lions' Matthew Stafford (2016) as the only QBs in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to achieve that feat, per ESPN Research. 
 The Commanders made the biggest climb of any team this week (three spots) after a Thursday night win over the Giants. Washington is 2-1 since its bye week, and it's still not out of the NFC East race yet, two games behind first-place New York while owning the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Giants. However, the Commanders have only one divisional game left to boost their playoff odds -- Week 18 versus the Cowboys . 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with a slight change at No. 1 from  last week .

 

 
 Jump to a team:

 1. San Francisco 49ers (8-1) 
 Week 10 result: Beat the Cowboys 46-40 
 Week 10 ranking: 2 

 Non-QB MVP at midseason: LB Fred Warner 

 

 While QB Brock Purdy is a top candidate for league MVP , Warner is making a strong case to be the first linebacker to win Defensive Player of the Year since Luke Kuechly in 2013. Warner's 88 tackles rank sixth in the NFL. He's tied for first in forced fumbles (five) to go with a fumble recovery, 0.5 sacks and three pass breakups. He has done all that after returning from a broken and dislocated right ankle injury that cost him most of last season. For a defense on its fifth coordinator in five years, Warner is the constant and one of the primary reasons the Niners are 8-1. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 

 2. Buffalo Bills (8-1) 
 Week 10 result: Beat the Jets 31-12 
 Week 10 ranking: 1 

 Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge rusher  Greg Rousseau 

 

 The transition from 4-3 defensive end to 3-4 outside linebacker has worked wonders for Rousseau. He is in the midst of a career season, leading the NFL in quarterback pressures (41) and quarterback hits (27). He is also tied for fourth in sacks (eight). Just over halfway through the season, Rousseau has already matched or set career highs in just about every meaningful pass rushing or defending stat. -- Nick Suss

 Week 10 result: Beat the Titans 40-23

 Washington has been quarterback  Trevor Lawrence 's top target -- his 64 targets are 21 more than the next-closest player ( Jakobi Meyers ). There's a good chance he surpasses his previous best yardage (847) before December. He also leads the NFL with 17.9 yards per catch. Sunday's game specifically showcased the trust Lawrence has in Washington's ability to win 50-50 balls. -- Michael DiRocco

 The Bears have maintained a top-five rushing offense (142 yards per game) despite a constant wave of injuries in the backfield. A big reason for that is the load Swift has carried in  Kyle Monangai 's five-game absence ( toe/thumb ). Swift has logged the third-most offensive snaps of any Bears skill player (63%), including 22 rushes against the Patriots and 27 at Seattle a week later . He ran in three second-half TDs against the Seahawks, has already reached a career high of 10 TDs and is five away from setting the franchise's single-season record. Despite dealing with injuries of his own, Swift has not missed a game. -- Courtney Cronin

 Week 10 result: Beat the Falcons 35-13 
 Week 10 ranking: 6 

 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Kenneth Walker III 

 

 Walker has been a blessing for the Chiefs' offense, considering he has produced many of the team's explosive plays since  signing a three-year deal  this past offseason. By being a stabilizing presence, Walker has helped quarterback Patrick Mahomes find his groove following his return from the most significant injury of his career. Walker missed Week 10 because of a groin injury .  -- Nate Taylor

 Non-QB MVP at midseason: OT Amarius Mims 

 

 Not even pass block win rate, which is a great metric, does Mims full justice. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Mims is in one-on-one blocking situations at the second-highest rate in the league (87.6%). Yet he has the lowest pressure rate allowed among all offensive tackles (3.1%). Coach Zac Taylor gave Mims the highest praise Sunday by saying he wouldn't trade him for any other right tackle. Given Cincinnati's offensive success on a high dropback rate, it's hard to argue with that. -- Ben Baby

 The Broncos are the league's foremost escape artists -- six of their seven wins have come by one score -- so we're looking for an MVP from the defense who has closed out those contests. Linebacker  Alex Singleton leads the league in tackles per game and run stop win rate, but Allen's down-to-down relentlessness is the tone-setter for the group. He is second in the league in quarterback hits despite a double-team rate of 79.4% on his pass-rush snaps. Allen impacts almost everything happening around him. -- Jeff Legwold

 There are multiple options to choose from on the Vikings' elite defense, and it's even reasonable to consider kicker Will Reichard . But Van Ginkel has been all over the field in coordinator Brian Flores' scheme. He leads the team in sacks (8.5) and pressure rate (15%) and is tied for the lead in forced fumbles (two). title: Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 11: Takes on four QBs, Lions, Rams, more
summary: Get ready for Week 11 with what makes Vikings-49ers must-watch football, Joe Burrow's MVP case and how Aidan Hutchinson's injury could impact the Lions.
full_text:
Are you excited for NFL Week 11 ? At first, it might look like a sleepy slate. Jaguars at Giants and Raiders at Broncos are two of our marquee games. But there's one contest that, to this enormous football nerd, is the game of the season.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 
 Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide' 

 
 This week, I'll expand on why Joe Burrow looks like an MVP, tell you about another Rams personnel innovation, project eventual QB changes for two NFC South teams and wonder if Aidan Hutchinson is the final defensive injury the Lions can't overcome. But first, here's one matchup you won't want to miss.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Shanahan vs. Flores is matchup of the best   
 Why Burrow is the MVP 
 Rams should lean on their RBs 
 Hutchinson's injury wounds Lions bad   
 Do Falcons need a new 2027 QB? 
 Do Saints need a new 2027 QB? 
 Mendoza's debut is a scratch 
 Some extra inklings 

 
 

 

 I think ... Vikings-49ers is the coolest game of the season 
 The Vikings have had a fraught three weeks. Everyone was excited to see them face the Lions in Week 8 -- the best offense they'd faced in a while. Detroit stuck it to 'em with a sick schematic wrinkle for which the Vikings were not prepared -- multiple tight ends lined up in the backfield as quasi-fullbacks to pave open rushing lanes.

 

 Then the Vikings played the Bills in Week 9 -- Josh Allen and another grindy running game -- and the Packers in Week 10 with Jordan Love coming off a flamethrower performance against the Patriots. At various points over those three weeks, it has felt like the upcoming test for the Vikings has been the test for the Vikings. Will this be the offense to build a blueprint against Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores' unique defense? Or will Flores prove that his defense is insurmountable even by the league's top attacks?

 The NFL rarely exists in such absolutes. All of those particular matchups were exciting and educational in their own ways. But if there's one game I've been waiting for with bated breath in the seasonlong pursuit of an answer to the Flores defense, it's this one: Vikings against 49ers in Week 11.

 This is quite literally the best against the best. The 49ers lead the league in points per drive (3.0), success rate and EPA per play on offense. The Vikings lead the league in points per drive (1.24), success rate and EPA per play (if you eliminate the Bucs' rainstorm game against the Falcons, which is cheating, but I don't care) on defense. It does not get better for offensive football than what the 49ers are doing right now. It does not get better for defensive football than what the Vikings are doing right now. Snap the pool stick, toss it down at midfield and let's see who survives.

 Not only are these the most effective units on their respective sides of the ball -- there's actually some structural similarity between the two. The Flores defense has been exhaustively covered this season, but if you've missed them to this point of the season: The Vikings are blitzing on 72.3% of opposing dropbacks through 10 weeks. I shouldn't need to tell you where that ranks among league defenses, but just in case: It's first.

 To blitz that much sounds deranged (and likely is), but Flores has greatly deepened the meaning of blitz packages in the modern NFL. He doesn't blitz to get the quarterback down, but blitzes to force the ball out fast to predictable hot reads. He blitzes to keep the back and tight end in protection and limit the pass-catching options the opponent can deploy. For many defensive coordinators, the blitz is an end to itself -- they want to get to third-and-long so they can blitz. For Flores, the blitz is a means to many different ends depending on the opponent and context.

 Let's consider the route distributions. Opposing offenses get all five routes into the concept 31.2% of the time against the Vikings, which is the lowest number in any season as far back as I have data (2017). The aggressive blitz fronts -- with five or six (or seven or eight) bodies on them -- keep backs and tight ends in the formation to protect, which makes the Vikings all the more dangerous when they drop bodies into coverage and only bring four on the rush. Against the Vikings' four-man rush, opposing quarterbacks are averaging an eternity to throw the ball (3.34 seconds, highest in the NFL Next Gen Stats database) and still suffer a 44% pressure rate, which leads the league.

 

 Flip the coin to the other side, and you'll discover that no offense gets five routes into the concept more often than the San Francisco 49ers . On 72.5% of Brock Purdy 's dropbacks this season, the 49ers have five eligible in the concept -- that's tied for the highest rate of any offense over the past two seasons with ... the 2025 49ers.

 Why so many players out in the concept? It is indicative of a change that's been underway in San Francisco's offense since the Christian McCaffrey trade in 2022.

 When you employ McCaffrey, you don't keep the back in to protect . Are you out of your mind? Have you seen this guy catch passes? The only season of the past five years in which the 49ers have been below 72.5% in five-out rate was 2024, when McCaffrey was hurt for much of the year. When the Cowboys called up a Cover 0 blitz in Week 10 in a got-to-have-it spot late against the 49ers, San Francisco had no issue getting McCaffrey into the route and quickly throwing him the ball against a defensive end ( Von Miller ) peeling off into coverage. A 74-yard touchdown later, the game was over.

 

 This peeling defensive end is a big part of how the Vikings like to deal with pass-catching backs, mind you. No edge rusher drops into coverage more often than Andrew Van Ginkel . But for as special of a Swiss Army knife as the Gink is ... do you like him dropping with McCaffrey in space?

 Much as Flores throws additional bodies at the offensive core to force players into protection, the 49ers throw as many eligible bodies as possible into the route to force defenders to win in coverage. Because the ball can go to George Kittle and McCaffrey at high volumes, it's hard to play man coverage against 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan -- your linebackers and safeties will be victimized -- so you have to drop into zone, which pulls players out of your blitz packages. Purdy has been blitzed on 29.1% of his dropbacks, 27th among 37 qualifying quarterbacks this season.

 When I say "five receivers in the route," you might instinctively think about spreading the defense out -- and you'd be right. But the 49ers, critically, do not play from spread formations. No offense has been more condensed in the entire Next Gen Stats era than the 2026 49ers, who have an average formational width of 18.9 yards -- a full yard tighter than second place (the 2025 49ers at 19.9 yards).

 This has been another big leap in the 49ers' offense since they acquired McCaffrey. From 2017 to 2021 -- B.C, or Before Christian -- the 49ers were in condensed sets on 42.3% of their offensive snaps. After the McCaffrey trade, that number leaps to 61.2% -- easily the highest among offenses.

 The condensed sets serve several purposes. They allow the 49ers to get extra blockers into the run concept more easily -- they wouldn't have nearly as complex of a running game otherwise. They allow pre-snap motions to hit faster across the formation, which strains how well a defense communicates -- linebackers have to see a lot more when all 11 players are in the offensive picture. They all…

title: The NFL's current worst team? Lamar-less Ravens making that case
summary: The Ravens have gone 38 days without a win. It has been 24 days since they've had a lead.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- In the final seconds of Monday night's 23-20 loss to the winless Los Angeles Chargers , Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry voiced his displeasure on the sideline while looking up at the scoreboard. 
 
 "This is horrible," Henry said. 
 
 In a matter of weeks, the Ravens have gone from being a Super Bowl contender to a team facing a once unthinkable question: Is Baltimore currently the NFL's worst team? The Lamar Jackson -less Ravens have certainly looked like it. 
 
 Over the last four weeks, Baltimore has a minus-74 point differential -- 21 points worse than any other NFL team. During this stretch, in which Jackson has been limited to one snap because of ankle and right thumb injuries, the Ravens offense ranks 30th in scoring (13.3 points) and their defense is 28th (31.8). 
 
 As far as where the Ravens' frustration ranks, let's just say it's off the charts. 
 
 Asked about the level of urgency on the team, Henry snapped back, "How many have we lost in a row? OK, so the urgency should tell you right there. I don't mean to be rude, but you all are asking questions I think you all know the answer to." 
 
 The Ravens have gone 38 days without a win. It's been 24 days since they've had a lead. 
 
 Baltimore has not led at any point in its past three games. The Ravens haven't had a stretch like this in 19 years. 
 
 
 
 The message from Ravens coach Jesse Minter to his players: There's no more margin for error. 
 
 "Honestly, we have a two-game stretch before our bye to stay alive," Minter said. "That's really where it's at." 
 
 After a 4-1 start, Baltimore has seen its season fall apart. The Ravens (4-6) now have a better chance at a top-five pick in the 2027 draft (8.6%) than a playoff spot (4.1%), according to ESPN Analytics. 
 
 ESPN's Football Power Index is projecting Baltimore to win one of its final seven games (Week 16 against the Cleveland Browns ). After playing on Monday night, the Ravens have a quick turnaround before playing at the Carolina Panthers (4-5) on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox) and at the Houston Texans (3-6) the following week. 
 
 "It's going to be about getting up off the mat and coming back to work," Minter said. "And I think we have the guys to do that, but we have to do it. We keep talking about things, and [we need] more action." 
 
 The Ravens' problems range from self-inflicted mistakes to missed assignments on defense to the inability to run the ball. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 BALTIMORE'S ISSUE ON offense has been getting out of its own way. The Ravens have been flagged for a league-worst 55 offensive penalties. 
 
 On Monday night, Baltimore hurt itself with a turnover. On a potential comeback drive, wide receiver Zay Flowers had the ball ripped out of his grasp around midfield with two minutes remaining. 
 
 Flowers left the locker room as soon as reporters entered, leaving others to explain his critical mistake. 
 
 
 
 "I mean, he should have held onto the ball," Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said. "There are plays that everybody has given up, that I've given up. That's my teammate, and he has made countless plays but he's human, too. The Ravens aren't the Ravens without him, and we believe in him. We love him." 
 
 This was Flowers' fourth fumble in the fourth quarter since 2023 (including playoffs), the most among wide receivers during this span. He also made a costly mistake in the 2023 AFC Championship Game, when he fumbled near the goal line in the fourth quarter of a 17-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs . Flowers did not talk after that game, too. 
 
 "He has made plays time and time again, and he's helped this team win a lot of games," tight end Mark Andrews said. "He's a guy who's going to learn from his mistakes and get better from this. I think that at the end of the day, we have to have each other's backs and be on one accord. We talk about that and just [to] stay together, and I for sure have his back." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 JESSE MINTER LANDED  the Ravens head coach job, in part, because of his defensive expertise. So far, Baltimore is on pace to give up the second-most points in team history. 
 
 The Ravens were no match for the top three quarterbacks in the AFC. Joe Burrow put up 35 points on them. Josh Allen totaled 36 points. Trevor Lawrence racked up 33 points. 
 
 Then, on Monday night, it wasn't about the quarterback. It was the collapse of the Baltimore run defense. 
 
 The common denominator in all those games: There is a disconnect on defense. 
 
 "I think the particular reason is everyone wasn't doing their job play in and play out," Ravens middle linebacker Roquan Smith said. "We can all put a hand in it. So, we have to get better. It just comes down to the details. Each and every player has to hone in on their details at the end of the day and be able to come out and play the game the way we want to play." 
 
 The Ravens are on pace to allow 440 points, which would fall one point shy of the franchise record (441 in the inaugural season 1996). Trey Hendrickson , the prized free agent addition, has two sacks and seven quarterback hits in eight games. Marlon Humphrey , the team's most experienced cornerback, has allowed the fifth-most passing yards in coverage (425) this season, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. 
 
 Minter believes accountability goes beyond showing up to meetings and practice on time. It's about attention to details. 
 
 "Accountability means a lot of different things," Minter said, "but to me, it's really what happens on the field when it matters." 
 
 Still, the long-standing identity of this franchise has been to stop the run and establish the run. Can the Ravens do both at a high level? 
 
 "I think we have guys that can," Minter said, "but talk is cheap." 
 
 
 
 
 THE RAVENS SET a team record on Monday night that they would rather forget. Baltimore managed no yards rushing in the first half. 
 
 "Unacceptable," Minter said before adding, "It's embarrassing." 
 
 The Ravens offensive line continually got pushed back, and Henry struggled to break tackles. Henry was hit at the line or behind it on eight of 10 carries, which resulted in 10 total rushing yards. 
 
 Baltimore finished with 16 yards rushing, which is the third fewest in Ravens history. 
 
 "We're just not doing a good enough job to be efficient in the run game," Henry said. "Sixteen total yards is a clear explanation." 
 
 What's also clear is how the Ravens perform with and without Jackson, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks after having right thumb surgery in early November. Baltimore acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett to try to keep the season alive in case Jackson can return, but the playoff chances are quickly dwindling without the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player. 
 
 With Jackson as their starting quarterback, the Ravens are 82-38 (.683) and average 27.6 points per game. Without Jackson as its starter since 2019, Baltimore is 7-16 (.304) and average 17.4 points per game. 
 
 "Lamar is a big part of what we do, but it's a grown-man's league," Henry said. "It hasn't been good enough, and I think losing five in a row shows that. So, of course having [No.] 8 will help, but at the end of the day, we have to go out there and do our jobs."

title: Fantasy buzz: Kirk Cousins, Stefon Diggs bring reliability to fantasy lineups
summary: Every lineup needs consistent, week-to-week performers and Tristan has three players to start down the stretch.
full_text:
As an avid fan of -- and our primary ranker for -- our new Knockout fantasy football game this season, I'm all about the consistency kings.

 (On an aside, it's a great week to join a new Knockout league , being that you need only eight managers to play!)

 Sure, those win-your-matchup-all-by-himself scores from  George Pickens , Jordan Love or Tee Higgins  the past three weeks are plenty of fun. But bolstering your lineup with the "old reliables" is important, too, and that's especially so in a game where avoiding a low statistical floor is paramount.

 That's why last week's trade which sent veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings piqued my interest. Cousins is tied for the fourth-most games as a top-10 fantasy quarterback this season (five), but he has also been the most consistent player at his position. Aside from his five top-10 weeks, Cousins' other games saw him finish 11th, 17th, 18th, 19th and 21st, and in only three of those was his score more than five points beneath the No. 10 score.

 Best yet, you can surely get Cousins for a song in trade, being that he has exceeded the one-third (33.3%) start rate in ESPN leagues only once all season (in Week 6), and sits at only 65.1% rostered today. He fits, almost perfectly, the mold of the old-reliable backup/weekly superflex quarterback. To that end, in a freshly drafting Knockout league of mine Tuesday night, my No. 1 quarterback target was Trevor Lawrence -- more on that in a moment -- but my backup was Cousins. It's a pairing that will bring much comfort at a discounted price from many of the other name brands.

 

 Cousins' reliability also benefits his receivers, who warrant trade inquiries as well. Justin Jefferson 's best seasons came with Cousins under center, and Jordan Addison 's thumb surgery, which is expected to cost him multiple weeks, locks Jefferson into the alpha role in Minnesota. Jefferson had a season-high 13 targets and 16.4 fantasy points in Cousins' return, which bolstered Jefferson's fantasy WR1 status. Tight end T.J. Hockenson   should also benefit from Cousins' installation and Addison's absence.

 To put a bow on it, the Vikings have the second-most-favorable remaining schedule for quarterbacks, and the fifth-most favorable for wide receivers.

 Cousins and his Vikings teammates, aren't the only ones on my consistency-oriented trade target list. Here are two others:

 Bhayshul Tuten , RB, Jacksonville Jaguars : I'm all-in on the Jaguars in fantasy, as they're on an unreal run over the past year, and they match up brilliantly, schedule-wise , down the stretch. It's the reason for my Lawrence interest in Tuesday's draft, but when examining an offense likely to remain on a roll, the running back is certainly someone you want. Tuten's 56% rushing share is 13th at the position, and only 14 running backs have delivered a top-25 "start worthy" score more often. In a season of injury-driven fantasy lineup volatility, he's a "set it and forget it" weekly RB2.

 Stefon Diggs , WR, Washington Commanders : He's a ho-hum type, started in greater than 40% of ESPN leagues only three times all season, but someone has to catch passes in Washington. Diggs has a 20% target rate for the season, and he's tied for 11th among wide receivers in top-25 fantasy weeks. Antonio Williams might be the exciting, high-ceiling receiver in the Commanders' offense, but there's Diggs week after week, delivering his 10-15 points to his fantasy managers. Also be aware that the Commanders have the position's fourth-most-favorable remaining schedule .

 - Tristan H. Cockcroft 

 

 Nov. 17: Henry has confusing night, Hampton breaks through 

 Derrick Henry had an interesting game on Monday night. I mean, it's hard to say he had a bad game when he scored 19 fantasy points. However, it was one of those games where you're happy with the result, but worried about what it means moving forward. Henry was quite inefficient as he turned his 15 touches into just 20 total yards. His 10 rushing yards are the second fewest he has had in any game with double-digit touches in his career. It was his also fifth consecutive game running for less than 60 yards.

 

 While Henry's struggles on the ground are worrisome, there's some good news. He was targeted much more frequently with Jacoby Brissett   under center for the  Baltimore Ravens .  His five catches tied for the second-highest total of his career. More targets could help make up for the lack of ground production. Henry has a potential rebound opportunity next week against the  Carolina Panthers  who rank top-two in both rushing touchdowns and fantasy PPG allowed to RBs.

 Other takeaways from Monday's game 

 
 The Ravens were not afraid to let Brissett air it out in his first start for the team. He threw 49 times, finishing with 340 passing yards and 11.8 fantasy points. Yes, the fact both Baltimore touchdowns came on the ground hurt his fantasy total, but the volume should not be ignored. With all the QB injuries, plus six teams taking their bye in Week 11, Brissett is in play as a streaming option against the Panthers. 
 Zay Flowers finished with six catches for 74 yards on seven targets. He has surpassed 11 fantasy points in every game -- except the two with QB  Joe Fagnano . That safe floor, paired with his upside, means he should be started every week. 
 Mark Andrews had his best game of the season, turning eight targets into eight catches for 82 yards. He finished with 16.2 fantasy points, all of which were season highs. I believe a resurgence has arrived for the star tight end, due to the team's QB change. Brissett has always targeted tight ends at a high rate. Fantasy managers in need of TE help should try to get Andrews on their roster this week -- whether it be adding off the waiver wire or trading for him. 
 Omarion Hampton had the best night for the no-longer winless  Los Angeles Chargers . He turned 22 carries into 105 yards and a touchdown. It was his second game of the season playing on over 60% of snaps and he reached 100 yards and scored a touchdown in both. Hopefully, the Chargers will continue to feature him. He has a favorable matchup coming up against the  New York Jets , who allow the second-most rushing yards before contact per carry. Consider him to be a low-end RB2 during the upcomng Bye-mageddon. 
 Justin Herbert had his best game of the season, scoring 16.26 fantasy points. He threw for only 129 yards with no touchdowns. However, the bulk of his fantasy points came via his legs, as he ran for 51 yards and a score. I'm reluctant to jump back on his bandwagon, though, due to the lack of passing results. 
 Tre' Harris finished with 86 receiving yards, which is even more impressive considering how few yards Herbert actually threw for in this one. Harris benefitted from  Ladd McConkey 's absence and is worth adding in deeper 12-team leagues. That said, I would be reluctant to trust any piece of this team's passing attack right now. 
 
 -- Michael F. Florio 

 
 Nov. 16: Who got the ball in Week 10? 
 

 The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out.

 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions 
 Rhamondre Stevenson  tried to play through his knee injury, but finished with just seven touches and 1.5 fantasy points. He narrowly outsnapped Corey Kiner , who had more rushing attempts (10-6) and ran more routes (14-12). Stevenson handled most of the backfield work early in the game but didn't play in the fourth quarter with the game out of reach. The upcoming bye week gives Stevenson more time to recover and, with TreVeyon Henderson on IR, he should remain the team's lead back. New England has upcoming favorable matchups against the Chargers and Bills, but much will depend on Drake Maye 's health .

 A.J. Brown returned from a two-game absence against the Lions, finishing with two receptions for 27 yards and 4.7 fantasy points before exiting with…

title: Super Bowl LXI odds: All 32 teams' odds to win the championship
summary: Every NFL team's win total, as well as odds to win the division, the conference and Super Bowl LXI.
full_text:
More than halfway through the 2026 NFL season, the shortest odds to win the Super Bowl are the same as they were going into the season, but there are two different teams sharing the top spot instead of the single team that began the campaign there.

 The Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers lead the championship odds board at +500 after beginning the season at a second-best 10-1 and 11th-best 19-1, respectively. Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Rams , who began the season as the standalone Super Bowl favorite at +500, have lengthened out to 12-1 amid a so-so start and some major injuries.

 

 One of the biggest positive improvers is the Minnesota Vikings , who jumped from 24-1 to 22-1 after reacquiring quarterback Kirk Cousins and are down to 15-1 after encouraging early returns from him. Minnesota began the campaign at 50-1 for the Super Bowl, behind every other team in the extremely competitive NFC North.

 There has also been a handful of incredible disappointments this season. The New England Patriots , Baltimore Ravens , Los Angeles Chargers and Philadelphia Eagles all began the season in the top eight for Super Bowl odds at 18-1 or shorter; more than halfway the campaign, they are all out to 100-1 or longer, with the latter two all the way out at 1,000-1.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change.

title: Is Chuba Hubbard the biggest X factor to spark a Panthers turnaround?
summary: Meet Carolina's team captain, a locker room leader and a relentless running back who is "chasing greatness myself."
full_text:
Editor's note: Panthers RB Chuba Hubbard finished Sunday's 20-17 win at New Orleans with 92 rushing yards, two rushing touchdowns and 80 receiving yards. This story originally published Friday, Nov. 13 as a preview to Carolina's Week 10 matchup. 

 CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Chuba Hubbard  knows that no one is perfect. But that hasn't stopped the Carolina Panthers ' running back from chasing perfection. And after a forgettable, injury-marred 2025 campaign, during which he lost his starting job after a career season in 2024, the team captain is leading the backfield again, and he's perhaps better than ever.

 "I pride myself in hard work and staying consistent in knowing what I can do and trying to bring my best every single day, so it's more so just fighting for excellence and fighting to be perfect in every way possible," Hubbard told ESPN.

 Hubbard, 27, signed a four-year, $33.2 million contract extension during his breakout 2024 campaign, when he rushed for 1,195 yards and produced 11 total touchdowns in 15 games. Through eight games in 2026, he has rushed for 619 yards and produced seven total touchdowns, bouncing back as the Panthers have struggled to find consistency almost everywhere else during a three-game losing streak and a 3-5 start.

 

 But those numbers don't tell the complete story of Hubbard's value. He's talented, sure, but his true worth is as a tone-setter for the organization.

 Though he was selected by the franchise, while Matt Rhule was the coach, in the fourth round of the 2021 NFL draft, Hubbard has established himself as the standard-bearer for the Dave Canales era over the past three seasons. And with Carolina fighting to maintain its position atop the NFC South, his value has become apparent, if not paramount, to the team's ability to recalibrate its season.

 "What I love about Chuba is that the things that we talk about wanting to be as an organization, he represents those in spades," Canales said. "His preparation, the way that he works, the way I have to kind of reel him in and call him back a little bit because he goes so hard."

 Hubbard could be the X factor who wills Carolina to a win Sunday at the Caesars Superdome ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ), where the Panthers haven't won since the 2022 season. Hubbard, who has 70.8% of the team's carries this season, will face the New Orleans Saints , who have one of the league's worst rushing defenses (ranked 29th). A win could reignite Carolina's hopes of securing consecutive division titles for the first time since the franchise owned the NFC South crown from 2013 to 2015.

 According to those who know him best, Hubbard is ready to shoulder that burden, not only because of who he is as a player, but also because of who he is as a person and a leader in the locker room.

 

 Chuba Hubbard's style 'keeps a defense honest' and could bode well in New Orleans 

 Hubbard entered Week 10 with the 10th-most rushing yards in the NFL. He has played one fewer game than five of the backs who are in front of him on that list, and three of those playmakers ( Derrick Henry with 689, Jonathan Taylor at 656 and Javonte Williams at 629) have fewer than 70 more yards than Hubbard.

 This week, the Panthers' top back will get an opportunity to make up ground on the rushing leader list against the Saints. New Orleans allows 133.9 rushing yards per game and 4.52 yards per carry. With New Orleans also struggling against the pass (ranked 28th with 236.6 passing yards allowed per game), Hubbard could take advantage of quarterback Bryce Young 's passing threat against potentially lighter tackle boxes.

 Hubbard's ability to gain momentum throughout a game has made him a steady presence in an otherwise erratic offense. And his north-south rushing style should be a challenge for a Saints defense that has struggled to bring down ball carriers.

 Through eight games, Hubbard has averaged 26.5 rushing yards in the first half of games. He has nearly doubled that number with a 50.9 rushing-yards average in the second half. Hubbard also has 110 rushing yards over expected (RYOE), defined as the difference between actual rushing yards and expected rushing yards on a series of plays, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That total ranks sixth in the league entering Week 10.

 "That aligns with who Chuba is as a player, a person," Panthers offensive coordinator Brad Idzik said recently. "He's going to outwork you. He's going to outlast you. He's going to out-prepare you. ... Whereas some people wear down throughout the game, it feels like he gets stronger, because he's prepared for that."

 

 Hubbard's lopsided first- and second-half splits are partially due to Young airing out the ball consistently in the first half, which is wearing down opposing defenses, particularly in the second and third levels. The other part is that Hubbard is fresh down the stretch of games, and can bulldoze past (and through) defenders. He has 16 explosive runs (10 yards or more gained), which ranks eighth in the NFL.

 Hubbard "keeps a defense honest," said a pro scout of an NFC team that played the Panthers in the first half of the season. "Good size and vision to run between the tackles; enough speed and agility to be used on outside runs. ... You can't put him in one box [with] what he does well and what he doesn't do well."

 ESPN NFL analyst Dan Orlovsky said Hubbard has a "really strong lower half, is a smart pass catcher in space [and he] runs with energy." Hubbard's vision and patience help the Panthers stay ahead of the sticks. Historically, he is not the type of player to lose yardage on a carry because of his ability to read blocks, break tackles and power to -- at worst -- the line of scrimmage.

 "You're never going to have too many zero-[yard] runs with him, or negative runs; that's the thing I like about him," Panthers run game coordinator Harold Goodwin said last week. "There's really no perfect run every play, but he creates something on every play, so just as long as we get on people [with blocking], he's always going to come out with positive yards."

 Hubbard has also improved considerably as a pass blocker and receiver throughout his career. He had seven drops on 37 targets as a rookie in 2021, while mostly filling in for All-Pro running back Christian McCaffrey . Hubbard also had a rough three-year stretch from a blitz-pickup perspective from 2022 to 2024.

 Those third-down woes impacted his playing time and the fan base's perception of him. So, the Edmonton, Alberta, native worked to improve himself by "chopping the tree every single day."

 

 

 Preparation is key for 27-year-old RB who 'wants to be able to do everything' 

 Hubbard has a relentless training regimen, which includes what Idzik calls "the most consistent pre- and post-practice routines I've been around."

 Hubbard spends roughly 30 minutes after practice working on the Jugs machine daily, an exercise several teammates, including tight end Tommy Tremble , have embraced over the years.

 In the five seasons since his rookie campaign, Hubbard has caught 141 passes for 965 yards and six touchdowns -- with 10 total drops (just one this season), according to ESPN Research -- as a result of the tedious steps he takes throughout the week.

 According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Hubbard gave up six sacks and 41 pressures in his first four seasons. He has allowed just nine pressures and zero sacks in the 23 games since that stretch.

 "I want to be able to do everything, from blocking to catching to running the ball," Hubbard said. "Obviously, that's something that I had to work on a lot and obviously felt the criticism. I told myself, 'I would be wrong if I didn't fix this thing.' Like, I'd be wrong if I didn't put my best foot forward to be the best I can be, especially for myself and my team."

 Hubbard has still had ups and downs on the field regardless of his preparation.

 Last season, he was effectively benched after a lingering calf injury soured the start of his…

title: Why Packers can't protect Jordan Love or rush successfully
summary: The two-year demise of the Packers' offensive line began on March 10, 2025, and has no end in sight.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The beginning of the downfall of the Green Bay Packers ' offensive line can be traced to a specific day: March 10, 2025.

 That was when general manager Brian Gutekunst signed then- San Francisco 49ers guard Aaron Banks to a four-year, $77 million free agent deal. Not only have the Packers not gotten their money's worth out of Banks due to injuries and poor performance, but his signing set in a motion a game of musical chairs at just about every position on the line.

 The result was what the Packers put on display in their most recent showing, the obliteration of their pass protection by the Minnesota Vikings in Sunday's 30-10 loss at Lambeau Field. In between that March 2025 day and Sunday has been 20 months of trying to get the offensive line settled.

 Combine that with a position coach, Luke Butkus, and an offensive coordinator, Adam Stenavich, who have come under fire, and there's plenty of blame to go around for nearly two seasons' worth of offensive line issues.

 "I think it's easy to pinpoint and point the finger and everybody wants to pinpoint blame, but the blame can go to everybody," coach Matt LaFleur said this week. "It's all of us in this together. Certainly it starts with myself and then it goes to everybody else. It's coaches and players collectively."

 

 Don't forget about Gutekunst.

 He started all this by signing Banks, who had played all but six of his 2,464 snaps for the 49ers at left guard. The problem was the Packers already had a left guard. A two-time Pro Bowl left guard in Elgton Jenkins . To accommodate Banks, the Packers moved Jenkins to center for the 2025 season. From a business perspective, Jenkins wasn't thrilled with it and sat out part of the offseason program in the hope that the team would adjust his contract. Jenkins eventually returned without a new deal, fractured his lower leg halfway through last season and was released in March.

 In theory, Jenkins could have still been the Packers' left guard for this season had they never signed Banks because Jenkins had one year left on his contract when he was cut.

 This season, the Packers have started four different left guards -- Banks, Donovan Jennings , Jager Burton and Laken Tomlinson . In all, they've started seven different guards, counting the three at right guard ( Jacob Monk , Travis Glover and Tomlinson). It would have been eight had Kevin Zeitler not sustained a triceps injury in practice late last week. The in-season addition was set to start at right guard with Tomlinson back at left guard. Instead, the Packers went back to Glover at right guard.

 That means Banks, who took home $29 million last season and will make $18 million this season, not only wasn't viewed as the best option at his natural left guard spot but couldn't beat out Glover, a 2024 sixth-round pick who missed all of last season because of a shoulder injury.

 "We were going to shuffle up the O-line a little bit," LaFleur said after the Vikings' game. "I think Laken's been doing a pretty good job and we put him back to his natural position, and we were going to let Banks compete at the right guard, and he doesn't have a ton of time on task at that position, so we went the way we did tonight."

 

 To make matters worse, the Packers probably can't move on from Banks after the season. They converted his $9.5 million roster bonus in March into a signing bonus for immediate salary cap help, but it means the Packers would have to count $26.288 million in dead money on next year's cap if they release him in the offseason. The only tenable way to cut him would be as a post-June 1 cut next year, but that wouldn't erase the dead money.

 Meanwhile, the franchise left tackle they thought they picked in the first round of the 2024 draft, Jordan Morgan , didn't get his crack at the job until this season. Instead, they made Morgan play guard for two seasons, mostly as a backup or fill-in starter, for two years while they stuck with Rasheed Walker at left tackle. Walker finished on such a downer with a poor performance in the playoff loss at the Bears last season that the best he could do in free agency was a one-year, $4 million deal with the Panthers.

 In the 2025 draft, Gutekunst used a second-round pick on Anthony Belton , who also has bounced between guard and right tackle. He has played the latter ever since Zach Bako-Bewele , their best lineman, went down with a season-ending knee injury for the second straight season in Week 2.

 Gutekunst tried to fix the line in midstream earlier this season when he signed a trio of former first-round picks in Tomlinson, Zeitler and Mekhi Becton within the span of a week in late September.

 Tomlinson seemed to settle the line, and then the Packers lost center Sean Rhyan to an ankle injury in Week 7 against Detroit. John Williams , who had never taken a regular-season snap before, held up for a while in Rhyan's place until the Vikings game, where he sailed a shotgun snap wide left of quarterback Jordan Love , allowing the Vikings to recover the fumble.

 In all, Love was sacked eight times on Sunday. In two games against the blitz-happy Vikings, Love has been sacked 12 times and hit 27 times.

 "I hope it's just a Vikings thing," LaFleur said. "But you're as good as your last game and unfortunately, it wasn't good enough."

 There's reason to think it's more than just "a Vikings thing."

 Not only have they been unable to open up holes in a running game that ranks last in the NFL in rushing yards per game, but the Packers have a seasonlong pass block win rate of 31%, which is on track to be the worst by any team since ESPN first introduced the metric in 2017.

 

 It has affected Love even when the pressure hasn't gotten home -- such as the potential touchdown he missed to Christian Watson in the third quarter on Sunday when Love appeared to rush the throw even though he actually had time for a change.

 "Yeah, that affects a quarterback," Stenavich said. "Jordan will take ownership of it. He'll say, 'I've got to make that play,' obviously, because that's the kind of guy he is. But it's on everybody to make sure the quarterback feels comfortable in the pocket. Coaches, we've got to do a better job of making sure that happens, and the players on the field, definitely do too. So, again, it's on everybody."

 It may not get any easier the next time out. After this week's bye, the Packers play at the Rams, who feature two of the best pass rushers in the game in Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett .

 "I'm very confident in this team still," Love said. "It's a frustrating loss. We've talked about it. We've been here before this season. We've had some frustrating losses. We've had some good wins. So it's all about just getting back to work, cleaning it up.

 "Still a lot of season out in front of us. We get a little bit of a break to be able to get some guys back, get some bodies back. But yeah, we've just got to find ways to overcome and be better."
